You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

1: **CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** *Counselors at Law* One Vanderbilt Avenue, 44th Floor New York, New York 10017
2: 
3: Telephone: (212) 814-6000 Facsimile: (212) 814-6001 www.calderwoodharkness.com
4: 
5: October 9, 2023
6: 
7: **VIA EMAIL AND HAND DELIVERY**
8: 
9: Ardent Capital Management LLC 590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor New York, New York 10022
10: 
11: > Attention: Marcus Aldridge, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
12: >
13: > Priya Narayanan, Co-Founder & Managing Partner
14: 
15: Dear Mr. Aldridge and Ms. Narayanan:
16: 
17: We are pleased to confirm the engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness,\" the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" or \"us\") by Ardent Capital Management LLC (the \"ManCo\" or the \"Client\") to serve as legal counsel in connection with the matters described herein. This letter (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions upon which we will provide legal services to the Client in connection with this engagement.
18: 
19: **[1. Purpose and Engagement]{.underline}**
20: 
21: This Engagement Letter confirms that Calderwood & Harkness has been engaged by the ManCo to serve as legal counsel in connection with a comprehensive restructuring of the management company and realignment of economics among the principals of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$2.8 billion in total commitments. The ManCo is a Delaware limited liability company and a registered investment adviser with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") under CRD #298417. The Fund\'s sole general partner is Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the \"General Partner\"), a Delaware limited liability company.
22: 
23: The engagement encompasses the formation of new holding entities, the negotiation of separation arrangements with departing principals, the realignment of carried interest and management fee economics among continuing and next-generation principals, the solicitation of necessary limited partner consents, compliance with existing side-letter obligations, and related tax structuring. The scope of the representation, the personnel assigned to the engagement, the fee arrangement, and other terms and conditions governing this engagement are set forth in the sections that follow.
24: 
25: **[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**
26: 
27: The engagement will comprise the following principal workstreams, each of which is described in greater detail below. We understand that the scope of the engagement may evolve as the restructuring progresses; any material expansion of the scope described herein will be discussed with the Client in advance.
28: 
29: **2.1 Entity Restructuring**
30: 
31: Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the restructuring of the organizational hierarchy of the Ardent Capital platform, including:
32: 
33: \(a\) Advising on the formation of a new Delaware limited liability company, to be named Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\"), which will serve as a parent holding company for both the General Partner and the ManCo, thereby consolidating the principals\' economic interests and governance rights in a single vehicle at the top of the organizational structure.
34: 
35: \(b\) Advising on the formation of an intermediate entity, Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\"), as a wholly owned subsidiary of HoldCo and the sole member of the General Partner. GP Intermediate will serve as an interposing entity between HoldCo and the General Partner, facilitating the allocation of carried interest economics and providing structural flexibility for the admission of future principals and the potential establishment of successor funds.
36: 
37: \(c\) Drafting and negotiating limited liability company agreements for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including provisions governing capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, distribution waterfalls, governance (including voting and consent requirements), transfer restrictions, withdrawal and removal mechanics, non-compete and non-solicitation covenants, and such other provisions as may be appropriate.
38: 
39: \(d\) Preparing amended and restated limited liability company agreements for the General Partner and the ManCo to reflect the new holding-company structure, including modifications to membership interest provisions, management and officer provisions, and capital account and allocation provisions necessitated by the interposition of HoldCo and GP Intermediate.
40: 
41: \(e\) Preparing and filing Certificates of Formation with the Delaware Secretary of State for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, together with any ancillary filings or registrations required in connection with the formation and qualification of such entities.
42: 
43: \(f\) Preparing Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund (the \"LPA\") to reflect the structural changes to the General Partner, including any required modifications to the definitions, representations, and governance provisions of the LPA necessitated by the interposition of GP Intermediate and HoldCo above the General Partner.
44: 
45: **2.2 Economics Realignment**
46: 
47: Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the reallocation and documentation of the economic arrangements among the principals of the Fund, including:
48: 
49: \(a\) Advising on the reallocation of carried interest percentages and management fee profit-share allocations among the remaining and next-generation principals, taking into account the departure of the principals described in Section 2.3 below, the contributions of continuing principals, and the Firm\'s understanding of the Client\'s objectives with respect to the incentivization and retention of key personnel.
50: 
51: \(b\) Drafting an amended and restated Carried Interest Allocation Agreement reflecting the revised carried interest percentages applicable to each principal, including vesting schedules, forfeiture and clawback provisions, and mechanics for the allocation of carried interest among HoldCo members through the GP Intermediate and General Partner chain.
52: 
53: \(c\) Drafting a Management Fee Sharing and Profit Allocation Agreement at the HoldCo level, setting forth the allocation of management fee revenue among HoldCo members, including base compensation allocations, discretionary bonus pools, and distribution priorities.
54: 
55: \(d\) Revising the co-investment allocation policy to reflect the revised principal group and to address any changes in co-investment rights and priorities resulting from the restructuring.
56: 
57: **2.3 Departing Principal Separation**
58: 
59: Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the negotiation and documentation of separation arrangements for two departing principals:
60: 
61: \(a\) **David Kellner** (Senior Partner), who is retiring from the Ardent Capital platform; and
62: 
63: \(b\) **Joanna Trask** (Partner), who is departing voluntarily.
64: 
65: In connection with each departing principal, the Firm will:
66: 
67: > \(i\) Draft comprehensive separation and release agreements, addressing, among other things, the departing principal\'s resignation from all positions with the ManCo, the General Partner, HoldCo (if applicable), and all affiliated entities; mutual releases of claims; confidentiality, non-disparagement, non-solicitation, and (as applicable) non-competition covenants; cooperation obligations; and any ongoing compensation or benefits arrangements.
68: >
69: > \(ii\) Draft carry retention and clawback side letters, specifying the portion of carried interest to be retained by each departing principal with respect to investments made during his or her tenure, the clawback obligations applicable thereto, and the mechanics for the calculation and payment of any retained carry distributions.
70: >
71: > \(iii\) As applicable, draft a senior advisor agreement in favor of Mr. Kellner, setting forth the terms of any ongoing advisory role, including the scope of services, compensation, expense reimbursement, and termination provisions.
72: >
73: > \(iv\) Coordinate, as necessary and appropriate, with Whitford & Chase LLP, counsel to the departing principals, led by Richard Beaulieu, Esq., in connection with the negotiation and finalization of all separation documentation.
74: 
75: **2.4 LP Consent and Side-Letter Compliance**
76: 
77: Calderwood & Harkness will advise on all limited partner notification, consent, and compliance matters arising from the restructuring, including:
78: 
79: \(a\) Preparing materials for notification to, and solicitation of consent from, the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, including a detailed memorandum describing the restructuring and its implications for the Fund and its limited partners.
80: 
81: \(b\) Analyzing compliance with the Fund\'s fourteen (14) existing side letters, with particular attention to key-person provisions under Section 5.2 of the LPA and any expanded or supplemental key-person provisions contained in certain side letters, to determine whether the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask or the structural changes contemplated by the restructuring trigger key-person events, consent requirements, or notification obligations under any such side letter.
82: 
83: \(c\) Preparing LP notification letters to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund, describing the restructuring, the changes to the General Partner structure, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, and any other information required to be disclosed under the LPA or the applicable side letters.
84: 
85: \(d\) Advising on the preparation and filing of an amended SEC Form ADV (Parts 1 and 2) to reflect the restructuring, and advising on any other regulatory filings or notifications required in connection with the restructuring, including any applicable state regulatory filings.
86: 
87: **2.5 Tax Structuring**
88: 
89: Calderwood & Harkness will provide tax analysis and structuring advice in connection with the restructuring, including:
90: 
91: \(a\) Federal income tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including the tax treatment of the contribution or transfer of interests in the General Partner and the ManCo to HoldCo.
92: 
93: \(b\) Delaware tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including any applicable Delaware franchise taxes, formation taxes, or annual reporting obligations.
94: 
95: \(c\) Federal income tax analysis of the reallocation of carried interest among the principals, including the application of Section 1061 of the Internal Revenue Code and any implications arising from the modification of existing partnership interests.
96: 
97: \(d\) Tax analysis of the economic arrangements with departing principals, including the characterization of carry retention payments and the tax treatment of any consideration paid in connection with the separation arrangements.
98: 
99: \(e\) Section 704(b) and Section 704(c) analysis of built-in gain allocations with respect to existing Fund investments, including the impact of the restructuring on the allocation of built-in gains and losses among the principals and the mechanics for tracking and allocating such amounts through the revised entity structure.
100: 
101: \(f\) All tax structuring advice under this engagement will be provided by Sylvia Hartwell, Specialist Partner (Tax), who will coordinate as necessary with the Client\'s independent accountants at Heathrow Whitman & Co.
102: 
103: **2.6 Limitations on Scope**
104: 
105: The scope of this engagement is limited to the matters described in Sections 2.1 through 2.5 above. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the following matters are expressly excluded from the scope of this engagement:
106: 
107: \(a\) Routine fund operations, portfolio company transactions, and ongoing limited partner communications unrelated to the restructuring described herein. We understand that such matters will continue to be handled by Pemberton Hale LLP (Victoria Langford, Partner), which serves as the Fund\'s existing fund formation and operations counsel.
108: 
109: \(b\) Accounting, auditing, and valuation services, which we understand are provided by Heathrow Whitman & Co. (accountants and auditors) and Broadleaf Consulting Group (valuation), respectively. Nothing in this engagement shall be construed as the provision of accounting, auditing, or valuation advice by Calderwood & Harkness.
110: 
111: \(c\) Representation of any departing principal, including David Kellner and Joanna Trask, in connection with the restructuring or any other matter. Each departing principal is separately represented by Whitford & Chase LLP.
112: 
113: \(d\) Representation of any limited partner of the Fund in connection with the restructuring or any other matter.
114: 
115: To the extent matters arise during the course of this engagement that fall outside the scope described herein but that may benefit from our involvement, we will discuss with the Client whether and on what terms such matters should be added to the scope of this engagement or addressed through a separate engagement.
116: 
117: **[3. Engagement Team]{.underline}**
118: 
119: The following attorneys will serve as the primary members of the engagement team:
120: 
121:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
122:   **Name**                **Role**                   **Responsibility**
123:   ----------------------- -------------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
124:   Nicholas Stern          Responsible Partner        Overall supervision of the engagement, strategic advice, and senior-level involvement in key negotiations and decision points
125: 
126:   Graham Sutherland       Billing Partner            Billing, engagement administration, and fee-related communications
127: 
128:   Owen Fischer            Lead Associate             Day-to-day management of the engagement, including document drafting and negotiation, coordination with counterparty counsel (Whitford & Chase LLP) and other advisors (Pemberton Hale LLP, Heathrow Whitman & Co., Broadleaf Consulting Group)
129: 
130:   Stephen Adler           Working Associate          Document drafting, due diligence, preparation of regulatory filings, and research support
131: 
132:   Sylvia Hartwell         Specialist Partner (Tax)   Tax structuring advice, Section 704(b) and 704(c) analysis, and coordination with Heathrow Whitman & Co. on tax-related matters
133:   ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
134: 
135: From time to time, additional attorneys or paraprofessionals may be assigned to the engagement as the Firm deems necessary or appropriate to ensure efficient and timely completion of the workstreams described herein. The Client will be notified in advance of any such additions to the engagement team.
136: 
137: **[4. Fee Arrangement and Billing]{.underline}**
138: 
139: **4.1 Hourly Rates**
140: 
141: Fees for services rendered in connection with this engagement will be charged on an hourly basis at the following standard rates:
142: 
143:   -----------------------------------------------------------------------
144:   **Timekeeper Level**                **Hourly Rate**
145:   ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
146:   Partner                             \$1,650
147: 
148:   Specialist Partner                  \$1,750
149: 
150:   Senior Associate                    \$950
151: 
152:   Associate                           \$750
153:   -----------------------------------------------------------------------
154: 
155: The foregoing rates are subject to annual adjustment, typically effective January 1 of each year. In the event of any rate adjustment during the term of this engagement, the Firm will communicate such adjustment to the Client in advance. Adjusted rates will apply to services rendered on or after the effective date of the adjustment.
156: 
157: **4.2 Estimated Fee Range**
158: 
159: Based on the anticipated scope and complexity of the engagement as described in Section 2 above, and taking into account the number of workstreams, the anticipated volume of document drafting and negotiation, and the extent of LP consent and regulatory compliance work expected to be required, we estimate that total professional fees for this engagement will fall within the range of **\$850,000 to \$1,100,000**.
160: 
161: This estimate is provided solely for budgeting purposes and does not constitute a cap, ceiling, or fixed fee. Actual fees may vary from this estimate based on a number of factors, including (without limitation) the ultimate scope and complexity of the work, the nature and duration of negotiations with Whitford & Chase LLP on behalf of the departing principals, the extent and complexity of LP consent solicitation and side-letter compliance matters, the number and complexity of tax structuring issues that arise, and any expansion of the scope of the engagement beyond the matters described herein. The Firm will endeavor to keep the Client informed on an ongoing basis of any circumstances that are likely to cause total fees to exceed the upper end of the estimated range, and will discuss with the Client any potential modifications to the scope or approach to the engagement that might mitigate such costs.
162: 
163: **4.3 Disbursements.** In addition to professional fees, the Client will be responsible for reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements incurred by the Firm in connection with the engagement. Disbursements may include, without limitation, filing fees (including Delaware Secretary of State filing fees for Certificates of Formation and other filings), messenger and courier charges, travel expenses (including transportation, lodging, and meals incurred in connection with travel reasonably necessary for the engagement), document production and reproduction costs, computerized legal research charges, and similar items. All disbursements will be itemized on the Firm\'s monthly invoices.
164: 
165: **4.4 Billing Procedures**
166: 
167: Invoices for professional fees and disbursements will be rendered monthly. All invoices are due and payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. Invoices will be directed to:
168: 
169: > Ardent Capital Management LLC 590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor New York, New York 10022
170: >
171: > Attention: Finance Department
172: 
173: Copies of all invoices will also be provided to Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan at the address set forth above, or at such other address or electronic mail address as the Client may designate in writing from time to time. The Client agrees to notify the Firm promptly if there is any question or dispute regarding any invoice, so that any such matter may be addressed in a timely manner.
174: 
175: **[5. Client Identity and Conflicts]{.underline}**
176: 
177: The Client for purposes of this engagement is Ardent Capital Management LLC. Calderwood & Harkness does not represent, and will not be deemed to represent, any individual principal of the Fund (including, without limitation, Marcus Aldridge, Priya Narayanan, or any other continuing principal), any departing principal (including David Kellner and Joanna Trask), any limited partner of the Fund, or any other entity in the Ardent Capital structure (including, without limitation, the Fund, the General Partner, HoldCo, GP Intermediate, or any portfolio company) in their individual or separate capacities. Each such person and entity should consult with its own independent legal counsel with respect to any matter in which its interests may differ from those of the ManCo.
178: 
179: The Firm has conducted a conflict check in accordance with its standard procedures and, as of the date hereof, has identified no conflicts of interest that would preclude this engagement. In the event that a conflict of interest arises during the course of the engagement, the Firm will promptly notify the Client and take appropriate action, which may include seeking an informed written waiver of the conflict from the affected parties or, if a waiver cannot be obtained or is not appropriate under the circumstances, withdrawing from the representation in whole or in part as required by applicable rules of professional conduct.
180: 
181: **[6. Confidentiality]{.underline}**
182: 
183: Calderwood & Harkness will maintain the confidentiality of all information provided by or on behalf of the Client in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s professional obligations and applicable rules of professional conduct. This obligation of confidentiality extends to all non-public information concerning the Fund, the General Partner, the ManCo, HoldCo, GP Intermediate, the principals (whether continuing or departing), the limited partners, the portfolio companies, and any other entities or persons about which information is provided to the Firm in connection with the engagement.
184: 
185: The Firm may disclose confidential information as required by applicable law, regulation, or court order, or with the prior written consent of the Client. In the event the Firm receives a subpoena, court order, or other compulsory process seeking the disclosure of confidential information relating to this engagement, the Firm will, to the extent permitted by law and practicable under the circumstances, provide prompt notice to the Client prior to making any such disclosure, so that the Client may seek protective measures or take other appropriate action.
186: 
187: **[7. Document Retention]{.underline}**
188: 
189: Calderwood & Harkness will retain engagement files, including correspondence, memoranda, agreements, and other documents generated or received in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy, as in effect from time to time. Upon completion or termination of the engagement, the Firm will, at the Client\'s request and expense, return original documents to the Client or make arrangements for the transfer of files. Documents retained by the Firm may be destroyed in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy following the expiration of the applicable retention period, unless the Client requests in writing that such documents be returned or otherwise preserved.
190: 
191: **[8. Governing Law]{.underline}**
192: 
193: This Engagement Letter and the terms and conditions set forth herein shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to the conflict-of-laws principles thereof.
194: 
195: **[9. Termination]{.underline}**
196: 
197: Either party may terminate this engagement at any time upon written notice to the other party. In the event of termination by either party, the Client will remain responsible for payment of all professional fees earned and disbursements incurred through the date of termination, in accordance with the billing and payment terms set forth in Section 4 above.
198: 
199: Upon termination, Calderwood & Harkness will take reasonable steps to protect the Client\'s interests, including cooperating in the orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel designated by the Client. The Firm will promptly deliver to the Client or its successor counsel all documents and materials necessary for the continued handling of the matter, subject to the Firm\'s right to retain copies of such documents in accordance with its document retention policy and applicable rules of professional conduct.
200: 
201: **[10. Acceptance and Counterparts]{.underline}**
202: 
203: We respectfully request that the Client confirm its acceptance of the terms and conditions of this engagement by having each of the undersigned representatives execute and return the enclosed copy of this Engagement Letter to Calderwood & Harkness at the address set forth above, or by transmitting an executed copy by electronic mail to Nicholas Stern at nstern@calderwoodharkness.com or Graham Sutherland at gsutherland@calderwoodharkness.com.
204: 
205: This Engagement Letter may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart by electronic mail in portable document format (.pdf) or by other electronic transmission shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart.
206: 
207: We look forward to working with you and the Ardent Capital team on this important matter. Please do not hesitate to contact either of us if you have any questions regarding the terms of this engagement or if you would like to discuss any aspect of the representation in greater detail.
208: 
209: Very truly yours,

Dear Mr. Aldridge and Ms. Narayanan:

We are pleased to confirm the engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness,\" the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" or \"us\") by Ardent Capital Management LLC (the \"ManCo\" or the \"Client\") to serve as legal counsel in connection with the matters described herein. This letter (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions upon which we will provide legal services to the Client in connection with this engagement.
**[1. Purpose and Engagement]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter confirms that Calderwood & Harkness has been engaged by the ManCo to serve as legal counsel in connection with a comprehensive restructuring of the management company and realignment of economics among the principals of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$2.8 billion in total commitments. The ManCo is a Delaware limited liability company and a registered investment adviser with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") under CRD #298417. The Fund\'s sole general partner is Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the \"General Partner\"), a Delaware limited liability company.

The engagement encompasses the formation of new holding entities, the negotiation of separation arrangements with departing principals, the realignment of carried interest and management fee economics among continuing and next-generation principals, the solicitation of necessary limited partner consents, compliance with existing side-letter obligations, and related tax structuring. The scope of the representation, the personnel assigned to the engagement, the fee arrangement, and other terms and conditions governing this engagement are set forth in the sections that follow.
**[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

The engagement will comprise the following principal workstreams, each of which is described in greater detail below. We understand that the scope of the engagement may evolve as the restructuring progresses; any material expansion of the scope described herein will be discussed with the Client in advance.
**2.1 Entity Restructuring**
Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the restructuring of the organizational hierarchy of the Ardent Capital platform, including:

\(a\) Advising on the formation of a new Delaware limited liability company, to be named Ardent Capital Holdings LLC (\"HoldCo\"), which will serve as a parent holding company for both the General Partner and the ManCo, thereby consolidating the principals\' economic interests and governance rights in a single vehicle at the top of the organizational structure.

\(b\) Advising on the formation of an intermediate entity, Ardent GP Intermediate LLC (\"GP Intermediate\"), as a wholly owned subsidiary of HoldCo and the sole member of the General Partner. GP Intermediate will serve as an interposing entity between HoldCo and the General Partner, facilitating the allocation of carried interest economics and providing structural flexibility for the admission of future principals and the potential establishment of successor funds.

\(c\) Drafting and negotiating limited liability company agreements for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including provisions governing capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, distribution waterfalls, governance (including voting and consent requirements), transfer restrictions, withdrawal and removal mechanics, non-compete and non-solicitation covenants, and such other provisions as may be appropriate.

\(d\) Preparing amended and restated limited liability company agreements for the General Partner and the ManCo to reflect the new holding-company structure, including modifications to membership interest provisions, management and officer provisions, and capital account and allocation provisions necessitated by the interposition of HoldCo and GP Intermediate.

\(e\) Preparing and filing Certificates of Formation with the Delaware Secretary of State for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, together with any ancillary filings or registrations required in connection with the formation and qualification of such entities.

\(f\) Preparing Amendment No. 1 to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund (the \"LPA\") to reflect the structural changes to the General Partner, including any required modifications to the definitions, representations, and governance provisions of the LPA necessitated by the interposition of GP Intermediate and HoldCo above the General Partner.
**2.2 Economics Realignment**
Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the reallocation and documentation of the economic arrangements among the principals of the Fund, including:

\(a\) Advising on the reallocation of carried interest percentages and management fee profit-share allocations among the remaining and next-generation principals, taking into account the departure of the principals described in Section 2.3 below, the contributions of continuing principals, and the Firm\'s understanding of the Client\'s objectives with respect to the incentivization and retention of key personnel.

\(b\) Drafting an amended and restated Carried Interest Allocation Agreement reflecting the revised carried interest percentages applicable to each principal, including vesting schedules, forfeiture and clawback provisions, and mechanics for the allocation of carried interest among HoldCo members through the GP Intermediate and General Partner chain.

\(c\) Drafting a Management Fee Sharing and Profit Allocation Agreement at the HoldCo level, setting forth the allocation of management fee revenue among HoldCo members, including base compensation allocations, discretionary bonus pools, and distribution priorities.
\(d\) Revising the co-investment allocation policy to reflect the revised principal group and to address any changes in co-investment rights and priorities resulting from the restructuring.
**2.3 Departing Principal Separation**
Calderwood & Harkness will advise on the negotiation and documentation of separation arrangements for two departing principals:
\(a\) **David Kellner** (Senior Partner), who is retiring from the Ardent Capital platform; and
\(b\) **Joanna Trask** (Partner), who is departing voluntarily.
In connection with each departing principal, the Firm will:

> \(i\) Draft comprehensive separation and release agreements, addressing, among other things, the departing principal\'s resignation from all positions with the ManCo, the General Partner, HoldCo (if applicable), and all affiliated entities; mutual releases of claims; confidentiality, non-disparagement, non-solicitation, and (as applicable) non-competition covenants; cooperation obligations; and any ongoing compensation or benefits arrangements.

> \(ii\) Draft carry retention and clawback side letters, specifying the portion of carried interest to be retained by each departing principal with respect to investments made during his or her tenure, the clawback obligations applicable thereto, and the mechanics for the calculation and payment of any retained carry distributions.

> \(iii\) As applicable, draft a senior advisor agreement in favor of Mr. Kellner, setting forth the terms of any ongoing advisory role, including the scope of services, compensation, expense reimbursement, and termination provisions.

> \(iv\) Coordinate, as necessary and appropriate, with Whitford & Chase LLP, counsel to the departing principals, led by Richard Beaulieu, Esq., in connection with the negotiation and finalization of all separation documentation.
**2.4 LP Consent and Side-Letter Compliance**
Calderwood & Harkness will advise on all limited partner notification, consent, and compliance matters arising from the restructuring, including:

\(a\) Preparing materials for notification to, and solicitation of consent from, the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") pursuant to Section 9.4 of the LPA, including a detailed memorandum describing the restructuring and its implications for the Fund and its limited partners.

\(b\) Analyzing compliance with the Fund\'s fourteen (14) existing side letters, with particular attention to key-person provisions under Section 5.2 of the LPA and any expanded or supplemental key-person provisions contained in certain side letters, to determine whether the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask or the structural changes contemplated by the restructuring trigger key-person events, consent requirements, or notification obligations under any such side letter.

\(c\) Preparing LP notification letters to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund, describing the restructuring, the changes to the General Partner structure, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, and any other information required to be disclosed under the LPA or the applicable side letters.

\(d\) Advising on the preparation and filing of an amended SEC Form ADV (Parts 1 and 2) to reflect the restructuring, and advising on any other regulatory filings or notifications required in connection with the restructuring, including any applicable state regulatory filings.
**2.5 Tax Structuring**
Calderwood & Harkness will provide tax analysis and structuring advice in connection with the restructuring, including:

\(a\) Federal income tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including the tax treatment of the contribution or transfer of interests in the General Partner and the ManCo to HoldCo.
\(b\) Delaware tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including any applicable Delaware franchise taxes, formation taxes, or annual reporting obligations.

\(c\) Federal income tax analysis of the reallocation of carried interest among the principals, including the application of Section 1061 of the Internal Revenue Code and any implications arising from the modification of existing partnership interests.

\(d\) Tax analysis of the economic arrangements with departing principals, including the characterization of carry retention payments and the tax treatment of any consideration paid in connection with the separation arrangements.

\(e\) Section 704(b) and Section 704(c) analysis of built-in gain allocations with respect to existing Fund investments, including the impact of the restructuring on the allocation of built-in gains and losses among the principals and the mechanics for tracking and allocating such amounts through the revised entity structure.

\(f\) All tax structuring advice under this engagement will be provided by Sylvia Hartwell, Specialist Partner (Tax), who will coordinate as necessary with the Client\'s independent accountants at Heathrow Whitman & Co.
**2.6 Limitations on Scope**

The scope of this engagement is limited to the matters described in Sections 2.1 through 2.5 above. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the following matters are expressly excluded from the scope of this engagement:

\(a\) Routine fund operations, portfolio company transactions, and ongoing limited partner communications unrelated to the restructuring described herein. We understand that such matters will continue to be handled by Pemberton Hale LLP (Victoria Langford, Partner), which serves as the Fund\'s existing fund formation and operations counsel.

\(b\) Accounting, auditing, and valuation services, which we understand are provided by Heathrow Whitman & Co. (accountants and auditors) and Broadleaf Consulting Group (valuation), respectively. Nothing in this engagement shall be construed as the provision of accounting, auditing, or valuation advice by Calderwood & Harkness.

\(c\) Representation of any departing principal, including David Kellner and Joanna Trask, in connection with the restructuring or any other matter. Each departing principal is separately represented by Whitford & Chase LLP.
\(d\) Representation of any limited partner of the Fund in connection with the restructuring or any other matter.

To the extent matters arise during the course of this engagement that fall outside the scope described herein but that may benefit from our involvement, we will discuss with the Client whether and on what terms such matters should be added to the scope of this engagement or addressed through a separate engagement.
**[3. Engagement Team]{.underline}**
The following attorneys will serve as the primary members of the engagement team:
**Name**                **Role**                   **Responsibility**
Nicholas Stern          Responsible Partner        Overall supervision of the engagement, strategic advice, and senior-level involvement in key negotiations and decision points
Graham Sutherland       Billing Partner            Billing, engagement administration, and fee-related communications

Owen Fischer            Lead Associate             Day-to-day management of the engagement, including document drafting and negotiation, coordination with counterparty counsel (Whitford & Chase LLP) and other advisors (Pemberton Hale LLP, Heathrow Whitman & Co., Broadleaf Consulting Group)
Stephen Adler           Working Associate          Document drafting, due diligence, preparation of regulatory filings, and research support
Sylvia Hartwell         Specialist Partner (Tax)   Tax structuring advice, Section 704(b) and 704(c) analysis, and coordination with Heathrow Whitman & Co. on tax-related matters

From time to time, additional attorneys or paraprofessionals may be assigned to the engagement as the Firm deems necessary or appropriate to ensure efficient and timely completion of the workstreams described herein. The Client will be notified in advance of any such additions to the engagement team.
**[4. Fee Arrangement and Billing]{.underline}**
**4.1 Hourly Rates**
Fees for services rendered in connection with this engagement will be charged on an hourly basis at the following standard rates:
**Timekeeper Level**                **Hourly Rate**
Partner                             \$1,650
Specialist Partner                  \$1,750
Senior Associate                    \$950
Associate                           \$750

The foregoing rates are subject to annual adjustment, typically effective January 1 of each year. In the event of any rate adjustment during the term of this engagement, the Firm will communicate such adjustment to the Client in advance. Adjusted rates will apply to services rendered on or after the effective date of the adjustment.
**4.2 Estimated Fee Range**

Based on the anticipated scope and complexity of the engagement as described in Section 2 above, and taking into account the number of workstreams, the anticipated volume of document drafting and negotiation, and the extent of LP consent and regulatory compliance work expected to be required, we estimate that total professional fees for this engagement will fall within the range of **\$850,000 to \$1,100,000**.

This estimate is provided solely for budgeting purposes and does not constitute a cap, ceiling, or fixed fee. Actual fees may vary from this estimate based on a number of factors, including (without limitation) the ultimate scope and complexity of the work, the nature and duration of negotiations with Whitford & Chase LLP on behalf of the departing principals, the extent and complexity of LP consent solicitation and side-letter compliance matters, the number and complexity of tax structuring issues that arise, and any expansion of the scope of the engagement beyond the matters described herein. The Firm will endeavor to keep the Client informed on an ongoing basis of any circumstances that are likely to cause total fees to exceed the upper end of the estimated range, and will discuss with the Client any potential modifications to the scope or approach to the engagement that might mitigate such costs.

**4.3 Disbursements.** In addition to professional fees, the Client will be responsible for reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements incurred by the Firm in connection with the engagement. Disbursements may include, without limitation, filing fees (including Delaware Secretary of State filing fees for Certificates of Formation and other filings), messenger and courier charges, travel expenses (including transportation, lodging, and meals incurred in connection with travel reasonably necessary for the engagement), document production and reproduction costs, computerized legal research charges, and similar items. All disbursements will be itemized on the Firm\'s monthly invoices.
**4.4 Billing Procedures**
Invoices for professional fees and disbursements will be rendered monthly. All invoices are due and payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. Invoices will be directed to:
> Ardent Capital Management LLC 590 Madison Avenue, 28th Floor New York, New York 10022
> Attention: Finance Department

Copies of all invoices will also be provided to Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan at the address set forth above, or at such other address or electronic mail address as the Client may designate in writing from time to time. The Client agrees to notify the Firm promptly if there is any question or dispute regarding any invoice, so that any such matter may be addressed in a timely manner.
**[5. Client Identity and Conflicts]{.underline}**

The Client for purposes of this engagement is Ardent Capital Management LLC. Calderwood & Harkness does not represent, and will not be deemed to represent, any individual principal of the Fund (including, without limitation, Marcus Aldridge, Priya Narayanan, or any other continuing principal), any departing principal (including David Kellner and Joanna Trask), any limited partner of the Fund, or any other entity in the Ardent Capital structure (including, without limitation, the Fund, the General Partner, HoldCo, GP Intermediate, or any portfolio company) in their individual or separate capacities. Each such person and entity should consult with its own independent legal counsel with respect to any matter in which its interests may differ from those of the ManCo.

The Firm has conducted a conflict check in accordance with its standard procedures and, as of the date hereof, has identified no conflicts of interest that would preclude this engagement. In the event that a conflict of interest arises during the course of the engagement, the Firm will promptly notify the Client and take appropriate action, which may include seeking an informed written waiver of the conflict from the affected parties or, if a waiver cannot be obtained or is not appropriate under the circumstances, withdrawing from the representation in whole or in part as required by applicable rules of professional conduct.
**[6. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will maintain the confidentiality of all information provided by or on behalf of the Client in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s professional obligations and applicable rules of professional conduct. This obligation of confidentiality extends to all non-public information concerning the Fund, the General Partner, the ManCo, HoldCo, GP Intermediate, the principals (whether continuing or departing), the limited partners, the portfolio companies, and any other entities or persons about which information is provided to the Firm in connection with the engagement.

The Firm may disclose confidential information as required by applicable law, regulation, or court order, or with the prior written consent of the Client. In the event the Firm receives a subpoena, court order, or other compulsory process seeking the disclosure of confidential information relating to this engagement, the Firm will, to the extent permitted by law and practicable under the circumstances, provide prompt notice to the Client prior to making any such disclosure, so that the Client may seek protective measures or take other appropriate action.
**[7. Document Retention]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will retain engagement files, including correspondence, memoranda, agreements, and other documents generated or received in connection with this engagement, in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy, as in effect from time to time. Upon completion or termination of the engagement, the Firm will, at the Client\'s request and expense, return original documents to the Client or make arrangements for the transfer of files. Documents retained by the Firm may be destroyed in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy following the expiration of the applicable retention period, unless the Client requests in writing that such documents be returned or otherwise preserved.
**[8. Governing Law]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter and the terms and conditions set forth herein shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to the conflict-of-laws principles thereof.
**[9. Termination]{.underline}**

Either party may terminate this engagement at any time upon written notice to the other party. In the event of termination by either party, the Client will remain responsible for payment of all professional fees earned and disbursements incurred through the date of termination, in accordance with the billing and payment terms set forth in Section 4 above.

Upon termination, Calderwood & Harkness will take reasonable steps to protect the Client\'s interests, including cooperating in the orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel designated by the Client. The Firm will promptly deliver to the Client or its successor counsel all documents and materials necessary for the continued handling of the matter, subject to the Firm\'s right to retain copies of such documents in accordance with its document retention policy and applicable rules of professional conduct.
**[10. Acceptance and Counterparts]{.underline}**

We respectfully request that the Client confirm its acceptance of the terms and conditions of this engagement by having each of the undersigned representatives execute and return the enclosed copy of this Engagement Letter to Calderwood & Harkness at the address set forth above, or by transmitting an executed copy by electronic mail to Nicholas Stern at nstern@calderwoodharkness.com or Graham Sutherland at gsutherland@calderwoodharkness.com.

This Engagement Letter may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart by electronic mail in portable document format (.pdf) or by other electronic transmission shall be effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart.

We look forward to working with you and the Ardent Capital team on this important matter. Please do not hesitate to contact either of us if you have any questions regarding the terms of this engagement or if you would like to discuss any aspect of the representation in greater detail.
Very truly yours,
**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP**
Nicholas Stern Partner
Graham Sutherland Partner
**ACKNOWLEDGMENT AND ACCEPTANCE**
The undersigned, on behalf of Ardent Capital Management LLC, hereby acknowledge receipt of the foregoing Engagement Letter and agree to the terms and conditions set forth therein.
**ARDENT CAPITAL MANAGEMENT LLC**

**Sylvia Hartwell** --- *Specialist Partner*, Tax Practice Group (New York office). Ms. Hartwell has eighteen (18) years of experience in partnership taxation, fund structuring, and international tax planning for private investment funds. She will advise on all fund-level tax structuring matters described in Section 2.5 above, including the design of the blocker entity, the structure of the parallel vehicles, the ERISA analysis, Section 1061 carried interest compliance, and international tax considerations for the Offshore Feeder and non-U.S. investors. Ms. Hartwell can be reached at shartwell@calderwoodharkness.com or (212) 555-9440.

Additional attorneys, paraprofessionals, or other support staff may be assigned to the Engagement as needed to ensure timely and efficient delivery of work product. The Client will be informed of any material changes to the composition of the core engagement team.
**[4. Client Responsibilities]{.underline}**

The efficient and timely completion of the Engagement will depend on the Client\'s cooperation in providing information, reviewing drafts, and coordinating with third parties. In particular, the Client agrees to the following:

> \(a\) **Information Provision.** The Client shall provide, on a timely basis, all information necessary for the preparation of the formation and offering documents, including (without limitation) information regarding the investment strategy, target geographies and sectors, fund terms (including management fees, carried interest, hurdle rate, waterfall structure, GP commitment, key person provisions, and investment period terms), and track record data for the predecessor funds (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund I LP through Harrowgate Private Equity Fund IV LP), including realized and unrealized performance data, attribution, and relevant disclaimers.

> \(b\) **Draft Review Timeline.** The Client shall review and provide comments on drafts within the timelines agreed upon between the Client and the Firm in order to meet the following target fundraise schedule:
> \(i\) PPM initial draft delivered by the Firm to the Client: **May 1, 2025**;
> \(ii\) LPA initial draft delivered by the Firm to the Client: **May 9, 2025**;
> \(iii\) Distribution of PPM, LPA summary, and subscription documents to prospective limited partners: **June 2, 2025**; and
> \(iv\) Target First Close: **August 15, 2025**.

> The foregoing timeline is subject to adjustment based on the Client\'s review and comment cycle and the progress of investor negotiations. The Firm and the Client will communicate regularly regarding the status of the fundraise timeline and will work cooperatively to address any delays or changes in schedule.
> \(c\) **Investor Counsel Coordination.** The Client shall coordinate communications with investor-side counsel, including but not limited to:
> \(i\) Aldworth & McBride LLP, counsel for Northmoor State Pension System;
> \(ii\) Pelham Chambers LLP, counsel for The Kingsbridge Endowment Fund; and
> \(iii\) Ramsden Clarke International LLP, counsel for Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority.
> The Client shall provide introductions and facilitate initial communications between the Firm and investor-side counsel as necessary to commence side letter negotiations.

> \(d\) **Third-Party Coordination.** The Client shall be responsible for the engagement and coordination of the placement agent (Osprey Capital Markets LLC) and the fund administrator (Pinnacle Fund Services LLC), and shall facilitate the Firm\'s access to such parties and their respective documentation as necessary for the Firm to perform the work described in Section 2.

> \(e\) **Cayman Islands Counsel.** The Client shall engage local Cayman Islands counsel as necessary for the formation and regulatory filings of the Offshore Feeder. The Client shall provide the Firm with the identity and contact information of such Cayman Islands counsel in a timely manner so that we may coordinate the drafting of the Offshore Feeder\'s exempted limited partnership agreement.

> \(f\) **PPM Data.** The Client shall provide final data for the predecessor fund performance tables, team biographies, and other factual content to be included in the PPM. The Client shall be responsible for the accuracy and completeness of all factual information provided for inclusion in the PPM.

31: **[1. Purpose and Introduction]{.underline}**
32: 
33: Calderwood & Harkness LLP is pleased to confirm its engagement by Cobalt Ventures LP to serve as fund counsel in connection with the structuring, formation, and fund-raising for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP (the \"Fund\" or \"CLSO Fund I\"), a proposed Delaware limited partnership. 36: 
37: This Letter sets forth the terms under which Calderwood & Harkness will provide legal services in connection with the structuring, formation, and fund-raising of the Fund and related entities, and it supersedes any prior oral or written understandings between the parties regarding the scope and terms of this engagement.
38: 
39: **[2. Client Identification]{.underline}**
40: 
41: The Client for purposes of this engagement is **Cobalt Ventures LP**, a Delaware limited partnership (Delaware LP File No. 7824931; California Secretary of State File No. 202118412387; EIN: 83-2947561), with its principal place of business at 3400 Sand Hill Road, Suite 220, Menlo Park, California 94025, and its registered agent for service of process in Delaware at Hollowell Technologies, 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.

44: 
45: > \(a\) **Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership, to be formed, which will serve as the main investment vehicle for the Fund;
46: >
47: > \(b\) **Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC** --- a Delaware limited liability company, to be formed, which will serve as the general partner of the Fund;
48: >
49: > \(c\) **Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC** --- a Delaware limited liability company, to be formed, which will serve as the management company and will be party to the management agreement with the Fund; and
50: >
51: > \(d\) **Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I (Blocker), Inc.** --- a Delaware C-Corporation, to be formed if and when determined to be necessary or advisable for purposes of establishing a taxable blocker structure for certain categories of investors, including tax-exempt and non-U.S. limited partners.
52: 
53: The foregoing entities are collectively referred to herein as the \"Fund Entities.\" As formation documents are prepared and filed for each Fund Entity, such entity shall be deemed a client of the Firm under the terms of this Letter without the need for a separate engagement letter, unless the Firm and the Client agree otherwise in writing.
54: 
55: **Important Clarification Regarding Scope of Representation.** Calderwood & Harkness does not represent, and will not represent in connection with this engagement, any individual limited partner or prospective limited partner of the Fund, any placement agent engaged by the Fund (including sagebrush Capital Partners LLC), or any other third-party service provider to the Fund. Each such party should retain and rely upon its own independent legal counsel with respect to its interests in or obligations to the Fund.

58:

To the extent the Client requests legal services that fall outside the scope described in this Section 3, such services will be provided only upon mutual written agreement and may be subject to a separate engagement letter or an amendment to this Letter.
60: 
61: **3.1 Fund Structuring and Entity Formation**
62: 
63: Calderwood & Harkness will advise the Client on the optimal legal and organizational structure for the Fund and will be responsible for the formation of each Fund Entity. This workstream will include the following:
64: 
65: > \(a\) **Structural Analysis.** Analysis of fund structure alternatives, including a single-tier Delaware limited partnership, parallel fund structures (including for non-U.S. investors or investors requiring a separately managed account), blocker corporation arrangements, alternative investment vehicle (\"AIV\") structures, and master-feeder options. Our analysis will take into account the anticipated investor base, the Client\'s investment strategy, tax efficiency, regulatory considerations, and administrative complexity.
66: >
67: > \(b\) **Fund Structuring Memorandum.** Preparation and delivery of a comprehensive Fund Structuring Memorandum setting forth Calderwood & Harkness\'s analysis and recommendations regarding the recommended fund architecture, including a diagram of the proposed entity structure, a summary of the principal advantages and disadvantages of each structural alternative considered, and our recommended approach. The target delivery date for the Fund Structuring Memorandum is **April 30, 2026**.
68: >
69: > \(c\) **Delaware Formation Filings.** Preparation and filing of the Certificate of Limited Partnership for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP, and the Certificates of Formation for Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC and Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC, with the Delaware Division of Corporations. 70: >
71: > \(d\) **EIN Applications.** Preparation and submission of IRS Form SS-4 (Application for Employer Identification Number) for CLSO Fund I, CLSO GP I, and CLSO Management I.
72: >
73: > \(e\) **Registered Agent Coordination.** Coordination with Hollowell Technologies, the Client\'s designated registered agent in Delaware, to ensure that each Fund Entity is properly set up for service of process and annual compliance filings.
74: 
75: **3.2 Tax Structuring**
76: 
77: Calderwood & Harkness will provide tax structuring advice in connection with the formation and operation of the Fund, including the following:
78: 
79: > \(a\) **Tax Structuring Memorandum.** Preparation and delivery of a Tax Structuring Memorandum addressing the following topics, among others: (i) unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") and effectively connected income (\"ECI\") planning for tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors; (ii) the application of IRC §1061 to carried interest allocations, including holding period analysis and the implications of the three-year holding period requirement; (iii) state income tax nexus considerations for the Fund, the general partner, and the management company, with a particular focus on Delaware, California, Oregon, Connecticut, and Massachusetts; (iv) blocker corporation structuring, including the use of a Delaware C-Corporation to mitigate UBTI and ECI for certain categories of investors; and (v) carry escrow implications, including the tax treatment of amounts held in escrow and the timing of income recognition. The target delivery date for the Tax Structuring Memorandum is **April 30, 2026**.
80: >
81: > \(b\) **Coordination with Tax Advisor.** Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Greystone Tax Advisors LLC (Kenneth Liu, Managing Director), the Client\'s independent tax advisor, on all tax structuring matters. 86:

The first draft of the LPA is targeted for delivery on or about **May 31, 2026**. The LPA will address, among other things, the following key economic and governance terms:
88: >
89: > *Economic Terms:*
90: >
91: > • Management Fee: 2.00% per annum of committed capital during the investment period, stepping down to 2.00% of invested capital (or net invested capital, as determined) thereafter;
92: >
93: > • Carried Interest: 20% of net profits, subject to the preferred return and GP catch-up described below;
94: >
95: > • Preferred Return: 8% per annum, compounded annually;
96: >
97: > • GP Catch-up: 100% of distributions after the preferred return has been achieved, until the general partner has received 20% of cumulative net profits;
98: >
99: > • Carry Escrow: 30% of carried interest distributions to be held in escrow pending final liquidation of the Fund to secure the general partner\'s clawback obligation;
100: >
101: > • Clawback: Standard general partner clawback obligation, net of taxes, to be triggered upon final liquidation of the Fund to the extent the general partner has received carried interest distributions in excess of amounts to which it is entitled on a cumulative basis;
102: >
103: > • Recycling Allowance: 15% of aggregate committed capital may be recycled (i.e., proceeds from realized investments may be recalled for reinvestment during the investment period);
104: >
105: > • Concentration Limit: No more than 15% of aggregate committed capital may be invested in any single portfolio company, measured at the time of investment;
106: >
107: > • Organizational Expense Cap: Organizational expenses in excess of \$1,500,000 shall be borne by the general partner or the management company;
108: >
109: > • Broken-Deal Expense Cap: Broken-deal expenses in excess of \$500,000 per unconsummated transaction shall be borne by the general partner or the management company.
110: >
111: > *Governance Provisions:*
112: >
113: > • Key Person Event provisions, identifying Dr. Marcus Yeung and Priya Dasgupta as key persons, with suspension of the investment period upon a key person event and reinstatement mechanics;
114: >
115: > • Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") provisions, including composition, authority, and procedures for the resolution of conflicts of interest;
116: >
117: > • Removal rights, including removal of the general partner for cause and no-fault removal by a supermajority in interest of the limited partners;
118: >
119: > • Default provisions, including the consequences of a limited partner\'s failure to fund a capital call;
120: >
121: > • Excuse and exclusion provisions, permitting limited partners to be excused or excluded from particular investments under specified circumstances (e.g., legal, regulatory, or tax impediments).
122: >
123: > *Regulatory Provisions:*
124: >
125: > • ERISA compliance provisions, including the Fund\'s election to qualify as a \"venture capital operating company\" (\"VCOC\") under Department of Labor Regulation §2510.3-101(d), and the related covenants and operating requirements necessary to maintain VCOC status.
126: >
127: > \(b\) **GP LLC Agreement.** Drafting of the Limited Liability Company Agreement of Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC (the \"GP LLC Agreement\"), setting forth the rights, obligations, and economic arrangements of the members of the general partner entity.
128: >
129: > \(c\) **Management Company LLC Agreement.** Drafting of the Limited Liability Company Agreement of Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC (the \"Management Company LLC Agreement\"), setting forth the organizational and operational terms of the management company.
130: >
131: > \(d\) **Subscription Agreement and Investor Questionnaire.** Preparation of the form Subscription Agreement and Investor Questionnaire to be executed by each limited partner at the time of its commitment to the Fund, including representations and warranties regarding accredited investor and qualified purchaser status, ERISA status, tax status, OFAC compliance, and beneficial ownership.

134: 
135: Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the confidential Private Placement Memorandum (the \"PPM\") for the Fund. The PPM will be the principal marketing and disclosure document used in connection with the offering of limited partnership interests in the Fund to prospective investors. We anticipate delivering an outline and first draft of the PPM on or about **June 30, 2026**. The PPM will include, among other things, the following:
136: 
137: > \(a\) An executive summary of the terms of the offering;
138: >
139: > \(b\) A description of the Fund\'s investment strategy, investment process, and target sectors within the life-sciences space;
140: >
141: > \(c\) A comprehensive discussion of risk factors associated with an investment in the Fund, including market risks, strategy-specific risks, regulatory risks, and structural risks;
142: >
143: > \(d\) Regulatory disclosures, including disclosures required under applicable federal and state securities laws;
144: >
145: > \(e\) Biographies of the principals and key investment professionals of Cobalt;
146: >
147: > \(f\) A summary of the material U.S. federal income tax considerations applicable to an investment in the Fund, including considerations for taxable U.S. investors, tax-exempt U.S. investors, and non-U.S. investors; and
148: >
149: > \(g\) Appendices containing the form of LPA and Subscription Agreement, or summaries thereof.

151: **3.5 Placement Agent Agreement**
152: 
153: Calderwood & Harkness will negotiate and draft the exclusive global placement agent agreement (the \"Placement Agent Agreement\") between the Client (or the general partner of the Fund, as applicable) and sagebrush Capital Partners LLC (\"Sagebrush\") (CRD No. 298714; primary contact: Jonathan Mercer, Managing Director).
