Details regarding the videoconference will be provided under separate cover. LPAC members may deliver their consent either by execution and return of the enclosed Consent in advance of the meeting or by affirmative vote at the meeting itself.
28: 
29: In connection with the Restructuring, the General Partner has engaged **Calderwood & Harkness LLP** (Nicholas Stern, responsible partner, and Owen Fischer, lead associate) as restructuring counsel to advise the General Partner on the structural, governance, and transactional aspects of the Restructuring. **Pemberton Hale LLP** (Victoria Langford, responsible partner) continues to serve as fund counsel for routine Fund operations and has provided guidance on LPA interpretation and side-letter compliance matters. The General Partner wishes to note that Calderwood & Harkness LLP and Pemberton Hale LLP represent the General Partner and the Fund, respectively, and do not represent any individual limited partner or the LPAC. LPAC members are encouraged to consult with their own legal and tax advisors as they deem appropriate.
30: 
31: **[2. Background on the Fund]{.underline}**
32: 
33: Ardent Capital Partners III LP is a Delaware limited partnership formed in 2019 for the purpose of making control-oriented equity investments in middle-market industrial and business-services companies, primarily in North America. The Fund targets companies with enterprise values between \$150 million and \$750 million, with a focus on sectors where the principals of Ardent Capital have deep operational expertise and established proprietary sourcing channels, including industrial technology, specialty distribution, environmental services, and facility management.
34: 
35: As of the date of this letter, the key parameters of the Fund are as follows:
36: 
37: **Total Commitments.** The Fund has aggregate capital commitments of **\$2.8 billion** from **47 limited partners**, including leading public pension systems, endowments and foundations, insurance companies, family offices, and other institutional investors.
38: 
39: **Capital Called and Invested.** As of the date of this letter, the Fund has called approximately **\$1.96 billion** in capital from its limited partners, representing approximately **70%** of total commitments. Of the capital called, approximately **\$1.88 billion** has been invested or is reserved for follow-on investments across the Fund\'s portfolio, with the remainder having been applied to management fees, organizational expenses, and other fund-level charges.
40: 
41: **Portfolio Overview.** The Fund currently holds **11 active portfolio companies** across the industrial and business-services sectors. Each portfolio company is actively managed by a dedicated deal team within Ardent Capital, and in each case Ardent Capital holds board representation and exercises significant operational influence.
42: 
43: **Fund Performance.** As of September 30, 2023, the most recent quarterly valuation date, the Fund\'s aggregate performance was as follows:
44: 
45: > • Gross multiple of invested capital (\"**MOIC**\"): **1.42x**
46: >
47: > • Net internal rate of return (\"**IRR**\"): **14.7%**
48: >
49: > • Total unrealized value: approximately **\$2.33 billion** (based on fair market valuations prepared by Broadleaf Consulting Group, the Fund\'s independent valuation advisor, and reviewed by Heathrow Whitman & Co., the Fund\'s auditor)
50: >
51: > • Total realized proceeds: approximately **\$445 million** (reflecting partial realizations and dividend recapitalizations from three portfolio companies)
52: 
53: **GP Commitment.** The General Partner and its principals have made an aggregate capital commitment to the Fund of **\$42 million**, representing **1.5%** of total Fund commitments, which is consistent with the minimum GP commitment described in the Fund\'s confidential private placement memorandum dated March 2019.
54: 
55: **Investment Period.** The investment period of the Fund commenced on June 30, 2019, and is scheduled to end on **June 30, 2025**. As of the date of this letter, the Fund has approximately \$840 million of uncalled capital commitments available for new investments during the remaining portion of the investment period.
56: 
57: **Fund Term.** The term of the Fund is scheduled to expire on **December 31, 2029**, subject to two one-year extensions at the discretion of the General Partner in accordance with Section 12.1 of the LPA.
58: 
59: **Management Fee.** The Fund pays an annual management fee equal to **1.75%** of aggregate capital commitments during the investment period (approximately **\$49 million** per year at current commitment levels) and **1.50%** of invested capital (net of write-downs and write-offs) following the expiration of the investment period. The management fee is payable quarterly in advance to Ardent Capital Management LLC (the \"**Management Company**\" or \"**ManCo**\"), the Fund\'s SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD #298417).
60: 
61: **Carried Interest.** The General Partner is entitled to receive carried interest equal to **20%** of the Fund\'s net profits (calculated on a whole-Fund basis), subject to an **8% per annum preferred return** to the limited partners and a **100% catch-up** to the General Partner thereafter, in each case as more fully described in Section 6.2 of the LPA.
62: 
63: **Current Principals.** As of the date of this letter, the principals of the General Partner are:
64: 
65: > • **Marcus Aldridge** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
66: >
67: > • **Priya Narayanan** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
68: >
69: > • **David Kellner** --- Senior Partner
70: >
71: > • **Joanna Trask** --- Partner
72: >
73: > • **Robert Hsiao** --- Partner
74: 
75: **[3. Summary of Proposed Restructuring]{.underline}**
76: 
77: **3.1 Overview.** The Restructuring involves four principal workstreams, each of which is described in detail below:
78: 
79: > 1\. **Entity Restructuring** --- the formation of new holding entities and the reorganization of the ownership structure of the General Partner and the Management Company;
80: >
81: > 2\. **Economics Realignment** --- the reallocation of carried interest and Management Company profit-share economics among the remaining and next-generation principals;
82: >
83: > 3\. **Departing Principal Separation** --- the orderly departure and separation of two senior principals, David Kellner and Joanna Trask, and the negotiation and execution of their respective separation and release agreements; and
84: >
85: > 4\. **LP Consent and Side-Letter Compliance** --- the solicitation of LPAC consent as required under the LPA and compliance with notification and consent provisions contained in individual side letters.
86: 
87: The principal rationale for the Restructuring is fourfold: (a) to implement a thoughtful succession plan that positions Ardent Capital for long-term stability and continuity across multiple fund cycles; (b) to enhance governance by establishing a consolidated holding company structure with clear lines of authority and accountability; (c) to integrate the next generation of talent --- specifically, Elena Marchetti and Samuel Okonkwo, each of whom has made significant contributions to the Fund\'s investment activities and portfolio management --- into the economic and governance framework of Ardent Capital; and (d) to facilitate the orderly transition of responsibilities and economics following the planned departure of David Kellner (who is retiring after a distinguished career) and the voluntary departure of Joanna Trask. The General Partner believes that the Restructuring will strengthen Ardent Capital\'s institutional platform and is in the best interests of the Fund and its limited partners.
88: 
89: **3.2 Entity Restructuring**
90: 
91: The structural component of the Restructuring involves the formation of two new Delaware limited liability companies and the reorganization of the ownership structure of the General Partner and the Management Company. Specifically:
92: 
93: **Formation of Ardent Capital Holdings LLC.** A new Delaware limited liability company, **Ardent Capital Holdings LLC** (\"**HoldCo**\"), will be formed to serve as the parent holding company of both the Management Company and the General Partner (through an intermediate entity). HoldCo will be governed by an amended and restated limited liability company agreement that provides for the rights, obligations, and economic entitlements of its members.
94: 
95: **Formation of Ardent GP Intermediate LLC.** A new Delaware limited liability company, **Ardent GP Intermediate LLC** (\"**GP Intermediate**\"), will be formed to serve as an intermediate holding entity between HoldCo and the General Partner. GP Intermediate will be a wholly owned subsidiary of HoldCo.
96: 
97: **Post-Restructuring Organizational Structure.** Upon completion of the Restructuring, the organizational structure will be as follows:
98: 
99: > • HoldCo will be the **sole member** of both (i) the Management Company (Ardent Capital Management LLC, SEC-registered investment adviser, CRD #298417) and (ii) GP Intermediate.
100: >
101: > • GP Intermediate will be the **sole member** of the General Partner (Ardent Capital GP III LLC).
102: >
103: > • The General Partner will continue to serve as the sole general partner of the Fund.
104: 
105: **Current Structure Being Replaced.** Under the current organizational structure, the five individual principals (Aldridge, Narayanan, Kellner, Trask, and Hsiao) hold direct membership interests in both the General Partner and the Management Company. The direct-ownership model was adopted at the time of the Fund\'s formation for simplicity, but as Ardent Capital has grown and matured as an institution, the General Partner has determined that a consolidated holding company structure is more appropriate and consistent with industry best practices for institutional-quality private equity platforms. The holding company structure also facilitates the admission and withdrawal of individual principals without requiring amendments to the organizational documents of the General Partner or the Management Company, thereby reducing administrative burden and the need for LP consents in connection with future personnel changes (to the extent otherwise permitted under the LPA).
106: 
107: **HoldCo Membership.** Following the Restructuring, the members of HoldCo will be:
108: 
109: > • **Marcus Aldridge** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
110: >
111: > • **Priya Narayanan** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
112: >
113: > • **Robert Hsiao** --- Partner
114: >
115: > • **Elena Marchetti** --- Principal
116: >
117: > • **Samuel Okonkwo** --- Principal
118: 
119: The **Managing Members** of HoldCo will be Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan, who will have the authority to manage the business and affairs of HoldCo (and, through HoldCo, the Management Company and the General Partner) in accordance with the terms of the HoldCo operating agreement.
120: 
121: **3.3 Principal Departures**
122: 
123: **David Kellner --- Retirement.** David Kellner, a Senior Partner of Ardent Capital and one of the founding members of the Fund III team, has informed the General Partner of his intention to retire from active investment management. Mr. Kellner, age 61, has had a distinguished 35-year career in private equity and has been instrumental in building Ardent Capital\'s industrial services franchise. His retirement will be effective **March 31, 2024**, following a transition period during which he will work with the remaining principals to ensure an orderly handover of his portfolio company board responsibilities and deal-team oversight functions. Following his retirement, Mr. Kellner will transition to a **Senior Advisor** role for a two-year advisory term (April 1, 2024 through March 31, 2026), during which he will be available for consultation on portfolio matters at an annual advisory fee of **\$350,000** per year.
124: 
125: The key economic terms of Mr. Kellner\'s departure are as follows:
126: 
127: > • **Current GP Interest:** Mr. Kellner currently holds a **15%** membership interest in the General Partner and is entitled to a **15%** share of the Fund\'s carried interest.
128: >
129: > • **Carried Interest Retention:** Mr. Kellner will retain **100%** of his vested carried interest in Fund III, which, based on the September 30, 2023 valuation, represents an accrued carried interest of approximately **\$13,140,000**. Such retained carried interest will be subject to a modified clawback obligation that will continue for a period of **three (3) years** following Mr. Kellner\'s retirement date (i.e., through March 31, 2027), at which time his clawback exposure will expire.
130: >
131: > • **Management Company Economics:** Mr. Kellner\'s share of ManCo profit distributions will cease effective as of his retirement date. He will receive no further profit-share or other economic distributions from the Management Company after March 31, 2024.
132: >
133: > • **Restrictive Covenants:** Mr. Kellner has agreed to a **non-competition** covenant for a period of **18 months** following his retirement date and **non-solicitation** covenants with respect to both employees and limited partners of Ardent Capital for a period of **24 months** each following his retirement date.
134: 
135: **Joanna Trask --- Voluntary Departure.** Joanna Trask, a Partner of Ardent Capital, has informed the General Partner of her decision to depart from Ardent Capital voluntarily to pursue a senior role at another investment firm. Ms. Trask, age 48, has been a valued member of the Ardent Capital team and has led several successful investments in the business-services sector during her tenure. Her departure will be effective **April 15, 2024**, following a transition period during which she will complete the handover of her responsibilities.
136: 
137: The key economic terms of Ms. Trask\'s departure are as follows:
138: 
139: > • **Current GP Interest:** Ms. Trask currently holds a **12%** membership interest in the General Partner and is entitled to a **12%** share of the Fund\'s carried interest.
140: >
141: > • **Carried Interest Retention:** Ms. Trask will retain **60%** of her vested carried interest in Fund III, representing approximately **\$6,307,200** based on the September 30, 2023 valuation. The remaining **40%** of her vested carried interest, representing approximately **\$4,204,800**, will be forfeited. In addition, Ms. Trask will forfeit **100%** of any unvested carried interest. Her retained carried interest will be subject to a clawback obligation for a period of **two (2) years** following her departure date (i.e., through April 15, 2026).
142: >
143: > • **Separation Payment:** Ms. Trask will receive a one-time lump-sum separation payment of **\$1,250,000**, payable within 30 days following her departure date, in consideration of her execution of a general release of claims and compliance with her ongoing restrictive covenants.
144: >
145: > • **Restrictive Covenants:** Ms. Trask has agreed to a **non-competition** covenant for a period of **12 months** following her departure date and **non-solicitation** covenants with respect to employees and limited partners of Ardent Capital for a period of **18 months** each following her departure date.
146: 
147: Both departures are subject to the terms of negotiated separation and release agreements (each, a \"**Separation Agreement**\") that are currently being finalized. Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask are each independently represented by **Whitford & Chase LLP** (Richard Beaulieu, partner) in connection with the negotiation of their respective Separation Agreements. Copies of the Separation Agreements (in substantially final form) will be made available to LPAC members upon request, subject to applicable confidentiality provisions.
148: 
149: **3.4 Economics Realignment**
150: 
151: Upon the effective dates of the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, the aggregate **27%** carried interest share held by the departing principals (representing Mr. Kellner\'s 15% plus Ms. Trask\'s 12%) will be redistributed among the remaining and next-generation principals. The proposed post-Restructuring allocation of carried interest is set forth in the following table:
152: 
153:   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
154:   **Principal**     **Pre-Restructuring Carry Share**   **Post-Restructuring Carry Share**   **Change**
155:   ----------------- ----------------------------------- ------------------------------------ -----------------
156:   Marcus Aldridge   35%                                 42%                                  +7%
157: 
158:   Priya Narayanan   30%                                 36%                                  +6%
159: 
160:   Robert Hsiao      8%                                  14%                                  +6%
161: 
162:   Elena Marchetti   0%                                  4%                                   +4%
163: 
164:   Samuel Okonkwo    0%                                  4%                                   +4%
165: 
166:   **Total**         **100%**                            **100%**                             **---**
167:   ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
168: 
169: The same percentage allocations reflected in the table above will apply to Management Company Profit Share distributions. For reference, Management Company Profit Share distributions (representing approximately 35% of annual management fee revenue retained by the Management Company after deduction of operating expenses) have averaged approximately **\$17,150,000 per year** over the life of the Fund to date. The economics realignment does not alter the overall quantum of management fees or carried interest payable by the Fund or its limited partners; rather, it reflects solely the internal allocation of such economics among the principals of the General Partner and the Management Company.
170: 
171: The following fundamental economic terms of the Fund remain **unchanged** by the Restructuring:
172: 
173: > • The carried interest rate remains at **20%** of net profits;
174: >
175: > • The preferred return remains at **8%** per annum;
176: >
177: > • The catch-up remains at **100%** to the General Partner;
178: >
179: > • The clawback structure remains unchanged, including **100% joint and several liability** of the General Partner and its principals, with a **30% individual escrow** of carried interest distributions (the \"**Escrow**\"); and
180: >
181: > • The mechanics of carried interest calculation (whole-Fund, European-style waterfall) remain unchanged.
182: 
183: With respect to **accrued carried interest**, as of September 30, 2023, the Fund\'s total accrued (but undistributed) carried interest was approximately **\$87,600,000**. The vested and retained portions of Mr. Kellner\'s and Ms. Trask\'s accrued carried interest will be carved out and preserved in accordance with the terms of their respective Separation Agreements, as described in Section 3.3 above. The redistribution set forth in the table above applies on a **go-forward basis** to carried interest attributable to future appreciation in the Fund\'s portfolio from and after the effective date of the Restructuring. The specific mechanics of the transition and allocation of accrued versus go-forward carry will be set forth in the amended carry allocation provisions of the GP\'s organizational documents and in Amendment No. 1 to the LPA.
184: 
185: **3.5 GP Commitment Reallocation**
186: 
187: The total GP commitment to the Fund is **\$42,000,000**. As a result of the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, their combined unfunded GP commitment of **\$3,402,000** (consisting of \$1,890,000 attributable to Mr. Kellner and \$1,512,000 attributable to Ms. Trask) must be assumed by the remaining principals to ensure that the GP commitment is fully funded through the remainder of the investment period and the balance of the Fund\'s term. The funded portions of Mr. Kellner\'s and Ms. Trask\'s GP commitments will remain in the Fund and will be treated in accordance with their respective Separation Agreements and the LPA.
188: 
189: The unfunded portion of the departing principals\' GP commitment will be assumed by the remaining HoldCo members on a pro rata basis, consistent with their post-Restructuring percentage interests, as follows:
190: 
191:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
192:   **Principal**           **Post-Restructuring %**   **Assumed Unfunded GP Commitment**
193:   ----------------------- -------------------------- ------------------------------------
194:   Marcus Aldridge         42%                        \$1,428,840
195: 
196:   Priya Narayanan         36%                        \$1,224,720
197: 
198:   Robert Hsiao            14%                        \$476,280
199: 
200:   Elena Marchetti         4%                         \$136,080
201: 
202:   Samuel Okonkwo          4%                         \$136,080
203: 
204:   **Total**               **100%**                   **\$3,402,000**
205:   ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
206: 
207: Each remaining principal has confirmed his or her willingness and ability to fund the assumed unfunded GP commitment in accordance with the Fund\'s capital call schedule. The General Partner has received written commitments from each of the above-named individuals to this effect.
208: 
209: **[4. Key-Person Analysis]{.underline}**
210: 
211: Section 5.2 of the LPA designates **Marcus Aldridge** and **Priya Narayanan** as \"Key Persons\" of the Fund. Under Section 5.2, a \"Key Person Event\" is triggered if: (a) both Key Persons cease to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund, or (b) one Key Person ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund and a replacement Key Person is not approved by the LPAC within 120 calendar days of such cessation.
212: 
213: The General Partner confirms that **neither David Kellner nor Joanna Trask is a designated Key Person** under Section 5.2 of the LPA. Accordingly, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask **do not trigger a Key Person Event** under the LPA, and the investment period will continue without suspension or interruption.
214: 
215: Both Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan will continue to serve as Co-Founders and Managing Partners of Ardent Capital and will continue to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund, consistent with their obligations under the LPA. Neither Mr. Aldridge nor Ms. Narayanan has any present intention to reduce his or her involvement with the Fund or to pursue other business activities that would be inconsistent with the Key Person requirements of Section 5.2.
216: 
217: **Expanded Key-Person Provisions in Side Letters.** In connection with its side-letter compliance review, the General Partner and its counsel have identified that **6 of the 14** side letters currently in effect contain \"expanded key person\" provisions that designate David Kellner as a \"Contributing Person\" or use analogous terminology. These provisions generally require that the General Partner provide the applicable limited partner with written notice within **15 business days** of any Contributing Person\'s departure from active involvement with the Fund. The General Partner will comply with all such notification requirements in a timely manner.
218: 
219: Additionally, the General Partner has identified that **3 of the 6** side letters containing expanded key-person provisions grant the applicable limited partner a right to request a **90-day suspension** of the investment period pending LPAC review in the event of a Contributing Person\'s departure. The General Partner does not believe that such a suspension is warranted in light of (i) the continued full-time involvement of both designated Key Persons (Aldridge and Narayanan), (ii) the orderly nature of Mr. Kellner\'s planned retirement and transition to a Senior Advisor role, (iii) the depth and continuity of the remaining investment team, and (iv) the ongoing strong performance of the Fund\'s portfolio. The General Partner intends to engage directly and proactively with each of the applicable limited partners to discuss these matters and to address any questions or concerns.
220: 
221: **[5. Side-Letter Compliance Summary]{.underline}**
222: 
223: The Fund has **14 side letters** currently in effect with various limited partners. In connection with the Restructuring, the General Partner and its counsel at Pemberton Hale LLP and Calderwood & Harkness LLP have conducted a comprehensive review of all 14 side letters to assess compliance with the terms thereof in light of the proposed Restructuring. The results of that review are summarized below:
224: 
225: **Most Favored Nation (\"MFN\") Provisions.** Eleven (11) of the 14 side letters contain MFN provisions requiring the General Partner to notify the applicable limited partner of, and/or extend to the applicable limited partner, any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner. The General Partner has determined that the Restructuring does not involve the granting of any more favorable terms to any limited partner and, accordingly, no MFN issues have been identified.
226: 
227: **Fee discount or Rebate Provisions.** Eight (8) of the 14 side letters contain provisions granting the applicable limited partner a fee discount, management fee rebate, or other fee accommodation. The Restructuring does not alter the management fee rates of the Fund (which remain at 1.75% of committed capital during the investment period and 1.50% of invested capital thereafter), and accordingly, no impact on fee-related side-letter provisions has been identified.
228: 
229: **Co-Investment Priority Rights.** Nine (9) of the 14 side letters contain provisions granting the applicable limited partner co-investment priority rights or preferential co-investment allocation rights. The General Partner intends to update its internal co-investment allocation policy to reflect the revised principal allocations and team responsibilities resulting from the Restructuring. The fundamental co-investment allocation framework --- which is based on commitment size, co-investment track record, and ability to respond to allocation opportunities within the required timeframe --- will remain substantively unchanged. LPAC members with co-investment priority rights will continue to receive advance notice of co-investment opportunities in accordance with their respective side letters.
230: 
231: **Material Change Notification and Consent Provisions.** Four (4) side letters --- those with **Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System**, **Pinnacle Insurance Group**, **Crestwood Endowment Partners**, and **Haverford Capital Partners** --- contain provisions requiring prior written notice and, in certain cases, affirmative consent to any \"material change in the management structure\" of the General Partner, the Management Company, or the Fund\'s investment team. This letter and the LPAC consent process described herein serve as the required notification to the three LPAC members (Ridgeline, Pinnacle, and Crestwood) that hold such provisions. Separate notice will be provided to Haverford Capital Partners in accordance with the specific requirements of its side letter.
232: 
233: A detailed **Side-Letter Compliance and Key-Person Analysis Memorandum** is currently being finalized by Pemberton Hale LLP and Calderwood & Harkness LLP. This memorandum, which will include a provision-by-provision analysis of each side letter and a comprehensive key-person analysis, will be made available to LPAC members upon request. LPAC members who wish to receive a copy of the memorandum should contact Nicholas Stern at Calderwood & Harkness LLP or Victoria Langford at Pemberton Hale LLP.
234: 
235: **[6. Impact on Fund Operations]{.underline}**
236: 
237: The General Partner wishes to assure the LPAC that the Restructuring has been designed to ensure continuity and stability in the Fund\'s operations and to minimize any disruption to the Fund\'s investment activities and portfolio management. Specifically, the General Partner confirms that the Restructuring will have **no impact** on the following:
238: 
239: > • **Investment Strategy:** The Fund\'s investment strategy --- control-oriented equity investments in middle-market industrial and business-services companies --- will remain unchanged. The Fund will continue to pursue its stated investment objectives in accordance with the investment guidelines and restrictions set forth in the LPA and the Fund\'s confidential private placement memorandum.

Dear Members of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee:
**[1. Introduction and Purpose]{.underline}**

Ardent Capital GP III LLC (the \"**General Partner**\"), as the sole general partner of Ardent Capital Partners III LP (the \"**Fund**\" or \"**Fund III**\"), is writing to provide notification of, and to solicit the consent of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"**LPAC**\" or the \"**Committee**\") to, a proposed restructuring of the management company and related realignment of economics among the Fund\'s principals (the \"**Restructuring**\"). This letter sets forth the material terms and circumstances of the Restructuring in detail, together with the background and rationale therefor, and identifies the specific consents being requested of the LPAC in connection therewith.

The consent of the LPAC is being solicited pursuant to **Section 9.4** of the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Fund, dated as of April 15, 2019 (as amended, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"**LPA**\"), which requires LPAC consent for certain material structural changes to the General Partner, the management company, or the economic arrangements among the principals, including without limitation any change in the ownership or control of the General Partner, any material amendment to the organizational documents of the General Partner, and any material realignment of the carried interest or management fee economics of the Fund.

The General Partner respectfully requests that each LPAC member review this letter and the enclosed materials carefully and execute and return the enclosed Form of Written Consent (the \"**Consent**\") at or prior to the LPAC meeting scheduled for **February 14, 2024**, which will be held virtually via videoconference. Details regarding the videoconference will be provided under separate cover. LPAC members may deliver their consent either by execution and return of the enclosed Consent in advance of the meeting or by affirmative vote at the meeting itself.

In connection with the Restructuring, the General Partner has engaged **Calderwood & Harkness LLP** (Nicholas Stern, responsible partner, and Owen Fischer, lead associate) as restructuring counsel to advise the General Partner on the structural, governance, and transactional aspects of the Restructuring. **Pemberton Hale LLP** (Victoria Langford, responsible partner) continues to serve as fund counsel for routine Fund operations and has provided guidance on LPA interpretation and side-letter compliance matters. The General Partner wishes to note that Calderwood & Harkness LLP and Pemberton Hale LLP represent the General Partner and the Fund, respectively, and do not represent any individual limited partner or the LPAC. LPAC members are encouraged to consult with their own legal and tax advisors as they deem appropriate.
**[2. Background on the Fund]{.underline}**

Ardent Capital Partners III LP is a Delaware limited partnership formed in 2019 for the purpose of making control-oriented equity investments in middle-market industrial and business-services companies, primarily in North America. The Fund targets companies with enterprise values between \$150 million and \$750 million, with a focus on sectors where the principals of Ardent Capital have deep operational expertise and established proprietary sourcing channels, including industrial technology, specialty distribution, environmental services, and facility management.
As of the date of this letter, the key parameters of the Fund are as follows:

**Total Commitments.** The Fund has aggregate capital commitments of **\$2.8 billion** from **47 limited partners**, including leading public pension systems, endowments and foundations, insurance companies, family offices, and other institutional investors.

**Capital Called and Invested.** As of the date of this letter, the Fund has called approximately **\$1.96 billion** in capital from its limited partners, representing approximately **70%** of total commitments. Of the capital called, approximately **\$1.88 billion** has been invested or is reserved for follow-on investments across the Fund\'s portfolio, with the remainder having been applied to management fees, organizational expenses, and other fund-level charges.

**Portfolio Overview.** The Fund currently holds **11 active portfolio companies** across the industrial and business-services sectors. Each portfolio company is actively managed by a dedicated deal team within Ardent Capital, and in each case Ardent Capital holds board representation and exercises significant operational influence.
**Fund Performance.** As of September 30, 2023, the most recent quarterly valuation date, the Fund\'s aggregate performance was as follows:
> • Gross multiple of invested capital (\"**MOIC**\"): **1.42x**
> • Net internal rate of return (\"**IRR**\"): **14.7%**

> • Total unrealized value: approximately **\$2.33 billion** (based on fair market valuations prepared by Broadleaf Consulting Group, the Fund\'s independent valuation advisor, and reviewed by Heathrow Whitman & Co., the Fund\'s auditor)
> • Total realized proceeds: approximately **\$445 million** (reflecting partial realizations and dividend recapitalizations from three portfolio companies)

**GP Commitment.** The General Partner and its principals have made an aggregate capital commitment to the Fund of **\$42 million**, representing **1.5%** of total Fund commitments, which is consistent with the minimum GP commitment described in the Fund\'s confidential private placement memorandum dated March 2019.

**Investment Period.** The investment period of the Fund commenced on June 30, 2019, and is scheduled to end on **June 30, 2025**. As of the date of this letter, the Fund has approximately \$840 million of uncalled capital commitments available for new investments during the remaining portion of the investment period.

**Fund Term.** The term of the Fund is scheduled to expire on **December 31, 2029**, subject to two one-year extensions at the discretion of the General Partner in accordance with Section 12.1 of the LPA.

**Management Fee.** The Fund pays an annual management fee equal to **1.75%** of aggregate capital commitments during the investment period (approximately **\$49 million** per year at current commitment levels) and **1.50%** of invested capital (net of write-downs and write-offs) following the expiration of the investment period. The management fee is payable quarterly in advance to Ardent Capital Management LLC (the \"**Management Company**\" or \"**ManCo**\"), the Fund\'s SEC-registered investment adviser (CRD #298417).

**Carried Interest.** The General Partner is entitled to receive carried interest equal to **20%** of the Fund\'s net profits (calculated on a whole-Fund basis), subject to an **8% per annum preferred return** to the limited partners and a **100% catch-up** to the General Partner thereafter, in each case as more fully described in Section 6.2 of the LPA.
**Current Principals.** As of the date of this letter, the principals of the General Partner are:
> • **Marcus Aldridge** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
> • **Priya Narayanan** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
> • **David Kellner** --- Senior Partner
> • **Joanna Trask** --- Partner
> • **Robert Hsiao** --- Partner
**[3. Summary of Proposed Restructuring]{.underline}**
**3.1 Overview.** The Restructuring involves four principal workstreams, each of which is described in detail below:
> 1\. **Entity Restructuring** --- the formation of new holding entities and the reorganization of the ownership structure of the General Partner and the Management Company;
> 2\. **Economics Realignment** --- the reallocation of carried interest and Management Company profit-share economics among the remaining and next-generation principals;

> 3\. **Departing Principal Separation** --- the orderly departure and separation of two senior principals, David Kellner and Joanna Trask, and the negotiation and execution of their respective separation and release agreements; and

> 4\. **LP Consent and Side-Letter Compliance** --- the solicitation of LPAC consent as required under the LPA and compliance with notification and consent provisions contained in individual side letters.

The principal rationale for the Restructuring is fourfold: (a) to implement a thoughtful succession plan that positions Ardent Capital for long-term stability and continuity across multiple fund cycles; (b) to enhance governance by establishing a consolidated holding company structure with clear lines of authority and accountability; (c) to integrate the next generation of talent --- specifically, Elena Marchetti and Samuel Okonkwo, each of whom has made significant contributions to the Fund\'s investment activities and portfolio management --- into the economic and governance framework of Ardent Capital; and (d) to facilitate the orderly transition of responsibilities and economics following the planned departure of David Kellner (who is retiring after a distinguished career) and the voluntary departure of Joanna Trask. The General Partner believes that the Restructuring will strengthen Ardent Capital\'s institutional platform and is in the best interests of the Fund and its limited partners.
**3.2 Entity Restructuring**

The structural component of the Restructuring involves the formation of two new Delaware limited liability companies and the reorganization of the ownership structure of the General Partner and the Management Company. Specifically:

**Formation of Ardent Capital Holdings LLC.** A new Delaware limited liability company, **Ardent Capital Holdings LLC** (\"**HoldCo**\"), will be formed to serve as the parent holding company of both the Management Company and the General Partner (through an intermediate entity). HoldCo will be governed by an amended and restated limited liability company agreement that provides for the rights, obligations, and economic entitlements of its members.

**Formation of Ardent GP Intermediate LLC.** A new Delaware limited liability company, **Ardent GP Intermediate LLC** (\"**GP Intermediate**\"), will be formed to serve as an intermediate holding entity between HoldCo and the General Partner. GP Intermediate will be a wholly owned subsidiary of HoldCo.
**Post-Restructuring Organizational Structure.** Upon completion of the Restructuring, the organizational structure will be as follows:
> • HoldCo will be the **sole member** of both (i) the Management Company (Ardent Capital Management LLC, SEC-registered investment adviser, CRD #298417) and (ii) GP Intermediate.
> • GP Intermediate will be the **sole member** of the General Partner (Ardent Capital GP III LLC).
> • The General Partner will continue to serve as the sole general partner of the Fund.

**Current Structure Being Replaced.** Under the current organizational structure, the five individual principals (Aldridge, Narayanan, Kellner, Trask, and Hsiao) hold direct membership interests in both the General Partner and the Management Company. The direct-ownership model was adopted at the time of the Fund\'s formation for simplicity, but as Ardent Capital has grown and matured as an institution, the General Partner has determined that a consolidated holding company structure is more appropriate and consistent with industry best practices for institutional-quality private equity platforms. The holding company structure also facilitates the admission and withdrawal of individual principals without requiring amendments to the organizational documents of the General Partner or the Management Company, thereby reducing administrative burden and the need for LP consents in connection with future personnel changes (to the extent otherwise permitted under the LPA).
**HoldCo Membership.** Following the Restructuring, the members of HoldCo will be:
> • **Marcus Aldridge** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
> • **Priya Narayanan** --- Co-Founder & Managing Partner
> • **Robert Hsiao** --- Partner
> • **Elena Marchetti** --- Principal
> • **Samuel Okonkwo** --- Principal

The **Managing Members** of HoldCo will be Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan, who will have the authority to manage the business and affairs of HoldCo (and, through HoldCo, the Management Company and the General Partner) in accordance with the terms of the HoldCo operating agreement.
**3.3 Principal Departures**

**David Kellner --- Retirement.** David Kellner, a Senior Partner of Ardent Capital and one of the founding members of the Fund III team, has informed the General Partner of his intention to retire from active investment management. Mr. Kellner, age 61, has had a distinguished 35-year career in private equity and has been instrumental in building Ardent Capital\'s industrial services franchise. His retirement will be effective **March 31, 2024**, following a transition period during which he will work with the remaining principals to ensure an orderly handover of his portfolio company board responsibilities and deal-team oversight functions. Following his retirement, Mr. Kellner will transition to a **Senior Advisor** role for a two-year advisory term (April 1, 2024 through March 31, 2026), during which he will be available for consultation on portfolio matters at an annual advisory fee of **\$350,000** per year.
The key economic terms of Mr. Kellner\'s departure are as follows:
> • **Current GP Interest:** Mr. Kellner currently holds a **15%** membership interest in the General Partner and is entitled to a **15%** share of the Fund\'s carried interest.

> • **Carried Interest Retention:** Mr. Kellner will retain **100%** of his vested carried interest in Fund III, which, based on the September 30, 2023 valuation, represents an accrued carried interest of approximately **\$13,140,000**. Such retained carried interest will be subject to a modified clawback obligation that will continue for a period of **three (3) years** following Mr. Kellner\'s retirement date (i.e., through March 31, 2027), at which time his clawback exposure will expire.

> • **Management Company Economics:** Mr. Kellner\'s share of ManCo profit distributions will cease effective as of his retirement date. He will receive no further profit-share or other economic distributions from the Management Company after March 31, 2024.

> • **Restrictive Covenants:** Mr. Kellner has agreed to a **non-competition** covenant for a period of **18 months** following his retirement date and **non-solicitation** covenants with respect to both employees and limited partners of Ardent Capital for a period of **24 months** each following his retirement date.

**Joanna Trask --- Voluntary Departure.** Joanna Trask, a Partner of Ardent Capital, has informed the General Partner of her decision to depart from Ardent Capital voluntarily to pursue a senior role at another investment firm. Ms. Trask, age 48, has been a valued member of the Ardent Capital team and has led several successful investments in the business-services sector during her tenure. Her departure will be effective **April 15, 2024**, following a transition period during which she will complete the handover of her responsibilities.
The key economic terms of Ms. Trask\'s departure are as follows:
> • **Current GP Interest:** Ms. Trask currently holds a **12%** membership interest in the General Partner and is entitled to a **12%** share of the Fund\'s carried interest.

> • **Carried Interest Retention:** Ms. Trask will retain **60%** of her vested carried interest in Fund III, representing approximately **\$6,307,200** based on the September 30, 2023 valuation. The remaining **40%** of her vested carried interest, representing approximately **\$4,204,800**, will be forfeited. In addition, Ms. Trask will forfeit **100%** of any unvested carried interest. Her retained carried interest will be subject to a clawback obligation for a period of **two (2) years** following her departure date (i.e., through April 15, 2026).

> • **Separation Payment:** Ms. Trask will receive a one-time lump-sum separation payment of **\$1,250,000**, payable within 30 days following her departure date, in consideration of her execution of a general release of claims and compliance with her ongoing restrictive covenants.

> • **Restrictive Covenants:** Ms. Trask has agreed to a **non-competition** covenant for a period of **12 months** following her departure date and **non-solicitation** covenants with respect to employees and limited partners of Ardent Capital for a period of **18 months** each following her departure date.

Both departures are subject to the terms of negotiated separation and release agreements (each, a \"**Separation Agreement**\") that are currently being finalized. Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask are each independently represented by **Whitford & Chase LLP** (Richard Beaulieu, partner) in connection with the negotiation of their respective Separation Agreements. Copies of the Separation Agreements (in substantially final form) will be made available to LPAC members upon request, subject to applicable confidentiality provisions.
**3.4 Economics Realignment**

Upon the effective dates of the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, the aggregate **27%** carried interest share held by the departing principals (representing Mr. Kellner\'s 15% plus Ms. Trask\'s 12%) will be redistributed among the remaining and next-generation principals. The proposed post-Restructuring allocation of carried interest is set forth in the following table:
**Principal**     **Pre-Restructuring Carry Share**   **Post-Restructuring Carry Share**   **Change**
Marcus Aldridge   35%                                 42%                                  +7%
Priya Narayanan   30%                                 36%                                  +6%
Robert Hsiao      8%                                  14%                                  +6%
Elena Marchetti   0%                                  4%                                   +4%
Samuel Okonkwo    0%                                  4%                                   +4%

The same percentage allocations reflected in the table above will apply to Management Company Profit Share distributions. For reference, Management Company Profit Share distributions (representing approximately 35% of annual management fee revenue retained by the Management Company after deduction of operating expenses) have averaged approximately **\$17,150,000 per year** over the life of the Fund to date. The economics realignment does not alter the overall quantum of management fees or carried interest payable by the Fund or its limited partners; rather, it reflects solely the internal allocation of such economics among the principals of the General Partner and the Management Company.
The following fundamental economic terms of the Fund remain **unchanged** by the Restructuring:
> • The carried interest rate remains at **20%** of net profits;
> • The preferred return remains at **8%** per annum;
> • The catch-up remains at **100%** to the General Partner;

> • The clawback structure remains unchanged, including **100% joint and several liability** of the General Partner and its principals, with a **30% individual escrow** of carried interest distributions (the \"**Escrow**\"); and
> • The mechanics of carried interest calculation (whole-Fund, European-style waterfall) remain unchanged.

With respect to **accrued carried interest**, as of September 30, 2023, the Fund\'s total accrued (but undistributed) carried interest was approximately **\$87,600,000**. The vested and retained portions of Mr. Kellner\'s and Ms. Trask\'s accrued carried interest will be carved out and preserved in accordance with the terms of their respective Separation Agreements, as described in Section 3.3 above. The redistribution set forth in the table above applies on a **go-forward basis** to carried interest attributable to future appreciation in the Fund\'s portfolio from and after the effective date of the Restructuring. The specific mechanics of the transition and allocation of accrued versus go-forward carry will be set forth in the amended carry allocation provisions of the GP\'s organizational documents and in Amendment No. 1 to the LPA.
**3.5 GP Commitment Reallocation**

The total GP commitment to the Fund is **\$42,000,000**. As a result of the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask, their combined unfunded GP commitment of **\$3,402,000** (consisting of \$1,890,000 attributable to Mr. Kellner and \$1,512,000 attributable to Ms. Trask) must be assumed by the remaining principals to ensure that the GP commitment is fully funded through the remainder of the investment period and the balance of the Fund\'s term. The funded portions of Mr. Kellner\'s and Ms. Trask\'s GP commitments will remain in the Fund and will be treated in accordance with their respective Separation Agreements and the LPA.

The unfunded portion of the departing principals\' GP commitment will be assumed by the remaining HoldCo members on a pro rata basis, consistent with their post-Restructuring percentage interests, as follows:
**Principal**           **Post-Restructuring %**   **Assumed Unfunded GP Commitment**
Marcus Aldridge         42%                        \$1,428,840
Priya Narayanan         36%                        \$1,224,720
Robert Hsiao            14%                        \$476,280
Elena Marchetti         4%                         \$136,080
Samuel Okonkwo          4%                         \$136,080

Each remaining principal has confirmed his or her willingness and ability to fund the assumed unfunded GP commitment in accordance with the Fund\'s capital call schedule. The General Partner has received written commitments from each of the above-named individuals to this effect.
**[4. Key-Person Analysis]{.underline}**

Section 5.2 of the LPA designates **Marcus Aldridge** and **Priya Narayanan** as \"Key Persons\" of the Fund. Under Section 5.2, a \"Key Person Event\" is triggered if: (a) both Key Persons cease to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund, or (b) one Key Person ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund and a replacement Key Person is not approved by the LPAC within 120 calendar days of such cessation.

The General Partner confirms that **neither David Kellner nor Joanna Trask is a designated Key Person** under Section 5.2 of the LPA. Accordingly, the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask **do not trigger a Key Person Event** under the LPA, and the investment period will continue without suspension or interruption.

Both Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan will continue to serve as Co-Founders and Managing Partners of Ardent Capital and will continue to devote substantially all of their business time and attention to the investment activities of the Fund, consistent with their obligations under the LPA. Neither Mr. Aldridge nor Ms. Narayanan has any present intention to reduce his or her involvement with the Fund or to pursue other business activities that would be inconsistent with the Key Person requirements of Section 5.2.

**Expanded Key-Person Provisions in Side Letters.** In connection with its side-letter compliance review, the General Partner and its counsel have identified that **6 of the 14** side letters currently in effect contain \"expanded key person\" provisions that designate David Kellner as a \"Contributing Person\" or use analogous terminology. These provisions generally require that the General Partner provide the applicable limited partner with written notice within **15 business days** of any Contributing Person\'s departure from active involvement with the Fund. The General Partner will comply with all such notification requirements in a timely manner.

Additionally, the General Partner has identified that **3 of the 6** side letters containing expanded key-person provisions grant the applicable limited partner a right to request a **90-day suspension** of the investment period pending LPAC review in the event of a Contributing Person\'s departure. The General Partner does not believe that such a suspension is warranted in light of (i) the continued full-time involvement of both designated Key Persons (Aldridge and Narayanan), (ii) the orderly nature of Mr. Kellner\'s planned retirement and transition to a Senior Advisor role, (iii) the depth and continuity of the remaining investment team, and (iv) the ongoing strong performance of the Fund\'s portfolio. The General Partner intends to engage directly and proactively with each of the applicable limited partners to discuss these matters and to address any questions or concerns.
**[5. Side-Letter Compliance Summary]{.underline}**

The Fund has **14 side letters** currently in effect with various limited partners. In connection with the Restructuring, the General Partner and its counsel at Pemberton Hale LLP and Calderwood & Harkness LLP have conducted a comprehensive review of all 14 side letters to assess compliance with the terms thereof in light of the proposed Restructuring. The results of that review are summarized below:

**Most Favored Nation (\"MFN\") Provisions.** Eleven (11) of the 14 side letters contain MFN provisions requiring the General Partner to notify the applicable limited partner of, and/or extend to the applicable limited partner, any more favorable terms granted to any other limited partner. The General Partner has determined that the Restructuring does not involve the granting of any more favorable terms to any limited partner and, accordingly, no MFN issues have been identified.

**Fee discount or Rebate Provisions.** Eight (8) of the 14 side letters contain provisions granting the applicable limited partner a fee discount, management fee rebate, or other fee accommodation. The Restructuring does not alter the management fee rates of the Fund (which remain at 1.75% of committed capital during the investment period and 1.50% of invested capital thereafter), and accordingly, no impact on fee-related side-letter provisions has been identified.

**Co-Investment Priority Rights.** Nine (9) of the 14 side letters contain provisions granting the applicable limited partner co-investment priority rights or preferential co-investment allocation rights. The General Partner intends to update its internal co-investment allocation policy to reflect the revised principal allocations and team responsibilities resulting from the Restructuring. The fundamental co-investment allocation framework --- which is based on commitment size, co-investment track record, and ability to respond to allocation opportunities within the required timeframe --- will remain substantively unchanged. LPAC members with co-investment priority rights will continue to receive advance notice of co-investment opportunities in accordance with their respective side letters.

**Material Change Notification and Consent Provisions.** Four (4) side letters --- those with **Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System**, **Pinnacle Insurance Group**, **Crestwood Endowment Partners**, and **Haverford Capital Partners** --- contain provisions requiring prior written notice and, in certain cases, affirmative consent to any \"material change in the management structure\" of the General Partner, the Management Company, or the Fund\'s investment team. This letter and the LPAC consent process described herein serve as the required notification to the three LPAC members (Ridgeline, Pinnacle, and Crestwood) that hold such provisions. Separate notice will be provided to Haverford Capital Partners in accordance with the specific requirements of its side letter.

A detailed **Side-Letter Compliance and Key-Person Analysis Memorandum** is currently being finalized by Pemberton Hale LLP and Calderwood & Harkness LLP. This memorandum, which will include a provision-by-provision analysis of each side letter and a comprehensive key-person analysis, will be made available to LPAC members upon request. LPAC members who wish to receive a copy of the memorandum should contact Nicholas Stern at Calderwood & Harkness LLP or Victoria Langford at Pemberton Hale LLP.
**[6. Impact on Fund Operations]{.underline}**

The General Partner wishes to assure the LPAC that the Restructuring has been designed to ensure continuity and stability in the Fund\'s operations and to minimize any disruption to the Fund\'s investment activities and portfolio management. Specifically, the General Partner confirms that the Restructuring will have **no impact** on the following:

> • **Investment Strategy:** The Fund\'s investment strategy --- control-oriented equity investments in middle-market industrial and business-services companies --- will remain unchanged. The Fund will continue to pursue its stated investment objectives in accordance with the investment guidelines and restrictions set forth in the LPA and the Fund\'s confidential private placement memorandum.

200:

202: 
203: **RESOLVED**, that the LPAC hereby authorizes the General Partner and each of its authorized officers, members, managers, and representatives to take all such further actions and to negotiate, execute, and deliver all such further documents, instruments, certificates, and agreements as may be necessary or desirable to carry out the purposes and intent of the foregoing resolutions, including without limitation the filing of any certificates or other documents with any governmental authority, the engagement of legal counsel, accountants, and other advisors, and the making of any notices, disclosures, or filings required by applicable law, regulation, or the terms of the LPA or any side letter.

206:

211: > \(ii\) the LPAC Presentation Memorandum, including all exhibits and appendices thereto, summarizing the Restructuring, the proposed entity structure, the economic realignment, and the departure arrangements; and
212: >
213: > \(iii\) summaries of each of the Restructuring Documents, including summary term sheets for the organizational documents, the LPA Amendment, the Carried Interest Allocation Agreement, the Management Fee Sharing and Profit Allocation Agreement, and the Separation and Release Agreements.

This Consent shall not be deemed to constitute a waiver of any other rights of the LPAC or any individual LPAC member under the LPA, nor shall it be deemed a waiver of any rights, claims, or remedies of any limited partner of the Fund under the LPA, any side letter, or applicable law.
216: 
217: Nothing in this Consent shall modify, limit, or waive any rights, obligations, or protections of any limited partner under any side letter or supplemental agreement executed in connection with such limited partner\'s subscription to the Fund, including without limitation any most-favored-nation (\"MFN\") rights, expanded key-person provisions, enhanced fee transparency or fee reduction provisions, co-investment rights or obligations, information rights, restructuring consent or notification provisions, or any other supplemental or protective provisions contained in any such side letter or supplemental agreement. The General Partner shall comply with any notification, consent, or other requirements applicable to the Restructuring under any such side letter or supplemental agreement.

Delivery of an executed counterpart of a signature page to this Consent by facsimile or electronic transmission (including portable document format (.pdf) or any electronic signature complying with the U.S. federal ESIGN Act of 2000 or the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act) shall be deemed delivery of an original executed counterpart and shall be effective as an original signature for all purposes.
