**AGREEMENT OF LIMITED PARTNERSHIP**
**HARROWGATE PRIVATE EQUITY FUND V LP**

This Agreement of Limited Partnership (this **\"Agreement\"**) of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the **\"Partnership\"** or the **\"Fund\"**), is entered into as of the date of the First Close (as defined below) by and among Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, as the general partner (the **\"General Partner\"** or **\"GP\"**), and each Person who is admitted as a limited partner of the Partnership (each, a **\"Limited Partner\"** or **\"LP\"** and, collectively, the **\"Limited Partners\"**), in each case in accordance with the terms and conditions set forth herein. The General Partner and the Limited Partners are sometimes referred to herein individually as a **\"Partner\"** and collectively as the **\"Partners.\"**
**RECITALS**

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner has caused a Certificate of Limited Partnership to be filed (or to be filed on or prior to the date hereof) with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, forming the Partnership as a limited partnership under and pursuant to the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, 6 Del. C. § 17-101 *et seq.*, as amended from time to time (the **\"Act\"**);

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner desires to establish the Fund as a private equity investment vehicle for the purpose of making equity and equity-related investments, directly or indirectly, primarily in North American mid-market and upper-mid-market companies in the industrials, business services, healthcare services, and technology-enabled services sectors;

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner is the sole general partner of the Partnership and is a Delaware limited liability company, the sole member of which is Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the **\"Sponsor\"**);

**WHEREAS**, the Sponsor has sponsored and managed four predecessor private equity funds (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund I LP through Harrowgate Private Equity Fund IV LP) and manages approximately \$5.8 billion in aggregate assets under management as of the date hereof;

**WHEREAS**, each Limited Partner desires to make a capital commitment to the Partnership on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement and in the Subscription Agreement executed by such Limited Partner; and
**WHEREAS**, the Partners desire to set forth their respective rights, obligations, and duties with respect to the Partnership.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Partners hereby agree as follows:
**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**
**[Section 1.1 --- Defined Terms]{.underline}**
As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:
**\"Act\"** means the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, 6 Del. C. § 17-101 *et seq.*, as it may be amended from time to time, and any successor statute thereto.

**\"Adjusted Capital Account\"** means, with respect to each Partner, such Partner\'s Capital Account as of the end of the relevant Fiscal Year or other applicable period, as adjusted in accordance with Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(4), (5), and (6), after giving effect to the following adjustments: (a) credit to such Capital Account any amounts that such Partner is obligated to restore or is treated as obligated to restore pursuant to Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(c), 1.704-2(g)(1), and 1.704-2(i)(5); and (b) debit to such Capital Account the items described in Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(4), (5), and (6). The foregoing definition is intended to comply with the provisions of Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d) and shall be interpreted consistently therewith.

**\"Affiliate\"** means, with respect to any Person, any other Person that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with, such Person. For purposes of this definition, **\"control\"** (including the correlative terms \"controlling,\" \"controlled by,\" and \"under common control with\") means the possession, directly or indirectly, of the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of a Person, whether through ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise, and shall be deemed to exist when a Person owns, directly or indirectly, fifty percent (50%) or more of the outstanding voting securities or equity interests of the applicable entity. Notwithstanding the foregoing, no Limited Partner shall be deemed to be an Affiliate of the General Partner, the Sponsor, or any other Limited Partner solely by reason of such Limited Partner\'s investment in the Fund.

**\"Aggregate Commitments\"** means the aggregate Capital Commitments of all Partners (including the GP Commitment), as set forth in the Schedule of Partners, as the same may be updated from time to time. At the hard cap, Aggregate Commitments shall not exceed Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000).
**\"Associate\"** means any member, partner, managing director, principal, officer, director, employee, or agent of the General Partner, the Sponsor, or any of their respective Affiliates.

**\"Benefit Plan Investor\"** means a \"benefit plan investor\" as defined in 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101(f)(2), as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA, including (a) any \"employee benefit plan\" as defined in Section 3(3) of ERISA that is subject to Part 4 of Subtitle B of Title I of ERISA, (b) any \"plan\" as defined in Section 4975(e)(1) of the Code that is subject to Section 4975 of the Code, and (c) any entity whose underlying assets include \"plan assets\" by reason of a plan\'s investment in such entity.

**\"Blocker Entity\"** means HGF V blocker Corp., a Delaware C corporation formed for the benefit of certain tax-exempt or non-U.S. Limited Partners to mitigate UBTI or effectively connected income concerns, as the General Partner may determine to be appropriate in connection with the Fund\'s investment program.

**\"Bridge Financing\"** means any short-term Fund-level borrowing (whether under the Subscription Credit Facility or otherwise) used to fund Portfolio Investments or other Partnership obligations in advance of or in lieu of issuing Capital Calls, which borrowing shall not remain outstanding for more than one hundred eighty (180) consecutive days from the date of the applicable borrowing.

**\"Business Day\"** means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or a day on which commercial banks in New York, New York or Wilmington, Delaware are authorized or required by law or executive order to remain closed.

**\"Capital Account\"** means, with respect to each Partner, the capital account established and maintained for such Partner in accordance with Section 704(b) of the Code and Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv), as further described in Section 6.1 of this Agreement.

**\"Capital Call\"** or **\"Drawdown Notice\"** means a written notice issued by the General Partner to the Partners requiring such Partners to fund all or a portion of their unfunded Capital Commitments, specifying the aggregate amount of such capital contribution, the purpose thereof, and the date on which such funds are due, in accordance with Section 4.2 of this Agreement.

**\"Capital Commitment\"** means, with respect to each Partner, the aggregate amount that such Partner has committed to contribute to the Partnership as capital contributions, as set forth in such Partner\'s Subscription Agreement and reflected in the Schedule of Partners, as the same may be updated from time to time.

**\"Carried Interest\"** means the General Partner\'s right to receive twenty percent (20%) of Net Profits distributed in excess of the Preferred Return, as more fully described in Section 8.2 of this Agreement (Tiers 3 and 4 of the distribution waterfall).
**\"Carry Distribution\"** means any Distribution of Carried Interest to the General Partner pursuant to Tier 3 or Tier 4 of the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 8.2.

**\"Catch-Up\"** or **\"GP Catch-Up\"** means the distribution priority described in Tier 3 of Section 8.2, pursuant to which eighty percent (80%) of distributable amounts are allocated to the General Partner and twenty percent (20%) to the Limited Partners until the cumulative distributions to the General Partner under Tier 3 and Tier 4 equal twenty percent (20%) of the sum of all cumulative distributions under Tiers 2, 3, and 4.

**\"Cause\"** means (a) the commission of fraud or willful misconduct by the General Partner, any Key Person, or any Associate acting on behalf of the General Partner in connection with the affairs of the Partnership; (b) a material breach by the General Partner of this Agreement that is not cured within the applicable cure period set forth in Section 12.6; or (c) the voluntary or involuntary bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership, or dissolution of the General Partner.
**\"Clawback Amount\"** means the amount of excess Carried Interest subject to return by the General Partner to the Partnership pursuant to Article IX of this Agreement.

**\"Code\"** means the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended from time to time, and any successor statute thereto. References to specific sections of the Code shall be deemed to include corresponding provisions of any successor statute.
**\"Commitment Period\"** has the meaning ascribed to the term \"Investment Period.\"

**\"Concentration Limit\"** means, with respect to any single Portfolio Investment, twenty percent (20%) of Aggregate Commitments, measured at the time of the initial commitment to such Portfolio Investment (i.e., a maximum of Four Hundred Million Dollars (\$400,000,000) at the hard cap of Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000)), as more fully described in Section 5.3(a).

**\"Defaulting Partner\"** means any Partner that fails to fund its share of a Capital Call by the applicable funding date, as set forth in Section 4.9 of this Agreement, and that has not cured such failure within five (5) Business Days of the funding date.

**\"Distribution\"** means any distribution of cash, securities, or other property by the Partnership to one or more Partners, whether as a return of capital, a share of income or gain, or otherwise, as determined by the General Partner in accordance with this Agreement.

**\"Early Close discount\"** means the ten (10) basis point reduction in the Management Fee rate applicable to Limited Partners admitted to the Partnership at the First Close, as described in Section 7.1(c) of this Agreement (resulting in a Management Fee rate of 1.65% per annum on Capital Commitments during the Investment Period, in lieu of 1.75%).

**\"ERISA\"** means the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended from time to time, and any successor statute thereto, together with all rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.

**\"Excess Organizational Expenses\"** means Organizational Expenses incurred by the Partnership in excess of Three Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$3,500,000), which Excess Organizational Expenses shall be borne solely by the Sponsor and shall not be charged to the Partnership or any Partner.

**\"Excluded Co-Investment\"** means a co-investment opportunity offered alongside the Fund to one or more Limited Partners or third parties in accordance with Section 5.4, which co-investment is made through a separate co-investment vehicle or on a direct basis and is not treated as a Portfolio Investment of the Fund for purposes of this Agreement.
**\"Final Close\"** means the last date on which Limited Partners may be admitted to the Partnership and Capital Commitments accepted, which date shall be no later than the Final Close Deadline.
**\"Final Close Deadline\"** means February 15, 2027, being eighteen (18) months after the target date of the First Close.

**\"First Close\"** means the initial closing of Capital Commitments to the Partnership, targeted for August 15, 2025, at which the General Partner shall have accepted Capital Commitments aggregating at least Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$750,000,000) (or such lesser amount as the General Partner may determine in its sole discretion).

**\"Fiscal Year\"** means the calendar year commencing on January 1 and ending on December 31 of each year; *provided*, that the first Fiscal Year of the Partnership shall commence on the date of the First Close and shall end on December 31 of such calendar year, and the final Fiscal Year of the Partnership shall end on the date of the final distribution of all Partnership assets and cancellation of the Certificate of Limited Partnership.

**\"For-Cause Removal\"** means the removal of the General Partner for Cause by a vote of a majority in interest of the Limited Partners (excluding GP-affiliated Capital Commitments) in accordance with Section 12.6(b).
**\"Fund\"** means Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership formed pursuant to this Agreement.
**\"Fund Expenses\"** means the ordinary and recurring expenses of the Partnership borne by the Partnership, as more fully described in Section 7.4 of this Agreement.

**\"General Partner\"** or **\"GP\"** means Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, the sole member of which is Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, in its capacity as the sole general partner of the Partnership, and any successor general partner admitted to the Partnership in accordance with this Agreement.
**\"GP Catch-Up\"** has the meaning set forth in the definition of \"Catch-Up\" above.

**\"GP Commitment\"** means the Capital Commitment of the General Partner (or its Affiliates) to the Partnership, which shall be equal to two and one-half percent (2.5%) of Aggregate Commitments (equal to Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000) at the hard cap of Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000)). The GP Commitment shall be funded pari passu with Capital Calls to the Limited Partners and on the same terms and conditions as the Capital Commitments of the Limited Partners, except that no Management Fee shall be charged with respect to the GP Commitment.

**\"Included Investors\"** means those Limited Partners that are (a) investment-grade institutional investors (as determined by the lender under the Subscription Credit Facility), (b) government plan investors, or (c) such other investors as may be included in the borrowing base under the Subscription Credit Facility, in each case whose unfunded Capital Commitments are pledged to secure such facility.

**\"Independent Auditor\"** means Caldwell, Fitch & Hartley LLP, or such other independent certified public accounting firm of national or regional standing as the General Partner may select from time to time, subject to LPAC approval for any change in the Independent Auditor.

**\"Investment Company Act\"** means the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended from time to time, and any successor statute thereto, together with all rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.

**\"Investment Period\"** means the period commencing on the date of the Final Close and expiring on the fifth (5th) anniversary of the Final Close, unless earlier terminated or suspended in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement (including Section 5.7 and Article X).
**\"Key Person\"** means each of Marcus J. Harrowgate and Diana R. Castellano, as identified in Schedule B.

**\"Key Person Event\"** means the occurrence of either Key Person ceasing to devote substantially all of his or her business time and professional efforts to the investment activities of the Fund and its Parallel Funds (excluding reasonable time devoted to (i) management and wind-down of predecessor funds (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund I LP through Harrowgate Private Equity Fund IV LP), (ii) civic, charitable, and educational activities, and (iii) personal investment activities that do not conflict with or detract from the Fund\'s investment activities), whether due to death, permanent disability, voluntary departure, termination, or otherwise, as more fully described in Article X.

**\"Large LP discount\"** means the additional five (5) basis point reduction in the Management Fee rate applicable to Limited Partners committing One Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$150,000,000) or more to the Partnership, as described in Section 7.1(c) of this Agreement (resulting in a cumulative Management Fee rate of 1.60% per annum during the Investment Period for a First Close Limited Partner committing \$150,000,000 or more).

**\"Limited Partner\"** or **\"LP\"** means each Person admitted to the Partnership as a limited partner in accordance with Article III of this Agreement and the Act, and **\"Limited Partners\"** means all such Persons collectively. For the avoidance of doubt, the term \"Limited Partner\" does not include the General Partner, except to the extent the General Partner holds an interest in the Partnership in its capacity as a limited partner (if applicable).

**\"Limited Partner Advisory Committee\"** or **\"LPAC\"** means the advisory committee of Limited Partner representatives established and maintained by the General Partner in accordance with Article XI of this Agreement.

**\"Management Fee\"** means the fee payable by the Partnership to the General Partner or its designee in consideration for the management and advisory services provided by the General Partner and its Associates to the Partnership, as set forth in Section 7.1 of this Agreement.

**\"MFN Election\"** means the Most Favored Nation election process described in Section 15.14 of this Agreement, pursuant to which qualifying Limited Partners may elect to receive the benefit of certain Side Letter provisions offered to other Limited Partners , with an election period of thirty (30) calendar days commencing upon delivery of the MFN Disclosure Notice, which the General Partner shall deliver within fifteen (15) Business Days after the Final Close.

**\"Minimum LP Commitment\"** means Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000), being the minimum Capital Commitment required to be made by each Limited Partner in order to be admitted to the Partnership, subject to waiver or reduction by the General Partner in its sole discretion.

**\"Net Asset Value\"** or **\"NAV\"** means, as of any date of determination, the fair market value of all assets of the Partnership (determined in accordance with the valuation policies adopted by the General Partner), less all liabilities of the Partnership (including accrued but unpaid Management Fees, Fund Expenses, and amounts owing under the Subscription Credit Facility), determined in a manner consistent with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America as applied by the General Partner on a consistent basis.

**\"Net Losses\"** means, for any Fiscal Year or other applicable period, the excess, if any, of the items of loss and deduction allocated to the Partnership over the items of income and gain allocated to the Partnership, in each case as computed for purposes of the Carried Interest allocation and the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 8.2.

**\"Net Profits\"** means, for any Fiscal Year or other applicable period, the excess, if any, of the items of income and gain allocated to the Partnership over the items of loss and deduction allocated to the Partnership, in each case as computed for purposes of the Carried Interest allocation and the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 8.2. For the avoidance of doubt, Net Profits shall be determined on a cumulative, whole-fund basis.

**\"No-Fault Removal\"** means the removal of the General Partner without Cause by a vote of seventy-five percent (75%) in interest of the Limited Partners (excluding GP-affiliated Capital Commitments) in accordance with Section 12.6(a).

**\"Offshore Feeder\"** means Harrowgate Fund V Offshore SLP, a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership formed to invest alongside the Fund for the benefit of certain non-U.S. investors and tax-exempt investors, as described in Section 2.7.

**\"Organizational Expenses\"** means the expenses incurred in connection with the organization and formation of the Partnership, the General Partner, the Parallel Fund, the Offshore Feeder, the blocker Entity, and any other parallel or related vehicles, including legal fees, accounting fees, filing fees, printing costs, travel expenses, and other expenses directly related to the formation and organization of the foregoing entities and the offering and sale of Partnership Interests, subject to the cap set forth in Section 7.3.

**\"Parallel Fund\"** means Harrowgate Fund V Parallel LP, a Delaware limited partnership, and any other parallel investment vehicle established by the General Partner to invest alongside the Fund on substantially similar economic terms, as described in Section 2.7.
**\"Partner\"** means the General Partner or any Limited Partner, and **\"Partners\"** means the General Partner and all Limited Partners collectively.
**\"Partnership\"** means Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, a Delaware limited partnership, as constituted from time to time.

**\"Partnership Interest\"** means a Partner\'s entire interest in the Partnership, including such Partner\'s right to receive allocations and Distributions, the right to vote on matters submitted to the Partners, and all other rights and obligations of such Partner under this Agreement and the Act.

**\"Percentage Interest\"** means, with respect to each Partner, the ratio (expressed as a percentage) of such Partner\'s Capital Commitment to Aggregate Commitments, as set forth in the Schedule of Partners. Percentage Interests shall be adjusted upon the admission of additional Partners at Subsequent Closes.

**\"Person\"** means any individual, corporation, limited liability company, partnership, joint venture, association, trust, estate, unincorporated organization, governmental authority or body, or any other entity of any kind.

**\"Placement Agent\"** means Osprey Capital Markets LLC, a broker-dealer registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and a member of the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA), engaged by the Sponsor as exclusive placement agent for certain distribution activities in connection with the offering of Partnership Interests, as more fully described in Section 15.15.

**\"Portfolio Company\"** or **\"Portfolio Investment\"** means any Person in which the Partnership, directly or indirectly (including through one or more holding companies, special purpose vehicles, or other intermediary entities), acquires or holds an investment, whether in the form of equity securities, debt securities, convertible instruments, or other financial interests.

**\"Preferred Return\"** means a cumulative, compounded annual rate of return equal to eight percent (8%) per annum on each Partner\'s net funded Capital Contributions (adjusted for the timing of contributions and prior Distributions), computed from the date of each Capital Contribution through the date of Distribution, as more fully described in Tier 2 of the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 8.2.
**\"Qualified Purchaser\"** means a \"qualified purchaser\" as defined in Section 2(a)(51)(A) of the Investment Company Act and the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.

**\"Regulatory Allocations\"** means the mandatory tax allocations required to be made pursuant to Code Sections 704(b) and 704(c) and the Treasury Regulations thereunder, including the qualified income offset, minimum gain chargeback, partner nonrecourse deduction allocations, and other allocations described in Section 6.3 of this Agreement.

**\"Reinvestment Amount\"** means the aggregate amount of proceeds from dispositions of Portfolio Investments held for less than twenty-four (24) months (and repayments of Bridge Financing) that may be re-invested by the Partnership during the Investment Period, subject to the cap set forth in Section 4.7.
**\"Securities Act\"** means the Securities Act of 1933, as amended from time to time, and any successor statute thereto, together with all rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.

**\"Side Letter\"** means any letter agreement, supplemental agreement, or similar arrangement entered into between the General Partner (or its Affiliate) and a Limited Partner that supplements, modifies, or waives any provision of this Agreement with respect to such Limited Partner, in each case as permitted by Section 15.14 and the other provisions of this Agreement.

**\"Sponsor\"** means Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, the sole member of the General Partner and the management company responsible for the investment advisory and management services provided to the Fund and its parallel vehicles.

**\"Subscription Agreement\"** means the subscription agreement and related documents executed by each Limited Partner in connection with such Limited Partner\'s commitment to the Partnership, in the form attached hereto as Exhibit D (or as otherwise prescribed by the General Partner), together with all exhibits, schedules, questionnaires, and certifications attached thereto.

**\"Subscription Credit Facility\"** means any revolving credit facility, letter of credit facility, or similar borrowing arrangement established by the Partnership (or a parallel vehicle) that is secured, in whole or in part, by the unfunded Capital Commitments of the Partners, as more fully described in Section 4.8 of this Agreement.

**\"Subscription Facility Limit\"** means an amount equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of the aggregate unfunded Capital Commitments of all Partners at the time of determination, being the maximum aggregate principal amount of borrowings permitted to be outstanding under the Subscription Credit Facility at any given time, as further described in Section 4.8.

**\"Subsequent Close\"** means any closing of Capital Commitments to the Partnership occurring after the First Close and on or prior to the Final Close Deadline, at which additional Limited Partners may be admitted to the Partnership and/or existing Limited Partners may increase their Capital Commitments, in accordance with Section 3.4 of this Agreement.

**\"Transaction Fees\"** means all transaction fees, monitoring fees, directors\' fees, advisory fees, consulting fees, break-up fees, topping fees, and similar fees and compensation received by the General Partner, the Sponsor, or any of their respective Affiliates from or in connection with Portfolio Companies or prospective Portfolio Companies (net of any unreimbursed out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection therewith).

**\"Transfer\"** means any direct or indirect sale, assignment, transfer, exchange, pledge, hypothecation, encumbrance, gift, bequest, or other disposition (whether voluntary, involuntary, or by operation of law) of all or any portion of a Partnership Interest or any economic or other right therein.

**\"Treasury Regulations\"** means the regulations promulgated under the Code by the United States Department of the Treasury, as such regulations may be amended from time to time (including corresponding provisions of successor regulations).
**\"UBTI\"** means \"unrelated business taxable income\" within the meaning of Code Sections 511 through 514, as amended.

**\"Waterfall\"** means the European-style (whole-fund) distribution waterfall set forth in Section 8.2 of this Agreement, pursuant to which all distributable amounts are distributed among the Partners in the priority order described therein.

**\"Withdrawal Event\"** means any event permitting or requiring the withdrawal or resignation of the General Partner from the Partnership as described in Section 12.7 of this Agreement or as otherwise provided by the Act.
**[Section 1.2 --- Interpretation and Construction]{.underline}**

\(a\) The headings and captions contained in this Agreement are included for convenience of reference only and shall not be deemed to constitute a part hereof or to affect the meaning or interpretation of any provision of this Agreement.

\(b\) Unless the context otherwise requires: (i) words importing the singular shall include the plural, and vice versa; (ii) words importing a gender shall include all genders; (iii) references to a Person include such Person\'s successors and permitted assigns; (iv) the word **\"including\"** (and correlative words such as \"include,\" \"includes,\" and \"included\") shall mean \"including, without limitation\" and shall not be construed to limit any general statement to the specific or similar items or matters immediately following it; and (v) the words \"hereof,\" \"herein,\" \"hereunder,\" and words of similar import shall refer to this Agreement as a whole and not to any particular provision of this Agreement.

\(c\) References to any statute, rule, or regulation shall be deemed to include all amendments thereto, all rules and regulations promulgated thereunder, and all successor statutes, rules, and regulations, unless the context otherwise requires.
\(d\) All references to \"dollars\" or \"\$\" shall mean United States dollars.

\(e\) This Agreement shall be interpreted and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, applying Delaware interpretive canons, without regard to conflicts of law principles that would result in the application of the laws of another jurisdiction.
\(f\) References to \"Articles,\" \"Sections,\" \"Schedules,\" and \"Exhibits\" are to the Articles, Sections, Schedules, and Exhibits of this Agreement, unless otherwise specified.

\(g\) Each accounting term used herein that is not otherwise defined shall have the meaning ascribed to it under generally accepted accounting principles in the United States of America, as in effect from time to time.
**[ARTICLE II --- FORMATION, NAME, AND PURPOSE]{.underline}**
**[Section 2.1 --- Formation]{.underline}**

The Partnership has been formed as a limited partnership under and pursuant to the Act by the filing (or the contemplated filing on or prior to the date of the First Close) of a Certificate of Limited Partnership with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware. The Certificate of Limited Partnership identifies Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC as the sole general partner of the Partnership. The registered office of the Partnership in the State of Delaware is located at 400 South Ashbury Asset Advisors, Suite 3000, Wilmington, Delaware 19801, in care of Calderwood & Harkness LLP, which serves as the registered agent of the Partnership for service of process in the State of Delaware. The General Partner shall cause such amendments to the Certificate of Limited Partnership and such other filings and recordings as may be required or appropriate under the Act and the laws of any other jurisdiction in which the Partnership conducts business.
**[Section 2.2 --- Name]{.underline}**

The Partnership shall operate under the name **\"Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP\"** and may conduct business under such other names as the General Partner may determine from time to time. The General Partner shall have the right to change the name of the Partnership at any time and from time to time; *provided*, that the General Partner shall give prior written notice to the Limited Partners of any such change.
**[Section 2.3 --- Purpose]{.underline}**
The purpose of the Partnership is:

\(a\) To make equity and equity-related investments, directly or indirectly (including through holding companies, special purpose vehicles, or other intermediary entities), primarily in North American mid-market and upper-mid-market companies operating in the industrials, business services, healthcare services, and technology-enabled services sectors, with target equity checks ranging from Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000) to Two Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$250,000,000) per platform investment;
\(b\) To hold, monitor, manage, and ultimately dispose of such investments with the objective of generating attractive risk-adjusted returns for the Partners;

We express no opinion as to whether a court outside of the State of Delaware would give effect to such exclusive forum selection provisions.
194:

Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC As General Partner of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP c/o Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC 1200 Concord Pike, Suite 600 Wilmington, Delaware 19803

> Ashford National Bank, N.A.

> 300 Vesey Street New York, New York 10282 (to the extent required under the subscription credit facility documentation)
CONFIDENTIAL
Ladies and Gentlemen:

We have acted as counsel to Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC (\"HCP\"), a Delaware limited liability company, in connection with the formation of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP (the \"Fund\" or \"HPE Fund V\"), a Delaware limited partnership, and Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC (the \"General Partner\" or \"Fund V GP\"), a Delaware limited liability company. The General Partner serves as the sole general partner of the Fund, and HCP is the sole member of the General Partner. This opinion letter (this \"Opinion\") is delivered in connection with the first closing (the \"First Close\") of the Fund occurring on the date hereof. We understand that the Fund has a target hard cap of Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000) in aggregate capital commitments and that the minimum First Close target is Seven Hundred Fifty Million Dollars (\$750,000,000) in aggregate capital commitments.

This Opinion is delivered to you pursuant to Section 3.02(c) of the Agreement of Limited Partnership of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, dated as of August 15, 2025 (as defined below, the \"LPA\"), and, to the extent applicable, pursuant to Section 4.01(a)(iii) of the Credit Agreement, dated as of August 8, 2025, among the Fund, the General Partner, and Ashford National Bank, N.A., as administrative agent and lender (the \"Credit Agreement\"). Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the LPA unless the context otherwise requires.
**[I. DOCUMENTS EXAMINED]{.underline}**

In connection with the opinions rendered herein, we have examined originals or copies, certified or otherwise identified to our satisfaction, of the following documents (collectively, the \"Opinion Documents\"):
1\. The Certificate of Limited Partnership of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, as filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on July 22, 2025 (the \"Fund Certificate\").
2\. The Agreement of Limited Partnership of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP, dated as of August 15, 2025, by and among the General Partner and the Limited Partners party thereto (the \"LPA\").
3\. The Certificate of Formation of Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, as filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on July 18, 2025 (the \"GP Certificate\").
4\. The Limited Liability Company Agreement of Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC, dated as of July 18, 2025, by Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC as sole member (the \"GP LLC Agreement\").

5\. The Certificate of Formation of Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, as on file with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, and the Amended and Restated Limited Liability Company Agreement of Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, dated as of March 10, 2017 (as amended through the date hereof) (collectively, the \"HCP Organizational Documents\").

6\. The Subscription Agreements executed by each Limited Partner subscribing at the First Close, together with the related Investor Questionnaires completed by each such Limited Partner in connection therewith (collectively, the \"Subscription Documents\").
7\. The side letters entered into between the General Partner and certain Limited Partners in connection with the First Close, including all schedules and exhibits thereto (the \"Side Letters\").
8\. A Certificate of Good Standing for Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP issued by the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, dated August 14, 2025.
9\. A Certificate of Good Standing for Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC issued by the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, dated August 14, 2025.
10\. A Certificate of Good Standing for Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC issued by the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, dated August 14, 2025.

11\. Resolutions of Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, as sole member of the General Partner, adopted by written consent effective as of August 12, 2025, authorizing the execution, delivery, and performance of the LPA and the transactions contemplated thereby, including the acceptance of capital commitments at the First Close and the execution and delivery of the Side Letters and the Credit Agreement (the \"Authorizing Resolutions\").

12\. An Officer\'s Certificate of the General Partner, executed by Marcus J. Harrowgate, Chief Executive Officer, and Jonathan P. Birch, Chief Financial Officer, dated the date hereof, as to certain factual matters set forth therein (the \"Officer\'s Certificate\").

13\. Such other documents, records, certificates, instruments, and matters of law as we have deemed necessary or appropriate for purposes of the opinions expressed herein, including telephone confirmations from the office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware with respect to the good standing of the Fund, the General Partner, and HCP as of the date hereof.
We refer to Items 1 through 13 above, together with all exhibits, schedules, annexes, and supplements thereto, collectively as the \"Opinion Documents.\"
**[II. ASSUMPTIONS]{.underline}**
In rendering the opinions set forth in Section III below, we have assumed, without independent investigation or verification, the following:

1\. **Authenticity and Conformity.** All documents submitted to us as originals are authentic. All documents submitted to us as certified, conformed, or photostatic copies conform to the originals thereof. All signatures on all documents examined by us are genuine, and all natural persons who executed any of the Opinion Documents were competent to do so at the time of execution.
2\. **Legal Capacity.** Each natural person executing any Opinion Document had the legal capacity to do so at the time of such execution.

3\. **Organization and Standing of Third Parties.** Each party to the Opinion Documents (other than the Fund, the General Partner, and HCP, as to matters expressly covered by our opinions herein) is duly organized or formed, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of its jurisdiction of organization or formation, and has all requisite organizational power and authority to own, lease, and operate its properties and to carry on its business as presently conducted.

4\. **Power, Authority, and Action of Third Parties.** Each party to the Opinion Documents (other than the Fund, the General Partner, and HCP, as to matters expressly covered by our opinions herein) has all requisite power and authority, and has taken all necessary corporate, limited liability company, limited partnership, trust, or other organizational action, to authorize the execution, delivery, and performance of each of the Opinion Documents to which it is a party and to consummate the transactions contemplated thereby.

5\. **Binding Obligations of Third Parties.** Each Opinion Document constitutes the legal, valid, and binding obligation of each party thereto (other than the Fund, the General Partner, and HCP, as to matters expressly covered by our opinions herein), enforceable against such party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity.

6\. **No Violations by Third Parties.** The execution and delivery of each Opinion Document and the performance of the obligations thereunder by each party thereto (other than the Fund, the General Partner, and HCP) do not and will not violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of or default under any agreement, instrument, order, judgment, decree, or applicable law to which any such party is a party or by which any such party or any of its properties or assets is bound.

7\. **Accuracy of Factual Statements.** The factual statements, representations, and warranties contained in the Officer\'s Certificate and in the Subscription Documents are true, correct, and complete in all material respects as of the date hereof, and no event has occurred that would render any such statement, representation, or warranty untrue or misleading in any material respect.

8\. **Qualified Purchaser and Accredited Investor Status.** Each Limited Partner subscribing at the First Close is a \"qualified purchaser\" as defined in Section 2(a)(51) of the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended, and the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder, and an \"accredited investor\" as defined in Rule 501 of Regulation D promulgated under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and such status has been accurately represented by each such Limited Partner in its Subscription Documents.

9\. **Due Subscription.** All capital commitments accepted at the First Close have been duly made in accordance with the procedures set forth in the Subscription Documents and the LPA, and the General Partner has accepted each such capital commitment in accordance with the terms and conditions of the LPA and the applicable Subscription Documents.

10\. **Adequate Consideration.** The consideration for each Limited Partner\'s interest in the Fund is adequate and lawful, and no Limited Partner\'s capital commitment is subject to any claim of avoidance, setoff, counterclaim, or defense.

We have made no independent factual investigation for the purpose of rendering this Opinion, and we have relied exclusively upon the Opinion Documents and the assumptions set forth above with respect to all factual matters. Where our opinions are qualified by the phrase \"to our knowledge\" or words of similar import, such phrase refers only to the actual knowledge of the attorneys in this firm who have given substantive legal attention to the matters addressed herein, without any duty of inquiry or investigation.
**[III. OPINIONS]{.underline}**
Based upon and subject to the foregoing, and subject further to the qualifications, exceptions, and limitations set forth in Section IV below, we are of the opinion that:
**[3.1 Due Formation and Valid Existence of the Fund]{.underline}**

Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP is a limited partnership duly formed and validly existing under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, 6 Del. C. §§ 17-101 *et seq.* (the \"DRULPA\"). The Fund Certificate has been duly executed by an authorized person and duly filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware in accordance with Section 17-201 of the DRULPA. Based upon the Certificate of Good Standing referenced in Item 8 of Section I above, the Fund is in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware as of the date of such certificate.
**[3.2 Due Formation and Valid Existence of the General Partner]{.underline}**

Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC is a limited liability company duly formed and validly existing under the Delaware Limited Liability Company Act, 6 Del. C. §§ 18-101 *et seq.* (the \"DLLCA\"). The GP Certificate has been duly executed by an authorized person and duly filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware in accordance with Section 18-201 of the DLLCA. Based upon the Certificate of Good Standing referenced in Item 9 of Section I above, the General Partner is in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware as of the date of such certificate. Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, as sole member of the General Partner, is duly formed, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the State of Delaware, based upon the Certificate of Good Standing referenced in Item 10 of Section I above and our review of the HCP Organizational Documents.
**[3.3 Power and Authority]{.underline}**

The Fund has the limited partnership power and authority under the DRULPA and the LPA to execute, deliver, and perform its obligations under the LPA and the other Opinion Documents to which it is a party, and to conduct its business as described in the LPA, including, without limitation, the making of investments in North American mid-market and upper-mid-market buyout transactions and platform and add-on acquisitions in the sectors and sub-sectors described in the LPA, the borrowing of funds and the granting of security interests in connection therewith, the making of distributions to the Partners, and the taking of such other actions as are contemplated by the LPA and reasonably incidental thereto.

The General Partner has the limited liability company power and authority under the DLLCA, the GP LLC Agreement, and the LPA to act as the sole general partner of the Fund, to execute, deliver, and perform the LPA on behalf of the Fund, and to execute and deliver the Side Letters, each Subscription Agreement to which it is a party, the Credit Agreement, and each other Opinion Document to which the General Partner is a party, and to perform its obligations thereunder.

Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, as sole member of the General Partner, has duly authorized the General Partner to take all actions contemplated by the Opinion Documents, including those actions authorized by the Authorizing Resolutions referenced in Item 11 of Section I above.
**[3.4 Due Authorization, Execution, and Delivery]{.underline}**

The execution, delivery, and performance of the LPA and the other Opinion Documents to which the Fund and the General Partner are parties have been duly authorized by all necessary limited partnership action (in the case of the Fund) and limited liability company action (in the case of the General Partner), including, without limitation, the adoption of the Authorizing Resolutions by HCP as sole member of the General Partner. No further action on the part of the Fund, the General Partner, or HCP is required to authorize the execution, delivery, or performance of any Opinion Document.

The LPA has been duly executed and delivered by the General Partner, acting in its capacity as the sole general partner of the Fund on behalf of the Fund, and has been duly executed and delivered by each Limited Partner executing a Subscription Agreement at the First Close and admitted to the Fund in accordance with the terms of the LPA and the applicable Subscription Documents.

Each Subscription Agreement, each Side Letter, and each other Opinion Document to which the General Partner is a party has been duly executed and delivered by the General Partner, acting through its duly authorized officers and representatives.
**[3.5 Enforceability]{.underline}**

The LPA constitutes the legal, valid, and binding obligation of the Fund and the General Partner, enforceable against each of them in accordance with its terms, subject in each case to the qualifications, exceptions, and limitations set forth in Section IV below.

Each Side Letter executed in connection with the First Close constitutes the legal, valid, and binding obligation of the General Partner, enforceable against the General Partner in accordance with its terms, subject in each case to the same qualifications, exceptions, and limitations set forth in Section IV below.
**[3.6 No Violations]{.underline}**
The execution, delivery, and performance of the LPA and the other Opinion Documents by the Fund and the General Partner do not and will not:

> \(a\) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of or default under (i) the Fund Certificate or the LPA (as applied to the Fund), (ii) the GP Certificate or the GP LLC Agreement (as applied to the General Partner), or (iii) the HCP Organizational Documents (as applied to HCP);

> \(b\) violate any existing law, statute, rule, or regulation of the State of Delaware that, in our experience, is generally applicable to transactions of the nature contemplated by the Opinion Documents and is applicable to the Fund, the General Partner, or HCP, including the DRULPA and the DLLCA; or

> \(c\) result in a breach of, or constitute a default or an event of default under, or result in the creation or imposition of any lien, charge, or encumbrance upon any of the assets of the Fund, the General Partner, or HCP pursuant to, any agreement, instrument, order, judgment, or decree identified in the Officer\'s Certificate to which the Fund, the General Partner, or HCP is a party or by which any of them or any of their respective properties or assets is bound.

We note that the opinion set forth in this Section 3.6 is limited to the laws of the State of Delaware as in effect on the date hereof, including the DRULPA and the DLLCA, and does not address federal securities laws, federal or state tax laws, the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended, or the laws of any jurisdiction other than the State of Delaware. Our opinion in clause (c) above is limited to the agreements, instruments, orders, judgments, and decrees identified in the Officer\'s Certificate, and we have not conducted any independent search or investigation to identify any additional agreements or instruments.
**[3.7 Limited Partner Status]{.underline}**

Based upon the terms of the LPA and the DRULPA, each person who has executed a Subscription Agreement that has been accepted by the General Partner at the First Close and who has been admitted as a limited partner of the Fund in accordance with the terms and conditions of the LPA is a limited partner of the Fund within the meaning of Section 17-101(8) of the DRULPA. The limited partnership interests acquired by the Limited Partners at the First Close have been validly issued in accordance with the LPA and the DRULPA, and each such Limited Partner\'s interest in the Fund, including such Limited Partner\'s capital commitment and its share of the profits, losses, and distributions of the Fund, is as set forth in the LPA and the applicable Subscription Documents.
**[IV. QUALIFICATIONS, EXCEPTIONS, AND LIMITATIONS]{.underline}**
The opinions set forth in Section III above are subject to and limited by the following qualifications, exceptions, and limitations:
**[4.1 Enforceability Qualifications]{.underline}**
The enforceability opinions expressed in Section 3.5 above (and to the extent the enforceability of any obligation is relevant to the other opinions expressed herein) are subject to and limited by:

> \(a\) **Bankruptcy and Insolvency Laws.** Applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, receivership, conservatorship, liquidation, fraudulent conveyance, fraudulent transfer, preferential transfer, and other similar laws relating to or affecting the enforcement of creditors\' rights generally, including, without limitation, Title 11 of the United States Code (the Bankruptcy Code), the Delaware Uniform Fraudulent Transfer Act (6 Del. C. §§ 1301--1311), and any successor statutes thereto.

> \(b\) **General Principles of Equity.** General principles of equity (regardless of whether enforcement is considered in a proceeding in equity or at law), including, without limitation, concepts of materiality, reasonableness, good faith, fair dealing, unconscionability, and the possible unavailability of equitable remedies where adequate remedies at law exist.

> \(c\) **Discretionary Equitable Remedies.** The possible unavailability of specific performance, injunctive relief, or other equitable remedies, which remedies are subject to the discretion of the court before which any proceeding therefor may be brought, and the court\'s determination that specific performance, injunctive relief, or other equitable remedies are appropriate in the circumstances.

> \(d\) **Public Policy --- Indemnification.** Public policy considerations that may limit the enforceability of provisions purporting to provide for indemnification, exculpation, contribution, or advancement of expenses to the extent that such provisions are found to contravene applicable public policy, including provisions of the DRULPA, the DLLCA, or applicable judicial precedent that impose minimum standards of liability for willful misconduct, bad faith, or knowing violations of law by a general partner or its affiliates.
**[4.2 Scope Limitations]{.underline}**

This Opinion is limited to the laws of the State of Delaware as in effect on the date hereof, including the statutory provisions of the DRULPA, the DLLCA, and the Delaware Revised Uniform Partnership Act, the applicable provisions of the Delaware Constitution, and the reported judicial decisions interpreting those laws, and we express no opinion as to the laws of any other jurisdiction. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, we express no opinion as to:

> \(a\) Federal securities laws, including the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the \"Securities Act\"), and the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (the \"Investment Company Act\"), and the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder. We note that matters of federal securities law compliance are addressed in a separate opinion letter of even date herewith delivered by this firm to the addressees hereof regarding Securities Law / Regulation D Compliance (the \"Securities Law Opinion\"), and this Opinion should be read in conjunction with the Securities Law Opinion.

> \(b\) Federal or state tax laws, including the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\"), the Treasury Regulations promulgated thereunder, and any state or local tax laws or regulations.

> \(c\) The Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), Section 4975 of the Code, or any regulations, rulings, or guidance promulgated thereunder, including the plan asset regulations set forth in 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101, as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA.
> \(d\) The Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended, or any state \"blue sky,\" securities, or broker-dealer laws or regulations.

> \(e\) Antitrust or competition laws (including the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, as amended), environmental laws, intellectual property laws, real property laws, labor and employment laws, data privacy and cybersecurity laws, anti-money laundering laws (including the Bank Secrecy Act and the USA PATRIOT Act), sanctions laws (including those administered by the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Office of Foreign Assets Control), the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act, or other specialized areas of law.

> \(f\) The laws of the Cayman Islands, the British Virgin Islands, the United Kingdom, Luxembourg, or any other foreign jurisdiction, including as applicable to Harrowgate Fund V Offshore SLP, any parallel vehicle, alternative investment vehicle, or any non-U.S. investor or feeder fund.

> \(g\) Any choice-of-law or conflicts-of-law analysis, including whether a court in any jurisdiction other than Delaware would give effect to the choice-of-law provisions of the LPA or would apply the laws of the State of Delaware to any dispute arising under or in connection with the LPA or any other Opinion Document.
**[4.3 Certain Additional Qualifications]{.underline}**
Without limiting the foregoing, we express no opinion as to the enforceability of any provision of the LPA or any other Opinion Document that purports to:
> \(a\) **Jury Trial Waiver.** Waive rights to trial by jury, to the extent such waiver is not enforceable under applicable law or is subject to judicial discretion as to enforcement.

> \(b\) **Liquidated Damages.** Establish liquidated damages or set a predetermined measure of damages, to the extent a court of competent jurisdiction were to determine that such provisions constitute a penalty rather than a reasonable pre-estimate of anticipated damages.

> \(c\) **Power of Attorney.** Grant a power of attorney that is not coupled with an interest, to the extent such power might be deemed revocable by operation of law, notwithstanding any provision of the LPA designating such power as irrevocable. We note that Section 17-1101(f) of the DRULPA provides that a power of attorney granted by a limited partner to the general partner may be irrevocable if so provided in the partnership agreement, and we express no opinion as to the application of such provision in any particular circumstance.

> \(d\) **Default Interest, Consent Fees, and Late Charges.** Impose consent fees, default interest rates, late charges, or prepayment premiums, to the extent any such amount might be deemed unenforceable as a penalty or as unconscionable under applicable law.

> \(e\) **Attorneys\' Fees.** Require payment of attorneys\' fees or other costs of collection by a non-prevailing party, to the extent limited or prohibited by applicable law, judicial precedent, or the inherent discretion of the court.

> \(f\) **Exculpation and Limitation of Liability.** Exculpate, indemnify, or otherwise limit the liability of the General Partner, HCP, or their respective affiliates, members, managers, officers, employees, or agents, to the extent such provisions are limited by Section 17-1101(d) or (e) of the DRULPA, applicable judicial precedent, or public policy. We note that Section 17-1101(d) of the DRULPA permits a partnership agreement to eliminate or limit personal liability of a partner or other person for breach of duties (including fiduciary duties), provided that a partnership agreement may not eliminate the implied contractual covenant of good faith and fair dealing.

We further note that the enforceability of the GP clawback obligations set forth in Article VIII of the LPA, including the several personal guarantees of Marcus J. Harrowgate, Diana R. Castellano, and Jonathan P. Birch (each a \"Clawback Guarantor\"), is subject to all of the qualifications and limitations set forth in this Section IV. We express no opinion as to the collectability, sufficiency, or ultimate recoverability of any amounts owing under the clawback provisions, the financial ability of any Clawback Guarantor to satisfy such obligations, or the enforceability of such obligations under the laws of any jurisdiction other than the State of Delaware.

We also note that the exclusive jurisdiction provisions set forth in Section 14.08 of the LPA, designating the Delaware Court of Chancery (or, if the Court of Chancery determines that it lacks subject matter jurisdiction, the Superior Court of the State of Delaware sitting in and for New Castle County) as the exclusive forum for the adjudication of disputes arising out of or relating to the LPA, are subject to principles of judicial discretion, applicable procedural rules, and applicable law, including questions relating to personal jurisdiction over the parties, venue, and *forum non conveniens*. We express no opinion as to whether a court outside of the State of Delaware would give effect to such exclusive forum selection provisions.
**[4.4 Reliance on Factual Matters]{.underline}**

We have relied, without independent investigation or verification, upon (a) the Officer\'s Certificate as to all factual matters set forth therein, including the identification of agreements, instruments, orders, judgments, and decrees to which the Fund, the General Partner, and HCP are parties or by which they are bound, and (b) the representations and warranties made by each Limited Partner in its Subscription Documents and by each party in the Side Letters, as to all factual matters relevant to the opinions expressed herein, including, without limitation, the accuracy of each Limited Partner\'s representations regarding its investor status, organizational authority, source of funds, and ERISA status.

We have not examined the financial condition, creditworthiness, or solvency of the Fund, the General Partner, HCP, any Limited Partner, or any other person or entity. We have not conducted any Uniform Commercial Code, tax lien, judgment, litigation, bankruptcy, or other public record searches in the State of Delaware or any other jurisdiction with respect to the Fund, the General Partner, HCP, or any Limited Partner, and we express no opinion with respect to any matters that such searches might reveal.
**[V. RELIANCE AND OTHER MATTERS]{.underline}**

This Opinion is rendered solely for the benefit of the addressees hereof and the Limited Partners admitted to the Fund at the First Close, and may not be relied upon, quoted, referred to, or furnished to any other person or entity without our prior written consent in each instance. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Ashford National Bank, N.A. may rely on this Opinion in connection with the subscription credit facility established under the Credit Agreement, to the extent expressly required under Section 4.01(a)(iii) thereof or otherwise required pursuant to the terms of the Credit Agreement or any ancillary facility documentation.

This Opinion is limited to the matters expressly stated herein, and no opinion is implied or may be inferred beyond the matters expressly so stated. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, we express no opinion regarding any transaction or matter not specifically addressed herein, including any future closing of the Fund, any subsequent admission of limited partners, or any amendment, modification, waiver, or supplement to any Opinion Document entered into after the date hereof.

We note that the LPA provides that it shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without giving effect to any choice-of-law or conflicts-of-law rules or provisions that would cause the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. We express no opinion as to whether a court in any jurisdiction other than Delaware would give effect to such governing law provision. We further note that the LPA provides for the resolution of disputes through litigation in the Delaware Court of Chancery (or the Superior Court of the State of Delaware sitting in and for New Castle County, as applicable), and we express no opinion as to the enforceability of such provisions in any jurisdiction other than the State of Delaware.

This Opinion is governed by, and is to be interpreted in accordance with, the Legal Opinion Accord of the ABA Section of Business Law (2022 Edition). As a consequence, it is subject to a number of qualifications, exceptions, definitions, and limitations, all as more particularly described in the Accord, and this Opinion should be read in conjunction therewith.

Very truly yours,
CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP

17: Dear Ms. Whitfield:
18: 
19: We are delighted to have the opportunity to work with Briarwood Family Office LLC in connection with the matter described below. This engagement letter (this \"Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions under which Calderwood & Harkness LLP will provide legal services to Briarwood Family Office LLC. We ask that you review this Letter carefully and, if the terms are acceptable, countersign where indicated below and return one fully executed copy to our offices. Your countersignature will confirm your agreement to the terms set forth herein.
20: 
21: **[1. Engagement and Scope of Representation]{.underline}**
22: 
23: **1.1 Description of the Engagement**
24: 
25: Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H,\" \"we,\" \"our,\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm our engagement by Briarwood Family Office LLC (\"BFO\" or the \"Client\"), a Delaware limited liability company, to serve as legal counsel in connection with the negotiation and documentation of a side letter (the \"Side Letter\") to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership dated December 20, 2023 (the \"LPA\") of Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. (\"Fund IV\"), a Delaware limited partnership, in connection with a proposed capital commitment of Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000) by BFO as a limited partner of Fund IV.
26: 
27: Fund IV is managed by Meridian Peak Capital Partners GP IV LLC (the \"General Partner\"), a Delaware limited liability company and the sole general partner of Fund IV. The General Partner is a wholly owned subsidiary of Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC (\"MPCA\"), a Delaware limited liability company registered as an investment adviser under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended, with its principal office located at 200 Clarendon Street, 42nd Floor, Boston, MA 02116. We understand that the placement agent for Fund IV is Pinnacle Capital Markets LLC (\"Pinnacle\"), a FINRA-registered broker-dealer, and that the fund administrator is Granite Ledger Fund Services LLC (\"Granite Ledger\").
28: 
29: The General Partner and Fund IV are represented by Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP, 1 Federal Street, Suite 3600, Boston, MA 02110 (attention: Margaret S. Alderman, Esq.), and we anticipate that the principal negotiations with respect to the Side Letter and subscription documentation will be conducted between our Firm and Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP on behalf of our respective clients.
30: 
31: **1.2 Scope of Services**
32: 
33: The scope of our engagement includes the following services:
34: 
35: > \(a\) **Review and Analysis of Governing Documents.** Review and analysis of the Fund IV LPA (dated December 20, 2023) and the Fund IV Private Placement Memorandum (dated December 15, 2023) (the \"PPM\"), including identification of key terms, risk factors, fee structures, governance provisions, withdrawal and redemption mechanics, and provisions that may be subject to negotiation, modification, or supplementation via side letter. This review will include an assessment of the rights and obligations of limited partners under the LPA and the identification of areas where BFO may seek enhanced protections, preferential terms, or clarifications through the Side Letter.
36: >
37: > \(b\) **Side Letter Negotiation and Documentation.** Preparation and negotiation of the Side Letter between BFO, Fund IV, and the General Partner, addressing, among other things:
38: >
39: > \(i\) most favored nation (\"MFN\") rights, including the scope and mechanics of MFN elections and any carve-outs or limitations thereon;
40: >
41: > \(ii\) excuse and exclusion rights, including the right of BFO to be excused from particular investments on regulatory, legal, tax, or policy grounds;
42: >
43: > \(iii\) management fee reductions or offsets, including any tiered fee arrangements applicable to BFO\'s commitment level;
44: >
45: > \(iv\) co-investment rights, including rights of first offer or first refusal with respect to co-investment opportunities alongside Fund IV;
46: >
47: > \(v\) enhanced reporting obligations, including the frequency, content, and format of financial, portfolio, and ESG-related reporting to BFO;
48: >
49: > \(vi\) key person provisions, including the identification of key persons and the consequences of a key person event;
50: >
51: > \(vii\) transfer rights, including any pre-approved transferees, rights of first refusal, or consent requirements applicable to transfers by BFO of its limited partnership interest;
52: >
53: > \(viii\) confidentiality carve-outs, including permitted disclosures to BFO\'s affiliates, advisors, family members, and regulatory authorities;
54: >
55: > \(ix\) tax reporting, including timely delivery of Schedule K-1s and other tax-related information, as well as any UBTI or ECI-related protections;
56: >
57: > \(x\) placement agent fee disclosures and offsets; and
58: >
59: > \(xi\) such other customary side letter provisions as BFO may reasonably request and the General Partner may agree to.
60: >
61: > \(c\) **Subscription Document Review.** Review and markup of Fund IV subscription documents, including the subscription agreement and investor questionnaire, as necessary for BFO\'s potential admission as a limited partner of Fund IV.
62: >
63: > \(d\) **Negotiation with Counterparty Counsel.** Correspondence and negotiation with Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP, counsel to the General Partner and Fund IV, regarding the Side Letter and related transaction documents, including all communications necessary to resolve open issues and reach agreement on the final form of the Side Letter.
64: >
65: > \(e\) **Advisory Services.** Advisory services related to the foregoing, including analysis of the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act (6 Del. C. § 17-101 *et seq.*) as applicable to the LPA and Side Letter, ERISA considerations (including an assessment of whether Fund IV constitutes a \"plan asset\" entity under 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101, as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA), and regulatory matters relevant to BFO\'s proposed commitment.
66: >
67: > \(f\) **Additional Services.** Such other legal services as may be reasonably requested by BFO in connection with the proposed commitment and as mutually agreed upon by the parties in writing.
68: 
69: **Limitations on Scope.** Notwithstanding the foregoing, our engagement does not extend to, and we will not be providing, any of the following: (i) tax advice, including analysis of the federal, state, or local income tax consequences of BFO\'s investment in Fund IV, the treatment of allocations and distributions under Subchapter K of the Internal Revenue Code, or the analysis of Schedule K-1 implications; (ii) investment advice or recommendations regarding the merits or risks of committing capital to Fund IV; (iii) business, financial, or operational due diligence on Fund IV, MPCA, or any of their affiliates, portfolio companies, or service providers; or (iv) representation of BFO in any dispute, litigation, arbitration, or regulatory proceeding. BFO should consult its own independent tax advisors, financial advisors, and other professionals with respect to such matters. Nothing in this Letter or in the performance of our services should be construed as investment advice or a recommendation to invest or not invest in Fund IV.
70: 
71: **1.3 Client Identification**
72: 
73: Our client in this engagement is Briarwood Family Office LLC (EIN: 27-4831956). We do not represent any individual member, manager, officer, director, or employee of BFO in his or her personal capacity, nor any affiliate, related entity, family trust, or family member of any principal of BFO, unless separately agreed upon in a writing signed by the Firm and such individual or entity. For the avoidance of doubt, our representation of BFO in this engagement does not create an attorney-client relationship between C&H and Julian R. Hargrove, Victoria L. Hargrove, or any other member or principal of BFO in their individual capacities.

75: **[2. Engagement Team and Staffing]{.underline}**
76: 
77: The following attorneys have been assigned to this matter and will comprise the principal engagement team:
78: 
79: > • **Pamela Cross** --- *Responsible Partner*, Funds & Asset Management group. Ms. Cross will have overall responsibility for the engagement and will serve as the primary relationship partner. Ms. Cross has extensive experience representing institutional investors, family offices, and sovereign wealth funds in connection with commitments to private equity, venture capital, real estate, and credit funds, and has negotiated side letters involving aggregate commitments in excess of \$20 billion. Ms. Cross will be available for strategic guidance, key negotiation calls, and final review of all material documents.
80: >
81: > • **Nicholas Stern** --- *Billing Partner*, Funds & Asset Management group. Mr. Stern will oversee billing and administrative matters related to this engagement and will provide supplemental partner-level review as needed. Mr. Stern will also be available to address questions relating to ERISA, regulatory compliance, and Delaware limited partnership law.
82: >
83: > • **Theresa Kim** --- *Lead Associate*, Funds & Asset Management group. Any changes to the composition of the team will be communicated promptly, and we will ensure continuity and quality of service throughout the engagement.

For matters requiring partner-level attention, BFO may contact Pamela Cross directly at (212) 555-8422 or pcross@calderwoodharkness.com.

113: **3.2 Soft Fee Cap**

115: Based on the anticipated scope of work described in Section 1.2 above, and assuming a negotiation process of customary complexity for a commitment of this size and type, we estimate that our total professional fees for this engagement will not exceed One Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$175,000) (the \"Fee Cap\"). 124: >

133: The Fee Cap is based on the scope of services described in Section 1.2 herein. Any material expansion of scope (including, without limitation, involvement in disputes, regulatory inquiries, restructuring of the proposed commitment structure, negotiation of additional investment vehicles or parallel fund arrangements, or extended negotiation beyond what is reasonably expected for a transaction of this nature) may result in fees exceeding the Fee Cap. In such event, we will discuss the anticipated additional fees with the Client in advance and seek the Client\'s written approval before incurring fees in excess of the Fee Cap.

136: 
137: In addition to professional fees, BFO will be responsible for reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket costs and disbursements incurred by C&H in connection with the engagement. These may include, but are not limited to, the following:
138: 
139: > • Document management, production, printing, and copying costs;
140: >
141: > • Charges for legal research databases (e.g., Westmark Data Systems, Sundial Solutions);
142: >
143: > • Messenger, courier, and delivery services;
144: >
145: > • Travel expenses (if any, which will be incurred only with the prior approval of the Client);
146: >
147: > • Filing fees and governmental charges;
148: >
149: > • Long-distance telephone and videoconference charges;
150: >
151: > • Overnight delivery and postage costs; and
152: >
153: > • Similar charges directly attributable to the engagement.
154: 
155: Disbursements will be itemized on each invoice and will be billed at cost, without markup. We anticipate that disbursements for this engagement will be modest, likely not exceeding \$2,500 in the aggregate.
156: 
157: **[4. Billing and Payment Terms]{.underline}**
158: 
159: **4.1 Invoicing.** C&H will issue invoices on a monthly basis, with each invoice covering the services rendered and disbursements incurred during the preceding calendar month. In the event that the engagement is completed prior to the end of a calendar month, a final invoice will be issued promptly upon completion. Each invoice will include a reasonably detailed summary of the professional services rendered during the billing period, the name of each timekeeper who performed such services, the hours expended by each timekeeper, the applicable hourly rate for each timekeeper, the total fees for the period, and an itemized list of disbursements. Invoices will be transmitted electronically to the attention of Sandra M. Whitfield at swhitfield@briarwoodfo.com (or such other address as BFO may designate in writing), with a copy to BFO\'s Chief Financial Officer, Martin A. Greer, at mgreer@briarwoodfo.com.
160: 
161: **4.2 Payment Terms**
162: 
163: All invoices are due and payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date (\"Net 30\"). Payments should be made by wire transfer to the account designated on each invoice or, alternatively, by check payable to \"Calderwood & Harkness LLP\" and mailed to our offices at the address set forth above. Wire transfer instructions will be provided on each invoice.
164: 
165: In the event that BFO has a good-faith dispute with respect to any portion of an invoice, BFO shall notify C&H in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt of the invoice, specifying the nature of the dispute. The undisputed portion of any invoice shall remain due and payable in accordance with the terms set forth herein, and the parties shall work in good faith to resolve any billing dispute promptly.
166: 
167: C&H reserves the right to suspend the provision of services in the event of non-payment for a period exceeding sixty (60) days following the invoice date, upon reasonable written notice to the Client of not less than ten (10) business days. Such suspension shall be without prejudice to any other rights or remedies available to C&H and shall be subject to our ethical obligations under the New York Rules of Professional Conduct.
168: 
169: **[5. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**
170: 
171: Prior to accepting this engagement, we conducted a comprehensive conflict of interest check in accordance with C&H\'s internal policies and procedures and the applicable provisions of the New York Rules of Professional Conduct (22 N.Y.C.R.R. Part 1200). Based on the information provided by BFO, our conflict check --- which was initiated on January 19, 2024 and cleared on January 22, 2024 --- did not identify any conflicts of interest that would preclude our representation of BFO in this matter.
