173: The parties and entities searched in connection with our conflict check included, among others: Briarwood Family Office LLC; Julian R. Hargrove; Victoria L. Hargrove; the Hargrove Family Trust; Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC; Meridian Peak Capital Partners GP IV LLC; Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P.; Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund III, L.P.; Conrad J. Ellsworth (Managing Partner, MPCA); Priya Narayan (Chief Investment Officer, MPCA); Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP; Pinnacle Capital Markets LLC; and Granite Ledger Fund Services LLC.
174: 
175: BFO acknowledges that C&H is a large, full-service law firm and that, during the course of this engagement, other attorneys in the Firm may represent other clients whose interests may be adverse to those of BFO in matters unrelated to this engagement. Nothing in this Letter shall preclude C&H from representing other clients in matters that are not substantially related to the subject matter of this engagement, provided that such representation does not involve the use of BFO\'s confidential information and does not create a conflict that cannot be waived under applicable professional responsibility rules.
176: 
177: If a conflict of interest arises during the course of this engagement, we will notify the Client promptly and, if appropriate, seek an informed written waiver of the conflict from the Client and/or the affected parties, or take such other steps as may be required by the New York Rules of Professional Conduct, including, if necessary, withdrawal from the engagement.
178: 
179: **[6. Confidentiality]{.underline}**
180: 
181: All information provided by BFO to C&H in connection with this engagement, whether in oral, written, or electronic form, will be treated as confidential and will be protected by the attorney-client privilege and/or the work product doctrine, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law. C&H will maintain appropriate safeguards to protect the confidentiality of BFO\'s information, including the use of secure communication channels, restricted-access electronic filing systems, and internal protocols designed to limit access to engagement-related materials to authorized personnel.
182: 
183: We will not disclose any confidential information received from BFO to third parties without the Client\'s prior written consent, except as may be required by law, court order, or applicable rules of professional conduct, or as may be necessary to defend C&H in any proceeding relating to the services provided hereunder.
184: 
185: BFO acknowledges that in the ordinary course of this engagement, C&H will communicate with Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP (counsel to the General Partner and Fund IV) and potentially with representatives of Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC, Pinnacle Capital Markets LLC (in its capacity as placement agent), and Granite Ledger Fund Services LLC (in its capacity as fund administrator), and that such communications will be limited to matters necessary for the negotiation and documentation of the Side Letter and related transaction documents. BFO hereby authorizes such communications, and C&H will exercise professional judgment in determining what information to disclose in the course of such negotiations, consistent with BFO\'s instructions and the objectives of the engagement.

187: BFO further acknowledges that the existence and terms of the Side Letter may be subject to confidentiality restrictions under the LPA and the Side Letter itself, and that C&H\'s ability to reference the terms of the Side Letter in future matters may be limited by such restrictions.
188: 
189: **[7. Document Retention]{.underline}**
190: 
191: Upon conclusion of this engagement, C&H will retain the Client\'s files and work product in accordance with our firm\'s document retention policy, a copy of which is available upon request. Unless otherwise instructed by BFO in writing, we will retain files related to this engagement for a period of seven (7) years following the closing of the matter, after which time files may be destroyed in the ordinary course without further notice to the Client.
192: 
193: \"Files\" for purposes of this Section include both physical and electronic documents, including correspondence, memoranda, drafts, research materials, and final executed documents. Notwithstanding the foregoing, C&H reserves the right to retain, at its sole discretion, copies of documents that are necessary for C&H\'s own records, quality control, or compliance with professional obligations, including conflict-checking records and administrative files.
194: 
195: The Client may request the return of original documents at any time during or after the engagement. C&H will comply with any such request within a reasonable period of time. The Client acknowledges that C&H may retain copies of returned documents for its records.
196: 
197: **[8. Termination of Engagement]{.underline}**
198: 
199: Either party may terminate this engagement at any time upon written notice to the other party. No specific reason need be stated for the termination.
200: 
201: In the event of termination by either party, BFO will be responsible for payment of all professional fees and disbursements incurred through the effective date of termination, in accordance with the billing and payment terms set forth in this Letter.
202: 
203: C&H\'s obligation to provide legal services will cease upon the effective date of termination, subject to our ethical obligations under the New York Rules of Professional Conduct to take reasonable steps to protect the Client\'s interests upon withdrawal from representation, including providing reasonable notice, allowing time for the engagement of successor counsel, and returning Client materials upon request.

Upon any such termination, C&H will issue a final invoice for all outstanding fees and disbursements, and the provisions of this Letter relating to billing, payment, confidentiality, and document retention shall survive.

208: 
209: This engagement letter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflicts of law principles.
210: 
211: Any dispute arising out of or relating to this engagement letter, the services provided hereunder, or the attorney-client relationship established hereby shall be resolved exclusively in the courts of the State of New York, County of New York, or the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, and each party hereby consents to the personal jurisdiction and venue of such courts.
212: 
213: Nothing in this Section shall limit C&H\'s right to seek injunctive or other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to protect its rights with respect to fees owed or confidential information.
214:

216: 
217: This Letter confirms the engagement of C&H solely for the matter described herein --- namely, the negotiation and documentation of a side letter in connection with BFO\'s proposed commitment to Fund IV. This Letter does not create an attorney-client relationship between C&H and BFO with respect to any other matter, transaction, fund commitment, or legal issue unless separately agreed in a writing signed by the Firm.

Hargrove holding a veto right over any proposed commitment. > \(b\) **Side Letter Negotiation and Documentation.** Preparation and negotiation of the Side Letter between BFO, Fund IV, and the General Partner, addressing, among other things:
> \(i\) most favored nation (\"MFN\") rights, including the scope and mechanics of MFN elections and any carve-outs or limitations thereon;
> \(ii\) excuse and exclusion rights, including the right of BFO to be excused from particular investments on regulatory, legal, tax, or policy grounds;
> \(iii\) management fee reductions or offsets, including any tiered fee arrangements applicable to BFO\'s commitment level;
> \(iv\) co-investment rights, including rights of first offer or first refusal with respect to co-investment opportunities alongside Fund IV;
> \(v\) enhanced reporting obligations, including the frequency, content, and format of financial, portfolio, and ESG-related reporting to BFO;
> \(vi\) key person provisions, including the identification of key persons and the consequences of a key person event;
> \(vii\) transfer rights, including any pre-approved transferees, rights of first refusal, or consent requirements applicable to transfers by BFO of its limited partnership interest;
> \(viii\) confidentiality carve-outs, including permitted disclosures to BFO\'s affiliates, advisors, family members, and regulatory authorities;
> \(ix\) tax reporting, including timely delivery of Schedule K-1s and other tax-related information, as well as any UBTI or ECI-related protections;
> \(x\) placement agent fee disclosures and offsets; and
> \(xi\) such other customary side letter provisions as BFO may reasonably request and the General Partner may agree to.

> \(c\) **Subscription Document Review.** Review and markup of Fund IV subscription documents, including the subscription agreement and investor questionnaire, as necessary for BFO\'s potential admission as a limited partner of Fund IV.

> \(d\) **Negotiation with Counterparty Counsel.** Correspondence and negotiation with Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP, counsel to the General Partner and Fund IV, regarding the Side Letter and related transaction documents, including all communications necessary to resolve open issues and reach agreement on the final form of the Side Letter.

> \(e\) **Advisory Services.** Advisory services related to the foregoing, including analysis of the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act (6 Del. C. § 17-101 *et seq.*) as applicable to the LPA and Side Letter, ERISA considerations (including an assessment of whether Fund IV constitutes a \"plan asset\" entity under 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101, as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA), and regulatory matters relevant to BFO\'s proposed commitment.
> \(f\) **Additional Services.** Such other legal services as may be reasonably requested by BFO in connection with the proposed commitment and as mutually agreed upon by the parties in writing.

**Limitations on Scope.** Notwithstanding the foregoing, our engagement does not extend to, and we will not be providing, any of the following: (i) tax advice, including analysis of the federal, state, or local income tax consequences of BFO\'s investment in Fund IV, the treatment of allocations and distributions under Subchapter K of the Internal Revenue Code, or the analysis of Schedule K-1 implications; (ii) investment advice or recommendations regarding the merits or risks of committing capital to Fund IV; (iii) business, financial, or operational due diligence on Fund IV, MPCA, or any of their affiliates, portfolio companies, or service providers; or (iv) representation of BFO in any dispute, litigation, arbitration, or regulatory proceeding. BFO should consult its own independent tax advisors, financial advisors, and other professionals with respect to such matters. Nothing in this Letter or in the performance of our services should be construed as investment advice or a recommendation to invest or not invest in Fund IV.
**1.3 Client Identification**

Our client in this engagement is Briarwood Family Office LLC (EIN: 27-4831956). We do not represent any individual member, manager, officer, director, or employee of BFO in his or her personal capacity, nor any affiliate, related entity, family trust, or family member of any principal of BFO, unless separately agreed upon in a writing signed by the Firm and such individual or entity. For the avoidance of doubt, our representation of BFO in this engagement does not create an attorney-client relationship between C&H and Julian R. Hargrove, Victoria L. Hargrove, or any other member or principal of BFO in their individual capacities.
**[2. Engagement Team and Staffing]{.underline}**
The following attorneys have been assigned to this matter and will comprise the principal engagement team:

> • **Pamela Cross** --- *Responsible Partner*, Funds & Asset Management group. Ms. Cross will have overall responsibility for the engagement and will serve as the primary relationship partner. Ms. Cross has extensive experience representing institutional investors, family offices, and sovereign wealth funds in connection with commitments to private equity, venture capital, real estate, and credit funds, and has negotiated side letters involving aggregate commitments in excess of \$20 billion. Ms. Cross will be available for strategic guidance, key negotiation calls, and final review of all material documents.

> • **Nicholas Stern** --- *Billing Partner*, Funds & Asset Management group. Mr. Stern will oversee billing and administrative matters related to this engagement and will provide supplemental partner-level review as needed. Mr. Stern will also be available to address questions relating to ERISA, regulatory compliance, and Delaware limited partnership law.

> • **Theresa Kim** --- *Lead Associate*, Funds & Asset Management group. Ms. Kim will serve as the primary day-to-day attorney responsible for drafting the initial Side Letter, conducting the detailed review and markup of the LPA, PPM, and subscription documents, negotiating directly with Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP on outstanding issues, and coordinating all communications with opposing counsel. Ms. Kim will serve as BFO\'s primary point of contact for routine matters and status updates.

> • **Owen Fischer** --- *Working Associate*, Funds & Asset Management group. Mr. Fischer will assist with document review, legal research, drafting support, and preparation of internal memoranda and analysis as directed by the engagement team.

Additional attorneys, paralegals, or other legal staff may be assigned to the engagement from time to time as needed to ensure the efficient and timely completion of the work. We will provide advance notice to the Client of any material changes to the engagement team. Any changes to the composition of the team will be communicated promptly, and we will ensure continuity and quality of service throughout the engagement.

The Client\'s primary day-to-day contact at C&H for purposes of this engagement shall be Theresa Kim, who may be reached at (212) 555-8467 or tkim@calderwoodharkness.com. For matters requiring partner-level attention, BFO may contact Pamela Cross directly at (212) 555-8422 or pcross@calderwoodharkness.com.
**[3. Billing Rates and Fee Arrangements]{.underline}**
**3.1 Hourly Rates**
Our services will be rendered on an hourly basis at the following 2024 standard rates for the attorneys assigned to this matter:
**Attorney**            **Position**            **2024 Hourly Rate**
Pamela Cross            Partner                 \$1,450
Nicholas Stern          Partner                 \$1,400
Theresa Kim             Senior Associate        \$975
Owen Fischer            Associate               \$725

Time will be recorded in increments of one-tenth (0.1) of an hour. In the event that paralegals or other legal support personnel are assigned to the matter, their time will be billed at prevailing rates, which currently range from \$350 to \$475 per hour depending on seniority and specialization. The Client will be informed of the applicable rates for any additional personnel prior to the commencement of their work on this engagement.

These rates are subject to periodic adjustment, typically on an annual basis effective January 1 of each calendar year, with at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice to the Client. Any rate adjustments during the term of this engagement will apply prospectively only and will not affect fees for services rendered prior to the effective date of such adjustment. Given that this engagement is expected to conclude during 2024, we do not anticipate any rate adjustments during the pendency of this matter; however, should the engagement extend into 2025, we will provide the required notice of any rate changes applicable to the new year.
**3.2 Soft Fee Cap**

Based on the anticipated scope of work described in Section 1.2 above, and assuming a negotiation process of customary complexity for a commitment of this size and type, we estimate that our total professional fees for this engagement will not exceed One Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$175,000) (the \"Fee Cap\"). This Fee Cap is a good-faith estimate and is intended as a \"soft cap\" --- meaning that we will use reasonable efforts to complete the engagement within this budget and will notify the Client promptly if we anticipate that fees may approach or exceed the Fee Cap.
To provide additional transparency, we anticipate the following approximate allocation of the Fee Cap across the principal workstreams:
> • LPA/PPM review and analysis: approximately \$30,000 -- \$40,000
> • Side Letter drafting and negotiation: approximately \$80,000 -- \$100,000
> • Subscription document review: approximately \$10,000 -- \$15,000
> • Advisory services (Delaware law, ERISA, regulatory): approximately \$10,000 -- \$15,000
> • Coordination and project management: approximately \$5,000 -- \$10,000
These estimates are indicative only and are subject to change depending on the complexity and duration of negotiations with the General Partner and its counsel.
The Fee Cap does not include disbursements and out-of-pocket expenses, which will be billed separately as described in Section 3.3 below.

The Fee Cap is based on the scope of services described in Section 1.2 herein. Any material expansion of scope (including, without limitation, involvement in disputes, regulatory inquiries, restructuring of the proposed commitment structure, negotiation of additional investment vehicles or parallel fund arrangements, or extended negotiation beyond what is reasonably expected for a transaction of this nature) may result in fees exceeding the Fee Cap. In such event, we will discuss the anticipated additional fees with the Client in advance and seek the Client\'s written approval before incurring fees in excess of the Fee Cap.
**3.3 Disbursements and Expenses**

In addition to professional fees, BFO will be responsible for reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket costs and disbursements incurred by C&H in connection with the engagement. These may include, but are not limited to, the following:
> • Document management, production, printing, and copying costs;
> • Charges for legal research databases (e.g., Westmark Data Systems, Sundial Solutions);
> • Messenger, courier, and delivery services;
> • Travel expenses (if any, which will be incurred only with the prior approval of the Client);
> • Filing fees and governmental charges;
> • Long-distance telephone and videoconference charges;
> • Overnight delivery and postage costs; and
> • Similar charges directly attributable to the engagement.

Disbursements will be itemized on each invoice and will be billed at cost, without markup. We anticipate that disbursements for this engagement will be modest, likely not exceeding \$2,500 in the aggregate.
**[4. Billing and Payment Terms]{.underline}**

**4.1 Invoicing.** C&H will issue invoices on a monthly basis, with each invoice covering the services rendered and disbursements incurred during the preceding calendar month. In the event that the engagement is completed prior to the end of a calendar month, a final invoice will be issued promptly upon completion. Each invoice will include a reasonably detailed summary of the professional services rendered during the billing period, the name of each timekeeper who performed such services, the hours expended by each timekeeper, the applicable hourly rate for each timekeeper, the total fees for the period, and an itemized list of disbursements. Invoices will be transmitted electronically to the attention of Sandra M. Whitfield at swhitfield@briarwoodfo.com (or such other address as BFO may designate in writing), with a copy to BFO\'s Chief Financial Officer, Martin A. Greer, at mgreer@briarwoodfo.com.
**4.2 Payment Terms**

All invoices are due and payable within thirty (30) days of the invoice date (\"Net 30\"). Payments should be made by wire transfer to the account designated on each invoice or, alternatively, by check payable to \"Calderwood & Harkness LLP\" and mailed to our offices at the address set forth above. Wire transfer instructions will be provided on each invoice.

In the event that BFO has a good-faith dispute with respect to any portion of an invoice, BFO shall notify C&H in writing within fifteen (15) days of receipt of the invoice, specifying the nature of the dispute. The undisputed portion of any invoice shall remain due and payable in accordance with the terms set forth herein, and the parties shall work in good faith to resolve any billing dispute promptly.

C&H reserves the right to suspend the provision of services in the event of non-payment for a period exceeding sixty (60) days following the invoice date, upon reasonable written notice to the Client of not less than ten (10) business days. Such suspension shall be without prejudice to any other rights or remedies available to C&H and shall be subject to our ethical obligations under the New York Rules of Professional Conduct.
**[5. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**

Prior to accepting this engagement, we conducted a comprehensive conflict of interest check in accordance with C&H\'s internal policies and procedures and the applicable provisions of the New York Rules of Professional Conduct (22 N.Y.C.R.R. Part 1200). Based on the information provided by BFO, our conflict check --- which was initiated on January 19, 2024 and cleared on January 22, 2024 --- did not identify any conflicts of interest that would preclude our representation of BFO in this matter.

The parties and entities searched in connection with our conflict check included, among others: Briarwood Family Office LLC; Julian R. Hargrove; Victoria L. Hargrove; the Hargrove Family Trust; Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC; Meridian Peak Capital Partners GP IV LLC; Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P.; Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund III, L.P.; Conrad J. Ellsworth (Managing Partner, MPCA); Priya Narayan (Chief Investment Officer, MPCA); Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP; Pinnacle Capital Markets LLC; and Granite Ledger Fund Services LLC.

BFO acknowledges that C&H is a large, full-service law firm and that, during the course of this engagement, other attorneys in the Firm may represent other clients whose interests may be adverse to those of BFO in matters unrelated to this engagement. Nothing in this Letter shall preclude C&H from representing other clients in matters that are not substantially related to the subject matter of this engagement, provided that such representation does not involve the use of BFO\'s confidential information and does not create a conflict that cannot be waived under applicable professional responsibility rules.

If a conflict of interest arises during the course of this engagement, we will notify the Client promptly and, if appropriate, seek an informed written waiver of the conflict from the Client and/or the affected parties, or take such other steps as may be required by the New York Rules of Professional Conduct, including, if necessary, withdrawal from the engagement.
**[6. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

All information provided by BFO to C&H in connection with this engagement, whether in oral, written, or electronic form, will be treated as confidential and will be protected by the attorney-client privilege and/or the work product doctrine, to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law. C&H will maintain appropriate safeguards to protect the confidentiality of BFO\'s information, including the use of secure communication channels, restricted-access electronic filing systems, and internal protocols designed to limit access to engagement-related materials to authorized personnel.

We will not disclose any confidential information received from BFO to third parties without the Client\'s prior written consent, except as may be required by law, court order, or applicable rules of professional conduct, or as may be necessary to defend C&H in any proceeding relating to the services provided hereunder.

BFO acknowledges that in the ordinary course of this engagement, C&H will communicate with Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP (counsel to the General Partner and Fund IV) and potentially with representatives of Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC, Pinnacle Capital Markets LLC (in its capacity as placement agent), and Granite Ledger Fund Services LLC (in its capacity as fund administrator), and that such communications will be limited to matters necessary for the negotiation and documentation of the Side Letter and related transaction documents. BFO hereby authorizes such communications, and C&H will exercise professional judgment in determining what information to disclose in the course of such negotiations, consistent with BFO\'s instructions and the objectives of the engagement.

BFO further acknowledges that the existence and terms of the Side Letter may be subject to confidentiality restrictions under the LPA and the Side Letter itself, and that C&H\'s ability to reference the terms of the Side Letter in future matters may be limited by such restrictions.
**[7. Document Retention]{.underline}**

Upon conclusion of this engagement, C&H will retain the Client\'s files and work product in accordance with our firm\'s document retention policy, a copy of which is available upon request. Unless otherwise instructed by BFO in writing, we will retain files related to this engagement for a period of seven (7) years following the closing of the matter, after which time files may be destroyed in the ordinary course without further notice to the Client.

\"Files\" for purposes of this Section include both physical and electronic documents, including correspondence, memoranda, drafts, research materials, and final executed documents. Notwithstanding the foregoing, C&H reserves the right to retain, at its sole discretion, copies of documents that are necessary for C&H\'s own records, quality control, or compliance with professional obligations, including conflict-checking records and administrative files.

The Client may request the return of original documents at any time during or after the engagement. C&H will comply with any such request within a reasonable period of time. The Client acknowledges that C&H may retain copies of returned documents for its records.
**[8. Termination of Engagement]{.underline}**
Either party may terminate this engagement at any time upon written notice to the other party. No specific reason need be stated for the termination.

In the event of termination by either party, BFO will be responsible for payment of all professional fees and disbursements incurred through the effective date of termination, in accordance with the billing and payment terms set forth in this Letter.

C&H\'s obligation to provide legal services will cease upon the effective date of termination, subject to our ethical obligations under the New York Rules of Professional Conduct to take reasonable steps to protect the Client\'s interests upon withdrawal from representation, including providing reasonable notice, allowing time for the engagement of successor counsel, and returning Client materials upon request.

This engagement shall also be deemed terminated upon: (i) the completion of the services described in Section 1.2 above and the execution and delivery of the Side Letter and related subscription documents; (ii) BFO\'s decision not to proceed with the proposed commitment to Fund IV; (iii) the General Partner\'s decision not to accept BFO\'s proposed commitment; or (iv) the mutual written agreement of the parties to terminate the engagement. Upon any such termination, C&H will issue a final invoice for all outstanding fees and disbursements, and the provisions of this Letter relating to billing, payment, confidentiality, and document retention shall survive.
**[9. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution]{.underline}**
This engagement letter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflicts of law principles.

Any dispute arising out of or relating to this engagement letter, the services provided hereunder, or the attorney-client relationship established hereby shall be resolved exclusively in the courts of the State of New York, County of New York, or the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, and each party hereby consents to the personal jurisdiction and venue of such courts.

Nothing in this Section shall limit C&H\'s right to seek injunctive or other equitable relief in any court of competent jurisdiction to protect its rights with respect to fees owed or confidential information.
**[10. Limitation of Engagement]{.underline}**

This Letter confirms the engagement of C&H solely for the matter described herein --- namely, the negotiation and documentation of a side letter in connection with BFO\'s proposed commitment to Fund IV. This Letter does not create an attorney-client relationship between C&H and BFO with respect to any other matter, transaction, fund commitment, or legal issue unless separately agreed in a writing signed by the Firm.

Our representation of BFO in this engagement does not constitute legal advice with respect to any investment decision, and BFO acknowledges that the decision to commit (or not commit) capital to Fund IV is a business decision to be made by BFO\'s investment committee and principals in their sole discretion, based on their own independent analysis, judgment, and due diligence. C&H shall have no responsibility or liability for BFO\'s investment decision, and nothing in our advice, analysis, or work product should be construed as a recommendation to invest or not invest in Fund IV.

BFO has informed us that its internal approval for the proposed commitment to Fund IV requires the affirmative vote of at least three (3) of the four (4) members of BFO\'s investment committee, with Julian R. Hargrove holding a veto right over any proposed commitment. C&H\'s engagement is independent of the outcome of that approval process, and the fees and disbursements incurred prior to any final investment decision by BFO shall remain the obligation of BFO regardless of whether the commitment is ultimately approved.
**[11. Miscellaneous]{.underline}**

This engagement letter constitutes the entire agreement between C&H and BFO with respect to the matters addressed herein and supersedes any and all prior oral or written communications, understandings, or agreements regarding this engagement.

This Letter may not be amended, modified, or supplemented except by a written instrument signed by both parties. No waiver of any provision of this Letter shall be effective unless made in writing and signed by the party against whom enforcement of the waiver is sought.

If any provision of this Letter is found by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect, and the invalid or unenforceable provision shall be modified to the minimum extent necessary to make it valid and enforceable while preserving its original intent.

This Letter may be executed in counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Signatures transmitted by facsimile, PDF, or other electronic means shall be deemed original signatures for all purposes.

All notices and communications under this Letter shall be in writing and shall be deemed given when delivered personally, sent by email (with confirmation of receipt), or sent by recognized overnight courier to the addresses set forth herein or to such other address as either party may designate in writing.
**[12. Acceptance and Execution]{.underline}**

We are grateful for the opportunity to represent Briarwood Family Office LLC in this matter and look forward to working with you and your team. If the terms set forth in this Letter are acceptable, please indicate your agreement by signing in the space provided below and returning one fully executed copy to our offices. We kindly request that the countersigned copy be returned no later than **February 7, 2024**, so that we may commence work promptly.

Should you have any questions regarding this Letter or wish to discuss any of its terms, please do not hesitate to contact Pamela Cross at (212) 555-8422 or pcross@calderwoodharkness.com, or Theresa Kim at (212) 555-8467 or tkim@calderwoodharkness.com.
We look forward to a productive engagement.
> Very truly yours,
CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP
Name: Pamela Cross
Title: Partner, Funds & Asset Management
425 Lexington Avenue New York, NY 10017
**ACKNOWLEDGED AND AGREED:**

The undersigned hereby acknowledges receipt of this engagement letter, confirms that the terms and conditions set forth herein are acceptable, and agrees to be bound by the terms of this Letter effective as of the date of countersignature below.
BRIARWOOD FAMILY OFFICE LLC

21: Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Pellegrino Capital Group LLC (\"Pellegrino\" or \"PCG\"), a Delaware limited liability company, in connection with Pellegrino\'s proposed Twenty-Five Million Dollar (\$25,000,000) co-investment alongside Ridgeline Equity Partners Fund IV, L.P. 33: Calderwood & Harkness does not represent, and shall not be deemed to represent, any affiliate, subsidiary, member, manager, officer, director, employee, or agent of Pellegrino individually in connection with this engagement, including without limitation Marco A. Pellegrino (Founder & Managing Member) or Daniella R. Pellegrino (Chief Financial Officer), unless a separate written engagement agreement is entered into between the Firm and such individual expressly establishing such a representation. No attorney-client relationship shall arise between the Firm and any such individual by virtue of this Engagement Letter or the Firm\'s performance of services hereunder, and the interests of any such individual may not necessarily be aligned with the interests of Pellegrino as an entity in all respects.
34: 
35: The primary client contact for this engagement shall be Adriana Voss, Vice President & General Counsel, Pellegrino Capital Group LLC. Unless otherwise directed in writing, all substantive communications, deliverables, and invoices will be directed to Ms. Voss. We understand that Ms. Voss is authorized to provide instructions, approve work product, and make decisions on behalf of Pellegrino in connection with this engagement, subject to such internal approvals as may be required under Pellegrino\'s organizational documents and governance procedures.

38: 
39: Calderwood & Harkness will provide legal services to Pellegrino in connection with the co-investment described above. The scope of our engagement is set forth in greater detail in Sections 3.1 through 3.5 below. We will endeavor to keep Pellegrino informed of material developments and to seek instructions on significant issues as they arise during the course of the representation.

41: **3.1 Review and Negotiation of Co-Investment Documentation**
42:

(the \"Co-Invest LPA\"). Our review will focus on the terms and provisions of the Co-Invest LPA that are material to Pellegrino\'s rights, obligations, and economic interests as a limited partner in the Co-Invest Vehicle, including but not limited to provisions relating to capital contributions and capital calls, distributions and distribution waterfalls, management fees and carried interest, clawback obligations, excuse and exclusion mechanisms, indemnification and exculpation of the general partner, transfer restrictions, dissolution and winding up, reporting and audit rights, key person events, and amendments and waivers.

45: In addition, Calderwood & Harkness will draft and negotiate a side letter agreement (the \"Side Letter\") between Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC (the \"Co-Invest GP\") and Pellegrino. The Side Letter is intended to contain investor-specific protections and additional rights for the benefit of Pellegrino, including the following:
46: 
47: > \(a\) most-favored-nation (\"MFN\") rights, entitling Pellegrino to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable term or right granted to any other limited partner of the Co-Invest Vehicle in a side letter or other agreement, subject to customary exclusions;
48: >
49: > \(b\) a right to a seat on the limited partner advisory committee (\"LPAC\") of the Co-Invest Vehicle, or, if no LPAC is formed for the Co-Invest Vehicle, a right to a seat on the LPAC of Ridgeline Fund IV, to the extent such rights are available;

54: >

68: >

Cheng, Partner, and Meredith L. Tanaka, Associate, at Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP, and reporting on the status of such negotiations to Pellegrino; and

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** *Attorneys at Law*

Adriana Voss, Esq. Vice President & General Counsel Pellegrino Capital Group LLC 1440 Brickell Avenue, Suite 3200 Miami, FL 33131
> **Re:** Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP in Connection with Pellegrino Capital Group LLC Co-Investment alongside Ridgeline Equity Partners Fund IV, L.P. in Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P.
Dear Ms. Voss:
**[1. Introduction and Purpose]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Pellegrino Capital Group LLC (\"Pellegrino\" or \"PCG\"), a Delaware limited liability company, in connection with Pellegrino\'s proposed Twenty-Five Million Dollar (\$25,000,000) co-investment alongside Ridgeline Equity Partners Fund IV, L.P. (\"Ridgeline Fund IV\") in Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P. (the \"Co-Invest Vehicle\"), a Delaware limited partnership formed for the purpose of facilitating co-investment alongside Ridgeline Fund IV.

As we understand the transaction, the Co-Invest Vehicle will co-invest alongside Ridgeline Fund IV in the equity of Clarion Holdings Acquisition Corp. (\"AcquisitionCo\"), a Delaware corporation formed to acquire one hundred percent (100%) of the equity interests of Clarion Hospitality Holdings, Inc. (\"Clarion\"), an integrated hospitality asset management platform headquartered in Nashville, Tennessee. The acquisition of Clarion by AcquisitionCo (the \"Acquisition\") is expected to be structured as a leveraged buyout, with the equity capitalization of AcquisitionCo funded through commitments from Ridgeline Fund IV, the Co-Invest Vehicle, and any other co-investment vehicles or equity participants designated by the sponsor.

Pellegrino\'s \$25,000,000 commitment to the Co-Invest Vehicle represents approximately thirty-three and one-third percent (33.33%) of the Co-Invest Vehicle\'s aggregate Seventy-Five Million Dollar (\$75,000,000) in commitments, and approximately ten percent (10.0%) of the total Two Hundred Fifty Million Dollar (\$250,000,000) equity capitalization of AcquisitionCo. We understand that the balance of the equity capitalization will be comprised of commitments from Ridgeline Fund IV and, potentially, other co-investment participants alongside the Co-Invest Vehicle.

This letter agreement (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions governing Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement by Pellegrino, including the scope of legal services to be provided, attorney staffing, fees and billing arrangements, conflict of interest disclosures, confidentiality obligations, and other terms and conditions of the attorney-client relationship. We ask that you review this Engagement Letter carefully and confirm Pellegrino\'s agreement to these terms by executing and returning a copy as described in Section 13 below.
**[2. Client Identification]{.underline}**

The client in this engagement is Pellegrino Capital Group LLC, and no other person or entity. Calderwood & Harkness\'s duties of loyalty, confidentiality, and professional responsibility in connection with this matter run solely to Pellegrino Capital Group LLC as an entity.

Calderwood & Harkness does not represent, and shall not be deemed to represent, any affiliate, subsidiary, member, manager, officer, director, employee, or agent of Pellegrino individually in connection with this engagement, including without limitation Marco A. Pellegrino (Founder & Managing Member) or Daniella R. Pellegrino (Chief Financial Officer), unless a separate written engagement agreement is entered into between the Firm and such individual expressly establishing such a representation. No attorney-client relationship shall arise between the Firm and any such individual by virtue of this Engagement Letter or the Firm\'s performance of services hereunder, and the interests of any such individual may not necessarily be aligned with the interests of Pellegrino as an entity in all respects.

The primary client contact for this engagement shall be Adriana Voss, Vice President & General Counsel, Pellegrino Capital Group LLC. Unless otherwise directed in writing, all substantive communications, deliverables, and invoices will be directed to Ms. Voss. We understand that Ms. Voss is authorized to provide instructions, approve work product, and make decisions on behalf of Pellegrino in connection with this engagement, subject to such internal approvals as may be required under Pellegrino\'s organizational documents and governance procedures.
**[3. Scope of Services]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will provide legal services to Pellegrino in connection with the co-investment described above. The scope of our engagement is set forth in greater detail in Sections 3.1 through 3.5 below. We will endeavor to keep Pellegrino informed of material developments and to seek instructions on significant issues as they arise during the course of the representation.
**3.1 Review and Negotiation of Co-Investment Documentation**

Calderwood & Harkness will undertake the review, analysis, markup, and negotiation of the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P. (the \"Co-Invest LPA\"). We understand that the initial draft of the Co-Invest LPA has been prepared by Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP, counsel to the sponsor, Ridgeline Equity Management LLC (the \"Sponsor\"). Our review will focus on the terms and provisions of the Co-Invest LPA that are material to Pellegrino\'s rights, obligations, and economic interests as a limited partner in the Co-Invest Vehicle, including but not limited to provisions relating to capital contributions and capital calls, distributions and distribution waterfalls, management fees and carried interest, clawback obligations, excuse and exclusion mechanisms, indemnification and exculpation of the general partner, transfer restrictions, dissolution and winding up, reporting and audit rights, key person events, and amendments and waivers.

In addition, Calderwood & Harkness will draft and negotiate a side letter agreement (the \"Side Letter\") between Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC (the \"Co-Invest GP\") and Pellegrino. The Side Letter is intended to contain investor-specific protections and additional rights for the benefit of Pellegrino, including the following:

> \(a\) most-favored-nation (\"MFN\") rights, entitling Pellegrino to elect to receive the benefit of any more favorable term or right granted to any other limited partner of the Co-Invest Vehicle in a side letter or other agreement, subject to customary exclusions;

> \(b\) a right to a seat on the limited partner advisory committee (\"LPAC\") of the Co-Invest Vehicle, or, if no LPAC is formed for the Co-Invest Vehicle, a right to a seat on the LPAC of Ridgeline Fund IV, to the extent such rights are available;

> \(c\) enhanced reporting rights, including quarterly unaudited financial statements, annual audited financial statements, and ad hoc reporting on material events affecting the Co-Invest Vehicle or the Acquisition;

> \(d\) ESG reporting covenants, requiring the Sponsor or the Co-Invest GP to provide Pellegrino with periodic environmental, social, and governance reporting with respect to Clarion and the portfolio, consistent with Pellegrino\'s own ESG reporting framework and investor disclosure obligations;

> \(e\) future co-investment allocation rights, entitling Pellegrino to a right of first offer or similar priority allocation right with respect to future co-investment opportunities originated by the Sponsor or Ridgeline Equity Management LLC in connection with Ridgeline Fund IV or any successor fund; and

> \(f\) excuse and exclusion protections, permitting Pellegrino to be excused from participation in, or excluded from the costs of, any investment or activity that would cause Pellegrino to violate applicable law, regulation, or any provision of its organizational documents or constituent fund documentation.

Calderwood & Harkness will also review, negotiate, and complete a subscription agreement (the \"Subscription Agreement\") for Pellegrino\'s Twenty-Five Million Dollar (\$25,000,000) limited partnership interest in the Co-Invest Vehicle, ensuring that the representations, warranties, and covenants contained therein are accurate and appropriate in the context of Pellegrino\'s organizational and regulatory status.

Finally, Calderwood & Harkness will assist Pellegrino with the completion of the investor questionnaire customarily required in connection with subscriptions of this nature, including representations and certifications relating to tax status (including U.S. tax-exempt status, if applicable), the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (\"FATCA\") and the Common Reporting Standard (\"CRS\"), the Office of Foreign Assets Control (\"OFAC\") sanctions programs, and anti-money laundering (\"AML\") requirements.
**3.2 Tax Analysis and Coordination**

Calderwood & Harkness will prepare an internal tax analysis memorandum (the \"Tax Memorandum\") addressing the federal income tax implications of the co-investment structure for Pellegrino. The Tax Memorandum will address, among other matters, the following topics:

> \(a\) classification of the Co-Invest Vehicle as a partnership for federal income tax purposes under Subchapter K of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\"), and the implications of its organization as a Delaware limited partnership;

> \(b\) unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") considerations, to the extent relevant to Pellegrino or its underlying investors, including analysis of potential UBTI generated through the use of acquisition indebtedness or other debt-financed structures in connection with the Acquisition;

> \(c\) analysis of the Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act of 1980 (\"FIRPTA\"), to the extent Clarion\'s assets include U.S. real property interests within the meaning of Section 897 of the Code;

> \(d\) the allocation methodology under Section 704(b) of the Code (economic effect and substantiality) and Section 704(c) of the Code (contributed property and reverse Section 704(c) allocations), as reflected in the Co-Invest LPA;

> \(e\) carried interest treatment under Section 1061 of the Code, including the three-year holding period requirement applicable to certain partnership interests held in connection with the performance of services; and

> \(f\) state and local tax nexus analysis, with a particular focus on the states of Delaware, Florida, Tennessee, and New York, addressing potential filing obligations, withholding requirements, and composite return elections.

In connection with the foregoing, Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with Pellegrino\'s independent tax and accounting advisor, Whitfield Greer & Associates LLP (\"Whitfield Greer\"), and specifically with Robert K. Anand, Engagement Partner at Whitfield Greer, regarding their independent tax structuring analysis, Schedule K-1 delivery mechanics and timing, and any other tax-related matters relevant to Pellegrino\'s participation in the Co-Invest Vehicle. Calderwood & Harkness\'s tax analysis is intended to supplement, and not to replace, the independent advice and analysis provided by Whitfield Greer.
**3.3 Closing Deliverables**
Calderwood & Harkness will prepare or coordinate the following deliverables in connection with the closing of Pellegrino\'s investment in the Co-Invest Vehicle:

> \(a\) a comprehensive closing checklist identifying all deliverables required in connection with the closing, the party responsible for preparation or delivery of each item, the applicable deadline or target date, and the current status of each item;

> \(b\) a funds flow memorandum detailing the movement of Pellegrino\'s Twenty-Five Million Dollar (\$25,000,000) capital contribution from Pellegrino\'s designated bank account, through the escrow account maintained by Continental Fiduciary Services, Inc. (the \"Escrow Agent\") pursuant to the terms of the applicable escrow agreement, to the Co-Invest Vehicle\'s account, and onward to AcquisitionCo in connection with the consummation of the Acquisition;

> \(c\) a legal opinion letter addressed to the Co-Invest GP, in customary form and substance, regarding the due organization, valid existence, and good standing of Pellegrino; the authorization by all necessary action of Pellegrino\'s execution, delivery, and performance of the Co-Invest LPA, the Side Letter, and the Subscription Agreement; and the enforceability of Pellegrino\'s obligations under such documents against Pellegrino in accordance with their respective terms, in each case subject to customary assumptions, qualifications, and exceptions; and

> \(d\) an officer\'s certificate or secretary\'s certificate of Pellegrino, certifying as to the authority of the person or persons executing the transaction documents on behalf of Pellegrino, the incumbency of such person or persons, and the authenticity of the organizational documents of Pellegrino delivered in connection with the closing.
**3.4 General Advisory**
In addition to the specific tasks described above, Calderwood & Harkness will provide the following general advisory services in connection with the co-investment:

> \(a\) preparation of internal memoranda summarizing the key terms of the Co-Invest LPA, identifying issues and risks, and setting forth our recommendations for Pellegrino\'s review and approval prior to the commencement of negotiations or the acceptance of proposed terms;

> \(b\) internal tracking of negotiation points and their resolutions as between Calderwood & Harkness (on behalf of Pellegrino) and Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP (on behalf of the Sponsor), including communications with Douglas W. Cheng, Partner, and Meredith L. Tanaka, Associate, at Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP, and reporting on the status of such negotiations to Pellegrino; and
> \(c\) general legal advice and counsel to Pellegrino in connection with the co-investment as may be reasonably requested by Pellegrino from time to time during the course of this engagement.
**3.5 Limitations on Scope**

The scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement is limited to the services described in Sections 3.1 through 3.4 above. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Pellegrino should be aware of the following limitations:

> \(a\) Calderwood & Harkness is **not** engaged to provide legal advice with respect to the underlying Acquisition of Clarion, including but not limited to the conduct of business, legal, financial, or operational due diligence on Clarion\'s business, assets, liabilities, contracts, regulatory compliance, intellectual property, or workforce matters. Pellegrino should satisfy itself, through its own due diligence or through the diligence conducted by the Sponsor, that the Acquisition and the underlying business of Clarion meet Pellegrino\'s investment criteria.

> \(b\) Calderwood & Harkness is **not** engaged to provide legal advice with respect to the credit facility or any other debt financing provided by Pinnacle National Bank, N.A. or any other lender in connection with the Acquisition, including the terms of any credit agreement, security agreement, guarantee, or intercreditor arrangement.

> \(c\) Calderwood & Harkness is **not** engaged to advise on the interests, rights, or obligations of any party other than Pellegrino, including the Sponsor, the Co-Invest GP, Ridgeline Fund IV, AcquisitionCo, Clarion, any seller, or any other co-investor in the Co-Invest Vehicle (including without limitation Brindoval Growth Capital Fund II, L.P., to the extent it is a participant).

> \(d\) Calderwood & Harkness is **not** engaged to provide tax advice as a substitute for the engagement of Whitfield Greer & Associates LLP. Any tax analysis provided by Calderwood & Harkness is supplemental in nature and is intended to inform Pellegrino\'s understanding of the tax aspects of the co-investment structure; such analysis should be reviewed in conjunction with, and does not supersede, the independent advice of Whitfield Greer & Associates LLP.

> \(e\) Calderwood & Harkness does **not** represent Pellegrino in connection with any regulatory filings, including but not limited to filings under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act of 1976, filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, or filings with any state regulatory authority, unless separately agreed in writing.

If the scope of our engagement needs to be expanded or modified at any point, we will discuss the matter with you and, if appropriate, confirm any revised scope in a supplemental engagement letter or amendment to this Engagement Letter.
**[4. Staffing]{.underline}**
The following attorneys have been assigned to this engagement and will be the primary members of the Calderwood & Harkness team working on this matter:

**Responsible Partner:** Nicholas Stern, Partner, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Stern will have overall responsibility for the engagement, including client relationship management, strategic direction, and supervision of all work product produced by the engagement team. Mr. Stern will serve as the primary point of contact for Pellegrino on significant issues, negotiations, and escalation matters.

**Billing Partner:** Graham Sutherland, Partner, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Sutherland will serve as the billing partner for purposes of rate approvals, billing administration, and invoice review. Mr. Sutherland will also be available to provide substantive legal advice as needed on particular issues within his areas of expertise.

**Lead Associate:** Owen Fischer, Associate, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Fischer will serve as the day-to-day lead on document review, drafting, markup, and negotiation of the Co-Invest LPA, Side Letter, Subscription Agreement, and related transaction documents. Mr. Fischer will also be responsible for coordinating with Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP on document exchanges and turn schedules.

**Working Associate:** Stephen Adler, Associate, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Adler will support Mr. Fischer in connection with legal research, preparation of the closing checklist, drafting of the funds flow memorandum and certificates, and coordination of closing mechanics.

Additional attorneys, paralegals, or other professional staff may be assigned to this engagement from time to time as the needs of the matter require. We will endeavor to staff this matter efficiently and to avoid unnecessary duplication of effort. Pellegrino will be notified of any material changes in staffing, including the substitution of any of the named attorneys listed above.
**[5. Fees and Billing]{.underline}**
**5.1 Hourly Rates**

This engagement will be billed on an hourly basis at Calderwood & Harkness\'s standard rates for the attorneys and professional staff assigned to the matter. The current rates for 2025 are as follows:
**Timekeeper Category**             **2025 Hourly Rate Range**
Partners                            \$1,050 -- \$1,250 per hour
Associates                          \$550 -- \$825 per hour
Paralegals                          \$350 -- \$450 per hour

The specific rate for each timekeeper will fall within the applicable range based on the individual\'s seniority and experience level. We will provide Pellegrino with a schedule of the specific rates applicable to each attorney and paralegal assigned to this matter upon request.

Rates are subject to periodic adjustment, typically effective January 1 of each calendar year. Calderwood & Harkness will notify Pellegrino in advance of any rate changes. Any adjusted rates will apply to services rendered on or after the effective date of the adjustment.
**5.2 Fee Estimate**

Based on the anticipated scope of work described in Section 3 above and our experience with comparable co-investment transactions, Calderwood & Harkness estimates that total legal fees for this engagement will be in the range of One Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand Dollars (\$175,000) to Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$250,000), exclusive of disbursements and out-of-pocket expenses. This estimate assumes a transaction of moderate complexity, involving two to three rounds of negotiation on the Co-Invest LPA and Side Letter, and a closing timeline of approximately six to eight weeks from the date of this Engagement Letter.

This estimate is provided for budgeting and planning purposes only and does not constitute a cap, ceiling, fixed fee, or guarantee of total fees. Actual fees will depend on a number of factors, including the complexity and duration of negotiations with Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP, the number and extent of drafts and revisions to the transaction documents, the scope and nature of issues that arise during the course of the engagement, and the extent of Pellegrino\'s requests for additional analysis or advisory services. If it appears at any point that our fees are likely to materially exceed this estimate, we will promptly notify Pellegrino and discuss appropriate steps.

Calderwood & Harkness will endeavor to keep Pellegrino informed of the status of accrued fees as the matter progresses, and is prepared to provide interim fee estimates or budget updates upon request.
**5.3 Expenses and Disbursements**

In addition to legal fees, Pellegrino will be responsible for the reimbursement of out-of-pocket costs and disbursements reasonably incurred by Calderwood & Harkness in connection with this engagement. Such costs and disbursements may include, without limitation, the following:
> \(a\) filing fees, including fees for filings with the Delaware Secretary of State, requests for certificates of good standing or certificates of status, and similar governmental charges;
> \(b\) messenger and courier charges;
> \(c\) travel expenses, including airfare, hotel, ground transportation, and meals, if travel is required in connection with the engagement (which we do not currently anticipate);
> \(d\) charges for outside photocopying, printing, or binding services in excess of routine in-office copying;
> \(e\) fees for third-party vendors, including document management platforms, virtual data room access fees, and similar services; and
> \(f\) long-distance telephone and videoconference charges, to the extent separately billable.

Filing fees for Delaware Secretary of State filings or good standing certificates will be billed at cost, without markup. Other disbursements will generally be billed at cost or at Calderwood & Harkness\'s standard internal charge rates, as applicable.
**5.4 Invoicing and Payment**

Invoices for fees and disbursements will be rendered on a monthly basis and are due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of receipt. Each invoice will contain reasonable detail regarding the services rendered, including the identity of the attorney or professional performing the work, the date on which the services were performed, a description of the services rendered, and the amount of time expended.

If Pellegrino has any questions regarding an invoice or wishes to discuss any charge, we encourage you to contact Mr. Sutherland or Mr. Stern promptly so that any concerns can be addressed in a timely manner. Calderwood & Harkness reserves the right to charge interest on past-due balances at a rate of one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is less, on any amounts remaining unpaid for more than sixty (60) days following the date of the applicable invoice.
**[6. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness has conducted a conflicts check in connection with this engagement in accordance with the Firm\'s standard conflict clearance procedures. Based on that review, the Firm is not aware of any conflict of interest that would prevent it from representing Pellegrino in this matter under the applicable Florida Rules of Professional Conduct.

Specifically, Calderwood & Harkness does not currently represent, and has not in the recent past represented, any of the following entities in connection with this transaction or any related matter: Ridgeline Equity Partners Fund IV, L.P.; Ridgeline Equity Management LLC; Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC; Clarion Hospitality Holdings, Inc.; Clarion Holdings Acquisition Corp.; Brindoval Growth Capital Fund II, L.P.; Pinnacle National Bank, N.A.; or any of their respective affiliates, general partners, managing members, or portfolio companies, insofar as such representation would relate to the subject matter of this engagement.

Pellegrino acknowledges and agrees that Calderwood & Harkness is a large, multi-office law firm with a diverse client base, and that the Firm may from time to time represent other clients whose interests may be adverse to Pellegrino in matters that are unrelated to this engagement. Nothing in this Engagement Letter shall be construed to preclude or restrict Calderwood & Harkness from accepting or continuing any such representation, provided that (i) the matter in question does not involve the same or a substantially related matter as this engagement, and (ii) such representation does not create a direct and impermissible conflict of interest with respect to the Firm\'s obligations to Pellegrino under this Engagement Letter and the applicable Rules of Professional Conduct.

In the event that a conflict of interest arises during the course of this engagement, Calderwood & Harkness will promptly notify Pellegrino of the conflict and discuss appropriate steps to address it. Such steps may include, depending on the nature and severity of the conflict, the implementation of an ethical wall or information barrier within the Firm, the obtaining of an informed written waiver from the affected parties, or, if the conflict cannot be adequately resolved, the withdrawal of Calderwood & Harkness from the representation in accordance with Section 9 of this Engagement Letter.
**[7. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will maintain the confidentiality of all information provided by Pellegrino, or obtained by the Firm on behalf of Pellegrino, in connection with this engagement. This obligation is consistent with, and in addition to, the Firm\'s duties of confidentiality under the applicable Florida Rules of Professional Conduct (including Rule 4-1.6) and other applicable law. All confidential information received from Pellegrino will be disclosed within the Firm only to those attorneys, paralegals, and staff who have a need to know such information in connection with the performance of services under this engagement.

Pellegrino hereby authorizes Calderwood & Harkness to disclose confidential information to the following parties to the extent reasonably necessary in connection with the negotiation and closing of the co-investment:
> \(a\) Hartwell Velmoran & Pratt LLP, counsel to the Sponsor, in connection with the negotiation of the Co-Invest LPA, Side Letter, Subscription Agreement, and related transaction documents;

> \(b\) Aldridge Mayer Stevens LLP, counsel to the seller(s) of Clarion, to the extent that the exchange of information with seller\'s counsel is reasonably required in connection with the co-investment closing process;
> \(c\) Whitfield Greer & Associates LLP, Pellegrino\'s independent tax and accounting advisor, in connection with the tax analysis and coordination described in Section 3.2 above; and
> \(d\) Continental Fiduciary Services, Inc., the Escrow Agent, in connection with the preparation and execution of the funds flow memorandum and the mechanics of capital contribution funding.

This authorization is limited to disclosures that are reasonably necessary for the purposes described above and does not constitute a general waiver of Pellegrino\'s right to confidentiality. Calderwood & Harkness will use reasonable efforts to ensure that any such disclosures are made in a manner that preserves applicable privileges, including the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine, to the greatest extent practicable.
**[8. Document Retention]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will maintain all files, documents, correspondence, memoranda, work product, and other materials related to this engagement (collectively, \"Engagement Files\") in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy, as in effect from time to time. The Engagement Files will include both physical and electronic files.

Upon completion or termination of this engagement, the Firm will retain the Engagement Files for a period of not less than seven (7) years, or such longer period as may be required by applicable professional standards, rules, or regulations. After the expiration of the applicable retention period, and upon reasonable advance written notice to Pellegrino (which notice shall be directed to the last known address of the primary client contact), Calderwood & Harkness may destroy the Engagement Files in accordance with its standard retention and destruction procedures. Pellegrino may request the return or transfer of original documents at any time during the retention period, and the Firm will accommodate such requests within a reasonable time, subject to the Firm\'s right to retain copies for its own records and any applicable lien rights.
**[9. Termination]{.underline}**

Either party may terminate this engagement at any time, with or without cause, upon written notice to the other party. Calderwood & Harkness\'s right to terminate is subject to the Firm\'s professional obligations, including the duty to provide reasonable notice and to avoid prejudice to the client\'s interests, and to any applicable rules governing the withdrawal of counsel.

In the event of termination by either party, Pellegrino will remain responsible for the payment of all fees and expenses incurred by Calderwood & Harkness through the effective date of termination, and all outstanding invoices shall become due and payable upon termination.

Upon termination, Calderwood & Harkness will cooperate with Pellegrino in the orderly transition and transfer of the matter to successor counsel designated by Pellegrino, including the timely delivery of all Engagement Files, work product, and other materials in the Firm\'s possession that are necessary for successor counsel to continue the representation, subject to any applicable lien rights of the Firm and any applicable court rules or professional obligations. Pellegrino agrees to execute any authorizations or consents reasonably necessary to facilitate such transfer.
**[10. Governing Law]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Florida, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Engagement Letter or the services provided hereunder shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Miami-Dade County, Florida, and each party hereby consents to the personal jurisdiction of such courts.
**[11. Limitation of Liability]{.underline}**

To the fullest extent permitted by applicable law and the Florida Rules of Professional Conduct, Calderwood & Harkness\'s aggregate liability to Pellegrino arising out of or relating to the services provided under this engagement, whether based in contract, tort, negligence, breach of fiduciary duty, or otherwise, shall not exceed the total amount of fees actually paid by Pellegrino to Calderwood & Harkness under this Engagement Letter. This limitation of liability shall not apply to claims arising from the Firm\'s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud.

Pellegrino acknowledges that this limitation of liability has been negotiated at arm\'s length and reflects a reasonable allocation of risk between the parties in light of the fees charged for the services rendered. Nothing in this Section 11 shall be construed to limit any rights or remedies available to Pellegrino under the applicable Rules of Professional Conduct or other non-waivable provisions of applicable law.
**[12. Miscellaneous]{.underline}**

This Engagement Letter constitutes the entire agreement between Calderwood & Harkness and Pellegrino with respect to the terms and conditions of the engagement described herein and supersedes all prior or contemporaneous discussions, representations, and agreements, whether written or oral, relating to the subject matter hereof.

No amendment, modification, or waiver of any provision of this Engagement Letter shall be effective unless set forth in a writing signed by both Calderwood & Harkness and Pellegrino. No failure or delay by either party in exercising any right or remedy hereunder shall constitute a waiver thereof.

This matter has been assigned the internal reference number **1027-00002** within Calderwood & Harkness\'s matter management system. Pellegrino is requested to reference this matter number on all correspondence and communications directed to the Firm in connection with this engagement, including payment remittances, to ensure proper application and recordkeeping.

The provisions of Sections 5 (Fees and Billing), 7 (Confidentiality), 8 (Document Retention), 10 (Governing Law), and 11 (Limitation of Liability) shall survive the termination or completion of this engagement.
**[13. Acceptance]{.underline}**

If the foregoing terms are acceptable to Pellegrino, we respectfully request that Adriana Voss, in her capacity as Vice President & General Counsel of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC, sign and date this Engagement Letter in the space provided below and return one fully executed copy to the undersigned at your earliest convenience. A countersigned copy may be returned via email (PDF) to nstern@calderwoodharkness.com or via hand delivery or overnight courier to our office address set forth above.

We are genuinely enthusiastic about the opportunity to work with Pellegrino Capital Group and the broader PCG team on this co-investment alongside Ridgeline Fund IV. We are confident that our Funds & Asset Management Practice Group is well positioned to provide Pellegrino with the high-quality legal counsel and responsive client service that this transaction requires, and we look forward to a successful collaboration.
Please do not hesitate to contact me or Owen Fischer if you have any questions regarding this Engagement Letter or if you wish to discuss any of its provisions.
> Very truly yours,
> **CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP**
CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP

> 6\. **Choice of Law and Forum Selection.** While the Transaction Documents designate the laws of the State of Delaware as the governing law thereof, no assurance can be given that a court in any particular jurisdiction would honor such designation in all respects, particularly if the application of Delaware law would be contrary to a fundamental policy of a jurisdiction that has a materially greater interest in the determination of a particular issue. Similarly, any consent-to-jurisdiction or forum-selection provisions contained in the Transaction Documents may not be enforceable in all circumstances and are subject to the discretion of the court before which any such matter is presented, including considerations of convenience, fairness, and public policy.

> 7\. **Severability.** The enforceability of any severability provision contained in the Transaction Documents will depend upon the nature and extent of the provision or provisions held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, and the relationship of any such provision or provisions to the other provisions of the applicable Transaction Document and to the overall transaction. A court could decline to sever an unenforceable provision if the effect of severance would be to alter the fundamental nature of the bargain struck by the parties.

> 8\. **Penalty and Forfeiture Provisions.** Provisions of the Transaction Documents that may be characterized as penalties or forfeitures, including, without limitation, any provisions imposing default interest at rates exceeding commercially reasonable levels, late charges, or forfeiture, reduction, or reallocation of limited partnership interests upon a limited partner\'s failure to satisfy capital calls or otherwise comply with its funding obligations under the Partnership Agreement, may be unenforceable, in whole or in part, to the extent such provisions are deemed by a court of competent jurisdiction to constitute penalties under applicable law rather than reasonable estimates of actual damages or commercially reasonable remedies for breach.
**[VI. Reliance and Other Matters]{.underline}**

This opinion letter is furnished solely for the benefit of Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC, in its capacity as General Partner of the Partnership, and may not be relied upon by any other person or entity without our prior written consent. Notwithstanding the foregoing, this opinion letter may be relied upon by Ridgeline Equity Partners Fund IV, L.P. and Ridgeline Equity Management LLC in connection with the transactions contemplated by the Transaction Documents, without the necessity of any further consent by us; provided, however, that such reliance shall be subject to the same assumptions, qualifications, exceptions, limitations, and other terms set forth herein.

This opinion letter is rendered as of the date hereof, and we assume no obligation to update or supplement this opinion letter to reflect any facts or circumstances that may hereafter come to our attention or any changes in law (whether by legislative action, judicial decision, regulatory action, or otherwise) that may hereafter occur, even if such changes would affect the opinions expressed herein. In rendering this opinion letter, we have not undertaken any independent investigation of the factual matters upon which this opinion is based. 19: **[1. Purpose and Acceptance]{.underline}**
20: 
21: Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (\"Solara\" or \"SDILP\"), a Delaware limited partnership, and its general partner, Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (\"Solara GP\"), a Delaware limited liability company (collectively, the \"Client\"), to provide the legal services described in this engagement letter (this \"Letter\"). We appreciate the confidence that Solara and Solara GP have placed in our Firm, and we look forward to working with your team on this significant and complex matter.

23: This Letter sets forth the terms and conditions upon which Calderwood & Harkness will provide legal services in connection with the matter described herein. By countersigning this Letter in the space provided below, the Client agrees to be bound by the terms and conditions set forth herein. This engagement shall be effective as of the date of the countersignature below. No attorney-client relationship will be deemed to have been established with respect to the matter described herein until this Letter has been signed by an authorized representative of the Client and returned to the Firm.

25: **[2. Description of the Client]{.underline}**
26: 
27: The client for this engagement is Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (EIN: 82-4917366) and Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (EIN: 82-4917365). For the avoidance of doubt, the \"Client\" as used throughout this Letter refers collectively to SDILP and Solara GP, except where the context clearly requires otherwise.
28: 
29: Solara is a Delaware-based private equity sponsor with approximately \$14.7 billion in assets under management as of March 31, 2025, operating across digital infrastructure and enterprise SaaS verticals. Solara sponsors private equity funds through a series of parallel fund structures established across Delaware, the Cayman Islands, and Luxembourg to accommodate U.S. taxable, U.S. tax-exempt, and non-U.S. investor pools. The fund platform reflects a multi-jurisdictional architecture that is common among institutional-scale private equity sponsors and is central to the reorganization that is the subject of this engagement.
30: 
31: The principal contact persons at Solara for purposes of this engagement are as follows:
32: 
33: > • **Priya Narasimhan**, General Counsel --- primary legal contact and authorized decision-maker for engagement-related matters;
34: >
35: > • **Stefan Dalmqvist**, Head of Tax --- primary contact for substantive tax matters, financial data, and coordination with the Client\'s independent auditors and valuation advisors.
36: 
37: The Managing Partner and Founder of Solara is **Viktor Raines**. Mr. Raines will serve as the authorized officer of Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC for purposes of executing any penalties of perjury declarations and other representations required in connection with Internal Revenue Service (\"IRS\") submissions, as described more fully in Section 8 below.
38: 
39: All communications from the Firm regarding this engagement should be directed to Ms. Narasimhan and Mr. Dalmqvist, unless otherwise instructed in writing by the Client.
