41: **[3. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**
42: 
43: **3.1 Overview of the Transaction**
44: 
45: Solara is undertaking a cross-border reorganization of its fund platform (the \"Reorganization\"), involving the domestication and merger of several Cayman Islands and Luxembourg fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure. The Reorganization is designed to simplify the Client\'s fund architecture, reduce administrative and operational costs, enhance investor reporting, and achieve certain tax efficiencies in connection with the ongoing management and eventual disposition of portfolio company interests.
46: 
47: The Reorganization involves the following existing fund vehicles (collectively, the \"Legacy Fund Vehicles\"):
48: 
49: > \(i\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$4.2 billion in committed capital (vintage 2021), approximately 72% deployed as of the date hereof;
50: >
51: > \(ii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$1.85 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors;
52: >
53: > \(iii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.15 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.24 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for certain European institutional investors;
54: >
55: > \(iv\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$5.6 billion in committed capital (vintage 2023), approximately 38% deployed as of the date hereof;
56: >
57: > \(v\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$2.45 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors; and
58: >
59: > \(vi\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.38 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.49 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for certain European institutional investors.
60: 
61: The Reorganization contemplates the formation of the following new entities (collectively, the \"New Fund Vehicles\"):
62: 
63: > \(i\) **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership to serve as the master fund in a restructured master-feeder architecture;
64: >
65: > \(ii\) **Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC** --- a Delaware limited liability company to serve as the general partner of the Consolidated Master Fund;
66: >
67: > \(iii\) **Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to serve as the feeder vehicle for non-U.S. investors; and
68: >
69: > \(iv\) **Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to serve as the feeder vehicle for U.S. tax-exempt investors.
70: 
71: The Reorganization involves a multi-step transaction that includes, among other things, asset contributions by the four offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, the dissolution of the legacy offshore vehicles following such contributions, and the migration of existing limited partners into the appropriate new feeder structure. The target effective date for the completion of the Reorganization is December 1, 2025. The precise sequencing and mechanics of the multi-step transaction will be developed and refined in the course of the engagement, in consultation with the Client and its other advisors.
72: 
73: **3.2 Scope of Legal Services**
74: 
75: Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement is limited to the following specific legal services in connection with the Reorganization:
76: 
77: > \(a\) **Tax Analysis Memoranda.** Preparation of comprehensive tax analysis memoranda addressing the U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Reorganization under, among other provisions, Internal Revenue Code (\"IRC\") §§ 721(a), 721(b), 723, 731(a), 731(c), 704(c), 752, 367(a), 367(b), 1446, and 897, and Treasury Regulations § 301.7701-3. The tax analysis memoranda will address the characterization of each step of the multi-step Reorganization, including the contribution of assets by the offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, the treatment of assumed or shifted liabilities, the application of the anti-mixing bowl rules, and the withholding tax implications for non-U.S. limited partners.
78: >
79: > \(b\) **Private Letter Ruling Request.** Drafting, revising, and finalizing a private letter ruling request (the \"PLR Request\") to be submitted to the Internal Revenue Service\'s Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) (\"CC:INTL\"), with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries) (\"CC:PSI\"). The PLR Request will seek rulings on the specific tax consequences of the Reorganization that are identified in the course of the engagement as requiring advance IRS guidance for purposes of transaction certainty.
80: >
81: > \(c\) **Ancillary IRS Procedural Documents.** Preparation and filing of all ancillary IRS procedural documents required in connection with the PLR Request, including IRS Forms 2848 (Powers of Attorney and Declarations of Representative), penalties of perjury declarations, user fee transmittals, and pre-submission and supplemental correspondence with the IRS.
82: >
83: > \(d\) **Pre-Submission Conference.** Coordination and participation in a pre-submission conference with IRS CC:INTL (requested for July 22, 2025) and any follow-up communications arising therefrom. The pre-submission conference is intended to confirm the jurisdictional assignment of the PLR Request, identify any threshold legal issues, and facilitate an efficient review process following formal submission.
84: >
85: > \(e\) **Submission of PLR Request.** Submission of the PLR Request to the IRS at the following address: Internal Revenue Service, Attn: CC:INTL, 1111 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20224, together with all required enclosures, exhibits, and transmittal documents.
86: >

This includes attendance at any conferences or telephone calls requested by the IRS examining branch.

Proc. 2025-1 equivalent).

**[1. Purpose and Acceptance]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (\"Solara\" or \"SDILP\"), a Delaware limited partnership, and its general partner, Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (\"Solara GP\"), a Delaware limited liability company (collectively, the \"Client\"), to provide the legal services described in this engagement letter (this \"Letter\"). No attorney-client relationship will be deemed to have been established with respect to the matter described herein until this Letter has been signed by an authorized representative of the Client and returned to the Firm.
**[2. Description of the Client]{.underline}**

The client for this engagement is Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (EIN: 82-4917366) and Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (EIN: 82-4917365). For the avoidance of doubt, the \"Client\" as used throughout this Letter refers collectively to SDILP and Solara GP, except where the context clearly requires otherwise.

Solara is a Delaware-based private equity sponsor with approximately \$14.7 billion in assets under management as of March 31, 2025, operating across digital infrastructure and enterprise SaaS verticals. Solara sponsors private equity funds through a series of parallel fund structures established across Delaware, the Cayman Islands, and Luxembourg to accommodate U.S. taxable, U.S. tax-exempt, and non-U.S. investor pools. The fund platform reflects a multi-jurisdictional architecture that is common among institutional-scale private equity sponsors and is central to the reorganization that is the subject of this engagement.
The principal contact persons at Solara for purposes of this engagement are as follows:
> • **Priya Narasimhan**, General Counsel --- primary legal contact and authorized decision-maker for engagement-related matters;
> • **Stefan Dalmqvist**, Head of Tax --- primary contact for substantive tax matters, financial data, and coordination with the Client\'s independent auditors and valuation advisors.

The Managing Partner and Founder of Solara is **Viktor Raines**. Mr. Raines will serve as the authorized officer of Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC for purposes of executing any penalties of perjury declarations and other representations required in connection with Internal Revenue Service (\"IRS\") submissions, as described more fully in Section 8 below.
All communications from the Firm regarding this engagement should be directed to Ms. Narasimhan and Mr. Dalmqvist, unless otherwise instructed in writing by the Client.
**[3. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**
**3.1 Overview of the Transaction**

Solara is undertaking a cross-border reorganization of its fund platform (the \"Reorganization\"), involving the domestication and merger of several Cayman Islands and Luxembourg fund vehicles into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure. The Reorganization is designed to simplify the Client\'s fund architecture, reduce administrative and operational costs, enhance investor reporting, and achieve certain tax efficiencies in connection with the ongoing management and eventual disposition of portfolio company interests.
The Reorganization involves the following existing fund vehicles (collectively, the \"Legacy Fund Vehicles\"):

> \(i\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$4.2 billion in committed capital (vintage 2021), approximately 72% deployed as of the date hereof;

> \(ii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$1.85 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors;

> \(iii\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.15 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.24 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund IV for certain European institutional investors;

> \(iv\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership with approximately \$5.6 billion in committed capital (vintage 2023), approximately 38% deployed as of the date hereof;

> \(v\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-A (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership with approximately \$2.45 billion in committed capital, operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors; and

> \(vi\) **Solara Digital Partners Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** --- a Luxembourg special limited partnership (*société en commandite spéciale*) with approximately €1.38 billion in committed capital (approximately \$1.49 billion at an assumed exchange rate of 1.08 EUR/USD), operating as a parallel fund to Fund V for certain European institutional investors.
The Reorganization contemplates the formation of the following new entities (collectively, the \"New Fund Vehicles\"):
> \(i\) **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership to serve as the master fund in a restructured master-feeder architecture;
> \(ii\) **Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC** --- a Delaware limited liability company to serve as the general partner of the Consolidated Master Fund;
> \(iii\) **Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to serve as the feeder vehicle for non-U.S. investors; and
> \(iv\) **Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to serve as the feeder vehicle for U.S. tax-exempt investors.

The Reorganization involves a multi-step transaction that includes, among other things, asset contributions by the four offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, the dissolution of the legacy offshore vehicles following such contributions, and the migration of existing limited partners into the appropriate new feeder structure. The target effective date for the completion of the Reorganization is December 1, 2025. The precise sequencing and mechanics of the multi-step transaction will be developed and refined in the course of the engagement, in consultation with the Client and its other advisors.
**3.2 Scope of Legal Services**
Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement is limited to the following specific legal services in connection with the Reorganization:

> \(a\) **Tax Analysis Memoranda.** Preparation of comprehensive tax analysis memoranda addressing the U.S. federal income tax consequences of the Reorganization under, among other provisions, Internal Revenue Code (\"IRC\") §§ 721(a), 721(b), 723, 731(a), 731(c), 704(c), 752, 367(a), 367(b), 1446, and 897, and Treasury Regulations § 301.7701-3. The tax analysis memoranda will address the characterization of each step of the multi-step Reorganization, including the contribution of assets by the offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles to the Consolidated Master Fund, the treatment of assumed or shifted liabilities, the application of the anti-mixing bowl rules, and the withholding tax implications for non-U.S. limited partners.

> \(b\) **Private Letter Ruling Request.** Drafting, revising, and finalizing a private letter ruling request (the \"PLR Request\") to be submitted to the Internal Revenue Service\'s Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) (\"CC:INTL\"), with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries) (\"CC:PSI\"). The PLR Request will seek rulings on the specific tax consequences of the Reorganization that are identified in the course of the engagement as requiring advance IRS guidance for purposes of transaction certainty.

> \(c\) **Ancillary IRS Procedural Documents.** Preparation and filing of all ancillary IRS procedural documents required in connection with the PLR Request, including IRS Forms 2848 (Powers of Attorney and Declarations of Representative), penalties of perjury declarations, user fee transmittals, and pre-submission and supplemental correspondence with the IRS.

> \(d\) **Pre-Submission Conference.** Coordination and participation in a pre-submission conference with IRS CC:INTL (requested for July 22, 2025) and any follow-up communications arising therefrom. The pre-submission conference is intended to confirm the jurisdictional assignment of the PLR Request, identify any threshold legal issues, and facilitate an efficient review process following formal submission.

> \(e\) **Submission of PLR Request.** Submission of the PLR Request to the IRS at the following address: Internal Revenue Service, Attn: CC:INTL, 1111 Constitution Avenue NW, Washington, DC 20224, together with all required enclosures, exhibits, and transmittal documents.

> \(f\) **Post-Submission Monitoring.** Post-submission monitoring of the status of the PLR Request, preparation of responses to IRS information requests and additional questions, and supplemental submissions as necessary through issuance of the private letter ruling or closure of the matter by the IRS. This includes attendance at any conferences or telephone calls requested by the IRS examining branch.

> \(g\) **Coordination with Other Advisors.** Coordination with the Client\'s other advisors as described in Section 3.3 below, to the extent necessary for the preparation and prosecution of the PLR Request and associated tax analysis memoranda.

> \(h\) **Supporting Documentation.** Preparation of supporting documentation in connection with the Reorganization, including review of and comment on IRS Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) filings for the New Fund Vehicles and any related check-the-box elections.
**3.3 Coordination with Other Advisors**

Calderwood & Harkness will coordinate with, but does not assume responsibility for the work of, the following advisors that have been retained by Solara or its affiliates in connection with the Reorganization or related matters. Each of the following advisors has been engaged separately by the Client, and the Firm\'s coordination with such advisors is limited to the exchange of information and consultation necessary for Calderwood & Harkness to perform the services described in Section 3.2:

Redstone\'s valuation reports will be included as exhibits to the PLR Request.

> \(iii\) **Meridian Offshore Legal** (Caledonia House, 69 Dr. Roy\'s Drive, George Town, Grand Cayman KY1-1103; Fiona McAllister, Partner) --- Cayman Islands counsel advising on the formation of the New Fund Vehicles organized in the Cayman Islands, the dissolution of the Legacy Fund Vehicles organized in the Cayman Islands, and related regulatory matters involving the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (\"CIMA\").

> \(iv\) **Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l.** (22, boulevard Royal, L-2449 Luxembourg; Marc Gérard, Managing Partner) --- Luxembourg counsel advising on the dissolution of the Luxembourg SCSp vehicles and notification requirements to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (\"CSSF\").

> \(v\) **Clarendon Fund Services Ltd.** (Windward 3, Regatta Office Park, West Bay Road, George Town, Grand Cayman KY1-1108; Rachel Okonkwo, Client Relationship Director) --- fund administrator for the offshore Legacy Fund Vehicles, providing net asset value computations, investor registries, and other administrative data relevant to the Reorganization.

Calderwood & Harkness will rely upon the work product of the foregoing advisors to the extent necessary for the preparation of the PLR Request and associated tax analysis memoranda. However, the Firm assumes no responsibility for the accuracy, completeness, or timeliness of work product prepared by any such advisor, and the Firm\'s reliance on such work product will be subject to the Firm\'s independent professional judgment.
**3.4 Matters Excluded from Scope**
For the avoidance of doubt, this engagement does not include the following:

> \(a\) Legal advice on the laws of the Cayman Islands or Luxembourg, including corporate, partnership, regulatory, or tax law of those jurisdictions. Such matters are addressed by Meridian Offshore Legal and Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l., respectively, as described in Section 3.3 above.

> \(b\) Ongoing tax compliance for any fund vehicle, including preparation of federal, state, or local tax returns, Schedules K-1, FATCA reporting (including IRS Forms W-8BEN, W-8BEN-E, and W-8IMY), or Common Reporting Standard (\"CRS\") reporting.

> \(c\) Post-ruling implementation of the Reorganization, including without limitation the filing of formation documents, execution of contribution agreements, amendment and restatement of limited partnership agreements, or preparation or filing of dissolution documents, except to the extent specifically set forth in Section 3.2 above.

> \(d\) Legal advice to, or representation of, any individual limited partner of any Legacy Fund Vehicle or New Fund Vehicle, the LP Advisory Committee of any fund (including the Fund IV LP Advisory Committee and the Fund V LP Advisory Committee), or any counterparty to any transaction involving Solara or its affiliates.
> \(e\) State and local tax advice, including analysis of state income, franchise, or other tax consequences of the Reorganization in any U.S. state or local jurisdiction.

> \(f\) Investment advice or securities law analysis, including advice under the Securities Act of 1933, the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, the Investment Company Act of 1940, or any state \"blue sky\" laws.

If the Client wishes to expand the scope of this engagement to include any of the foregoing matters or any other matters not described in Section 3.2, the parties will enter into a separate engagement letter or written amendment to this Letter.

Calderwood & Harkness may, from time to time, engage additional attorneys or professional staff to assist with the matter as the needs of the engagement require. **[5. Fees and Billing]{.underline}**
**5.1 Hourly Rates**

Legal services rendered in connection with this engagement will be billed at a blended hourly rate of **\$1,175.00 per hour** for all engagement team members. The blended rate applies uniformly to all timekeepers assigned to the engagement, including partners, associates, counsel, and any other attorneys who may be assigned to the matter from time to time.

Calderwood & Harkness\'s standard billing rates are subject to annual adjustment, typically effective January 1 of each calendar year. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the blended rate of \$1,175.00 per hour will be maintained for the duration of this engagement and will not be adjusted unless otherwise agreed in writing by both Calderwood & Harkness and the Client.
**5.2 Estimated Fees**

Based on the scope of services described in Section 3, Calderwood & Harkness estimates that total legal fees for this engagement will be in the range of **\$1,800,000 to \$2,400,000**. This estimate reflects the Firm\'s current understanding of the complexity of the Reorganization, the anticipated number of issues to be addressed in the PLR Request, and the expected level of IRS engagement.

This estimate is provided for budgeting purposes only and does not constitute a cap, maximum, fixed fee, or guaranteed price. The matter will be billed on a time-and-materials basis, and the Client will be responsible for actual fees incurred regardless of whether they fall within the estimated range.

Actual fees may be higher or lower than the estimate depending on a number of factors, including but not limited to: the complexity of tax issues encountered during the course of the engagement; the number of drafts of the PLR Request and tax analysis memoranda required; the extent and nature of IRS engagement, including the number and duration of conferences, information requests, and supplemental submissions; any expansion of the scope of services; and the availability and completeness of financial and transactional data provided by the Client and its other advisors.

Calderwood & Harkness will provide quarterly budget-to-actual comparisons to the Client and will promptly advise the Client if fees are projected to exceed the estimated range. The Firm will work collaboratively with the Client to manage costs and to ensure that the Client is informed of budgetary developments on a timely basis.
**5.3 Fee Cap / Budget**

There is no fee cap on this engagement. As noted in Section 5.2, the matter is billed on a time-and-materials basis. Quarterly budget updates will be provided to the Client, and the Firm will promptly notify the Client of any material developments that are expected to result in fees significantly exceeding the estimated range.
**5.4 Disbursements and Expenses**

In addition to professional fees, the Client will be responsible for reimbursement of all reasonable disbursements and out-of-pocket expenses incurred by Calderwood & Harkness in connection with the engagement. Estimated total disbursements for the engagement are approximately **\$85,000**, and are expected to include the following categories:

> \(i\) **IRS User Fee:** \$38,000, payable in connection with the submission of the PLR Request. This amount reflects the current schedule of user fees applicable to ruling requests involving multiple entities with combined assets exceeding \$50 million, as set forth in the IRS\'s annual revenue procedure governing letter ruling requests (Rev. Proc. 2025-1 equivalent).

> \(ii\) **Travel Expenses:** Reasonable travel expenses for the pre-submission conference with IRS CC:INTL in Washington, D.C. (scheduled for July 22, 2025) and any subsequent IRS meetings or conferences, including airfare, hotel, ground transportation, and meals.
> \(iii\) **Courier and Filing Costs:** Sundial Data Systems, courier, and filing costs associated with the submission of the PLR Request and related documents to the IRS.

> \(iv\) **Document Reproduction:** Costs of copying, printing, and binding the PLR Request and exhibits for submission to the IRS, including production of multiple copies as required by IRS procedures.
> \(v\) **Electronic Research:** Costs of electronic legal research (e.g., Westmark Data Systems, Tidewater Technologies, Sundial Solutions) incurred in connection with the engagement.

All disbursements will be billed at cost without markup. The Firm will exercise reasonable judgment in incurring disbursements and will seek the Client\'s prior approval for any individual disbursement exceeding \$5,000 (other than the IRS user fee).
**5.5 Billing Cycle and Payment Terms**
Invoices for professional fees and disbursements will be rendered on a **monthly** basis, typically within fifteen (15) business days following the close of each calendar month.

Payment is due within **thirty (30) days** of the date of each invoice (net 30 days). Late payments may be subject to interest at the rate of 1.0% per month (12.0% per annum) on the outstanding balance, to the extent permitted by applicable law.

Each invoice will include detailed time entries reflecting the date of service, the name of the timekeeper, the number of hours billed, a narrative description of the services rendered, and the applicable hourly rate. Disbursements will be itemized separately.
All inquiries regarding invoices, billing, or payment should be directed to **Sylvia Hartwell** at (212) 554-8142 or shartwell@calderwoodharkness.com.
**[6. Matter Identification]{.underline}**

This engagement has been assigned Calderwood & Harkness matter number **20250527-SDILP-PLR**. All time entries, correspondence, work product, and billing will be recorded under this matter number. The Client should reference this matter number in all communications with the Firm regarding this engagement.

The matter has been opened in the Firm\'s records as of May 27, 2025. The administrative opening date reflects the Firm\'s internal processing timeline and does not alter the effective date of this engagement, which is as set forth in Section 1 above.
**[7. Key Milestones and Timeline]{.underline}**
The following target milestones have been identified for the engagement in consultation with the Client:
**Target Date**                     **Milestone**
June 16, 2025                       Completion of initial comprehensive tax analysis memorandum
July 1, 2025                        Circulation of draft PLR Request (Version 1.0) to Client for review
July 15, 2025                       LPAC review of final PLR Request draft
July 22, 2025                       Pre-submission conference with IRS CC:INTL Branch 1
August 15, 2025                     Submission of PLR Request to IRS

The foregoing dates are targets and are subject to change based on the progress of the engagement, the availability of financial and transactional data from the Client and its advisors, and the IRS\'s scheduling of the pre-submission conference. Calderwood & Harkness will use commercially reasonable efforts to adhere to the timeline set forth above and will promptly advise the Client of any anticipated delays.

Post-submission milestones relating to entity formation, execution of transactional documents, and the implementation of the Reorganization steps are outside the primary scope of this engagement but will be coordinated with the Client as necessary. For reference, the Client has identified the following additional target dates: formation of the New Fund Vehicles (September 15, 2025) and the Step 5 effective date for completion of the Reorganization (December 1, 2025).
**[8. IRS Procedural Matters]{.underline}**

The PLR Request will be submitted to the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) (\"CC:INTL\") of the Internal Revenue Service, with secondary jurisdiction in the Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (Passthroughs & Special Industries) (\"CC:PSI\"). The jurisdictional assignment reflects the cross-border nature of the Reorganization and the involvement of both international tax provisions (including IRC §§ 367(a), 367(b), 1446, and 897) and partnership tax provisions (including IRC §§ 721, 723, 731, 704(c), and 752).

A pre-submission conference with IRS CC:INTL has been requested for **July 22, 2025**. The purpose of the pre-submission conference is to discuss the proposed PLR Request in general terms, confirm the jurisdictional assignment, identify any threshold legal or procedural issues, and facilitate an efficient post-submission review process. Mr. Cross and Mr. Jansen will attend the pre-submission conference on behalf of the Client.

IRS Forms 2848 (Power of Attorney and Declaration of Representative) will be filed with the IRS designating **Leonard Cross** and **Sylvia Hartwell** as authorized representatives for Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (EIN: 82-4917366), Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (EIN: 82-4917365), and all related fund entities involved in the Reorganization. The Client will be asked to execute the Forms 2848 in advance of the pre-submission conference.

A penalties of perjury statement, as required by Rev. Proc. 2025-1 (or its equivalent) for submission of the PLR Request, will be required to be signed by **Viktor Raines** in his capacity as an authorized officer of Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC, the general partner of Solara Digital Infrastructure LP. Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the penalties of perjury statement and circulate it to the Client for execution prior to the submission date.

The IRS user fee of **\$38,000** will be submitted with the PLR Request by check or wire transfer payable to the United States Treasury. Calderwood & Harkness will advance this fee on behalf of the Client and will include it as a disbursement on the next monthly invoice following submission. The Client will be responsible for reimbursing the Firm for this amount in accordance with the payment terms set forth in Section 5.5.
**[9. Confidentiality and Attorney-Client Privilege]{.underline}**

All communications between Calderwood & Harkness and the Client in connection with this engagement are intended to be privileged and confidential, protected by the attorney-client privilege, the work product doctrine, and any other applicable evidentiary or testimonial privileges. The Firm will take reasonable steps to maintain the confidentiality and privileged nature of all such communications and work product.

The Client agrees to maintain the confidentiality of all work product, memoranda, draft documents, analyses, and communications provided by Calderwood & Harkness in connection with this engagement. The Client should not disclose or disseminate such materials to any third party without first consulting with the engagement team regarding the potential impact on applicable privileges.

Disclosure of privileged or confidential materials to the Client\'s other advisors identified in Section 3.3 --- namely, Caldwell Pierce & Co. LLP, Redstone Advisory Group LLC, Meridian Offshore Legal, Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l., and Clarendon Fund Services Ltd. --- may be appropriate in certain circumstances to facilitate the engagement. However, such disclosures should be coordinated with **Leonard Cross** in advance to ensure that applicable privileges are preserved and that appropriate common interest, joint defense, or other protective arrangements are in place where necessary.

Similarly, any disclosure of engagement materials to the LP Advisory Committee\'s independent counsel, **Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP** (200 South Biscayne Boulevard, Suite 4000, Miami, FL 33131; Diana Carruthers, Partner), should be coordinated with the engagement team. The LP Advisory Committee\'s counsel represents the interests of the advisory committee members and not the Client, and disclosures to such counsel may implicate separate privilege considerations.

Communications with independent tax counsel retained by individual limited partners --- for example, **Bramhall & Quelwick LLP** (44 Montgomery Street, Suite 3600, San Francisco, CA 94104; Jason Tremaine, Partner), which has been retained by Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund --- will be subject to separate privilege considerations. The Client should coordinate with the engagement team before sharing any Calderwood & Harkness work product or privileged communications with any limited partner\'s independent counsel to ensure that the Client\'s privileges are not inadvertently waived.
**[10. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness has conducted a conflicts check in accordance with the Firm\'s standard procedures and the applicable New York Rules of Professional Conduct. Based on the information provided by the Client, including the identities of the Legacy Fund Vehicles, the New Fund Vehicles, the engagement team members, and the Client\'s other advisors, no disqualifying conflicts of interest have been identified with respect to this engagement.

Calderwood & Harkness does not currently represent any party adverse to Solara, Solara GP, or any of the Legacy Fund Vehicles or New Fund Vehicles in any matter related to the Reorganization or in any other matter that would create a material conflict of interest under applicable professional responsibility rules.

The Firm\'s conflicts check is based on the information provided by the Client as of the date of this Letter. If a conflict of interest arises during the course of the engagement --- whether as a result of new information, changes in the Firm\'s client base, or other developments --- Calderwood & Harkness will promptly notify the Client and, if necessary, seek an appropriate informed consent waiver or withdraw from the engagement in whole or in part, in accordance with the applicable rules of professional conduct. The Client agrees to cooperate with the Firm in identifying and resolving any potential conflicts that may arise.
**[11. Document Retention]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness will retain engagement files in accordance with its standard document retention policies, which are consistent with the Firm\'s obligations under applicable rules of professional conduct and any other legal requirements. Engagement files may include correspondence, memoranda, drafts, research materials, billing records, and other documents created or received in connection with the engagement.

Upon conclusion of the engagement, the Client may request the return or delivery of original documents provided to the Firm by the Client. Copies of work product prepared by Calderwood & Harkness will be retained by the Firm for a period consistent with the Firm\'s professional obligations. The Firm reserves the right to destroy engagement files after the expiration of the applicable retention period, subject to any legal hold or preservation obligation then in effect.
**[12. Limitation of Engagement]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness\'s representation in this engagement is limited to the specific scope described in Section 3 of this Letter. The Firm does not, by virtue of this engagement, undertake to represent the Client in any other matter, nor does the Firm assume any obligation to advise the Client on developments in law or regulation outside the scope of this engagement.

Calderwood & Harkness does not represent any individual partner, officer, director, manager, or employee of Solara, Solara GP, or any of the Legacy Fund Vehicles or New Fund Vehicles in their personal capacity. Any such individual who requires personal legal advice in connection with the Reorganization or otherwise should retain independent counsel.

Calderwood & Harkness does not represent, and will not provide legal advice to, any limited partner of any fund vehicle, including without limitation the following institutional investors: Pinnacle State Employees\' Retirement System, Grandview University Endowment, Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund, Kestrel Pacific Insurance Group, Argyle Family Office Holdings LLC, or any other limited partner or investor in any Legacy Fund Vehicle or New Fund Vehicle. Each such limited partner should consult its own legal, tax, and financial advisors regarding the Reorganization and its impact on such limited partner\'s investment.

Calderwood & Harkness does not represent any lender, credit facility party, or other financing source, including without limitation Ashford National Bank, N.A. or Sentinel Capital Markets LLC, in connection with this engagement or any related matter.

This engagement does not include advice on insurance coverage matters. The Client has advised Calderwood & Harkness that Solara maintains directors\' and officers\' / errors and omissions liability insurance coverage with an aggregate limit of \$50 million, placed with Hawkstone Specialty Insurance Co. Analysis of such coverage, or any other insurance matters, is outside the scope of this engagement.
**[13. Termination]{.underline}**

Either party may terminate this engagement at any time upon written notice to the other party. Termination by the Client shall be effective upon receipt of written notice by Calderwood & Harkness. Termination by the Firm shall be effective upon reasonable notice to the Client, taking into account the status of any pending IRS submission or correspondence and the need to protect the Client\'s interests during any transition period.

Upon termination, the Client will remain responsible for payment of all fees incurred and disbursements advanced through the date of termination, in accordance with the billing and payment terms set forth in Section 5. Calderwood & Harkness will render a final invoice within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination.

In the event of termination while IRS proceedings are pending, Calderwood & Harkness will take reasonable steps to protect the Client\'s interests, including providing the Client with copies of all pending submissions and correspondence, notifying the IRS of the change in representation as required by applicable procedures, and cooperating with successor counsel to facilitate an orderly transition.
**[14. Governing Law]{.underline}**

This engagement letter shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Letter or the engagement described herein shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the State of New York located in the County of New York or the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York.
**[15. Entire Agreement]{.underline}**

This Letter constitutes the entire agreement between Calderwood & Harkness LLP and Solara Digital Infrastructure LP (together with Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC) with respect to the engagement described herein and supersedes all prior negotiations, representations, warranties, commitments, offers, and agreements (whether oral or written) relating to the subject matter hereof.

Any amendment, modification, or supplement to this Letter must be in writing and signed by both Calderwood & Harkness and the Client. No waiver of any provision of this Letter shall be effective unless set forth in a writing signed by the party against whom enforcement is sought.

We look forward to working with you and your team on this important matter. We believe Calderwood & Harkness is well positioned to deliver the high-quality, efficient legal services that Solara requires in connection with the Reorganization, and we are committed to achieving a successful outcome for the Client.
If the foregoing accurately reflects your understanding of our engagement, please sign and return a copy of this letter to the undersigned at your earliest convenience.
> Very truly yours,
CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP

83: # V. Tax Treatment — Overview of Rulings Requested

94: # Ruling 1: IRC § 721(a) — Tax-Free Contributions
95: Each offshore vehicle contributes its entire portfolio to Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP in exchange for a limited partnership interest
96: Under IRC § 721(a), no gain or loss is recognized by the contributing partnerships or their partners on the contribution of property to a partnership
97: Carryover basis under IRC § 723 — Master Fund takes the same tax basis as the contributing vehicle
98: Holding period of contributed assets tacks under IRC § 1223(2)
99: No cash boot or other consideration beyond partnership interests

101: <!-- Slide number: 12 -->
102: # Ruling 2: IRC § 721(b) — Not an Investment Company
103: IRC § 721(b) denies tax-free treatment if the contribution results in 'diversification' and the partnership is an 'investment company'
104: Treas. Reg. § 1.351-1(c)(1)(ii) defines 'investment company' by reference to holdings of 'stocks, securities, or other investment assets'
105: Solara's portfolio consists entirely of operating company interests — digital infrastructure and enterprise SaaS platforms
106: All 23 portfolio companies are active operating businesses, not passive investment assets
107: Conclusion: § 721(b) exception does not apply; contributions remain tax-free

110: # Rulings 3–4: § 367 Inapplicability & § 731 Distributions

112: Ruling 4 (§ 731): Distributions by legacy vehicles of Master Fund LP interests to LPs in Step 5 are tax-free under § 731(a) — no gain recognized because LPs receive only partnership interests, not money
113: IRC § 731(c) marketable securities exception does not apply — Master Fund LP interests are not 'marketable securities' as they are not actively traded or readily tradable on a secondary market

118: Netting under Treas. Reg. § 1.752-1(f) and tiered partnership rules applied to demonstrate no net gain recognition under § 731
119: Ruling 6 (§ 704(c)): $1.72B in built-in gain accounts carry over from legacy vehicles to Master Fund LP
120: Master Fund LP will continue to use the remedial allocation method under Treas. Reg. § 1.704-3(d) for each contributed property
121: Ensures historic investors continue to bear their appropriate share of built-in gain on eventual disposition

# Solara Digital Infrastructure LP — Cross-Border Fund-Platform Reorganization
Presentation to the LP Advisory Committee
Prepared by Calderwood & Harkness LLP
CONFIDENTIAL — Attorney-Client Privileged
Date: For LPAC Review — July 15, 2025
<!-- Slide number: 2 -->
# Agenda
I. Executive Summary & Business Rationale
II. Current Fund Platform Structure
III. Proposed Post-Reorganization Structure
IV. Five-Step Transaction Overview
V. Tax Treatment — Summary of Rulings Requested
VI. Key Financial Data
VII. Impact by Investor Category
VIII. Third-Party Consents & Coordination
IX. Timeline & Key Milestones
X. LP Consent Requirements & Next Steps
<!-- Slide number: 3 -->
# I. Executive Summary
Solara Digital Infrastructure LP ($14.7 billion AUM as of March 31, 2025) proposes to consolidate its cross-border fund platform
Four offshore parallel fund vehicles (two Cayman, two Luxembourg) to be reorganized into a single Delaware-domiciled master fund structure with Cayman feeder vehicles
Transaction designed to qualify as tax-free under IRC §§ 721 and 731
Private letter ruling request to be submitted to IRS Office of the Associate Chief Counsel (International) — target August 15, 2025
Target effective date: December 1, 2025
<!-- Slide number: 4 -->
# Business Rationale for the Reorganization
Operational Cost Reduction: Elimination of approximately $3.8 million in annual duplicative offshore administration, audit, and regulatory fees
OECD Pillar Two GloBE Rules: Forthcoming Pillar Two rules effective for Luxembourg entities from FY 2025 diminish the benefits of the Luxembourg SCSp structures
FATCA/CRS Compliance Simplification: Consolidated reporting reduces complexity and compliance risk across multiple jurisdictions
Governance Simplification: LP-requested streamlining of parallel fund governance, voting, and reporting across multiple vehicles
<!-- Slide number: 5 -->
# II. Current Fund Platform Structure
Fund IV Family (Vintage 2021; 72% deployed):
— Solara Digital Partners Fund IV LP (Delaware) — $4.2B — U.S. taxable investors
— Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP — $1.85B — Non-U.S. and U.S. tax-exempt investors
— Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp — €1.15B ($1.24B) — Non-U.S. investors (treaty access)
Fund V Family (Vintage 2023; 38% deployed):
— Solara Digital Partners Fund V LP (Delaware) — $5.6B — U.S. taxable investors
— Fund V-A (Cayman) LP — $2.45B — Non-U.S. and U.S. tax-exempt investors
— Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp — €1.38B ($1.49B) — Non-U.S. investors (treaty access)
Three GP entities: Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC (DE), Solara Offshore GP Ltd. (Cayman), Solara Luxembourg Management S.à r.l. (Luxembourg)
<!-- Slide number: 6 -->
# Representative Investor Base
U.S. Tax-Exempt: Pinnacle State Employees' Retirement System ($275M Fund IV / $340M Fund V); Grandview University Endowment ($120M Fund IV / $185M Fund V)
Non-U.S. Sovereign: Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund ($380M Fund IV-A Cayman / $500M Fund V-A Cayman)
Non-U.S. Insurance: Kestrel Pacific Insurance Group (€200M Fund IV-B Lux / €275M Fund V-B Lux)
U.S. Taxable: Argyle Family Office Holdings LLC ($95M Fund IV / $130M Fund V)
Each category has distinct tax sensitivities driving post-reorganization feeder/direct investment channel
<!-- Slide number: 7 -->
# III. Proposed Post-Reorganization Structure
Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP (Delaware) — new master fund consolidating all offshore vehicle assets
— GP: Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC (Delaware)
Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP — feeder for non-U.S. investors investing into the Master Fund
Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP — feeder for U.S. tax-exempt investors (pensions, endowments) to mitigate UBTI concerns
Fund IV LP and Fund V LP (Delaware) — remain as-is; U.S. taxable investors continue to invest directly alongside the Master Fund
All new entities to elect partnership classification via IRS Form 8832 (check-the-box)
<!-- Slide number: 8 -->
# IV. Five-Step Transaction Overview
Step 1 — Formation of New Entities (Sept. 15, 2025): Form Master Fund GP LLC, Master Fund LP, International Feeder, Tax-Exempt Feeder; file Form 8832 elections
Step 2 — Contribution of Fund IV-A Cayman Assets (Oct. 1, 2025): All portfolio assets (FMV $2.31B; basis $1.62B; BIG $690M) contributed to Master Fund LP
Step 3 — Contribution of Fund IV-B Luxembourg Assets (Oct. 15, 2025): All portfolio assets (FMV $1.16B; basis $844.6M; BIG $311M) contributed to Master Fund LP
Step 4 — Contribution of Fund V Offshore Assets (Nov. 1, 2025): Fund V-A Cayman (FMV $2.89B; BIG $550M) and Fund V-B Lux (FMV $1.39B; BIG $162M) contributed to Master Fund LP

Step 5 — Dissolution & LP Migration (Dec. 1, 2025): Legacy vehicles dissolve; Master Fund LP interests distributed to LPs; non-U.S. LPs roll into International Feeder; U.S. tax-exempt LPs roll into Tax-Exempt Feeder
<!-- Slide number: 9 -->
# Aggregate Financial Summary of the Reorganization
Total FMV of assets transferred to Consolidated Master Fund: $7.75 billion
Total adjusted tax basis: $6.03 billion
Total aggregate built-in gain: $1.72 billion
Aggregate liabilities assumed by Master Fund: $1.34 billion (subject to § 752 analysis)
Total portfolio companies across all funds: 23 (11 in Fund IV vehicles; 12 in Fund V vehicles)
EUR/USD exchange rate applied uniformly: 1.08
<!-- Slide number: 10 -->
# V. Tax Treatment — Overview of Rulings Requested
Ruling 1 (§ 721): Tax-free contributions of portfolio assets to Master Fund LP — no gain/loss recognized
Ruling 2 (§ 721(b)): Master Fund LP does not constitute an 'investment company' (operating company portfolio)
Ruling 3 (§ 367): §§ 367(a)/(b) do not apply — provisions apply only to transfers to/from corporations, not partnerships
Ruling 4 (§ 731): Tax-free distributions of Master Fund LP interests to LPs upon dissolution of legacy vehicles
Ruling 5 (§ 752): Liability shifts do not trigger gain recognition under § 731 after netting analysis
Ruling 6 (§ 704(c)): Built-in gain/loss accounts carry over; remedial allocation method continues
Ruling 7 (§ 1446): No withholding required on contributions or distributions (nonrecognition transactions)
Ruling 8 (Entity Classification): All new entities properly classified as partnerships under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3
<!-- Slide number: 11 -->
# Ruling 1: IRC § 721(a) — Tax-Free Contributions
Each offshore vehicle contributes its entire portfolio to Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP in exchange for a limited partnership interest
Under IRC § 721(a), no gain or loss is recognized by the contributing partnerships or their partners on the contribution of property to a partnership
Carryover basis under IRC § 723 — Master Fund takes the same tax basis as the contributing vehicle
Holding period of contributed assets tacks under IRC § 1223(2)
No cash boot or other consideration beyond partnership interests
<!-- Slide number: 12 -->
# Ruling 2: IRC § 721(b) — Not an Investment Company
IRC § 721(b) denies tax-free treatment if the contribution results in 'diversification' and the partnership is an 'investment company'
Treas. Reg. § 1.351-1(c)(1)(ii) defines 'investment company' by reference to holdings of 'stocks, securities, or other investment assets'
Solara's portfolio consists entirely of operating company interests — digital infrastructure and enterprise SaaS platforms
All 23 portfolio companies are active operating businesses, not passive investment assets
Conclusion: § 721(b) exception does not apply; contributions remain tax-free
<!-- Slide number: 13 -->
# Rulings 3–4: § 367 Inapplicability & § 731 Distributions
Ruling 3 (§ 367): IRC §§ 367(a) and 367(b) by their terms apply only to transfers to or from corporations — the Master Fund LP is a partnership; § 367 does not apply

Ruling 4 (§ 731): Distributions by legacy vehicles of Master Fund LP interests to LPs in Step 5 are tax-free under § 731(a) — no gain recognized because LPs receive only partnership interests, not money
IRC § 731(c) marketable securities exception does not apply — Master Fund LP interests are not 'marketable securities' as they are not actively traded or readily tradable on a secondary market
<!-- Slide number: 14 -->
# Rulings 5–6: Liability Shifts (§ 752) & Built-In Gain Carryover (§ 704(c))
Ruling 5 (§ 752): $1.34B in aggregate liabilities shift from legacy vehicles to Master Fund LP — §§ 752(a)/(b) create deemed contributions and distributions as partner shares change
Netting under Treas. Reg. § 1.752-1(f) and tiered partnership rules applied to demonstrate no net gain recognition under § 731
Ruling 6 (§ 704(c)): $1.72B in built-in gain accounts carry over from legacy vehicles to Master Fund LP
Master Fund LP will continue to use the remedial allocation method under Treas. Reg. § 1.704-3(d) for each contributed property
Ensures historic investors continue to bear their appropriate share of built-in gain on eventual disposition
<!-- Slide number: 15 -->
# Rulings 7–8: Withholding (§ 1446) & Entity Classification
Ruling 7 (§ 1446): No withholding on Steps 2–4 contributions or Step 5 distributions — nonrecognition events generate no effectively connected taxable income
Particularly relevant for non-U.S. investors (Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund, Kestrel Pacific Insurance Group)
Ruling 8 (Entity Classification): Master Fund LP, International Feeder, and Tax-Exempt Feeder each properly classified as partnerships under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3 via check-the-box elections
Form 8832 elections to be filed for each new entity with effective dates coordinated to precede the first contribution step
<!-- Slide number: 16 -->
# VI. Key Financial Data — Portfolio Company Highlights
NovaBright Data Systems Inc. (DE corp) — Data center operator — FMV $890M / Basis $520M / BIG $370M — Fund IV-A Cayman 60%, Fund IV LP 40%
Veridian Edge Computing Corp. (DE corp) — Edge computing infra — FMV $1.12B / Basis $780M / BIG $340M — Fund V-A Cayman 55%, Fund V LP 45%
Thorngate Fiber Networks LP (DE LP) — Fiber-optic networks — FMV $670M / Basis $490M / BIG $180M — Fund IV-A Cayman 100%
Crestline Cloud Solutions LLC (DE LLC, disregarded) — SaaS platform — FMV €340M ($367M) / Basis €195M ($211M) / BIG $156M — Fund IV-B Lux 100%
Helix SaaS Holdings Ltd. (Cayman exempted co.) — SaaS holding — FMV $445M / Basis $310M / BIG $135M — Fund V-A Cayman 100%
Plus 18 additional portfolio companies across Fund IV and Fund V vehicles
<!-- Slide number: 17 -->
# VII. Impact by Investor Category
U.S. Taxable Investors (e.g., Argyle Family Office): No change — remain directly in Fund IV LP and Fund V LP; co-invest alongside Master Fund
U.S. Tax-Exempt Investors (e.g., Pinnacle SERS, Grandview Endowment): Migrate from Cayman parallel vehicles to Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP → Master Fund; UBTI blocker benefits preserved
Non-U.S. Investors — Cayman (e.g., Nordhaven SWF): Migrate from Fund IV-A/V-A Cayman to International Feeder (Cayman) LP → Master Fund; no U.S. withholding on reorganization steps

Non-U.S. Investors — Luxembourg (e.g., Kestrel Pacific): Migrate from Fund IV-B/V-B Lux to International Feeder (Cayman) LP → Master Fund; Luxembourg SCSps dissolved; no Luxembourg capital gains tax expected
All categories: No gain recognition anticipated; built-in gain accounts carry over; tax attributes preserved
<!-- Slide number: 18 -->
# VIII. Third-Party Consents & Coordination

Lender Consents: Ashford National Bank, N.A. — Fund IV subscription facility ($1.1B) and Fund V subscription facility ($1.5B); Sentinel Capital Markets LLC — co-lender/administrative agent on Fund V facility
Insurance: Hawkstone Specialty Insurance Co. — endorsement of $50M D&O/E&O policies to cover new entities
Fund Administrator: Clarendon Fund Services Ltd. — transition of NAV calculation and investor reporting to Master Fund structure
Cayman Counsel: Meridian Offshore Legal (Fiona McAllister) — formation of new Cayman feeders; CIMA deregistration of Fund IV-A (MF-72491) and Fund V-A (MF-89103)
Luxembourg Counsel: Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l. (Marc Gérard) — dissolution of Fund IV-B SCSp (RCS B 248193) and Fund V-B SCSp (RCS B 271056); CSSF notification
Accounting: Caldwell Pierce & Co. LLP — financial data and tax compliance support for PLR submission
<!-- Slide number: 19 -->
# IX. Timeline & Key Milestones
March 14, 2025 — GP board approval of reorganization exploration
April 22, 2025 — LPAC meeting; preliminary consent obtained (78% in interest)
May 12, 2025 — Calderwood & Harkness engagement letter executed
June 16, 2025 — Initial tax analysis memorandum completed
July 1, 2025 — Draft PLR request circulated to Solara
July 15, 2025 — LPAC review of final PLR request
July 22, 2025 — Pre-submission conference with IRS CC:INTL Branch 1
August 15, 2025 — PLR request submitted to IRS
September 15, 2025 — Formation of new entities; Form 8832 elections filed
October 1, 2025 — Step 2: Fund IV-A Cayman contribution to Master Fund
October 15, 2025 — Step 3: Fund IV-B Luxembourg contribution to Master Fund
November 1, 2025 — Step 4: Fund V-A Cayman and Fund V-B Luxembourg contributions
December 1, 2025 — Step 5: Dissolution of legacy vehicles; LP migration (target effective date)
<!-- Slide number: 20 -->
# X. LP Consent Requirements & Next Steps
Formal LP consent required under LPA amendment provisions for Fund IV and Fund V (and all parallel vehicles)
Preliminary consent of 78% in interest obtained at April 22, 2025 LPAC meeting — formal solicitation to follow
LP Consent Solicitation Letter and Form of LP Consent to be distributed to all LPs
Draft Amendments to Fund IV LPA and Fund V LPA to authorize asset contributions and formation of new entities
LP Tax Impact Summary Letter to be provided to all LPs — each LP encouraged to consult its own tax advisors
LPAC counsel (Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP) reviewing PLR Draft v3.0 — comments due July 15, 2025
<!-- Slide number: 21 -->
# Key Advisors & Contacts
U.S. Tax Counsel: Calderwood & Harkness LLP — Leonard Cross (Responsible Partner), Sylvia Hartwell (Billing Partner), Robert Jansen (Lead Associate), Garrett Simmons (Working Associate)
LPAC Counsel: Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP — Diana Carruthers (Partner)
Nordhaven SWF Independent Tax Counsel: Bramhall & Quelwick LLP — Jason Tremaine (Partner)

Luxembourg Counsel: Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l. — Marc Gérard (Managing Partner)

Solara Contacts: Viktor Raines (Managing Partner), Priya Narasimhan (GC), Stefan Dalmqvist (Head of Tax), Douglas Wexford (CFO), Meredith Tsao (COO)
<!-- Slide number: 22 -->
# Appendix: Key Tax Code Provisions Referenced

21: Dear Mr. Aldren:
22: 
23: **[1. Introduction and Engagement]{.underline}**
24: 
25: We are pleased to confirm that Pinnacle Capital Management LLC (\"Pinnacle Mgmt\" or the \"Client\"), a limited liability company organized under the laws of the State of Delaware (EIN 82-6140538), in its capacity as the management company of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP (\"Fund II\"), has engaged Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") to serve as tax structuring counsel in connection with the proposed formation, capitalization, and closing of Pinnacle Continuation Vehicle LP (the \"CV\" or \"PCV\").
26: 
27: As we understand it, this engagement arises in connection with a GP-led secondary transaction in which Fund II will contribute its portfolio of three software and software-as-a-service investments --- Luminos Systems Inc., ClearArc Software Inc., and Vectral Cloud Inc. --- with an aggregate fair market value of approximately \$1.34 billion (based on independent valuations as of June 30, 2025) to the CV. The transaction is designed to provide liquidity to existing limited partners electing to cash out, while permitting rolling limited partners and new secondary investors to participate in the continued growth of these portfolio companies through a newly formed continuation vehicle structure.
28: 
29: We understand that the general partner entity for Fund II is Pinnacle Capital Partners II LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (EIN 84-3291104), and that the proposed general partner entity for the CV is Pinnacle CV Partners LLC, which is to be formed as a Delaware limited liability company in connection with the CV transaction.
30: 
31: This letter (this \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions of our engagement, including the scope of services to be provided, the personnel assigned to the matter, our fee arrangements, the responsibilities of the Client, and other important terms governing the attorney-client relationship between C&H and Pinnacle Mgmt. We ask that you review this letter carefully and, if it accurately reflects our mutual understanding, execute and return a copy to us in accordance with the instructions set forth in Section 13 below.
32: 
33: **[2. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**
34: 
35: **2.1 Tax Structuring Services**
36: 
37: C&H will provide U.S. federal income tax structuring advice, and where specifically indicated below, state-level income tax structuring advice, in connection with the CV transaction. The scope of our tax structuring services will specifically include the following work streams:
38: 
39: **(a) Entity Selection and Formation Advice.** C&H will advise on the selection of entity type for the CV, which is proposed to be formed as a Delaware limited partnership, and for the general partner entity, Pinnacle CV Partners LLC, which is proposed to be formed as a Delaware limited liability company classified as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes. In addition, C&H will advise on the formation and tax classification of blocker entities to be used in the CV structure, specifically: (i) PCV Domestic blocker Inc., which is proposed to be organized as a Delaware C-corporation, and (ii) PCV International Holdings Ltd., which is proposed to be organized as a Cayman Islands exempted company. Our advice will address the tax implications of each entity\'s classification, the interposition of blocker vehicles in the investment structure, and the tax elections and filings necessary to achieve the intended tax treatment of each entity.
40: 
41: **(b) Section 721 Contribution Mechanics.** C&H will analyze and advise on the structuring of the contribution of Fund II\'s portfolio company interests to the CV as a tax-free contribution under Section 721 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\"). Section 721 generally provides that no gain or loss is recognized to a partnership or any of its partners upon a contribution of property to the partnership in exchange for a partnership interest. Our analysis will address the application of Section 721 to the specific facts of the contribution, including whether the requirements for non-recognition treatment are satisfied and whether any exceptions to Section 721 (including contributions to investment companies under Section 721(b)) may apply.
42: 
43: In connection with the Section 721 analysis, C&H will analyze the risk that all or a portion of the contribution could be recharacterized as a disguised sale under Section 707(a)(2)(B) of the Code and the Treasury Regulations promulgated thereunder. This analysis will consider the allocation of liabilities, the timing and nature of distributions to contributing partners, and the application of the two-year presumption under Treasury Regulation Section 1.707-3. We will recommend structures to mitigate disguised sale risk, including appropriate liability allocation provisions and distribution timing restrictions.
44: 
45: Upon completion of our analysis, C&H will prepare a tax opinion letter addressed to the Client addressing the non-recognition treatment of the Section 721 contribution (the \"Section 721 Opinion\"). The opinion will set forth the relevant facts, applicable law, and our conclusions regarding the tax treatment of the contribution, subject to customary assumptions and qualifications.
46: 
47: **(c) Section 1202 QSBS Preservation.** C&H will analyze whether the transfer of the portfolio company shares --- specifically, the shares of Luminos Systems Inc., ClearArc Software Inc., and Vectral Cloud Inc. --- to the CV will preserve the qualified small business stock (\"QSBS\") status of such shares under Section 1202 of the Code. Section 1202 provides a partial or full exclusion from gross income for gain realized on the sale or exchange of QSBS held for more than five years, subject to certain per-issuer and aggregate limitations, and our analysis will address whether the interposition of the CV structure disrupts or preserves the availability of this exclusion.
48: 
49: Our QSBS analysis will give specific attention to the tacking of holding periods under Section 1202(h) of the Code, including the treatment of contributions to partnerships and the look-through rules applicable to partnership interests. We will pay particular attention to the Vectral Cloud Inc. holding period issue: as we understand it, the five-year holding period required under Section 1202(a)(1) for the Vectral Cloud shares will not be satisfied until March 2026, and we will analyze whether the contribution of these shares to the CV prior to the satisfaction of the five-year holding period creates any risk to the availability of the QSBS exclusion upon a future disposition.
50: 
51: Additionally, C&H will evaluate the aggregate gross asset thresholds applicable under Section 1202(d) at the time of original issuance for each of the three portfolio companies. Under Section 1202(d)(1), stock qualifies as QSBS only if, at the time of issuance, the aggregate gross assets of the issuing corporation did not exceed \$50 million (taking into account amounts received in the issuance). We will review available financial records and representations from portfolio company management to confirm compliance with this threshold.
52: 
53: **(d) Section 1061 Carried Interest Analysis.** C&H will analyze the holding period implications under Section 1061 of the Code for the GP\'s existing carried interest in Fund II, which we understand constitutes a twenty percent (20%) carried interest that has been held since December 2019. Based on these facts, the three-year holding period required under Section 1061(a) for long-term capital gain treatment of gain allocated in respect of an applicable partnership interest (\"API\") was satisfied as of December 2022, and the existing carried interest should be eligible for long-term capital gain rates without recharacterization under Section 1061.
54: 
55: In connection with the roll of the GP\'s carried interest into the CV, C&H will structure a \"legacy carry\" tranche designed to preserve the existing Section 1061 holding period for the rolled carried interest. This structure will rely on the non-recognition contribution under Section 721 and the tacking rules applicable to partnership interests contributed to a new partnership, with the objective of ensuring that the three-year holding period that has already been satisfied for the legacy carried interest is not restarted upon the formation of the CV.
56: 
57: C&H will separately analyze the new CV carried interest --- which we understand will be structured as a fifteen percent (15%) carried interest over a seven percent (7%) preferred return, utilizing a European-style (whole-fund) distribution waterfall --- as a new applicable partnership interest under Section 1061 with a holding period commencing at the CV closing. Based on the target closing date of October 31, 2025, the three-year holding period for the new carried interest would be satisfied on October 31, 2028. We will advise on the implications of the bifurcated carry structure, including the allocation of gain between the legacy carry tranche and the new carry tranche.
58: 
59: In addition, C&H will advise on the bifurcation of legacy and new carry tranches among the three GP principals: Marcus Aldren (holding sixty-two percent (62%) of GP economics), Diana Tsao (holding twenty-eight percent (28%) of GP economics), and Rafael Montoya (holding ten percent (10%) of GP economics). Our advice will address the structuring of the GP entity\'s partnership agreement to reflect these allocations and the Section 1061 implications for each individual principal.
60: 
61: **(e) blocker Architecture for Tax-Exempt and Non-U.S. Investors.** C&H will design and advise on the domestic blocker entity, PCV Domestic blocker Inc., which is intended to block unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") under Section 512 of the Code for U.S. tax-exempt limited partners investing in the CV. We understand that the following tax-exempt investors are expected to invest through the domestic blocker:
62: 
63: > • Meridian Public Employees\' Retirement System --- anticipated commitment of \$125 million
64: >
65: > • Ashford University Endowment --- anticipated commitment of \$50 million
66: >
67: > • Aggregate tax-exempt capital through domestic blocker: \$175 million
68: 
69: C&H will also design and advise on the offshore blocker entity, PCV International Holdings Ltd., which is intended to block effectively connected income (\"ECI\") and withholding obligations under Sections 897 and 1446 of the Code (including obligations arising under the Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act, or \"FIRPTA\") for non-U.S. limited partners investing in the CV. We understand that the following non-U.S. investor is expected to invest through the offshore blocker:
70: 
71: > • Sovereign Capital Partners (Cayman) Ltd. --- anticipated commitment of \$75 million
72: 
73: The total capital to be invested through the blocker entities is estimated at \$250 million, representing approximately 23.3% of the total CV capitalization of approximately \$1.074 billion. C&H will advise on the structural placement of the blockers within the CV capital structure, the flow of income and distributions through the blockers, and the tax reporting obligations of each blocker entity.
74: 
75: In connection with the offshore blocker, C&H will advise on the appropriate check-the-box election under Treasury Regulation Section 301.7701-3 for PCV International Holdings Ltd. We will prepare or review the Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) to be filed with the Internal Revenue Service to ensure that PCV International Holdings Ltd. is classified as intended for U.S. federal income tax purposes.
76: 
77: **(f) Section 704(b) and 704(c) Allocation Provisions.** C&H will advise on the allocation methodology for the built-in gain inherent in the portfolio company interests to be contributed to the CV. Based on the information provided to us, the aggregate built-in gain on the three portfolio company investments is approximately \$1.202 billion, calculated as the difference between the aggregate fair market value of \$1.34 billion and the aggregate adjusted tax basis of \$138 million. Proper allocation of this built-in gain is required under Section 704(c) of the Code to prevent the shifting of tax burdens between contributing partners and non-contributing partners.
78: 
79: C&H will analyze and recommend the appropriate Section 704(c) allocation method for the CV, evaluating the relative advantages and disadvantages of the traditional method, the traditional method with curative allocations, and the remedial allocation method, in light of the specific facts of the CV transaction, including the magnitude of the built-in gain, the expected holding periods for the portfolio companies, and the composition of the CV\'s investor base.
80: 
81: In addition, C&H will review and provide a markup of the tax-related provisions of the CV limited partnership agreement (the \"LPA\"), which will be drafted by Hawthorne Reid LLP. Our review will focus on the allocation provisions (including Section 704(b) economic effect and substantiality compliance, Section 704(c) methodology elections, and Section 754 election provisions), distribution waterfall mechanics as they relate to tax distributions, and any other provisions of the LPA that have material tax implications.
82:
