**[TRANSMITTAL NOTE]{.underline}**
Dear Vanessa:

We write on behalf of our client, Pinnacle Capital Management LLC (the \"Sponsor\"), in connection with the proposed formation of Pinnacle Continuation Vehicle LP (the \"Partnership\" or the \"CV\"). We have reviewed the draft Limited Partnership Agreement of the Partnership prepared by your office and dated July 28, 2025 (the \"Draft LPA\"), and we are providing herewith our markup limited to the tax-related provisions contained therein.

**Scope of Review.** Our review encompasses all Articles and Sections of the Draft LPA dealing with the following subject matters: (a) definitions of tax-related terms; (b) capital account maintenance and allocations of income, gain, loss, and deduction under Section 704(b) and Section 704(c) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\"); (c) the distribution waterfall, including carried interest bifurcation and tax distribution mechanics; (d) tax elections, tax returns, and information reporting; (e) designation of the partnership representative under the centralized partnership audit regime enacted by the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2015; (f) qualified small business stock (\"QSBS\") preservation covenants under Section 1202 of the Code; (g) Section 1061 carried interest compliance provisions; (h) withholding and indemnification provisions; (i) disguised sale protections under Section 707 of the Code; (j) Section 752 liability allocation provisions; and (k) blocker entity participation provisions for Tax-Exempt Partners and Non-U.S. Partners.

**Limitations.** Our review is limited to U.S. federal, state, and local tax provisions. Hawthorne Reid LLP retains primary responsibility for all non-tax provisions of the Draft LPA, including but not limited to governance, management authority, transfer restrictions, fiduciary duties, default remedies, exculpation and indemnification of the General Partner, and all other provisions not specifically addressed in this markup. We express no opinion on the non-tax provisions and have not reviewed them for this purpose.

**Companion Deliverables.** This markup is being transmitted together with the following companion deliverables, each dated August 8, 2025, which provide detailed analysis supporting the revisions proposed herein:
> 1\. Tax Structure Memorandum (August 8, 2025);
> 2\. QSBS Preservation Analysis Memorandum;
> 3\. Section 1061 Carried Interest Memorandum;
> 4\. Blocker Entity Structure Memorandum;
> 5\. Section 704(c) Allocation Methodology Memorandum; and
> 6\. Draft Tax Protection Agreement.
**Summary of Key Revisions.** We highlight below the principal revisions and additions reflected in the attached markup:

> \(a\) **Comprehensive Rewrite of Section 704(c) Provisions.** The Draft LPA\'s Section 704(c) provisions are substantially incomplete and do not specify an allocation method. We have proposed a comprehensive rewrite specifying the remedial allocation method under Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-3(d) for the \$1.202 billion of aggregate built-in gain in the Contributed Assets. The remedial method is the most equitable approach given the magnitude of the built-in gain and the negotiated expectation of the Secondary Investors (principally Garrison Secondaries Fund IV LP) that they will not bear pre-contribution tax gain. See the companion Section 704(c) Allocation Methodology Memorandum for a detailed comparative analysis of the traditional method, curative method, and remedial method.

> \(b\) **Addition of Legacy Carry Tranche / New Carry Tranche Bifurcation for Section 1061 Compliance.** The Draft LPA does not address Section 1061 of the Code or the three-year holding period requirement applicable to carried interest. We have added a new section bifurcating the General Partner\'s carried interest into a Legacy Carry Tranche (inheriting the Fund II holding period commencing December 2019, which has already satisfied the three-year requirement) and a New Carry Tranche (commencing on the Final Closing Date, with the three-year period not satisfied until October 31, 2028). This bifurcation is essential to preserve the favorable tax treatment of the legacy carry.

> \(c\) **Addition of QSBS Preservation Covenants.** The Draft LPA contains no QSBS-related provisions. Given that the three portfolio companies contributed to the Partnership are believed to qualify as QSBS under Section 1202 of the Code, and the potential Section 1202 exclusion represents a significant component of the value proposition for eligible Partners, we have added comprehensive QSBS preservation covenants.

> \(d\) **Addition of Mandatory Tax Distribution Provisions.** The Draft LPA does not include a mechanism for mandatory tax distributions. We have added a new section providing for quarterly tax distributions to each Partner based on such Partner\'s allocable share of estimated taxable income, multiplied by the highest combined marginal rate applicable to an individual residing in California (approximately 50.3%).

> \(e\) **Expanded Withholding and Indemnification Provisions.** The Draft LPA\'s withholding provisions are skeletal. We have expanded them to address Section 1446 (ECI withholding on Non-U.S. Partners), Section 1445 (FIRPTA withholding), state and local withholding obligations, and a comprehensive indemnification framework.

> \(f\) **BBA Partnership Audit Regime Provisions.** The Draft LPA\'s partnership representative provisions are outdated and reference the pre-BBA \"tax matters partner\" regime. We have proposed a complete rewrite to comply with the centralized audit regime under Sections 6221 through 6241 of the Code, including a commitment to the push-out election under Section 6226.

> \(g\) **blocker Entity Participation Provisions.** The Draft LPA makes passing reference to the use of blocker entities but does not include detailed provisions. We have added a new Article addressing the formation, capitalization, tax treatment, and governance of the Domestic blocker (PCV Domestic blocker Inc.) and the Offshore blocker (PCV International Holdings Ltd.).

We look forward to discussing these revisions with you and the Pinnacle team at the next working group call. Please do not hesitate to reach out to Sylvia Hartwell at (415) 555-7200 or shartwell@calderwoodharkness.com, or Garrett Simmons at (415) 555-7218 or gsimmons@calderwoodharkness.com, with any questions.
Very truly yours,
**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP**
**[ARTICLE X --- DEFINITIONS (Tax-Related Definitions)]{.underline}**
**[Section X.1 --- Defined Terms (Additions and Revisions)]{.underline}**

The following defined terms are hereby added to, or revised within, Article I of the Agreement. Unless otherwise defined herein, capitalized terms used in this Article shall have the meanings ascribed to them in Article I of the Agreement. To the extent any defined term set forth in this Section X.1 conflicts with a defined term set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, the definition set forth in this Section X.1 shall control with respect to the tax-related provisions of this Agreement.

\*\*\"Applicable Partnership Interest\" or \"API\"\*\* means any interest in the Partnership that is transferred to (or is held by) a Partner in connection with the performance of substantial services by such Partner (or a Related Person of such Partner) in any Applicable Trade or Business, within the meaning of Section 1061(c)(1) of the Code. For the avoidance of doubt, the term \"Applicable Partnership Interest\" specifically includes the Carried Interest (both the Legacy Carry Tranche and the New Carry Tranche) held by the General Partner and its Affiliates, but does not include any capital interest acquired in exchange for a capital contribution to the extent such interest qualifies for the exception set forth in Section 1061(c)(4) of the Code.

\*\*\"BBA Audit Rules\"\*\* means the centralized partnership audit regime enacted by the Bipartisan Budget Act of 2015, as amended by the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 and the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2018, codified at Sections 6221 through 6241 of the Code, including the Treasury Regulations promulgated thereunder and any administrative guidance issued by the Internal Revenue Service with respect thereto.
\*\*\"Blocker Entity\"\*\* means either or both of the Domestic blocker and the Offshore blocker, as the context requires.

**\"Book Value\"** means, with respect to any Partnership asset, the value of such asset as maintained on the Partnership\'s books and records for purposes of computing Capital Accounts in accordance with Section 704(b) of the Code and Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv). The initial Book Value of each Contributed Asset shall be equal to its fair market value at the time of contribution to the Partnership, as determined by the Kessler Pratt LLP valuation dated as of June 30, 2025 (specifically: \$612,000,000 for the Luminos Systems Inc. stake, \$468,000,000 for the ClearArc Software Inc. stake, and \$260,000,000 for the Vectral Cloud Inc. stake, for an aggregate initial Book Value of \$1,340,000,000). Thereafter, Book Value shall be adjusted for depreciation, amortization, cost recovery deductions, and gain or loss (computed by reference to Book Value rather than Tax Basis), and shall be subject to revaluation to fair market value upon the occurrence of a Revaluation Event as described in Section Y.1.

\*\*\"Built-In Gain\"\*\* means, with respect to each Contributed Asset that constitutes Section 704(c) Property, the excess of the Book Value of such asset over the Tax Basis of such asset at the time of its contribution to the Partnership. The aggregate Built-In Gain with respect to the Contributed Assets is \$1,202,000,000, allocated as follows: (i) Luminos Systems Inc.: \$553,500,000 (being the excess of \$612,000,000 Book Value over \$58,500,000 Tax Basis); (ii) ClearArc Software Inc.: \$430,600,000 (being the excess of \$468,000,000 Book Value over \$37,400,000 Tax Basis); and (iii) Vectral Cloud Inc.: \$217,900,000 (being the excess of \$260,000,000 Book Value over \$42,100,000 Tax Basis). For the avoidance of doubt, Built-In Gain is determined at the time of contribution and is not adjusted for subsequent changes in value.
**\"Capital Account\"** has the meaning set forth in Section Y.1, and shall be maintained in accordance with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv) and the provisions of this Agreement.

**\"Carried Interest\"** means the General Partner\'s (or its designees\') interest in Partnership distributions and allocations of Net Income in excess of the Preferred Return, equal to fifteen percent (15%) of the aggregate net profits of the Partnership above the seven percent (7%) annual Preferred Return, as more fully described in Section Z.1. The Carried Interest shall be allocated between the Legacy Carry Tranche and the New Carry Tranche as set forth in Section Z.2.

**\"Code\"** means the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended from time to time, and any successor statute. Any reference herein to a specific section of the Code shall include any successor provision thereto and any Treasury Regulation promulgated thereunder.

\*\*\"Contributed Assets\"\*\* means the portfolio company interests contributed to the Partnership by Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, a Delaware limited partnership (EIN 84-3291067), at the Initial Closing, consisting of the following: (i) shares of common stock (and any preferred stock convertible into common stock) of Luminos Systems Inc., a Delaware corporation (EIN 47-8823156); (ii) shares of common stock (and any preferred stock convertible into common stock) of ClearArc Software Inc., a Delaware corporation (EIN 83-5519274); and (iii) shares of common stock (and any preferred stock convertible into common stock) of Vectral Cloud Inc., a Delaware corporation (EIN 85-1102847). The Contributed Assets are described in further detail in Schedule A hereto.

\*\*\"Domestic blocker\"\*\* means PCV Domestic blocker Inc., a Delaware C-corporation to be formed on or before September 30, 2025, interposed between the Partnership and certain Tax-Exempt Partners for the purpose of blocking UBTI, as more fully described in Section BB.1.

\*\*\"Effectively Connected Income\" or \"ECI\"\*\* means income that is effectively connected with the conduct of a trade or business within the United States within the meaning of Section 864 of the Code, including income treated as ECI under Section 897 of the Code (relating to dispositions of U.S. real property interests).
\*\*\"FIRPTA\"\*\* means the Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act of 1980, as amended, codified at Sections 897 and 1445 of the Code, and the Treasury Regulations promulgated thereunder.

\*\*\"GP Co-Invest\"\*\* means the aggregate capital commitment of \$14,000,000 by the General Partner or its Affiliates to the Partnership, which shall be funded in cash on or before the Final Closing Date and shall constitute a capital interest (and not an Applicable Partnership Interest) to the extent provided in Section AA.5(e).

\*\*\"Legacy Carry Tranche\"\*\* means the portion of the Carried Interest attributable to the General Partner\'s pre-existing carried interest in Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP (EIN 84-3291067), which is contributed (or \"rolled\") into the Partnership by means of a non-recognition transaction under Section 721 of the Code, and which inherits the original Section 1061 holding period commencing on or about December 2019 (the date of the final closing of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP). The three-year holding period applicable to the Legacy Carry Tranche under Section 1061(a) of the Code was satisfied as of December 2022. The Legacy Carry Tranche is further described in Section Z.2(a).

\*\*\"New Carry Tranche\"\*\* means the portion of the Carried Interest attributable to new performance-based allocations in the Partnership, constituting a new Applicable Partnership Interest with a Section 1061 holding period commencing on the Final Closing Date (target: October 31, 2025). The three-year holding period applicable to the New Carry Tranche under Section 1061(a) of the Code will not be satisfied until October 31, 2028. The New Carry Tranche is further described in Section Z.2(b).

\*\*\"Non-U.S. Partner\"\*\* means any Partner that is not a \"United States person\" within the meaning of Section 7701(a)(30) of the Code. For the avoidance of doubt, the term \"Non-U.S. Partner\" includes any Partner that is a foreign corporation, a nonresident alien individual, a foreign partnership, a foreign trust, or a foreign estate.

\*\*\"Offshore blocker\"\*\* means PCV International Holdings Ltd., a Cayman Islands exempted company to be formed on or before September 30, 2025, which shall file a Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) to elect classification as a corporation for U.S. federal income tax purposes, interposed between the Partnership and certain Non-U.S. Partners for the purpose of blocking ECI and FIRPTA withholding, as more fully described in Section BB.2.

\*\*\*\* \"Partnership Representative\" means the Person designated under Section AA.3 to serve as the partnership representative of the Partnership for purposes of Section 6223 of the Code and the BBA Audit Rules. The initial Partnership Representative shall be Marcus Aldren.

**\"Preferred Return\"** means a cumulative, compounded annual return of seven percent (7%) per annum on each Partner\'s Unreturned Capital Contributions, computed from the date of each such Partner\'s capital contribution through and including the date of distribution.

\*\*\"QSBS\"\*\* means \"qualified small business stock\" within the meaning of Section 1202(c) of the Code, being stock in a domestic C-corporation that (i) was acquired by the taxpayer at original issuance in exchange for money or other property (other than stock) or as compensation for services, (ii) was issued by a corporation that is a \"qualified small business\" as defined in Section 1202(d) (i.e., a domestic C-corporation with aggregate gross assets not exceeding \$50,000,000 at all times prior to and immediately after the issuance), and (iii) meets the active business requirements of Section 1202(e).

\*\*\"Remedial Allocation\"\*\* means a notional allocation of tax items (income, gain, loss, or deduction) made pursuant to the remedial allocation method under Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-3(d), which is used to eliminate distortions caused by the ceiling rule and to ensure that the tax consequences to Non-Contributing Partners mirror their book allocations with respect to Section 704(c) Property.

\*\*\"Rolling LP\"\*\* means any limited partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP that has elected to contribute its pro rata interest in the Contributed Assets to the Partnership in exchange for a limited partnership interest in the Partnership, representing in the aggregate approximately \$680,000,000 in net asset value.

\*\*\"Secondary Investor\"\*\* means Garrison Secondaries Fund IV LP, a Delaware limited partnership, and any other investor acquiring a limited partnership interest in the Partnership in exchange for new cash capital contributions, and not by way of a contribution of interests in Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP.

\*\*\"Section 704(c) Property\"\*\* means each Contributed Asset, to the extent such asset has a Built-In Gain or Built-In Loss at the time of contribution to the Partnership, and any other Partnership asset that is subject to the principles of Section 704(c) of the Code by reason of a Revaluation Event (i.e., \"reverse Section 704(c)\" property).

\*\*\"Tax Basis\"\*\* means the adjusted tax basis of an asset for U.S. federal income tax purposes, as determined under Section 1011 and other applicable provisions of the Code. The aggregate Tax Basis of the Contributed Assets at the time of contribution to the Partnership is \$138,000,000, allocated as follows: (i) Luminos Systems Inc.: \$58,500,000; (ii) ClearArc Software Inc.: \$37,400,000; and (iii) Vectral Cloud Inc.: \$42,100,000.
\*\*\"Tax Distribution\"\*\* has the meaning set forth in Section Z.4.

\*\*\"Tax-Exempt Partner\"\*\* means any Partner that is exempt from U.S. federal income tax under Section 501(a) of the Code, including (without limitation) Meridian Public Employees\' Retirement System and Ashford University Endowment, or any successor entity thereto that maintains tax-exempt status under Section 501(a).
\*\*\"UBTI\"\*\* means \"unrelated business taxable income\" within the meaning of Section 512 of the Code, including income from debt-financed property within the meaning of Section 514 of the Code.

**\[C&H Comment: We have added approximately twenty-five (25) new defined terms and revised several existing definitions to support the tax-related provisions set forth in the Articles below. We recommend that Hawthorne Reid update all cross-references to Article I definitions throughout the Draft LPA to incorporate these additions and revisions. In particular, the deletion of the \"Tax Matters Partner\" definition and its replacement with \"Partnership Representative\" will require conforming changes in multiple locations.\]**
**[ARTICLE Y --- CAPITAL ACCOUNTS AND ALLOCATIONS]{.underline}**
**[Section Y.1 --- Capital Accounts]{.underline}**

\(a\) **Establishment and Maintenance.** The Partnership shall establish and maintain a separate Capital Account for each Partner in accordance with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv). The Capital Accounts shall be maintained for the full term of the Partnership and through the completion of the liquidation and winding up of the Partnership\'s affairs.
\(b\) **Credits to Capital Accounts.** Each Partner\'s Capital Account shall be *credited* with:
> \(i\) the amount of cash actually contributed by such Partner to the Partnership;

> \(ii\) the fair market value of any property contributed by such Partner to the Partnership (net of any liabilities secured by such property that the Partnership is considered to assume or take subject to under Section 752 of the Code), as determined by the General Partner in good faith; provided that, with respect to the Contributed Assets, the fair market value shall be the Book Value thereof as set forth in the definition of \"Book Value\" in Section X.1 (aggregate fair market value of \$1,340,000,000, as determined by the Kessler Pratt LLP valuation as of June 30, 2025);

> \(iii\) allocations to such Partner of Net Income and items of income and gain (including income and gain exempt from tax and income and gain described in Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(g), but excluding income and gain described in Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(4)(i)); and
> \(iv\) such other items as are required to be credited to a Partner\'s Capital Account under Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv).
\(c\) **Debits to Capital Accounts.** Each Partner\'s Capital Account shall be *debited* with:
> \(i\) the amount of cash distributed to such Partner by the Partnership;

> \(ii\) the fair market value of any property distributed to such Partner by the Partnership (net of any liabilities secured by such property that such Partner is considered to assume or take subject to under Section 752 of the Code), as determined by the General Partner in good faith;

> \(iii\) allocations to such Partner of Net Loss and items of deduction and loss (including expenditures described in Section 705(a)(2)(B) of the Code and loss and deduction described in Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(g), but excluding items described in Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(4)(i)); and
> \(iv\) such other items as are required to be debited from a Partner\'s Capital Account under Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv).

\(d\) \*\*Contribution of Contributed Assets --- Rolling LP Capital Accounts.\*\* Upon the contribution of the Contributed Assets to the Partnership at the Initial Closing, the Capital Accounts of the Rolling LPs shall be credited with the fair market value of their respective pro rata share of the Contributed Assets, as determined by the valuation performed by Kessler Pratt LLP (101 Montgomery Street, Suite 1800, San Francisco, California 94104; contact: David Kessler, Managing Partner) as of June 30, 2025. Each Rolling LP\'s initial Capital Account balance shall equal the net asset value of such Rolling LP\'s pro rata interest in the Contributed Assets, determined by reference to such Rolling LP\'s percentage interest in Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP immediately prior to the contribution. The aggregate initial Capital Account balances of the Rolling LPs shall equal approximately \$680,000,000.

\(e\) \*\*Revaluation Events.\*\* Upon the occurrence of any of the following events (each, a \"Revaluation Event\"), the Book Values of all Partnership assets shall be adjusted to equal their respective fair market values (as determined by the General Partner in good faith, and taking into account Section 7701(g) of the Code), and the resulting unrealized Book gain or loss shall be allocated among the Partners\' Capital Accounts in the same manner as if the Partnership had recognized such gain or loss upon an actual sale of all Partnership assets at their fair market values:
> \(i\) the admission of any new Partner to the Partnership, including at any subsequent closing;
> \(ii\) the distribution of Partnership property (other than cash) to a Partner in partial or complete liquidation of such Partner\'s interest in the Partnership;
> \(iii\) the liquidation of the Partnership within the meaning of Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(g);

> \(iv\) the grant of an interest in the Partnership (other than a *de minimis* interest) as consideration for the provision of services to or for the benefit of the Partnership within the meaning of Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(f)(5)(iii); and

> \(v\) at such other times as the General Partner reasonably determines that a revaluation is necessary to comply with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(f) or to properly reflect the economic arrangement among the Partners.

Any Book gain or loss resulting from a Revaluation Event shall thereafter be treated as Section 704(c) gain or loss with respect to each revalued asset (\"reverse Section 704(c)\" gain or loss) and shall be subject to the allocation provisions of Section Y.3(b).

\(f\) **Transfers of Partnership Interests.** In the event of a transfer of all or a portion of a Partner\'s interest in the Partnership in accordance with the terms of this Agreement, the transferee shall succeed to the Capital Account of the transferor to the extent it relates to the transferred interest.

\(g\) **Interpretation.** The provisions of this Section Y.1 and the other provisions of this Agreement relating to the maintenance of Capital Accounts are intended to comply with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b) and shall be interpreted and applied in a manner consistent with such Treasury Regulations. In the event the General Partner determines that it is prudent to modify the manner in which the Capital Accounts, or any credits or debits thereto, are computed in order to comply with such Treasury Regulations, the General Partner may make such modification, provided that such modification is not likely to have a material effect on the amounts distributable to any Partner pursuant to Article Z upon the dissolution of the Partnership.
**[Section Y.2 --- Allocations of Net Income and Net Loss (Section 704(b) Allocations)]{.underline}**
**Section Y.2(a) --- General Allocation Rule**

After giving effect to the regulatory allocations set forth in Section Y.2(b) and the curative allocations set forth in Section Y.2(c), Net Income and Net Loss (and, to the extent necessary, individual items of income, gain, loss, and deduction) for each fiscal year shall be allocated among the Partners in a manner that is intended to have \"substantial economic effect\" within the meaning of Section 704(b) of the Code and Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b). Specifically, allocations of Net Income and Net Loss shall be made so as to cause each Partner\'s Capital Account balance, after all allocations for the applicable fiscal year have been made and all distributions for such fiscal year have been made (or, if earlier, after all distributions through the date of determination have been made), to equal, as nearly as possible, the amount that would be distributed to such Partner if the Partnership were to liquidate on the last day of such fiscal year (or on such date of determination), all Partnership assets were sold for their respective Book Values, all Partnership liabilities were satisfied in full according to their terms (limited with respect to each nonrecourse liability to the Book Value of the assets securing such liability), and the net proceeds were distributed in full pursuant to the distribution waterfall set forth in Section Z.1.

This \"target capital account\" approach is intended to ensure that, at any point in the Partnership\'s existence, each Partner\'s Capital Account reflects the economic entitlement of such Partner under the distribution waterfall, thereby satisfying the economic effect equivalence test of Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(i).

**\[C&H Comment: The Hawthorne Reid draft\'s simplified pro rata allocation of income and loss is inappropriate for a vehicle with a carried interest and a preferred return. A target capital account (or \"targeted allocation\") approach is the standard methodology for private equity fund LPAs with a waterfall structure. This approach ensures that if the Partnership were liquidated at any point, each Partner\'s Capital Account balance would be equal to the amount such Partner would receive under the waterfall. We have replaced the Hawthorne Reid draft\'s allocation provisions accordingly.\]**
**Section Y.2(b) --- Regulatory Allocations**
Notwithstanding the general allocation rule set forth in Section Y.2(a), the following special allocations shall be made in the following order of priority:

\(i\) **Minimum Gain Chargeback.** Notwithstanding any other provision of this Article Y, if there is a net decrease in Partnership Minimum Gain (as defined in Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-2(b)(2) and 1.704-2(d)) during any fiscal year, each Partner shall be allocated items of income and gain for such fiscal year (and, if necessary, subsequent fiscal years) in an amount equal to such Partner\'s share of the net decrease in Partnership Minimum Gain, determined in accordance with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-2(g). Allocations pursuant to the preceding sentence shall be made in proportion to the respective amounts required to be allocated to each Partner pursuant thereto. The items to be so allocated shall be determined in accordance with Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-2(f)(6) and 1.704-2(j)(2). This Section Y.2(b)(i) is intended to comply with the \"minimum gain chargeback\" requirement in Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-2(f) and shall be interpreted consistently therewith.

\(ii\) **Partner Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain Chargeback.** Notwithstanding any other provision of this Article Y (other than Section Y.2(b)(i)), if there is a net decrease in Partner Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain (as defined in Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-2(i)(2)) attributable to a Partner Nonrecourse Debt (as defined in Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-2(b)(4)) during any fiscal year, each Partner who has a share of the Partner Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain attributable to such Partner Nonrecourse Debt, determined in accordance with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-2(i)(5), shall be specially allocated items of income and gain for such fiscal year (and, if necessary, subsequent fiscal years) in an amount equal to such Partner\'s share of the net decrease in Partner Nonrecourse Debt Minimum Gain attributable to such Partner Nonrecourse Debt, determined in accordance with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-2(i)(4). Allocations pursuant to the preceding sentence shall be made in proportion to the respective amounts required to be allocated to each Partner pursuant thereto. The items to be so allocated shall be determined in accordance with Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-2(i)(4) and 1.704-2(j)(2). This Section Y.2(b)(ii) is intended to comply with the \"partner nonrecourse debt minimum gain chargeback\" requirement in Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-2(i)(4) and shall be interpreted consistently therewith.

\(iii\) **Qualified Income Offset.** In the event any Partner unexpectedly receives any adjustments, allocations, or distributions described in Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d)(4), (5), or (6) that cause or increase a deficit balance in such Partner\'s Capital Account (in excess of any amount such Partner is obligated to restore or is deemed obligated to restore pursuant to the penultimate sentences of Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-2(g)(1) and 1.704-2(i)(5)), items of income and gain shall be specially allocated to such Partner in an amount and manner sufficient to eliminate, to the extent required by the Treasury Regulations, such deficit balance as quickly as possible. This Section Y.2(b)(iii) is intended to constitute a \"qualified income offset\" within the meaning of Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(ii)(d) and shall be interpreted consistently therewith.

\(iv\) **Nonrecourse Deductions.** Nonrecourse Deductions (as defined in Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-2(b)(1) and 1.704-2(c)) for any fiscal year shall be allocated among the Partners in proportion to their respective Percentage Interests.

\(v\) **Partner Nonrecourse Deductions.** Any Partner Nonrecourse Deductions (as defined in Treasury Regulation Sections 1.704-2(i)(1) and 1.704-2(i)(2)) for any fiscal year shall be allocated one hundred percent (100%) to the Partner who bears the economic risk of loss with respect to the Partner Nonrecourse Debt to which such Partner Nonrecourse Deductions are attributable, in accordance with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-2(i)(1).

\(vi\) **Code Section 754 Adjustments.** To the extent an adjustment to the adjusted Tax Basis of any Partnership asset pursuant to Section 734(b) or Section 743(b) of the Code is required, pursuant to Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(2) or Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(4), to be taken into account in determining Capital Accounts as the result of a distribution to a Partner in complete liquidation of such Partner\'s interest in the Partnership, the amount of such adjustment to the Capital Accounts shall be treated as an item of gain (if the adjustment increases the basis of the asset) or loss (if the adjustment decreases such basis) and such gain or loss shall be specially allocated to the Partners in accordance with their interests in the Partnership in the event that Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(2) applies, or to the Partner to whom such distribution was made in the event that Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b)(2)(iv)(m)(4) applies.

**\[C&H Comment: The regulatory allocations set forth in Section Y.2(b) are required by the Treasury Regulations to maintain the \"substantial economic effect\" safe harbor under Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b). These allocations override the general allocation rule in Section Y.2(a) to the extent required by the Treasury Regulations. The ordering of these allocations is intentional: minimum gain chargeback first, then partner nonrecourse debt minimum gain chargeback, then qualified income offset, followed by the general allocation provisions.\]**
**Section Y.2(c) --- Curative / Corrective Allocations**

The regulatory allocations set forth in Section Y.2(b) (the \"Regulatory Allocations\") are intended to comply with certain requirements of the Treasury Regulations promulgated under Section 704(b) of the Code. It is the intent of the Partners that, to the extent possible, all Regulatory Allocations shall be offset either with other Regulatory Allocations or with special allocations of other items of Partnership income, gain, loss, or deduction pursuant to this Section Y.2(c). Accordingly, to the extent the Regulatory Allocations cause the Partners\' Capital Account balances to deviate from the target balances described in Section Y.2(a), subsequent allocations of Net Income, Net Loss, and items of income, gain, loss, and deduction shall be made among the Partners so as to bring each Partner\'s Capital Account balance as close as possible to the target balance that would have resulted under Section Y.2(a) if the Regulatory Allocations had not occurred. The General Partner shall have reasonable discretion, exercised in good faith, in determining the manner in which such curative allocations are made, taking into account the character of the items available for allocation and the need to comply with the requirements of Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-1(b).
**[Section Y.3 --- Section 704(c) Allocations]{.underline}**

**\[C&H Comment: The Hawthorne Reid draft contained a single sentence stating that \"the Partnership shall make allocations in accordance with Section 704(c) of the Code.\" This is wholly inadequate given the \$1.202 billion of Built-In Gain in the Contributed Assets and the critical importance of the Section 704(c) allocation method to the economic deal between the Rolling LPs and the Secondary Investors. We have provided a comprehensive rewrite of this section.\]**
**Section Y.3(a) --- Contributed Property --- Remedial Allocation Method**

\(i\) **Election of Remedial Method.** In accordance with Section 704(c) of the Code and Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-3(d), the Partnership hereby elects and shall use the **remedial allocation method** to allocate items of income, gain, loss, and deduction with respect to each Contributed Asset that constitutes Section 704(c) Property. The remedial allocation method is adopted to eliminate the distortions that would otherwise be created by the \"ceiling rule\" under Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-3(b)(1) and to ensure that the Secondary Investors (principally Garrison Secondaries Fund IV LP) and the blocker Entities are not allocated any portion of the pre-contribution Built-In Gain attributable to the Contributed Assets.
\(ii\) **Built-In Gain Amounts.** The Built-In Gain with respect to each Contributed Asset, determined as of the date of contribution, is as follows:
> \(A\) **Luminos Systems Inc.**: Fair market value of \$612,000,000 less Tax Basis of \$58,500,000, resulting in Built-In Gain of \$553,500,000;
> \(B\) **ClearArc Software Inc.**: Fair market value of \$468,000,000 less Tax Basis of \$37,400,000, resulting in Built-In Gain of \$430,600,000;
> \(C\) **Vectral Cloud Inc.**: Fair market value of \$260,000,000 less Tax Basis of \$42,100,000, resulting in Built-In Gain of \$217,900,000;
> \(D\) **Aggregate Built-In Gain**: \$1,202,000,000.
\(iii\) **Application of the Remedial Method.** Under the remedial allocation method, the Partnership shall allocate tax items with respect to each Contributed Asset as follows:

> \(A\) Upon a sale, exchange, or other disposition (including a deemed disposition) of a Contributed Asset, the Partnership shall first allocate the actual tax gain or loss recognized on such disposition to the Contributing Partners (i.e., the Rolling LPs) to the extent of the Built-In Gain (or Built-In Loss) remaining with respect to such Contributed Asset at the time of the disposition. For this purpose, the Built-In Gain remaining at the time of disposition shall be the excess (if any) of the Book Value of the Contributed Asset over its Tax Basis, each as adjusted through the date of disposition.

> \(B\) To the extent that the actual tax gain recognized by the Partnership on a disposition of a Contributed Asset is insufficient to match the book gain allocated to the Non-Contributing Partners (i.e., the Secondary Investors, the blocker Entities, and any other Partner whose interest in the Partnership was acquired for cash), the Partnership shall create a Remedial Allocation consisting of (1) a notional allocation of additional tax gain to the Contributing Partners (Rolling LPs) in an amount equal to the shortfall, and (2) a corresponding notional allocation of an offsetting tax deduction (or loss) to the Non-Contributing Partners, such that each Non-Contributing Partner\'s cumulative tax allocation with respect to the Contributed Asset equals such Non-Contributing Partner\'s cumulative book allocation with respect thereto.

> \(C\) With respect to depreciation, amortization, and other cost recovery deductions attributable to a Contributed Asset (to the extent any Contributed Asset is depreciable or amortizable), the Partnership shall compute such deductions separately for book purposes and tax purposes. The book depreciation or amortization shall be computed by reference to the Book Value of the Contributed Asset; the tax depreciation or amortization shall be computed by reference to the Tax Basis of the Contributed Asset. To the extent the tax depreciation available is less than the book depreciation allocated to the Non-Contributing Partners, the Partnership shall create a Remedial Allocation consisting of (1) a notional allocation of additional tax depreciation (or deduction) to the Non-Contributing Partners in an amount equal to the shortfall, and (2) a corresponding notional allocation of an offsetting item of taxable income to the Contributing Partners.

\(iv\) **Character.** The character of any Remedial Allocation (as ordinary income, capital gain, etc.) shall be determined in accordance with Treasury Regulation Section 1.704-3(d)(4)(ii) and shall be consistent with the character of the corresponding book item that gives rise to the need for the Remedial Allocation.

**\[C&H Comment: The remedial method is recommended as the most equitable and economically appropriate approach for this transaction. The magnitude of the Built-In Gain (\$1.202 billion on an aggregate Tax Basis of only \$138 million) means that the ceiling rule under the traditional method would impose substantial phantom income on the Secondary Investors, which is commercially unacceptable. The curative method, while also capable of addressing ceiling rule distortions, is less flexible and may not have sufficient offsetting items available to fully cure the distortion. See the companion Section 704(c) Allocation Methodology Memorandum dated August 8, 2025, for a detailed comparative analysis of all three methods (traditional, curative, and remedial) and the basis for our recommendation.\]**

11: > **Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP --- GP Advisory Regarding Key-Person Event, Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd.**
12: >
13: > **Matter No.: 1024-00002**
14: 
15: Dear Ms. Sato:
16: 
17: **[1. Introduction and Engagement Overview]{.underline}**
18: 
19: Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Driftwood Capital Management LLC (\"DCM\"), a Delaware limited liability company (EIN: 82-4917653), in its capacity as the General Partner of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (\"DARF\" or the \"Fund\"), a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership registered with the Cayman Islands Registrar of Exempted Limited Partnerships under Registration No. ELP-87234. This engagement letter sets forth the terms and conditions under which C&H will provide legal advisory services to DCM and the Fund in connection with the Key Person Event (as defined below) and related governance matters described herein.
20: 
21: The Fund is governed by its Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement dated March 15, 2017 (as amended from time to time, the \"A&R LPA\"), which is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. The A&R LPA provides for certain key-person protections in favor of the Fund\'s limited partners, as more fully described in Section 3 below.
22: 
23: This engagement is precipitated by the medical incapacitation of Marcus J. Whitmore, Founder, Chief Investment Officer, and Managing Member (holding a ninety percent (90%) membership interest) of DCM. Mr. Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke on June 3, 2024, and has been incapacitated since that date. Mr. Whitmore is the sole individual designated as a \"Key Person\" under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA. As a result of Mr. Whitmore\'s continued incapacitation for a period exceeding seven consecutive calendar days from the date of the medical event, a Key Person Event under Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA is deemed to have been triggered as of June 10, 2024 (the \"Key Person Event\"). The occurrence of the Key Person Event gives rise to a number of contractual obligations, rights, and remedies under the A&R LPA that require prompt legal attention and careful navigation by DCM in its capacity as General Partner of the Fund.
24: 
25: This engagement letter confirms the terms and conditions under which C&H will provide legal advisory services to the Clients (as defined below) in connection with the Key Person Event, including, without limitation, analysis of the A&R LPA\'s key-person provisions, preparation of required limited partner notifications, development of a successor governance framework, drafting of LPA amendments, and coordination of the limited partner consent solicitation process.
26: 
27: **[2. Clients]{.underline}**
28: 
29: For purposes of this engagement, C&H\'s clients shall consist of both DCM and DARF (collectively, the \"Clients\").
30: 
31: DCM\'s principal office is located at 680 Lexington Avenue, 31st Floor, New York, NY 10022. DCM\'s registered agent for service of process in the State of Delaware is Capitol Registered Agents, Inc., located at 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.
32: 
33: DARF\'s registered office is located at 4th Floor, Harbour Place, 103 South Church Street, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1104, Cayman Islands. DARF\'s registered agent in the Cayman Islands is Archipelago Corporate Services Ltd., P.O. Box 2681, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1111, Cayman Islands.
34: 
35: It is important that the scope of this representation be clearly understood. C&H represents DCM and DARF as described herein and does not represent any individual limited partner of the Fund, the Investor Advisory Committee of the Fund (the \"IAC\"), or any individual member or officer of DCM in his or her personal capacity. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, C&H does not represent Mr. Whitmore individually, nor does C&H represent any member of the IAC in his, her, or its individual or fiduciary capacity. Each such person and entity is encouraged to seek independent legal counsel to the extent such person or entity deems it necessary or appropriate.
36: 
37: Elaine R. Sato, in her capacity as Deputy Chief Investment Officer and Managing Member (holding a ten percent (10%) membership interest) of DCM, will serve as the primary point of contact for the Clients in connection with this engagement. All communications from C&H regarding this engagement will be directed to Ms. Sato unless otherwise instructed in writing by Ms. Sato. C&H will take direction from Ms. Sato with respect to all matters within the scope of this engagement, subject to the Firm\'s professional obligations.
38: 
39: **[3. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**
40: 
41: C&H\'s representation of the Clients will encompass the following workstreams in connection with the Key Person Event triggered under Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA. Each workstream is described in further detail below.
42: 
43: **3.1 Key-Person Event Analysis**
44: 
45: C&H will undertake a comprehensive analysis of the mechanics and consequences of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, including the following:
46: 
47: > \(a\) **Section 8.04(a) --- Definition of \"Key Person.\"** C&H will confirm the scope of the \"Key Person\" designation under the A&R LPA, which identifies Marcus J. Whitmore as the sole designated Key Person. C&H will analyze the definition for purposes of establishing the factual predicate for the Key Person Event and for advising on the requirements for designating any Successor Key Person(s) (as described in Section 3.3 below).
48: >
49: > \(b\) **Section 8.04(b) --- Trigger Conditions.** C&H will analyze the trigger conditions set forth in Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA in light of the facts surrounding Mr. Whitmore\'s incapacitation. Specifically, Section 8.04(b) provides that a Key Person Event is deemed to occur when the Key Person becomes unable, whether by reason of death, disability, incapacity, departure, or otherwise, to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Fund for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days. Based on the information provided to C&H, Mr. Whitmore has been continuously incapacitated since June 3, 2024, and the seven-consecutive-calendar-day threshold was met as of June 10, 2024. C&H will prepare a memorandum confirming the legal basis for this determination.
50: >
51: > \(c\) **Section 8.04(c) --- Consequences of the Key Person Event.** C&H will advise the Clients regarding the full range of consequences triggered by the occurrence of the Key Person Event under Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, which include the following:
52: >
53: > \(i\) *Immediate Suspension of the Investment Period.* The Investment Period (as defined in Section 1.01 of the A&R LPA) is automatically suspended upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event. During such suspension, the General Partner may not make new portfolio investments on behalf of the Fund, except as provided in clause (ii) below.
54: >
55: > \(ii\) *Follow-On Investment Cap.* Notwithstanding the suspension of the Investment Period, the General Partner retains limited authority to make follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions in an aggregate amount not to exceed one percent (1%) of the Fund\'s assets under management as of the date of the Key Person Event. Based on the Fund\'s most recently reported AUM of approximately \$2.87 billion, the follow-on investment cap is \$28.7 million.
56: >
57: > \(iii\) *LP Notification Requirement.* The General Partner is required to provide written notice to all limited partners of the occurrence of the Key Person Event within five (5) business days of the date on which the Key Person Event is deemed to have occurred. Given that the Key Person Event is deemed to have occurred on June 10, 2024, the contractual deadline for delivery of such notice is June 17, 2024.
58: >
59: > \(iv\) *Commencement of the 90-Calendar-Day Cure Period.* Upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, a cure period of ninety (90) calendar days (the \"Cure Period\") commences, during which the General Partner may propose one or more Successor Key Persons for approval by the limited partners. The Cure Period with respect to the current Key Person Event will expire on September 8, 2024.
60: >
61: > \(v\) *LP Consent Threshold.* Approval of any proposed Successor Key Person(s) requires the affirmative written consent of limited partners holding at least sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the aggregate capital commitments of all limited partners of the Fund, excluding for this purpose any co-investment by the General Partner. C&H will advise on the calculation of this threshold based on the most current LP commitment schedule maintained by the Fund\'s administrator.
62: >
63: > \(d\) **Consequences of Failure to Cure.** C&H will further analyze the consequences under Section 8.04(d) of the A&R LPA if no cure is achieved within the Cure Period, including the limited partners\' right to elect, by the same 66⅔% consent threshold described above, either (x) to extend the Cure Period for one or more additional periods or (y) to direct the General Partner to commence an orderly wind-down of the Fund\'s portfolio. C&H will advise the Clients on the mechanics, timing, and fiduciary considerations associated with each of these alternatives.
64: >
65: > \(e\) **Delaware Law Fiduciary Duty Analysis.** C&H will advise the Clients regarding the fiduciary duties owed by DCM, as General Partner, to the limited partners of the Fund during the Key Person Event and throughout the consent solicitation process, as a matter of Delaware law. This analysis will address, among other things, the duty of care and the contractual modification of fiduciary duties under the A&R LPA, including the exculpation and indemnification provisions set forth in Article XII thereof.
66: 
67: **3.2 LP Notification**
68: 
69: C&H will draft the formal written notice to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund disclosing the occurrence of the Key Person Event in compliance with Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA (the \"Key Person Notice\"). The Key Person Notice will describe the factual basis for the Key Person Event, the contractual consequences thereof, the commencement and expected expiration date of the Cure Period, and the process by which the General Partner intends to propose Successor Key Person(s) for approval by the limited partners.
70: 
71: C&H will coordinate with Pinnacle Fund Services (Cayman) Ltd. (the \"Administrator\"), the Fund\'s third-party administrator, regarding the maintenance and accuracy of LP contact information, the appropriate method of delivery (including any notice provisions specified in the A&R LPA or in individual side letters), and the mechanics of distributing the Key Person Notice to all limited partners within the contractual timeframe. C&H will confirm with the Administrator that notice is delivered by a method that satisfies the delivery requirements of Section 15.01 of the A&R LPA.
72: 
73: It is critical that the Key Person Notice be delivered within the five (5) business-day contractual notification deadline, which, as noted above, falls on June 17, 2024. C&H will prioritize this workstream accordingly and will endeavor to deliver a draft of the Key Person Notice to Ms. Sato for review no later than June 13, 2024.
74: 
75: **3.3 Successor Governance Framework**
76: 
77: C&H will advise the Clients regarding the identification and evaluation of proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the development of a recommended successor governance framework for the Fund. This advisory work may encompass the following elements:
78: 
79: > \(a\) **Designation of Successor Key Person(s).** C&H will advise on the criteria and process for designating one or more Successor Key Persons under the A&R LPA, including the qualifications, investment experience, and operational capabilities that limited partners are likely to consider in evaluating any proposed successor. C&H will assist in preparing biographical and professional materials for inclusion in the consent solicitation package.
80: >
81: > \(b\) **Establishment of an Investment Committee.** In the event that the Clients determine that the successor governance framework should include the establishment of a formal Investment Committee or similar collective governance body (in lieu of, or in addition to, a sole Key Person designation), C&H will advise on the structure, composition, authority, and operating procedures of such body, and will prepare the necessary amendments to the A&R LPA to implement such structure.
82: >
83: > \(c\) **Modifications to Key-Person Clause Mechanics.** C&H will advise on potential modifications to the key-person provisions of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, which may include revised replacement periods, modified trigger events (including, for example, a threshold requiring the departure or incapacitation of more than one designated Key Person before a Key Person Event is deemed to occur), and other structural changes to reduce single-person dependency risk.
84: >
85: > \(d\) **Carried Interest Reallocation.** C&H will advise the Clients on the legal and governance considerations associated with any proposed reallocation of carried interest among GP personnel in connection with the transition, including the interplay between the carried interest provisions of the A&R LPA and the operating agreement of DCM.
86: >
87: > \(e\) **Designation of Senior Advisor or Emeritus Role.** To the extent the Clients determine it appropriate, C&H will advise on the creation of a Senior Advisor or emeritus role for Mr. Whitmore, including the scope of any continuing economic interest, advisory responsibilities, and governance rights that may be associated with such role.
88: >
89: > \(f\) **Fiduciary Duty Obligations.** Throughout the development of the successor governance framework, C&H will advise the Clients regarding their fiduciary duty obligations under applicable Delaware law, including the duty to act in good faith and in the best interests of the limited partners in proposing any successor governance arrangements.
90: 
91: **3.4 LPA Amendment Drafting**
92: 
93: C&H will prepare one or more amendments to the A&R LPA (each, an \"LPA Amendment\") to implement the successor governance framework developed pursuant to Section 3.3 above. It is anticipated that the LPA Amendments will include modifications to the following provisions of the A&R LPA, among others:
94: 
95: > \(a\) Section 8.04 (Key Person), to reflect the designation of Successor Key Person(s) and any revised key-person clause mechanics;
96: >
97: > \(b\) Section 9.02 (Investor Advisory Committee), to the extent any changes to the composition, authority, or procedures of the IAC are contemplated in connection with the successor governance framework;
98: >
99: > \(c\) Section 14.01 (Amendments), to the extent any changes to the amendment mechanics are necessary or advisable; and
100: >
101: > \(d\) Related schedules and exhibits, including the schedule of Key Persons attached to the A&R LPA.
102: 
103: All LPA Amendments will be subject to the consent requirements set forth in Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA, which generally requires the written consent of the General Partner and limited partners holding at least 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments (excluding GP co-investment) for amendments to certain specified provisions, including Section 8.04. C&H will advise the Clients regarding the applicable consent thresholds for each proposed amendment.
104: 
105: **3.5 LP Consent Solicitation**
106: 
107: C&H will advise on and coordinate the consent solicitation process necessary to obtain limited partner approval of the proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the related LPA Amendments. This workstream will include the following:
108: 
109: > \(a\) **Successor Key Person Proposal Letter.** C&H will draft a detailed letter to all limited partners setting forth the proposed Successor Key Person(s), the rationale for the proposed designation(s), the terms of the proposed successor governance framework, and a summary of the proposed LPA Amendments (the \"Proposal Letter\"). The Proposal Letter will be designed to provide limited partners with all information reasonably necessary to make an informed decision regarding the proposed successor arrangements.
110: >
111: > \(b\) **Form of LP Written Consent.** C&H will prepare a Form of LP Written Consent (the \"Consent Form\") for execution by limited partners approving the proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the related LPA Amendments. The Consent Form will be structured to comply with the requirements of Section 14.01 and Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA.
112: >
113: > \(c\) **Coordination of Consent Solicitation Process.** C&H will coordinate the distribution of the Proposal Letter and Consent Form to all forty-seven (47) limited partners, working in conjunction with the Administrator to ensure accurate and timely delivery. C&H will manage the consent solicitation timeline with a view toward obtaining the requisite LP consents prior to the expiration of the Cure Period on September 8, 2024.
114: >
115: > \(d\) **Tabulation and Certification.** C&H will tabulate the LP consents received and prepare a closing certificate confirming that the requisite consent threshold (66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments, excluding GP co-investment) has been satisfied and that the LPA Amendments are effective as of the date specified therein (the \"Closing Certificate\").
116: >
117: > \(e\) **Engagement with IAC Counsel.** C&H will engage with counsel to the Investor Advisory Committee, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, as necessary and appropriate regarding the IAC\'s review of and comments on the proposed Successor Key Person(s), the successor governance framework, and the LPA Amendments. C&H will coordinate with the Clients regarding any modifications to the proposed arrangements that may be requested by the IAC or its counsel.
118: 
119: **[4. Limitations on Scope]{.underline}**
120: 
121: The Clients should be aware of the following limitations on the scope of C&H\'s engagement:
122: 
123: > \(a\) **Cayman Islands Law.** C&H does not provide legal advice regarding the laws of the Cayman Islands. The Clients should consult separately with qualified Cayman Islands counsel regarding any Cayman Islands regulatory, partnership law, or other legal matters that may arise in connection with the Key Person Event or the transactions contemplated by this engagement, including any filings or notifications required under Cayman Islands law in connection with changes to the Fund\'s governance structure.
124: >
125: > \(b\) **Tax Advice.** C&H is not engaged to provide tax advice in connection with this engagement. The Clients should consult their own tax advisors regarding the U.S. federal, state, local, and non-U.S. tax implications of any carried interest reallocation, structural changes to the Fund or DCM, or other transactions contemplated by this engagement.
126: >
127: > \(c\) **Investment Advice.** C&H is not engaged to provide investment advice or to evaluate the investment merits of any portfolio positions held by the Fund. The Clients acknowledge that any decisions regarding the management, disposition, or retention of portfolio positions during the suspension of the Investment Period or otherwise are solely the responsibility of the Clients and their investment professionals.
128: >
129: > \(d\) **Third-Party Service Providers.** C&H does not represent the Fund\'s independent auditor (Graystone & Whitfield LLP), the Fund\'s prime broker (Halcyon Securities International Ltd.), the Administrator, or any other third-party service provider to the Fund or DCM. Each such service provider is represented by its own counsel, and the Clients should not assume that C&H\'s representation extends to any of those parties.
130: >
131: > \(e\) **Litigation and Regulatory Matters.** This engagement does not extend to any litigation, arbitration, regulatory investigation, enforcement action, or other adversarial or contested proceeding, whether existing or threatened, unless separately agreed in writing between C&H and the Clients. In the event any such matter arises during the course of this engagement, C&H will promptly advise the Clients and, if requested, discuss the terms of a separate engagement to address such matter.
132:

Mr. Sutherland will be the Clients\' primary legal point of contact for substantive matters, and all material legal memoranda, draft documents, and advice letters will be reviewed and approved by Mr. Sutherland prior to delivery to the Clients.

Theresa Kim will support Mr. Adler on all workstreams, with particular focus on document drafting and consent solicitation logistics.

155: C&H may assign additional attorneys, paralegals, or other professionals to this engagement as reasonably necessary to ensure the timely and effective completion of the workstreams described herein. C&H will provide prior notice to Ms. Sato before assigning any additional professionals whose time will be billed to the Clients.

158: 
159: **6.1 Hourly Rates**
160: 
161: Services rendered by C&H attorneys in connection with this engagement will be billed on an hourly basis at the following standard rates:
162:

164: >

C&H will provide the Clients with at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of any rate increase. 169: **6.2 Fee Cap**
170: 
171: Total professional fees for the engagement shall not exceed Three Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$385,000) (the \"Fee Cap\") without the prior written consent of the Clients. The Fee Cap encompasses all professional fees of C&H attorneys assigned to this engagement for the workstreams described in Section 3 above. The Fee Cap does not include out-of-pocket disbursements, which are addressed separately in Section 6.3 below.
172: 
173: **6.3 Disbursements and Expenses**
174: 
175: The Clients will reimburse C&H for reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements incurred in connection with this engagement, including, without limitation, costs of document production, photocopying, overnight courier and delivery charges, filing fees, database and research charges, and travel expenses (including airfare, lodging, and ground transportation), if any. All disbursements will be billed at cost, without markup. Disbursements are not subject to the Fee Cap set forth in Section 6.2. C&H will exercise reasonable judgment in incurring disbursements and will obtain the Clients\' prior approval before incurring any single disbursement in excess of Five Thousand Dollars (\$5,000).
176: 
177: **6.4 Billing and Payment**
178: 
179: C&H will issue monthly invoices to DCM at the address set forth in Section 2 above (or to such other address as DCM may designate in writing). Each invoice will include a reasonably detailed description of the services rendered and disbursements incurred during the applicable billing period. Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. C&H reserves the right to suspend the performance of services in the event of non-payment of any invoice for a period exceeding sixty (60) days following the date of such invoice, provided that C&H shall provide at least ten (10) days\' prior written notice to the Clients before exercising such right.
180: 
181: **[7. Governing Law]{.underline}**
182: 
183: This engagement letter and the terms and conditions set forth herein shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflicts of law principles that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.
184: 
185: For the avoidance of doubt, the A&R LPA is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware, and C&H\'s analysis and advice rendered under this engagement with respect to the interpretation and enforcement of the provisions of the A&R LPA, including Section 8.04 and the fiduciary duties of the General Partner, will apply the substantive law of the State of Delaware. Nothing in this Section 7 is intended to alter the governing law of the A&R LPA or any other agreement to which the Clients are a party.
186: 
187: **[8. Conflicts of Interest]{.underline}**
188: 
189: C&H has conducted a conflicts check in accordance with the Firm\'s standard procedures and the applicable rules of professional conduct. Based on the results of that check, C&H confirms that it is not aware of any current conflict of interest that would preclude the Firm from undertaking this engagement on behalf of the Clients.
190: 
191: C&H confirms that it does not currently represent any limited partner of the Fund, any member of the Investor Advisory Committee, or the IAC\'s counsel, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, in any matter related to the Fund, DCM, or the Key Person Event. C&H may represent other clients in matters unrelated to this engagement, and the Clients acknowledge that such representations do not constitute a conflict of interest for purposes of this engagement.
192: 
193: In the event that a conflict of interest arises during the course of this engagement, C&H will promptly notify the Clients and take appropriate steps in accordance with the applicable rules of professional conduct governing attorneys admitted to practice in the State of New York, including, where appropriate, seeking a waiver of the conflict or, if necessary, withdrawing from the engagement.
194: 
195: **[9. Confidentiality]{.underline}**
196: 
197: C&H will maintain the confidentiality of all information received from or on behalf of the Clients in connection with this engagement, consistent with the Firm\'s professional responsibility obligations under the applicable rules of professional conduct and the protections afforded by the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine. C&H will implement reasonable safeguards to protect the confidentiality of such information within the Firm.
198: 
199: Notwithstanding the foregoing, C&H may disclose confidential information: (a) as required by applicable law, regulation, or court order; (b) as authorized or directed by the Clients; or (c) to the extent reasonably necessary in connection with the performance of the services described in this engagement letter, including, without limitation, in communications with the Administrator, counsel to the IAC, or other third parties as directed by the Clients.
200: 
201: **[10. Document Retention]{.underline}**
202: 
203: Upon completion of the engagement, C&H will retain client files (including electronic files) in accordance with the Firm\'s document retention policy, which currently provides for retention of engagement files for a period of ten (10) years from the date of engagement closure. Following the expiration of such retention period, C&H may destroy or dispose of the engagement files without further notice to or consent from the Clients, unless the Clients have previously requested the return of such files.

In the event of termination by either party, the Clients will remain responsible for payment of all fees and disbursements incurred by C&H through the effective date of termination, subject to the Fee Cap set forth in Section 6.2.

C&H\'s obligation to assist in the orderly transition of the matter shall survive the termination of this engagement.
