**[FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE AMENDED AND RESTATED LIMITED PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT OF DRIFTWOOD ABSOLUTE RETURN FUND LTD.]{.underline}**
*Effective as of August 26, 2024*
By and Among
**DRIFTWOOD CAPITAL MANAGEMENT LLC** a Delaware limited liability company, as General Partner
and
**THE LIMITED PARTNERS** of
**DRIFTWOOD ABSOLUTE RETURN FUND LTD.** a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership (Registration No. ELP-87234)
**FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE AMENDED AND RESTATED LIMITED PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT OF DRIFTWOOD ABSOLUTE RETURN FUND LTD.**

This First Amendment (this \"Amendment\") to the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement, dated as of March 15, 2017 (as in effect immediately prior to the effectiveness of this Amendment, the \"Agreement\" or the \"A&R LPA\"), of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd., a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership registered under the Exempted Limited Partnership Law (as revised) of the Cayman Islands under Registration No. ELP-87234 (the \"Partnership\" or \"DARF\"), is entered into as of August 26, 2024 (the \"Amendment Effective Date\"), by and among Driftwood Capital Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (\"DCM\" or the \"General Partner\"), having its principal office at 680 Lexington Avenue, 31st Floor, New York, New York 10022, and the limited partners of the Partnership (each, a \"Limited Partner\" and collectively, the \"Limited Partners\").

The Partnership maintains its registered office at 4th Floor, Harbour Place, 103 South Church Street, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1104, Cayman Islands, and its registered agent is Archipelago Corporate Services Ltd., P.O. Box 2681, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1111, Cayman Islands. The Delaware registered agent of DCM is Capitol Registered Agents, Inc., 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801. The employer identification number of DCM is 82-4917653.
**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, the Partnership was formed as an exempted limited partnership under the laws of the Cayman Islands with an inception date of March 15, 2017, and the parties entered into the A&R LPA on such date, which A&R LPA is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware (Recital A);

**WHEREAS**, pursuant to Section 8.04(a) of the Agreement, Marcus J. Whitmore was designated as the sole \"Key Person\" of the Partnership, and the rights, obligations, and protections associated with the Key Person provisions were established in reliance upon Mr. Whitmore\'s continued active involvement in the management of the Partnership\'s investment portfolio (Recital B);

**WHEREAS**, on June 3, 2024, Marcus J. Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke resulting in his medical incapacitation, and, pursuant to Section 8.04(b) of the Agreement, a Key Person Event was deemed to have occurred effective June 10, 2024, as the Key Person was unable to devote substantially all of his professional time to the affairs of the Partnership for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days following the date of such medical event (Recital C);

**WHEREAS**, as a consequence of the Key Person Event, and in accordance with Section 8.04(c) of the Agreement, the Investment Period was immediately suspended, follow-on investments were capped at Twenty-Eight Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$28,700,000) (representing 1.0% of assets under management as of the most recent net asset value determination), and a ninety (90) calendar day Cure Period commenced on June 10, 2024, such Cure Period being scheduled to expire on September 8, 2024 (Recital D);

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner notified all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners in writing of the Key Person Event on June 14, 2024, within the five (5) business day deadline prescribed by Section 8.04(c) of the Agreement (such deadline being June 17, 2024), and such notices were delivered by electronic mail and overnight courier in accordance with the notice provisions of the Agreement (Recital E);

**WHEREAS**, following the Key Person Event, the General Partner proposed the designation of Elaine R. Sato, Deputy Chief Investment Officer and Managing Member (holding a 10% membership interest) of DCM, and Jonathan K. Huang, Head of Credit Strategies of DCM, as Successor Key Persons pursuant to Section 8.04 of the Agreement, and the General Partner circulated this Amendment to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners on July 15, 2024 for their review and consent (Recital F);

**WHEREAS**, the Investor Advisory Committee of the Partnership (the \"IAC\"), established pursuant to Section 9.02 of the Agreement, reviewed the proposed Amendment at its duly convened meeting on July 29, 2024, at which a quorum was present, and the IAC discussed the qualifications of the proposed Successor Key Persons, the terms of the proposed Investment Committee, the proposed modifications to the Key Person provisions, and the proposed reallocation of carried interest (Recital G);

**WHEREAS**, pursuant to Section 14.01 of the Agreement, amendments to the Agreement require the written consent of Limited Partners holding not less than sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment) (Recital H);

**WHEREAS**, as of the date hereof, aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments for voting purposes equal Two Billion Seven Hundred Ninety-Eight Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$2,798,250,000), being Two Billion Eight Hundred Seventy Million Dollars (\$2,870,000,000) of total net asset value less Fifty-Seven Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$57,400,000) attributable to Marcus J. Whitmore and Fourteen Million Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,350,000) attributable to Elaine R. Sato, each committed through the General Partner vehicle and therefore excluded from the voting base, and the required consent threshold equals One Billion Eight Hundred Sixty-Five Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$1,865,500,000), representing 66⅔% of \$2,798,250,000 (Recital I);

**WHEREAS**, written consents to this Amendment were received from thirty-eight (38) of forty-seven (47) Limited Partners by August 19, 2024, prior to the consent deadline of August 23, 2024, representing aggregate capital commitments of Two Billion Four Hundred Twelve Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,412,800,000), constituting approximately 86.2% of voting Limited Partner capital commitments, which exceeds the required 66⅔% threshold by a substantial margin (Recital J); and

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner desires to amend the Agreement to reflect the designation of Successor Key Persons, the establishment of an Investment Committee, the modification of the Key Person provisions, the reallocation of carried interest among the principals of DCM, and the designation of Marcus J. Whitmore as Senior Advisor to the Partnership, all as more fully set forth herein (Recital K).

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto agree as follows:
**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION]{.underline}**

**Section 1.1 --- Defined Terms.** Unless otherwise defined herein, capitalized terms used in this Amendment shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Agreement. The following new or amended defined terms are hereby added to, or shall replace existing definitions in, Article I of the Agreement, as applicable:
> \(a\) **\"Amendment Effective Date\"** means August 26, 2024.
> \(b\) **\"Investment Committee\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 8.05 of the Agreement, as added by Section 3.1 of this Amendment.

> \(c\) **\"Key Person\"** means, as of the Amendment Effective Date, Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang, jointly. This definition replaces the prior definition of \"Key Person\" in its entirety, pursuant to which Marcus J. Whitmore was designated as the sole Key Person.
> \(d\) **\"Key Person Event\"** has the meaning set forth in amended Section 8.04(b) of the Agreement, as amended by Section 2.2 of this Amendment.
> \(e\) **\"Replacement Period\"** means the one hundred eighty (180) calendar day period described in amended Section 8.04(c)(ii) of the Agreement, as amended by Section 2.3 of this Amendment.
> \(f\) **\"Senior Advisor\"** means Marcus J. Whitmore, in the capacity described in Section 8.06 of the Agreement, as added by Section 4.1 of this Amendment.
> \(g\) **\"Single Key Person Departure\"** has the meaning set forth in amended Section 8.04(b) of the Agreement, as amended by Section 2.2 of this Amendment.
> \(h\) **\"Successor Key Person\"** means each of Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang, designated as such pursuant to Section 8.04(a) of the Agreement as amended by this Amendment.

**Section 1.2 --- Interpretation.** References in this Amendment to \"Sections\" are to Sections of the Agreement as amended by this Amendment, and references to \"Schedules\" are to Schedules of the Agreement as amended by this Amendment, in each case unless the context otherwise requires. The Agreement, as amended by this Amendment, shall be read and construed as one integrated document. In the event of any conflict between the provisions of this Amendment and the provisions of the Agreement as in effect immediately prior to the Amendment Effective Date, the provisions of this Amendment shall control.
**[ARTICLE II --- AMENDMENT OF SECTION 8.04 (KEY PERSON PROVISIONS)]{.underline}**
**Section 2.1 --- Amendment of Section 8.04(a) --- Definition of Key Person.** Section 8.04(a) of the Agreement is hereby amended and restated in its entirety to read as follows:

> \"**Section 8.04(a)** --- *Definition of Key Person.* \'Key Person\' shall mean Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang, jointly. Both Successor Key Persons must remain actively engaged in the management of the Partnership\'s investment portfolio, and each must devote substantially all of his or her respective professional time to the affairs of the Partnership, for the Key Person requirement to be satisfied. For the avoidance of doubt, Marcus J. Whitmore is no longer designated as a Key Person as of the Amendment Effective Date and his designation as Senior Advisor pursuant to Section 8.06 hereof shall not, under any circumstances, be construed as constituting him as a Key Person for any purpose under this Agreement.\"
**Section 2.2 --- Amendment of Section 8.04(b) --- Key Person Event Trigger.** Section 8.04(b) of the Agreement is hereby amended and restated in its entirety to read as follows:

> \"**Section 8.04(b)** --- *Key Person Event.* A \'Key Person Event\' shall be deemed to have occurred if **both** Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang are, at the same time, unable to devote substantially all of their respective professional time to the affairs of the Partnership, by reason of death, permanent disability (as determined in good faith by the General Partner based on medical evidence reasonably available), voluntary or involuntary departure from DCM or the Partnership, termination for cause, or any other cause, for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days. If only **one** of the two Key Persons ceases active involvement in the management of the Partnership\'s investment portfolio for any reason whatsoever (a \'Single Key Person Departure\'), a Key Person Event shall not be deemed to have occurred; provided, however, that the provisions of Section 8.04(c)(ii) (Replacement Period) shall apply in the case of a Single Key Person Departure. The determination of whether a Key Person Event or a Single Key Person Departure has occurred shall be made by the General Partner in good faith, and the General Partner shall promptly notify the Investor Advisory Committee and all Limited Partners of any such determination.\"

**Section 2.3 --- Amendment of Section 8.04(c) --- Consequences of Key Person Event and Single Key Person Departure.** Section 8.04(c) of the Agreement is hereby amended and restated in its entirety to read as follows:
> \"**Section 8.04(c)** --- *Consequences of Key Person Event and Single Key Person Departure.*

> **(i) Full Key Person Event (Both Key Persons).** Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event (i.e., both Key Persons ceasing active involvement simultaneously or within seven (7) consecutive calendar days of each other):
> \(A\) the Investment Period shall be immediately suspended, and no new investments shall be permitted during the period of such suspension;

> \(B\) follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions shall be capped at Fourteen Million Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,350,000), representing 0.5% of assets under management as of the most recent net asset value determination available at the time of the Key Person Event (for the avoidance of doubt, this cap replaces the prior cap of \$28,700,000 representing 1.0% of assets under management that was applicable under the Agreement as in effect prior to the Amendment Effective Date);

> \(C\) the General Partner shall notify all Limited Partners in writing within five (5) business days of the occurrence of the Key Person Event, setting forth in reasonable detail the circumstances giving rise to the Key Person Event and the General Partner\'s initial assessment of the impact on the Partnership\'s investment activities;

> \(D\) a Cure Period of ninety (90) calendar days shall commence on the date of the Key Person Event, during which the General Partner may propose one or more replacement Key Persons for approval by the Limited Partners;

> \(E\) approval of any proposed replacement Key Person shall require the written consent of Limited Partners holding not less than sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment), such consent to be solicited in writing in accordance with the notice provisions of the Agreement; and

> \(F\) if no replacement Key Person is approved within the Cure Period, Limited Partners holding a majority-in-interest of aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment) may elect, by written notice delivered to the General Partner within thirty (30) calendar days following the expiration of the Cure Period, to (x) extend the Cure Period by up to ninety (90) additional calendar days on the same terms set forth in this Section 8.04(c)(i), or (y) direct the General Partner to commence an orderly wind-down of the Partnership in accordance with Section 12.01 of this Agreement.
> **(ii) Single Key Person Departure (One Key Person).** Upon the occurrence of a Single Key Person Departure (i.e., only one of the two Key Persons ceasing active involvement):
> \(A\) the Investment Period shall **not** be automatically suspended;
> \(B\) a Replacement Period of one hundred eighty (180) calendar days shall commence on the date of the Single Key Person Departure;

> \(C\) during the Replacement Period, the remaining Key Person shall continue to manage the Partnership\'s investments in the ordinary course, subject to oversight by the Investment Committee established under Section 8.05 of this Agreement, and the remaining Key Person shall not have the authority to make any new investment or commitment in excess of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000) without the prior approval of the Investment Committee;

> \(D\) during the Replacement Period, the General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to identify and propose a replacement for the departed Key Person, and any such proposed replacement shall be subject to approval by Limited Partners holding not less than sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment);

> \(E\) follow-on investments during the Replacement Period shall be capped at Fourteen Million Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,350,000), representing 0.5% of assets under management as of the most recent net asset value determination;

> \(F\) the General Partner shall notify all Limited Partners in writing within five (5) business days of a Single Key Person Departure, setting forth in reasonable detail the circumstances giving rise to the Single Key Person Departure, the identity of the remaining Key Person, and the General Partner\'s plan for identifying a replacement Key Person; and

> \(G\) if no replacement Key Person is approved prior to the expiration of the Replacement Period, a Key Person Event shall be deemed to have occurred on the date of such expiration, and the provisions of Section 8.04(c)(i) shall thereupon apply as if such Key Person Event had occurred on such date.\"
**[ARTICLE III --- ADDITION OF SECTION 8.05 (INVESTMENT COMMITTEE)]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- New Section 8.05.** A new Section 8.05 is hereby added to the Agreement immediately following Section 8.04 (as amended by Article II of this Amendment), which Section 8.05 shall read in its entirety as follows:
> \"**Section 8.05** --- *Investment Committee.*

> **(a) Establishment.** Effective as of the Amendment Effective Date, the General Partner shall establish an Investment Committee of the Partnership (the \'Investment Committee\'). The Investment Committee shall be a standing committee of the Partnership and shall continue in existence for so long as the Partnership continues to conduct investment operations.
> **(b) Composition.** The Investment Committee shall consist of three (3) members, as follows:
> \(i\) Elaine R. Sato, who shall serve as Chair of the Investment Committee and who shall preside over all meetings of the Investment Committee;
> \(ii\) Jonathan K. Huang, who shall serve as a member of the Investment Committee; and

> \(iii\) one independent member (the \'IAC-Designated Member\') to be designated by a majority vote of the members of the Investor Advisory Committee established under Section 9.02 of this Agreement, such designation to occur within sixty (60) days of the Amendment Effective Date. The IAC-Designated Member shall be a natural person who is not an employee, officer, member, partner, or affiliate of the General Partner, DCM, or any of their respective affiliates. The IAC-Designated Member shall serve at the pleasure of the Investor Advisory Committee and may be removed and replaced by a majority vote of the IAC members at any time.

> Vacancies on the Investment Committee arising by reason of death, resignation, removal, or incapacity of any member shall be filled in the same manner as the original appointment of such member (i.e., vacancies in positions (i) or (ii) above shall be filled by the General Partner, and vacancies in position (iii) shall be filled by a majority vote of the Investor Advisory Committee). Any vacancy shall be filled within thirty (30) calendar days of its occurrence, and pending the filling of any vacancy, the remaining members of the Investment Committee shall continue to exercise the authority and functions of the Investment Committee.

> **(c) Authority and Functions.** The Investment Committee shall oversee the investment activities of the Partnership, including, without limitation, the review and approval of all new investments, all material follow-on investments, all material dispositions of portfolio investments, and all other material portfolio decisions as determined in good faith by the Chair of the Investment Committee. All investment decisions requiring Investment Committee approval shall require the affirmative vote of at least two (2) of the three (3) members of the Investment Committee. In the event of a tie or deadlock, the Chair of the Investment Committee shall not have a casting vote, and the matter shall be tabled for further discussion at the next meeting of the Investment Committee unless the Chair determines, in her reasonable judgment, that the matter requires immediate action to protect the interests of the Partnership, in which case the Chair may take such action as she deems reasonably necessary and shall promptly report such action to the full Investment Committee and the Investor Advisory Committee.

> The Investment Committee shall meet not less frequently than monthly, either in person or by telephonic or video conference, and shall keep written minutes of its proceedings, which minutes shall be made available to the Investor Advisory Committee upon request.

> **(d) Reporting.** The Investment Committee shall provide quarterly written reports to the Investor Advisory Committee and to all Limited Partners summarizing the activities and investment decisions of the Investment Committee during the preceding quarter, including a summary of all new investments approved, all investments declined, all material portfolio actions taken, and any other matters the Investment Committee deems relevant to the Limited Partners\' understanding of the Partnership\'s investment activities. Such quarterly reports shall be delivered within thirty (30) calendar days following the end of each calendar quarter.\"
**[ARTICLE IV --- ADDITION OF SECTION 8.06 (SENIOR ADVISOR)]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- New Section 8.06.** A new Section 8.06 is hereby added to the Agreement immediately following Section 8.05 (as added by Article III of this Amendment), which Section 8.06 shall read in its entirety as follows:
> \"**Section 8.06** --- *Senior Advisor.*

> **(a) Designation.** Marcus J. Whitmore is hereby designated as \'Senior Advisor\' to the Partnership, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date, in recognition of his foundational role in establishing and building the Partnership and his contributions to the Partnership\'s investment strategy and performance since inception.

> **(b) Role and Limitations.** The Senior Advisor shall have no governance authority, voting rights, or decision-making power with respect to the Partnership\'s investments, operations, or other affairs. The Senior Advisor shall not serve as a member of the Investment Committee. The Senior Advisor shall not have the authority to bind the Partnership or the General Partner in any respect, and shall not hold himself out as having any such authority. The Senior Advisor may, at the request of the General Partner (acting through its authorized officers), provide non-binding advisory input on investment strategy, portfolio construction, risk management, or such other matters as the General Partner may reasonably request from time to time, but the Senior Advisor shall have no obligation to provide any such advisory input, and any advisory input provided by the Senior Advisor shall be solely for informational purposes and shall not be binding on the General Partner, the Investment Committee, or the Partnership.

> For the avoidance of doubt, the designation of Marcus J. Whitmore as Senior Advisor does not constitute the Senior Advisor as a Key Person, general partner, managing member, officer, director, or employee of the Partnership or DCM, and shall not give rise to any fiduciary duty or obligation on the part of the Senior Advisor to the Partnership, the General Partner, or any Limited Partner, except to the extent that the Senior Advisor\'s continued status as a Managing Member of DCM may give rise to obligations under DCM\'s operating agreement or applicable law.

> **(c) Compensation and Carried Interest.** The Senior Advisor\'s carried interest entitlement shall be as set forth in amended Schedule A to this Agreement, as amended by Section 5.1 of this Amendment. The Senior Advisor\'s carried interest shall vest in accordance with the schedule set forth in Section 5.2 of this Amendment. The Senior Advisor shall not be entitled to any management fee, salary, bonus, or other compensation from the Partnership or DCM in respect of his role as Senior Advisor, except for the carried interest allocation described in this Section 8.06(c) and in Schedule A.\"
**[ARTICLE V --- AMENDMENT OF SCHEDULE A (CARRIED INTEREST ALLOCATION)]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Amended Schedule A.** Schedule A to the Agreement (Carried Interest Allocation) is hereby amended and restated in its entirety, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date, as set forth in Exhibit A attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference. For convenience of reference, the material terms of the amended carried interest allocation are summarized as follows:

The General Partner\'s aggregate incentive allocation shall remain at twenty percent (20%) of net new profits above the high-water mark, subject to the six percent (6%) annualized hurdle rate with full catch-up, as provided in the Agreement. This Amendment does not modify the aggregate incentive allocation or the hurdle rate and catch-up provisions. The internal allocation of the General Partner\'s twenty percent (20%) incentive allocation among the principals of DCM shall be as follows, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date:
**Individual**       **Role**               **Pre-Amendment Allocation**                         **Post-Amendment Allocation**
Marcus J. Whitmore   Senior Advisor         18% of GP\'s 20% (= 3.6% of net new fund profits)    9% of GP\'s 20% (= 1.8% of net new fund profits)
Elaine R. Sato       Key Person, IC Chair   1.5% of GP\'s 20% (= 0.3% of net new fund profits)   7% of GP\'s 20% (= 1.4% of net new fund profits)
Jonathan K. Huang    Key Person             0.5% of GP\'s 20% (= 0.1% of net new fund profits)   4% of GP\'s 20% (= 0.8% of net new fund profits)

For the avoidance of doubt, the GP-level total incentive allocation of twenty percent (20%) of net new fund profits above the high-water mark is unchanged by this Amendment. The reallocation set forth in this Section 5.1 affects only the internal allocation of the General Partner\'s incentive allocation among the individual principals of DCM and does not alter the aggregate economics payable by the Partnership to the General Partner.

**Section 5.2 --- Whitmore Carried Interest Vesting Schedule.** Marcus J. Whitmore\'s accrued and future carried interest entitlement under amended Schedule A shall vest in accordance with the following schedule:

> \(a\) **Immediate Vesting.** Fifty percent (50%) of the carried interest accrued to the account of Marcus J. Whitmore as of June 10, 2024 (the date of the Key Person Event) shall vest immediately as of the Amendment Effective Date. For purposes of this Section 5.2(a), the amount of accrued carried interest as of June 10, 2024 shall be determined by the Fund Administrator based on the net asset value of the Partnership as of such date, calculated in accordance with the valuation provisions of the Agreement.

> \(b\) **Ratable Vesting.** The remaining fifty percent (50%) of such accrued carried interest, together with any carried interest accruing on or after June 10, 2024 attributable to the Senior Advisor\'s nine percent (9%) allocation under amended Schedule A, shall vest ratably on a monthly basis over a period of thirty-six (36) months commencing on June 10, 2024. Specifically, one thirty-sixth (1/36th) of such carried interest shall vest on the 10th day of each calendar month following June 10, 2024, with the first installment having vested on July 10, 2024 and the final installment vesting on June 10, 2027. For the avoidance of doubt, installments that vested prior to the Amendment Effective Date pursuant to the foregoing schedule shall be deemed to have vested retroactively as of the applicable vesting date.

> \(c\) **Acceleration Upon Death.** In the event of the Senior Advisor\'s death during the thirty-six (36) month vesting period described in Section 5.2(b), all unvested carried interest of the Senior Advisor shall immediately vest in full as of the date of the Senior Advisor\'s death and shall be payable to the Senior Advisor\'s estate or designated beneficiary in accordance with the distribution provisions of the Agreement.

> \(d\) **Payment of Vested Carried Interest.** Vested carried interest of the Senior Advisor shall be payable in accordance with the distribution provisions of Section 6.03 of the Agreement, subject to the clawback provisions of Section 6.04 of the Agreement. Unvested carried interest shall not be distributable and shall remain subject to the vesting schedule set forth in this Section 5.2 until vested in accordance with its terms.

**Section 5.3 --- No Change to Management Fee.** For the avoidance of doubt, this Amendment does not modify the management fee of two percent (2.0%) of net asset value per annum, payable quarterly in advance, or any other fee provisions of the Agreement. The management fee shall continue to be calculated and payable in accordance with the terms of the Agreement as in effect immediately prior to the Amendment Effective Date.
**[ARTICLE VI --- AMENDMENT OF SECTION 14.01 (AMENDMENTS)]{.underline}**
**Section 6.1 --- Conforming Amendment to Section 14.01.** Section 14.01 of the Agreement is hereby amended to add the following proviso at the end of the first sentence thereof:

> \"; *provided, further,* that any future amendment to Section 8.04 (Key Person Provisions), Section 8.05 (Investment Committee), Section 8.06 (Senior Advisor), or Schedule A (Carried Interest Allocation) of this Agreement (each as amended by the First Amendment to this Agreement dated as of August 26, 2024) shall require the written consent of Limited Partners holding not less than sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment), and in no event shall any such amendment be effected by the consent of the General Partner alone or by action of the Investment Committee.\"
**[ARTICLE VII --- CONFIRMATION OF LP CONSENT]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- LP Consent.** The General Partner hereby confirms that, in accordance with Section 14.01 of the Agreement, the requisite consent of the Limited Partners to this Amendment has been obtained, as follows:

> \(a\) This Amendment was circulated to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners on July 15, 2024, together with explanatory materials, a summary of the proposed changes, biographical information regarding the proposed Successor Key Persons, and a form of written consent.
> \(b\) The consent deadline established by the General Partner was August 23, 2024, being forty (40) calendar days from the date of circulation.
> \(c\) Written consents were received from thirty-eight (38) of forty-seven (47) Limited Partners by August 19, 2024, four (4) calendar days prior to the consent deadline.

> \(d\) The consenting Limited Partners represent aggregate capital commitments of Two Billion Four Hundred Twelve Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,412,800,000), constituting approximately 86.2% of voting Limited Partner capital commitments of Two Billion Seven Hundred Ninety-Eight Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$2,798,250,000).

> \(e\) This percentage exceeds the required threshold of sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%), which equals One Billion Eight Hundred Sixty-Five Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$1,865,500,000).

> \(f\) Accordingly, the requisite consent has been duly obtained, and this Amendment is effective as of August 26, 2024. Nine (9) Limited Partners did not return written consents by the consent deadline; the failure of such Limited Partners to return written consents shall not affect the validity or enforceability of this Amendment.

**Section 7.2 --- Investor Advisory Committee Review.** The Investor Advisory Committee of the Partnership, consisting of the following members, reviewed and discussed the proposed Amendment at its duly convened meeting on July 29, 2024:

> \(b\) Richard Oshima, Sycamore Endowment Partners LP;
> \(c\) Catherine Mercer, Velthorn Institutional Fund of Funds III, L.P.;
> \(d\) Thomas Ashworth, Bridlewood Family Office Holdings Ltd.; and
> \(e\) Nadia Al-Rashid, Atlas Sovereign Wealth Advisory LLC.

All five (5) members of the IAC were present at the July 29, 2024 meeting, either in person or by video conference. The IAC reviewed the qualifications and experience of the proposed Successor Key Persons, the terms of the proposed Investment Committee, the proposed modifications to the Key Person provisions (including the new Single Key Person Departure and Replacement Period framework), the proposed reallocation of carried interest, and the proposed designation of Marcus J. Whitmore as Senior Advisor. The IAC did not raise any objection to the proposed Amendment and expressed its support for the General Partner\'s proposal. The IAC\'s review was advisory in nature, and the IAC did not have approval rights with respect to this Amendment.
**[ARTICLE VIII --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES OF THE GENERAL PARTNER]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Authority.** DCM represents and warrants that it has full power and authority to execute and deliver this Amendment on behalf of the Partnership. This Amendment has been duly authorized by all necessary action on the part of DCM, including without limitation the approval of the Managing Members of DCM, and the execution, delivery, and performance of this Amendment by DCM do not require any further action, approval, or consent on the part of DCM or any of its members. Elaine R. Sato, the person executing this Amendment on behalf of DCM in her capacity as Deputy Chief Investment Officer and Managing Member, is duly authorized to execute and deliver this Amendment on behalf of DCM and the Partnership.

**Section 8.2 --- No Conflict.** The execution, delivery, and performance of this Amendment by DCM does not and will not (a) conflict with or result in a breach of any term or provision of the Amended and Restated Limited Liability Company Operating Agreement of DCM, dated as of March 15, 2017, or any other organizational document of DCM, (b) conflict with or result in a breach of, or constitute a default under, any agreement, contract, indenture, or other instrument to which DCM or the Partnership is a party or by which DCM, the Partnership, or any of their respective assets is bound, or (c) violate any applicable law, rule, regulation, order, judgment, or decree of any governmental authority having jurisdiction over DCM, the Partnership, or any of their respective assets.

**Section 8.3 --- Valid and Binding.** This Amendment constitutes a valid and binding obligation of DCM and the Partnership, enforceable against DCM and the Partnership in accordance with its terms, subject to (a) applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, fraudulent transfer, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally, (b) general principles of equity (regardless of whether such enforceability is considered in a proceeding in equity or at law), and (c) the implied covenant of good faith and fair dealing.

The Agreement, as amended by this Amendment, is hereby ratified and confirmed as the governing document of the Partnership. On and after the Amendment Effective Date, each reference in the Agreement to \"this Agreement,\" \"hereunder,\" \"hereof,\" \"herein,\" or words of similar import shall be deemed to refer to the Agreement as amended by this Amendment, unless the context otherwise requires.

**Section 9.2 --- Governing Law.** This Amendment shall be governed by, and construed and enforced in accordance with, the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to the conflicts of law principles thereof that would require the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. Each of the parties hereto irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the State of Delaware and the United States District Court for the District of Delaware for the purposes of any action, suit, or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Amendment, and each party irrevocably waives any objection to the laying of venue of any such action, suit, or proceeding in any such court.

**Section 9.3 --- Entire Agreement.** The Agreement, as amended by this Amendment, constitutes the entire agreement among the parties hereto with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior agreements, understandings, negotiations, and representations, whether written or oral, with respect to such subject matter. No party has relied on any statement, representation, warranty, or agreement of any other party except for those expressly set forth in the Agreement as amended by this Amendment.

**Section 9.4 --- Counterparts.** This Amendment may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of a signature page to this Amendment by facsimile, electronic mail (including .pdf or any electronic signature complying with the U.S. federal ESIGN Act of 2000 or the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act), or other electronic transmission shall be effective as delivery of an originally executed counterpart.

**Section 9.5 --- Severability.** If any provision of this Amendment (or any portion thereof) is held by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable in any respect, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision (or the remaining portion of the affected provision) of this Amendment, and this Amendment shall be construed as if such invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision (or portion thereof) had never been contained herein, so long as the economic or legal substance of the transactions contemplated hereby is not affected in any manner materially adverse to any party.

**Section 9.6 --- Notices.** All notices, requests, demands, consents, waivers, and other communications required or permitted under this Amendment shall be in writing and shall be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions set forth in Section 13.01 of the Agreement. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Marcus J. Whitmore is an intended third-party beneficiary of Section 8.06 (Senior Advisor) and Section 5.2 (Whitmore Carried Interest Vesting Schedule) of this Amendment with respect to his rights as Senior Advisor and the vesting of his carried interest, and Marcus J. Whitmore shall be entitled to enforce the provisions of such Sections as if he were a party to this Amendment.

27: This memorandum documents the formal closing and termination of Matter No. 1026-00001 and is prepared in accordance with Calderwood & Harkness LLP\'s matter closing policies and procedures. The purpose of this memorandum is to create a comprehensive record of the work performed, the status of all documents and deliverables, the financial summary of the engagement, and the circumstances surrounding the termination of the matter, so that the firm\'s files may be properly closed and archived.

29: The matter involved the representation of Briarwood Family Office LLC (\"BFO\") in the negotiation of a side letter in connection with a proposed Seventy-Five Million Dollar (\$75,000,000) limited partnership commitment to Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. (\"Fund IV\" or the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership managed by Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC (\"MPCA\" or the \"Sponsor\"). Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") was retained to review the Fund\'s offering and governing documents, advise BFO on the terms thereof, negotiate a side letter containing customized economic, governance, and reporting provisions on BFO\'s behalf, and review and mark up the subscription documents in anticipation of the commitment.
30: 
31: On April 2, 2024, BFO\'s investment committee reconvened and voted to decline the proposed commitment to Fund IV. On April 3, 2024, Sandra M. Whitfield, General Counsel of BFO, notified the undersigned of BFO\'s decision and instructed C&H to transmit a formal withdrawal letter to counsel for the Fund\'s general partner and to the Sponsor. On April 4, 2024, the undersigned transmitted such withdrawal letter, confirming that all draft side-letter provisions had lapsed without execution, that no subscription agreement had been executed, and that no capital commitment had been made by BFO to Fund IV.

No subscription agreement was executed, and no capital commitment of any kind was made by BFO to Fund IV or to any affiliated vehicle.

**[MATTER CLOSING MEMORANDUM]{.underline}**
**[Matter No. 1026-00001]{.underline}**
**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** 425 Lexington Avenue New York, NY 10017
**INTERNAL MEMORANDUM --- PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL**

This memorandum constitutes attorney work product and is protected by the attorney-client privilege and the work product doctrine. It is intended solely for internal use by the attorneys and professional staff of Calderwood & Harkness LLP involved in this matter. This memorandum should not be disclosed to any third party without the prior written consent of the Responsible Partner.
**Date:** April 5, 2024
**To:** File --- Matter No. 1026-00001
**From:** Pamela Cross, Responsible Partner, Funds & Asset Management
**Re:** Matter Closing Memorandum --- Briarwood Family Office LLC / Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. --- Side-Letter Negotiation
**Matter Number:** 1026-00001
**Status:** CLOSED --- TERMINATED
**[1. Purpose]{.underline}**

This memorandum documents the formal closing and termination of Matter No. 1026-00001 and is prepared in accordance with Calderwood & Harkness LLP\'s matter closing policies and procedures. The purpose of this memorandum is to create a comprehensive record of the work performed, the status of all documents and deliverables, the financial summary of the engagement, and the circumstances surrounding the termination of the matter, so that the firm\'s files may be properly closed and archived.

The matter involved the representation of Briarwood Family Office LLC (\"BFO\") in the negotiation of a side letter in connection with a proposed Seventy-Five Million Dollar (\$75,000,000) limited partnership commitment to Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. (\"Fund IV\" or the \"Fund\"), a Delaware limited partnership managed by Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC (\"MPCA\" or the \"Sponsor\"). Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") was retained to review the Fund\'s offering and governing documents, advise BFO on the terms thereof, negotiate a side letter containing customized economic, governance, and reporting provisions on BFO\'s behalf, and review and mark up the subscription documents in anticipation of the commitment.

On April 2, 2024, BFO\'s investment committee reconvened and voted to decline the proposed commitment to Fund IV. On April 3, 2024, Sandra M. Whitfield, General Counsel of BFO, notified the undersigned of BFO\'s decision and instructed C&H to transmit a formal withdrawal letter to counsel for the Fund\'s general partner and to the Sponsor. On April 4, 2024, the undersigned transmitted such withdrawal letter, confirming that all draft side-letter provisions had lapsed without execution, that no subscription agreement had been executed, and that no capital commitment had been made by BFO to Fund IV.

As a consequence of BFO\'s decision, all draft side-letter provisions --- including, without limitation, the most favored nation rights, excuse and exclusion rights, management fee concessions, co-investment rights, enhanced reporting obligations, key person enhancements, transfer rights, confidentiality carve-outs, tax reporting commitments, and placement fee offset provisions that had been the subject of negotiation over the preceding approximately ten weeks --- lapsed and are of no further force or effect. No subscription agreement was executed, and no capital commitment of any kind was made by BFO to Fund IV or to any affiliated vehicle.
This matter is hereby closed effective as of the date hereof.
**[2. Client Information]{.underline}**
**Client:** Briarwood Family Office LLC
**Entity Type:** Delaware limited liability company
**Principal Business Address:** 780 Park Avenue, Suite 3200, New York, NY 10021
**Registered Agent:** Capitol Registered Agents Inc., 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801
**Employer Identification Number (EIN):** 27-4831956
**Assets Under Management:** Approximately \$1.8 billion (as of December 31, 2023, per information provided by BFO)
**Primary Contacts:**

> • **Julian R. Hargrove** --- Managing Director & Chief Investment Officer. Mr. Hargrove serves as the principal decision-maker for BFO\'s investment activities and holds a veto right over all investment committee determinations. He was the ultimate authority on the proposed commitment to Fund IV and participated in strategic discussions regarding the scope and priority of side-letter negotiations.

> • **Sandra M. Whitfield** --- General Counsel. Ms. Whitfield served as BFO\'s primary point of contact with C&H throughout the engagement. She executed the engagement letter on behalf of BFO on January 24, 2024, and communicated BFO\'s instructions, feedback, and ultimate decision to decline the commitment. All formal communications between C&H and BFO were directed through Ms. Whitfield.

> • **Derek T. Calloway** --- Director of External Investments. Mr. Calloway was responsible for BFO\'s evaluation of the Fund IV opportunity from an investment and due diligence perspective. He participated in the four-party conference call on March 11, 2024 and provided input on the commercial terms of the side letter, including fee economics and co-investment structuring.
> • **Renata Vasquez** --- Investment Analyst. Ms. Vasquez supported Mr. Calloway in the due diligence process and served as a secondary contact for document production and information requests.

**Client Background:** BFO is a single-family office established in 2007 for the purpose of managing the wealth of the Hargrove family. The Hargrove family\'s wealth was principally derived from commercial real estate development activities in the northeastern United States, including the development and management of office, mixed-use, and multifamily properties across the greater New York metropolitan area and New England. BFO\'s investment strategy encompasses four primary verticals: (i) direct real estate investments, (ii) real estate credit strategies, (iii) private equity, and (iv) liquid alternatives. BFO typically allocates between fifteen percent (15%) and twenty percent (20%) of its total assets under management to third-party managed funds, with a preference for commingled vehicles managed by established sponsors with demonstrated track records. The proposed commitment to Fund IV fell within this allocation strategy and was consistent with BFO\'s historical appetite for institutional-quality real estate private equity vehicles.
**[3. Counterparty and Fund Information]{.underline}**
**[3.1 Fund Sponsor]{.underline}**
**Name:** Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC (\"MPCA\")
**Entity Type:** Delaware limited liability company
**Employer Identification Number (EIN):** 45-3297104

**Co-Founders:**
> • **Conrad J. Ellsworth** --- Managing Partner & Chief Executive Officer
> • **Priya Narayan** --- Managing Partner & Chief Investment Officer

**Firm Overview:** MPCA was founded in 2011 and operates as a mid-market private equity firm focused on value-add and opportunistic real estate investments, real estate operating companies, and asset-management platform acquisitions across North America. Since its founding, MPCA has raised and managed three prior funds (Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund I, L.P.; Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund II, L.P.; and Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund III, L.P.), which in the aggregate have attracted approximately \$3.2 billion in limited partner commitments. MPCA\'s investment team is based primarily in Boston, with additional professionals in New York and Los Angeles. Mr. Ellsworth and Ms. Narayan serve as the key persons for Fund IV, and their continued involvement was a significant focus of the side-letter negotiation as described in Section 5.2 of this memorandum.

1: PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL --- ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION
2: 
3: **CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** **Counselors at Law**
4: 
5: 125 Broad Street, 44th Floor New York, New York 10004
6: 
7: Telephone: (212) 558-4000 Facsimile: (212) 558-3588 www.calderwoodharkness.com
8: 
9: July 14, 2022
10: 
11: Marcus J. Calloway Founder & Chief Investment Officer Ironside Capital Management LP 590 Madison Avenue, 38th Floor New York, New York 10022
12: 
13: > **Re:** Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP by Ironside Capital Management LP --- Co-Investment Vehicle Formation and Related Matters
14: >
15: > **Matter Number:** 1023-00001
16: 
17: Dear Mr. Calloway:
18: 
19: We are pleased that Ironside Capital Management LP has selected Calderwood & Harkness LLP to serve as its outside legal counsel in connection with the co-investment opportunity described below. This letter sets forth the terms and conditions of our engagement and the scope of the legal services we will provide. We ask that you review this letter carefully and, if the terms are acceptable, countersign and return a copy to us as described in Section 9 below. We look forward to working with you and your team on this important transaction.
20: 
21: **[1. Engagement and Scope of Representation]{.underline}**
22: 
23: Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Ironside Capital Management LP (\"Ironside\" or the \"Client\"), a Delaware limited partnership, to serve as outside legal counsel in connection with the matters described in Sections 1.1 through 1.4 below (collectively, the \"Engagement\"). The scope of representation is subject to the limitations set forth in Section 1.5. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, the Firm\'s representation shall be limited to the specific matters described herein and shall not extend to other legal matters of the Client or any of its affiliates.
24: 
25: **1.1 Formation of the Co-Investment Vehicle**
26: 
27: The Firm will advise and assist the Client with the formation and organization of a Delaware limited partnership co-investment vehicle, which is expected to be named \"ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP\" (or such other name as the parties may agree upon) (the \"Co-Investment Vehicle\"). The Co-Investment Vehicle is being formed to co-invest alongside Meridian Infrastructure Partners Fund IV, LP (\"Fund IV\") in connection with the proposed acquisition of one hundred percent (100%) of the issued and outstanding equity interests of Cascadia Renewables Holdings, Inc. (\"Cascadia\"), an Oregon corporation engaged in the development, construction, and operation of renewable energy generation assets in the Pacific Northwest. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, our work in connection with the formation of the Co-Investment Vehicle is expected to include the following:
28: 
29: > \(a\) Preparation and filing of the Certificate of Limited Partnership of the Co-Investment Vehicle with the Office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, including coordination with a registered agent in Delaware and ensuring compliance with all applicable filing requirements under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act (6 Del. C. §§ 17-101 *et seq.*);
30: >
31: > \(b\) Negotiation, drafting, and review of the Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Co-Investment Vehicle (the \"LPA\"), including provisions relating to capital commitments, capital calls, management and governance, distributions (including the distribution waterfall), carried interest allocations, fees and expenses, transfer restrictions, key-person provisions, default remedies, reporting obligations, term and dissolution, indemnification, and such other terms as may be agreed upon by the parties;
32: >
33: > \(c\) Negotiation and drafting of the Side Letter between Ironside and Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC (the \"GP\"), in its capacity as the general partner of both Fund IV and the Co-Investment Vehicle, addressing, among other things, co-investor protections, most-favored-nation rights, information rights, consent rights, and any other supplemental terms applicable to Ironside\'s participation in the Co-Investment Vehicle;
34: >
35: > \(d\) Negotiation and review of the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement between Fund IV and the Co-Investment Vehicle, which is expected to set forth the terms and conditions governing the allocation of the co-investment opportunity, including the relative commitments, co-investment allocation methodology, expense-sharing arrangements, and the rights and obligations of Fund IV and the Co-Investment Vehicle with respect to the Cascadia investment;
36: >
37: > \(e\) Review and comment on subscription documentation, including subscription agreements, investor questionnaires, accredited investor representations, and related admission documents for limited partners of the Co-Investment Vehicle;
38: >
39: > \(f\) Review and comment on placement agent arrangements, including the engagement letter, distribution agreement, or other arrangements with Rivermark Capital Markets Inc. (\"Rivermark\"), as the placement agent retained in connection with the syndication of co-investment interests in the Co-Investment Vehicle, to the extent applicable to Ironside\'s participation;
40: >
41: > \(g\) Anti-money laundering (\"AML\") and know-your-customer (\"KYC\") certifications and compliance procedures for the Co-Investment Vehicle, including review of applicable requirements under the Bank Secrecy Act, the USA PATRIOT Act, and related regulations, and assistance with the preparation and filing of any necessary certifications, representations, or reports in connection therewith; and
42: >
43: > \(h\) Such other matters as may be reasonably necessary or desirable in connection with the formation and organization of the Co-Investment Vehicle.
44: 
45: **1.2 Transaction Diligence and Documentation**
46: 
47: The Firm will advise and assist the Client in connection with the legal due diligence and transaction documentation relating to the proposed acquisition of Cascadia by Fund IV and the Co-Investment Vehicle (the \"Transaction\"). Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, our work in connection with the Transaction is expected to include the following:
48: 
49: > \(a\) Legal due diligence review of Cascadia and its direct and indirect subsidiaries (collectively, the \"Tarvex Group\") in connection with the proposed acquisition, including review of corporate organizational documents, material contracts, real property interests, intellectual property, permits and licenses, environmental matters, employment matters, litigation and pending claims, regulatory compliance, tax matters, and such other areas as may be identified during the course of the diligence process. The Firm anticipates coordinating its diligence efforts with the broader diligence workstream being managed by Breckenridge Sloane & Pratt LLP (\"BSP\") on behalf of Meridian Infrastructure Partners LP (\"Meridian\") as lead sponsor of the Transaction;
50: >
51: > \(b\) Review, negotiation, and comment on the Equity Purchase Agreement (the \"Purchase Agreement\") and related transaction documentation (including disclosure schedules, ancillary agreements, officer\'s certificates, and closing deliverables), to the extent that Ironside\'s interests as co-investor require separate or supplemental representation beyond the work being performed by BSP on behalf of Meridian. The Client acknowledges that BSP is serving as lead transaction counsel to the buy-side and that the Firm\'s role with respect to the Purchase Agreement is supplemental in nature, focused on ensuring that Ironside\'s specific interests, rights, and obligations as co-investor are adequately addressed;
52: >
53: > \(c\) Review and analysis of the debt commitment letter, credit agreement documentation (including any term loan, revolving credit facility, or other debt instruments), and related intercreditor or subordination arrangements, as they affect the Co-Investment Vehicle\'s rights, obligations, and economic interests. The Firm\'s review of debt documentation will focus on the implications for the Co-Investment Vehicle and will be coordinated with counsel to the lenders and with BSP, as appropriate;
54: >
55: > \(d\) Review and analysis of the terms, conditions, and coverage of the representations and warranties insurance (\"RWI\") policy being procured in connection with the Transaction, including assessment of any exclusions, retention amounts, coverage limitations, or subrogation provisions that may affect the Co-Investment Vehicle\'s rights in the event of a breach of representations and warranties by the sellers; and
56: >
57: > \(e\) Such other transaction-related matters as may arise and as may be reasonably necessary to protect Ironside\'s interests as co-investor in the Transaction.
58: 
59: **1.3 Regulatory Matters**
60: 
61: The Firm will advise and assist the Client in connection with the analysis and assessment of regulatory approvals and filings required for the consummation of the Transaction, as they affect Ironside\'s co-investment position. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, our work in connection with regulatory matters is expected to include the following:
62: 
63: > \(a\) Analysis and advice regarding the requirements for, and the preparation of, filings with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (\"FERC\") under the Federal Power Act and related regulations, to the extent that the Transaction or Ironside\'s participation therein triggers FERC filing or approval requirements;
64: >
65: > \(b\) Analysis and advice regarding the requirements for, and the preparation of, filings with the Oregon Public Utility Commission (\"OPUC\") under applicable Oregon statutes and regulations, including any change-of-control or transfer-of-ownership filings that may be required in connection with the Transaction;
66: >
67: > \(c\) Analysis and advice regarding the requirements for, and the preparation of, any voluntary or mandatory filings with the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (\"CFIUS\") under Section 721 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, and the implementing regulations thereof (31 C.F.R. Part 800 *et seq.*), to the extent that any limited partner of the Co-Investment Vehicle or any other participant in the Transaction may be a foreign person or foreign-controlled entity within the meaning of the applicable regulations, and to the extent that Cascadia\'s assets or operations may involve critical infrastructure or other sensitive areas subject to CFIUS jurisdiction;
68: >
69: > \(d\) Coordination with BSP, as counsel to Meridian, on regulatory filing strategy, including the sequencing and timing of regulatory filings, the allocation of responsibility for the preparation and submission of filings, and the management of any regulatory review or comment process; and
70: >
71: > \(e\) Such other regulatory matters as may arise in connection with the Transaction and as may be reasonably necessary to protect Ironside\'s interests.
72: 
73: **1.4 Governance and Ongoing Matters**
74: 
75: Following the formation of the Co-Investment Vehicle and the closing of the Transaction, the Firm will continue to advise and assist the Client with respect to the governance, administration, and ongoing legal needs of the Co-Investment Vehicle, including, without limitation, the following:
76: 
77: > \(a\) Ongoing advice on the governance of the Co-Investment Vehicle, including matters relating to capital calls, distributions, investor communications and reporting, advisory committee proceedings, consent solicitations, and limited partner relations;
78: >
79: > \(b\) Tax structuring analysis and ongoing tax advice relating to the Co-Investment Vehicle, including advice on federal, state, and local tax matters, partnership tax allocations, withholding obligations, UBTI analysis, and any tax elections or filings to be made by or on behalf of the Co-Investment Vehicle. Tax advice will be provided in coordination with the Firm\'s Tax Practice Group, led by Ms. Sylvia Hartwell;
80: >
81: > \(c\) Analysis under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), and the regulations promulgated thereunder, including the \"plan assets\" rules under 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101, to determine whether the assets of the Co-Investment Vehicle constitute \"plan assets\" for purposes of ERISA and Section 4975 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\"), and advice regarding the \"benefit plan investor\" limitations and the availability of any applicable exemptions (including the \"venture capital operating company\" and \"real estate operating company\" exemptions);
82: >
83: > \(d\) Ongoing entity maintenance and compliance for the Co-Investment Vehicle, including the timely filing of Delaware franchise tax returns, annual reports, and any other periodic filings required to maintain the Co-Investment Vehicle\'s good standing in Delaware and any other jurisdiction in which it is qualified to do business, as well as coordination with the registered agent in Delaware;
84: >
85: > \(e\) Advice on dormancy management, wind-down, dissolution, or reactivation of the Co-Investment Vehicle, as circumstances may require, including the preparation and filing of any necessary certificates of cancellation, final tax returns, or other dissolution-related documents; and
86: >
87: > \(f\) Such other ongoing matters as may arise from time to time in connection with the Co-Investment Vehicle or Ironside\'s participation therein.
88: 
89: **1.5 Limitations on Scope**
90: 
91: The Client acknowledges and agrees that the scope of the Firm\'s representation is limited to the matters described in Sections 1.1 through 1.4 above. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the Client acknowledges the following:
92: 
93: > \(a\) C&H does not represent, and has not been engaged to represent, Meridian Infrastructure Partners LP, Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC, Fund IV, Cascadia Renewables Holdings, Inc., any member of the Tarvex Group, the selling shareholders of Cascadia (including, without limitation, Timberline Growth Equity Fund III, LP and the Weir Family Trust), Rivermark Capital Markets Inc., or any other party to the Transaction (collectively, the \"Other Parties\"). The Firm\'s duties and obligations run solely to the Client, and the Firm will exercise its independent professional judgment in advising the Client, even where the interests of the Client and the Other Parties may be aligned;
94: >
95: > \(b\) The Client is aware that each of the Other Parties is separately represented by its own legal counsel:
96: >
97: > \(i\) Meridian Infrastructure Partners LP and its affiliates (including Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC and Fund IV) are represented by Breckenridge Sloane & Pratt LLP, with Charles A. Delacroix serving as lead partner;
98: >
99: > \(ii\) Cascadia Renewables Holdings, Inc. is represented by Ridgeway, Ashford & Malone PC, with Nina R. Castellano serving as lead partner; and
100: >
101: > \(iii\) Timberline Growth Equity Fund III, LP (as a selling shareholder) is represented by Garvey Lennox LLP, with Steven F. Yun serving as lead partner.
102: >
103: > \(c\) C&H\'s representation of the Client is limited to the matters expressly described in this engagement letter and does not extend to any general corporate, regulatory, compliance, litigation, employment, intellectual property, or other legal matters of Ironside or any of its affiliated entities, funds, portfolio companies, general partners, officers, directors, employees, or agents, unless separately agreed in a written engagement letter or amendment to this engagement letter.
104: 
105: **[2. Responsible Attorneys]{.underline}**
106:

219: The Firm will maintain all files, documents, and records relating to this Engagement (whether in physical or electronic form) in accordance with the Firm\'s standard document retention policies as in effect from time to time. Upon the conclusion of the Engagement, whether by completion of the matters described herein, termination pursuant to Section 7, or otherwise, the Firm will retain files relating to the Engagement for a period of not less than seven (7) years from the date of conclusion of the Engagement.
