**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** **Counselors at Law**
125 Broad Street, 44th Floor New York, New York 10004
Telephone: (212) 558-4000 Facsimile: (212) 558-3588 www.calderwoodharkness.com
Marcus J. Calloway Founder & Chief Investment Officer Ironside Capital Management LP 590 Madison Avenue, 38th Floor New York, New York 10022
> **Re:** Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP by Ironside Capital Management LP --- Co-Investment Vehicle Formation and Related Matters
> **Matter Number:** 1023-00001
Dear Mr. Calloway:

We are pleased that Ironside Capital Management LP has selected Calderwood & Harkness LLP to serve as its outside legal counsel in connection with the co-investment opportunity described below. This letter sets forth the terms and conditions of our engagement and the scope of the legal services we will provide. We ask that you review this letter carefully and, if the terms are acceptable, countersign and return a copy to us as described in Section 9 below. We look forward to working with you and your team on this important transaction.
**[1. Engagement and Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Ironside Capital Management LP (\"Ironside\" or the \"Client\"), a Delaware limited partnership, to serve as outside legal counsel in connection with the matters described in Sections 1.1 through 1.4 below (collectively, the \"Engagement\"). The scope of representation is subject to the limitations set forth in Section 1.5. Unless otherwise agreed in writing, the Firm\'s representation shall be limited to the specific matters described herein and shall not extend to other legal matters of the Client or any of its affiliates.
**1.1 Formation of the Co-Investment Vehicle**

The Firm will advise and assist the Client with the formation and organization of a Delaware limited partnership co-investment vehicle, which is expected to be named \"ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP\" (or such other name as the parties may agree upon) (the \"Co-Investment Vehicle\"). The Co-Investment Vehicle is being formed to co-invest alongside Meridian Infrastructure Partners Fund IV, LP (\"Fund IV\") in connection with the proposed acquisition of one hundred percent (100%) of the issued and outstanding equity interests of Cascadia Renewables Holdings, Inc. (\"Cascadia\"), an Oregon corporation engaged in the development, construction, and operation of renewable energy generation assets in the Pacific Northwest. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, our work in connection with the formation of the Co-Investment Vehicle is expected to include the following:

> \(a\) Preparation and filing of the Certificate of Limited Partnership of the Co-Investment Vehicle with the Office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, including coordination with a registered agent in Delaware and ensuring compliance with all applicable filing requirements under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act (6 Del. C. §§ 17-101 *et seq.*);

> \(b\) Negotiation, drafting, and review of the Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Co-Investment Vehicle (the \"LPA\"), including provisions relating to capital commitments, capital calls, management and governance, distributions (including the distribution waterfall), carried interest allocations, fees and expenses, transfer restrictions, key-person provisions, default remedies, reporting obligations, term and dissolution, indemnification, and such other terms as may be agreed upon by the parties;

> \(c\) Negotiation and drafting of the Side Letter between Ironside and Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC (the \"GP\"), in its capacity as the general partner of both Fund IV and the Co-Investment Vehicle, addressing, among other things, co-investor protections, most-favored-nation rights, information rights, consent rights, and any other supplemental terms applicable to Ironside\'s participation in the Co-Investment Vehicle;

> \(d\) Negotiation and review of the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement between Fund IV and the Co-Investment Vehicle, which is expected to set forth the terms and conditions governing the allocation of the co-investment opportunity, including the relative commitments, co-investment allocation methodology, expense-sharing arrangements, and the rights and obligations of Fund IV and the Co-Investment Vehicle with respect to the Cascadia investment;

> \(e\) Review and comment on subscription documentation, including subscription agreements, investor questionnaires, accredited investor representations, and related admission documents for limited partners of the Co-Investment Vehicle;

> \(f\) Review and comment on placement agent arrangements, including the engagement letter, distribution agreement, or other arrangements with Rivermark Capital Markets Inc. (\"Rivermark\"), as the placement agent retained in connection with the syndication of co-investment interests in the Co-Investment Vehicle, to the extent applicable to Ironside\'s participation;

> \(g\) Anti-money laundering (\"AML\") and know-your-customer (\"KYC\") certifications and compliance procedures for the Co-Investment Vehicle, including review of applicable requirements under the Bank Secrecy Act, the USA PATRIOT Act, and related regulations, and assistance with the preparation and filing of any necessary certifications, representations, or reports in connection therewith; and
> \(h\) Such other matters as may be reasonably necessary or desirable in connection with the formation and organization of the Co-Investment Vehicle.
**1.2 Transaction Diligence and Documentation**

The Firm will advise and assist the Client in connection with the legal due diligence and transaction documentation relating to the proposed acquisition of Cascadia by Fund IV and the Co-Investment Vehicle (the \"Transaction\"). Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, our work in connection with the Transaction is expected to include the following:

> \(a\) Legal due diligence review of Cascadia and its direct and indirect subsidiaries (collectively, the \"Tarvex Group\") in connection with the proposed acquisition, including review of corporate organizational documents, material contracts, real property interests, intellectual property, permits and licenses, environmental matters, employment matters, litigation and pending claims, regulatory compliance, tax matters, and such other areas as may be identified during the course of the diligence process. The Firm anticipates coordinating its diligence efforts with the broader diligence workstream being managed by Breckenridge Sloane & Pratt LLP (\"BSP\") on behalf of Meridian Infrastructure Partners LP (\"Meridian\") as lead sponsor of the Transaction;

> \(b\) Review, negotiation, and comment on the Equity Purchase Agreement (the \"Purchase Agreement\") and related transaction documentation (including disclosure schedules, ancillary agreements, officer\'s certificates, and closing deliverables), to the extent that Ironside\'s interests as co-investor require separate or supplemental representation beyond the work being performed by BSP on behalf of Meridian. The Client acknowledges that BSP is serving as lead transaction counsel to the buy-side and that the Firm\'s role with respect to the Purchase Agreement is supplemental in nature, focused on ensuring that Ironside\'s specific interests, rights, and obligations as co-investor are adequately addressed;

> \(c\) Review and analysis of the debt commitment letter, credit agreement documentation (including any term loan, revolving credit facility, or other debt instruments), and related intercreditor or subordination arrangements, as they affect the Co-Investment Vehicle\'s rights, obligations, and economic interests. The Firm\'s review of debt documentation will focus on the implications for the Co-Investment Vehicle and will be coordinated with counsel to the lenders and with BSP, as appropriate;

> \(d\) Review and analysis of the terms, conditions, and coverage of the representations and warranties insurance (\"RWI\") policy being procured in connection with the Transaction, including assessment of any exclusions, retention amounts, coverage limitations, or subrogation provisions that may affect the Co-Investment Vehicle\'s rights in the event of a breach of representations and warranties by the sellers; and
> \(e\) Such other transaction-related matters as may arise and as may be reasonably necessary to protect Ironside\'s interests as co-investor in the Transaction.
**1.3 Regulatory Matters**

The Firm will advise and assist the Client in connection with the analysis and assessment of regulatory approvals and filings required for the consummation of the Transaction, as they affect Ironside\'s co-investment position. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, our work in connection with regulatory matters is expected to include the following:

> \(a\) Analysis and advice regarding the requirements for, and the preparation of, filings with the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (\"FERC\") under the Federal Power Act and related regulations, to the extent that the Transaction or Ironside\'s participation therein triggers FERC filing or approval requirements;

> \(b\) Analysis and advice regarding the requirements for, and the preparation of, filings with the Oregon Public Utility Commission (\"OPUC\") under applicable Oregon statutes and regulations, including any change-of-control or transfer-of-ownership filings that may be required in connection with the Transaction;

> \(c\) Analysis and advice regarding the requirements for, and the preparation of, any voluntary or mandatory filings with the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States (\"CFIUS\") under Section 721 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as amended, and the implementing regulations thereof (31 C.F.R. Part 800 *et seq.*), to the extent that any limited partner of the Co-Investment Vehicle or any other participant in the Transaction may be a foreign person or foreign-controlled entity within the meaning of the applicable regulations, and to the extent that Cascadia\'s assets or operations may involve critical infrastructure or other sensitive areas subject to CFIUS jurisdiction;

> \(d\) Coordination with BSP, as counsel to Meridian, on regulatory filing strategy, including the sequencing and timing of regulatory filings, the allocation of responsibility for the preparation and submission of filings, and the management of any regulatory review or comment process; and
> \(e\) Such other regulatory matters as may arise in connection with the Transaction and as may be reasonably necessary to protect Ironside\'s interests.
**1.4 Governance and Ongoing Matters**

Following the formation of the Co-Investment Vehicle and the closing of the Transaction, the Firm will continue to advise and assist the Client with respect to the governance, administration, and ongoing legal needs of the Co-Investment Vehicle, including, without limitation, the following:

> \(a\) Ongoing advice on the governance of the Co-Investment Vehicle, including matters relating to capital calls, distributions, investor communications and reporting, advisory committee proceedings, consent solicitations, and limited partner relations;

> \(b\) Tax structuring analysis and ongoing tax advice relating to the Co-Investment Vehicle, including advice on federal, state, and local tax matters, partnership tax allocations, withholding obligations, UBTI analysis, and any tax elections or filings to be made by or on behalf of the Co-Investment Vehicle. Tax advice will be provided in coordination with the Firm\'s Tax Practice Group, led by Ms. Sylvia Hartwell;

> \(c\) Analysis under the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), and the regulations promulgated thereunder, including the \"plan assets\" rules under 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101, to determine whether the assets of the Co-Investment Vehicle constitute \"plan assets\" for purposes of ERISA and Section 4975 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\"), and advice regarding the \"benefit plan investor\" limitations and the availability of any applicable exemptions (including the \"venture capital operating company\" and \"real estate operating company\" exemptions);

> \(d\) Ongoing entity maintenance and compliance for the Co-Investment Vehicle, including the timely filing of Delaware franchise tax returns, annual reports, and any other periodic filings required to maintain the Co-Investment Vehicle\'s good standing in Delaware and any other jurisdiction in which it is qualified to do business, as well as coordination with the registered agent in Delaware;

> \(e\) Advice on dormancy management, wind-down, dissolution, or reactivation of the Co-Investment Vehicle, as circumstances may require, including the preparation and filing of any necessary certificates of cancellation, final tax returns, or other dissolution-related documents; and
> \(f\) Such other ongoing matters as may arise from time to time in connection with the Co-Investment Vehicle or Ironside\'s participation therein.
**1.5 Limitations on Scope**

The Client acknowledges and agrees that the scope of the Firm\'s representation is limited to the matters described in Sections 1.1 through 1.4 above. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the Client acknowledges the following:

> \(a\) C&H does not represent, and has not been engaged to represent, Meridian Infrastructure Partners LP, Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC, Fund IV, Cascadia Renewables Holdings, Inc., any member of the Tarvex Group, the selling shareholders of Cascadia (including, without limitation, Timberline Growth Equity Fund III, LP and the Weir Family Trust), Rivermark Capital Markets Inc., or any other party to the Transaction (collectively, the \"Other Parties\"). The Firm\'s duties and obligations run solely to the Client, and the Firm will exercise its independent professional judgment in advising the Client, even where the interests of the Client and the Other Parties may be aligned;
> \(b\) The Client is aware that each of the Other Parties is separately represented by its own legal counsel:

> \(i\) Meridian Infrastructure Partners LP and its affiliates (including Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC and Fund IV) are represented by Breckenridge Sloane & Pratt LLP, with Charles A. Delacroix serving as lead partner;
> \(ii\) Cascadia Renewables Holdings, Inc. is represented by Ridgeway, Ashford & Malone PC, with Nina R. Castellano serving as lead partner; and
> \(iii\) Timberline Growth Equity Fund III, LP (as a selling shareholder) is represented by Garvey Lennox LLP, with Steven F. Yun serving as lead partner.

> \(c\) C&H\'s representation of the Client is limited to the matters expressly described in this engagement letter and does not extend to any general corporate, regulatory, compliance, litigation, employment, intellectual property, or other legal matters of Ironside or any of its affiliated entities, funds, portfolio companies, general partners, officers, directors, employees, or agents, unless separately agreed in a written engagement letter or amendment to this engagement letter.
**[2. Responsible Attorneys]{.underline}**
The following attorneys have been assigned to the Engagement and will have primary responsibility for the delivery of legal services to the Client:

**Responsible Partner:** Pamela Cross, Partner, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Ms. Cross will have overall supervisory responsibility for the Engagement and will serve as the primary relationship partner for Ironside. Ms. Cross brings more than twenty years of experience advising institutional investors, fund sponsors, and asset managers on fund formation, co-investment structuring, and complex transactional matters. She will be available to the Client for strategic guidance, senior-level negotiations, and resolution of any significant issues that may arise during the course of the Engagement.

**Billing Partner:** Nicholas Stern, Partner, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Stern will serve as the billing partner and will be responsible for staffing, billing, day-to-day management, and overall work coordination for the Engagement. Mr. Stern has extensive experience in the formation and structuring of private equity, infrastructure, and co-investment vehicles, and in the negotiation of fund documentation and side letters on behalf of institutional investors and sponsors.

**Lead Associate:** Theresa Kim, Associate, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Ms. Kim will serve as the lead associate on the matter and will be the primary day-to-day contact for Ironside\'s deal team. Ms. Kim will be responsible for the preparation of initial drafts of fund formation documents, coordination of the diligence process, management of the document production and review workflow, and regular communication with the Client regarding the status of the Engagement.

**Working Associate:** Owen Fischer, Associate, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group. Mr. Fischer will provide additional associate-level support as needed, including assistance with due diligence, regulatory analysis, document review, and drafting of ancillary transaction documents.

**Tax Specialist:** Sylvia Hartwell, Partner, Tax Practice Group. Ms. Hartwell will advise the Client on tax structuring, partnership tax matters, federal and state income tax issues, and state and local tax considerations relating to the Co-Investment Vehicle. Ms. Hartwell has deep expertise in the taxation of private investment funds and co-investment vehicles and will coordinate closely with the Funds & Asset Management team to ensure that the structure of the Co-Investment Vehicle is optimized from a tax perspective.

The Firm reserves the right to assign additional attorneys, paralegals, legal assistants, and other professional staff to the Engagement as the scope of work requires, in order to provide the Client with the most efficient and effective representation possible. The Firm will keep the Client informed of any significant changes in staffing, and the Firm will endeavor to maintain continuity of the core team throughout the Engagement.
**[3. Fees and Billing Arrangements]{.underline}**
**3.1 Hourly Rates**

Fees for legal services rendered in connection with this Engagement will be charged on an hourly basis at the Firm\'s standard rates in effect at the time the services are rendered. The Firm\'s hourly rates are reviewed and adjusted annually, with adjustments typically taking effect on January 1 of each calendar year. The Firm will provide the Client with prior written notice of any rate adjustments. Current standard hourly rate ranges for the categories of professionals assigned to this matter are as follows:
**Professional Category**           **Hourly Rate Range**
Senior Associates                   \$950 -- \$1,250
Associates                          \$725 -- \$950
Paralegals / Legal Assistants       \$375 -- \$475
The specific hourly rates applicable to the attorneys currently assigned to this matter are set forth below:
**Attorney**            **Role**                   **Current Hourly Rate**
Pamela Cross            Responsible Partner        \$1,800
Nicholas Stern          Billing Partner            \$1,750
Sylvia Hartwell         Tax Specialist (Partner)   \$1,650
Theresa Kim             Lead Associate             \$1,100
Owen Fischer            Working Associate          \$850

Rates for any additional attorneys, paralegals, or other professionals assigned to the Engagement will be communicated to the Client upon assignment and will be consistent with the Firm\'s standard rate schedule for professionals of comparable seniority and experience. The rates set forth above are subject to annual adjustment as described in this Section 3.1.
**3.2 Disbursements and Expenses**

In addition to professional fees, the Client will be responsible for reimbursement of all reasonable disbursements and out-of-pocket expenses incurred by the Firm in connection with the Engagement. Such disbursements and expenses may include, but are not limited to, the following:

> \(a\) Filing fees payable to the Delaware Secretary of State, FERC, OPUC, CFIUS, or any other governmental authority in connection with filings made on behalf of the Client or the Co-Investment Vehicle;

> \(b\) Travel expenses, including airfare, ground transportation, lodging, and meals, incurred in connection with the Engagement (travel expenses will be incurred in accordance with the Firm\'s standard travel policies and, to the extent practicable, will be pre-approved by the Client for any single trip expected to exceed \$5,000);
> \(c\) Overnight delivery, courier, and postage charges;
> \(d\) Photocopying, printing, and document production costs;
> \(e\) Online legal research charges (including Westlaw, Sundial Solutions, and other legal databases);
> \(f\) Long-distance telephone and conference call charges; and
> \(g\) Other third-party costs and vendor charges reasonably incurred in connection with the Engagement.

Third-party vendor costs, including without limitation the costs of filing agents, registered agent services, and any other vendors engaged by the Firm on behalf of the Client, will be passed through to the Client at the Firm\'s actual cost, without markup.
**3.3 Billing Cycle and Payment Terms**

Invoices for professional fees and disbursements will be rendered on a monthly basis, or at such other intervals as the Firm and the Client may agree in writing. Each invoice will contain a reasonably detailed description of the services rendered and the expenses incurred during the applicable billing period, organized by timekeeper and date of service.

Payment of each invoice is due within thirty (30) days of the date of the invoice. Payments should be made by wire transfer or check to the account specified on the invoice. The Firm reserves the right to charge interest at the rate of one percent (1.0%) per month (equivalent to twelve percent (12%) per annum) on any invoice or portion thereof that remains unpaid for more than sixty (60) days from the date of the invoice; *provided*, *however*, that no interest will accrue on any amount that is the subject of a good-faith billing dispute raised by the Client in writing within thirty (30) days of the Client\'s receipt of the applicable invoice. The Firm and the Client agree to work cooperatively and in good faith to resolve any billing disputes promptly.
**3.4 Fee Estimates**

The Firm does not provide fee caps, fixed-fee arrangements, or \"not-to-exceed\" budgets for this Engagement. The nature and complexity of fund formation and co-investment structuring matters, and the transactional and regulatory work associated with a transaction of this magnitude, make it impracticable to predict total legal fees with certainty at the outset of the Engagement.

However, the Firm is prepared to provide the Client with periodic, non-binding estimates of anticipated fees for specific phases of the work upon request. Such estimates will be based on the Firm\'s best assessment of the work required at the time of the estimate and will be subject to revision as the scope and complexity of the Engagement evolve. The Client acknowledges and agrees that actual fees will depend on, among other things, the scope and complexity of the matters as they develop, the extent and depth of the legal due diligence required, the pace and complexity of negotiations among the parties, the nature and timing of regulatory filings and approvals, and any dormancy, reactivation, or wind-down proceedings relating to the Co-Investment Vehicle that may arise during the term of the Engagement.
**[4. Client Identification and Conflicts]{.underline}**

The Client for purposes of this Engagement is Ironside Capital Management LP, a Delaware limited partnership. The Firm\'s representation does not extend to any affiliated entities, funds (including any predecessor or successor funds managed or advised by Ironside), portfolio companies, general or limited partners, or individual officers, directors, members, managers, employees, or agents of Ironside, except as may be separately agreed in a written engagement letter or amendment to this engagement letter.

The Firm has conducted a conflicts check in accordance with its standard conflicts clearance procedures as of the date hereof and has determined that no conflict of interest exists that would prevent the Firm from undertaking this representation under applicable rules of professional conduct, including the New York Rules of Professional Conduct. The Firm\'s conflicts clearance memorandum (dated July 14, 2022) covers the following parties and their respective principals and affiliates identified to date: Ironside Capital Management LP; Meridian Infrastructure Partners LP; Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC; Meridian Infrastructure Partners Fund IV, LP; Cascadia Renewables Holdings, Inc.; Timberline Growth Equity Fund III, LP; and the Weir Family Trust. If additional parties or counterparties are identified during the course of the Engagement, the Firm will conduct supplemental conflicts checks as appropriate.

The Client acknowledges that Calderwood & Harkness LLP is a large, diversified law firm with hundreds of attorneys and numerous clients across a wide range of industries and practice areas. The Client understands and agrees that the Firm may currently represent, or may in the future represent, other entities, funds, or individuals whose interests may differ from or be adverse to those of Ironside in matters unrelated to this Engagement. The Firm does not, by reason of this Engagement, undertake any obligation to decline or withdraw from the representation of any other client in any matter not substantially related to this Engagement. The Firm will at all times comply with its ethical obligations and the applicable rules of professional conduct in managing any situations that may arise involving the concurrent representation of clients with differing interests.
**[5. Confidentiality]{.underline}**

All information provided by the Client to the Firm in connection with this Engagement, including without limitation documents, financial data, business plans, investment strategies, investor information, term sheets, and communications of every kind and nature (collectively, \"Confidential Information\"), and all work product generated by the Firm in connection with this Engagement (including memoranda, draft documents, legal analyses, and advice), will be treated as confidential and will be protected to the fullest extent permitted by law, including pursuant to the attorney-client privilege, the work-product doctrine, and any other applicable privilege or protection.

The Firm will not disclose Confidential Information to any third party without the Client\'s prior written consent, except (a) as required by applicable law, court order, or legal process; (b) as required by the applicable rules of professional conduct; or (c) to the Firm\'s own partners, associates, paralegals, staff, and professional advisors who have a need to know such information in connection with the Engagement and who are bound by obligations of confidentiality.

The Client hereby authorizes the Firm to share Confidential Information as reasonably necessary with the following parties and their respective counsel, to the extent reasonably required in connection with the Transaction and the formation and operation of the Co-Investment Vehicle:
> \(a\) Breckenridge Sloane & Pratt LLP, as counsel to Meridian Infrastructure Partners LP, Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC, and Fund IV;
> \(b\) Ridgeway, Ashford & Malone PC, as counsel to Cascadia Renewables Holdings, Inc.;
> \(c\) Garvey Lennox LLP, as counsel to Timberline Growth Equity Fund III, LP;
> \(d\) Rivermark Capital Markets Inc., as placement agent for the Co-Investment Vehicle; and
> \(e\) Other transaction parties, co-investors, lenders, insurers, accountants, and professional advisors, to the extent reasonably required in connection with the Transaction.

Such sharing of information shall be subject to any applicable confidentiality agreements, non-disclosure agreements, or common-interest agreements that may be in effect among the parties. The Firm will use reasonable efforts to ensure that any Confidential Information shared pursuant to this authorization is subject to appropriate confidentiality protections.
**[6. Document Retention]{.underline}**

The Firm will maintain all files, documents, and records relating to this Engagement (whether in physical or electronic form) in accordance with the Firm\'s standard document retention policies as in effect from time to time. Upon the conclusion of the Engagement, whether by completion of the matters described herein, termination pursuant to Section 7, or otherwise, the Firm will retain files relating to the Engagement for a period of not less than seven (7) years from the date of conclusion of the Engagement. Following the expiration of such seven-year period, the Firm may, in its discretion, destroy or dispose of such files without further notice to the Client, unless the Client has, prior to the expiration of such period, made a written request for the return of the files.

The Client may request the return of original documents, including but not limited to executed agreements, certificates, corporate records, and other original instruments, at any time during or after the Engagement. The Firm will comply with any such request within a reasonable period of time, and the Client will bear any reasonable costs associated with the retrieval, copying, and delivery of such documents.

The Firm may retain copies (including electronic copies) of all documents in the Client\'s files for the Firm\'s own records and for compliance with applicable legal and professional obligations, notwithstanding the return of original documents to the Client.
**[7. Termination]{.underline}**

Either the Client or the Firm may terminate this Engagement at any time upon written notice to the other party. The Client\'s right to terminate is absolute. The Firm\'s right to terminate is subject to the Firm\'s obligations under applicable rules of professional conduct, including the obligation to provide reasonable notice to the Client and to take steps to the extent reasonably practicable to protect the Client\'s interests (including the avoidance of prejudice to the Client) in connection with any such termination.

Upon termination of the Engagement by either party, the Client will remain responsible for the payment of all professional fees and expenses incurred by the Firm through the date of termination, in accordance with the billing and payment terms set forth in Section 3 of this engagement letter. The Firm will render a final invoice promptly following the effective date of termination, and payment of such final invoice will be due in accordance with the payment terms set forth herein.

Upon termination, the Firm will cooperate fully in the orderly transition of the matter to successor counsel designated by the Client, if applicable, including by making available to successor counsel all files, documents, and work product relating to the Engagement (subject to payment of all outstanding fees and expenses) and by providing such reasonable assistance as successor counsel may request to facilitate a seamless transition.

The provisions of this engagement letter relating to payment of fees and expenses (Section 3), confidentiality (Section 5), document retention (Section 6), and governing law (Section 8) shall survive the termination of the Engagement.
**[8. Governing Law]{.underline}**

This engagement letter, and the relationship between the Firm and the Client arising hereunder, shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of Delaware, without giving effect to any choice-of-law or conflict-of-laws rules or provisions (whether of the State of Delaware or any other jurisdiction) that would cause the application of the laws of any jurisdiction other than the State of Delaware. The parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in the State of Delaware for the resolution of any disputes arising out of or relating to this engagement letter or the Engagement.
**[9. Acknowledgment and Acceptance]{.underline}**

We are delighted to have the opportunity to represent Ironside Capital Management LP in connection with this important co-investment opportunity and look forward to a productive working relationship. If the terms set forth in this engagement letter are acceptable to you, please confirm your agreement by countersigning and returning a copy of this letter to the undersigned at Calderwood & Harkness LLP, 125 Broad Street, 44th Floor, New York, New York 10004, or by email to Pamela Cross (pcross@calderwoodharkness.com) and Nicholas Stern (nstern@calderwoodharkness.com). Your countersignature will constitute your acknowledgment and acceptance of the terms and conditions of this engagement letter.

If you have any questions regarding the terms of this letter, or if you would like to discuss any aspect of the Engagement, please do not hesitate to contact either of us directly. We are available at your convenience.
Very truly yours,
**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP**
Pamela Cross Partner, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group Telephone: (212) 558-4112
Email: pcross@calderwoodharkness.com
Nicholas Stern Partner, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group Telephone: (212) 558-4247

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner and the Limited Partner desire to form a limited partnership under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, 6 Del. C. §§ 17-101, *et seq.* (the \"Act\"), for the purpose set forth herein;

**WHEREAS**, the terms of the co-investment between the Partnership and Fund IV are governed by a Co-Investment Allocation Agreement of even date herewith (the \"Co-Investment Allocation Agreement\");

180: 
181: The economic terms of the Vehicle have been negotiated to reflect the co-investment nature of the arrangement and are significantly more favorable to Ironside than the standard economic terms applicable to Fund IV\'s main limited partnership. The key economic terms are summarized below:
182: 
183: **Management Fee.** No management fee (0%) is charged on the Vehicle. The Side Letter expressly confirms that no management fee, monitoring fee, or similar ongoing fee is payable by the Partnership to the General Partner or any of its affiliates in connection with the Vehicle. This is a material economic benefit to Ironside, as Fund IV\'s main limited partnership is subject to a management fee of 2% per annum on committed capital during the investment period and 2% per annum on invested capital thereafter.
184: 
185: **Carried Interest.** The General Partner is entitled to a carried interest of 10% of net profits above the preferred return, as compared to the 20% carried interest applicable in Fund IV\'s main limited partnership. The reduced carried interest rate reflects the co-investment nature of the Vehicle and Ironside\'s significant capital commitment. The carried interest is subject to the distribution waterfall mechanics described in Section XI of this memorandum.
186: 
187: **Preferred Return.** The Limited Partner and the General Partner are entitled to a preferred return of 8% per annum, compounded quarterly, on their respective contributed capital. The preferred return must be satisfied in full before any carried interest is payable to the General Partner.

189: **GP Commitment.** The General Partner has committed \$30,000 (0.01% of total committed capital) as its capital contribution to the Partnership. 201: **[A. General Partner Authority (§3.01 of LP Agreement)]{.underline}**

Specifically, the General Partner\'s authority includes, without limitation, the following:
204: 
205: > \(a\) making, monitoring, and disposing of the Partnership\'s investment in Cascadia, including all decisions relating to the acquisition, post-closing management, restructuring, refinancing, and ultimate disposition of the investment;
206: >
207: > \(b\) issuing capital calls to the partners and managing capital contributions in accordance with the terms of the LP Agreement;
208: >
209: > \(c\) making distributions to the partners in accordance with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.01 of the LP Agreement;
210: >
211: > \(d\) executing transaction documents on behalf of the Partnership, including the Equity Purchase Agreement, ancillary acquisition agreements, financing agreements, and all other instruments and documents necessary or desirable in connection with the Cascadia acquisition;
212: >
213: > \(e\) engaging service providers on behalf of the Partnership, including fund administrators, independent auditors, tax preparers, legal counsel, valuation consultants, and any other advisors or consultants deemed necessary or appropriate by the General Partner;
214: >
215: > \(f\) incurring and paying expenses on behalf of the Partnership, including organizational expenses, ongoing operating expenses, and transaction-related expenses;
216: >
217: > \(g\) taking all actions necessary or desirable in connection with the Cascadia acquisition, including the negotiation and execution of the Equity Purchase Agreement, the stockholders\' agreement, the management services agreement, and all related transaction documents; and
218: >
219: > \(h\) generally taking all actions that the General Partner deems necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes of the Partnership and to protect the Partnership\'s investment.
220: 
221: The General Partner acts through its managers --- David R. Hargreaves (Managing Partner), Lillian Fong (Partner, Portfolio), and Graham Whitfield (Partner, Operations) --- or such other authorized officers or representatives as the managers may designate from time to time in accordance with the GP\'s operating agreement. Decisions of the General Partner are made by majority vote of the managers, except as otherwise provided in the GP\'s operating agreement.
222: 
223: **[B. Limitations on GP Authority]{.underline}**
224: 
225: Notwithstanding the broad grant of authority to the General Partner described above, the LP Agreement imposes certain limitations on the General Partner\'s authority. Specifically, the General Partner may not take any of the following actions without the prior written consent of the Limited Partner (Ironside):
226: 
227: > \(a\) amend, modify, or waive any provision of the LP Agreement or the Side Letter;
228: >
229: > \(b\) admit additional limited partners to the Partnership;
230: >
231: > \(c\) increase the aggregate capital commitments of the Partnership beyond \$300,000,000;
232: >
233: > \(d\) merge, consolidate, or convert the Partnership into another entity or form of organization;
234: >
235: > \(e\) voluntarily file for bankruptcy, make an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or consent to the appointment of a receiver or trustee for the Partnership or any substantial part of its assets;
236: >
237: > \(f\) enter into any related-party transaction (including any transaction with the General Partner, its affiliates, Fund IV, or their respective principals, officers, or employees) that is not expressly contemplated by the LP Agreement or the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement; and
238: >
239: > \(g\) extend the investment period or term of the Partnership beyond the limits set forth in the LP Agreement.
240: 
241: These consent requirements are designed to protect Ironside\'s interests as the sole limited partner and to ensure that the General Partner does not take any material action that could adversely affect Ironside\'s investment without Ironside\'s knowledge and approval. The consent requirements are consistent with market practice for single-LP co-investment vehicles and reflect the negotiated balance of authority between the General Partner and the Limited Partner.
242: 
243: **[C. LP Advisory Committee]{.underline}**
244: 
245: No formal Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") is established under the LP Agreement. The absence of a formal LPAC is appropriate given the single-LP structure of the Vehicle --- there is no need for a committee to represent the interests of multiple limited partners, as Ironside is the sole limited partner and has direct consent rights on all material matters.
246: 
247: In lieu of a formal LPAC, the Side Letter provides for direct consultation between the General Partner and Ironside on material matters affecting the Partnership and its investment. The GP has agreed to consult with Ironside in good faith on matters that would customarily be brought before an LPAC in a multi-investor fund, including conflict-of-interest matters, related-party transactions, valuation issues, and material deviations from the investment thesis.
248: 
249: **[D. Investment Decisions]{.underline}**
250: 
251: All investment decisions relating to the Partnership\'s investment in Cascadia are made by the General Partner in its sole discretion, subject to the limitations described in Section IV.B above. This includes decisions relating to the initial acquisition of Cascadia, any post-closing add-on investments or capital expenditures at the portfolio-company level, any restructuring, recapitalization, or refinancing of Cascadia, and any ultimate disposition or exit of the investment.
252: 
253: The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement governs the parallel investment mechanics between Fund IV and the Vehicle, ensuring that both entities participate in the acquisition and all subsequent investment decisions on a pro rata basis (28.57% Vehicle / 71.43% Fund IV). The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement provides for parallel economic treatment, meaning that Fund IV and the Vehicle receive the same terms with respect to the acquisition, any subsequent investments, and the ultimate disposition of the investment, subject to differences in their respective economic terms (e.g., the Vehicle\'s lower carried interest rate).
254: 
255: Any deviation from the pro rata allocation set forth in the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement requires the prior written consent of the Limited Partner (Ironside). This provision protects Ironside against dilution or adverse reallocation of investment economics as between Fund IV and the Vehicle.

Co-Investment Allocation Agreement.** A co-investment allocation agreement (the \"Co-Investment Allocation Agreement\") between Meridian Infrastructure Partners Fund IV, LP (Fund IV) and ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP (the Vehicle) has been negotiated and is in final form. The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement governs the allocation of the co-investment between Fund IV and the Vehicle, establishing the 28.57% (Vehicle) / 71.43% (Fund IV) pro rata split and the parallel investment mechanics applicable to the Cascadia acquisition. The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement ensures that Fund IV and the Vehicle participate in the acquisition on a pari passu basis, with proportionate economics, voting rights, and information rights at the portfolio-company level.

**3. Subscription Agreement.** Ironside\'s subscription agreement for its limited partner interest in the Partnership (the \"Subscription Agreement\") has been prepared and is scheduled for execution on July 29, 2022. The Subscription Agreement contains customary representations and warranties of the subscriber, including representations regarding accredited investor and qualified purchaser status, investment intent, and compliance with applicable securities laws.

**4. AML/KYC Certification.** Anti-money-laundering and know-your-customer certification documentation has been prepared separately and is dated July 28, 2022. The AML/KYC package includes all required identification and verification materials for Ironside and its principals, as well as the applicable certifications under the USA PATRIOT Act and the Bank Secrecy Act.

**5. Placement Agent Agreement.** Rivermark Capital Markets Inc. (\"Rivermark\") has been engaged as the placement agent for the Vehicle pursuant to a placement agent agreement executed between Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC and Rivermark. The placement agent fee is 0.35% of committed capital, resulting in a fee of One Million Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$1,050,000), payable at first close. C&H has reviewed the placement agent agreement and provided its analysis in a separate memorandum dated July 18, 2022.
**[D. Pending Formation Steps]{.underline}**
As of the date of this memorandum, the following formation steps remain pending and are expected to be completed in the near term:

> 1\. **Execution of Transaction Documents.** The LP Agreement, Side Letter, Subscription Agreement, and Co-Investment Allocation Agreement are anticipated to be executed by all parties on July 29, 2022, at first close.

> 2\. **First Capital Call.** The first capital call under the LP Agreement is anticipated for mid-August 2022. Based on preliminary estimates, the first capital call is expected to be approximately 7.5% of committed capital, or approximately \$22,500,000, to fund organizational expenses, the placement-agent fee, the representations and warranties insurance premium deposit, due-diligence costs and deposits, and the working-capital reserve.

> 3\. **Bank Account Opening.** A bank account for the Partnership\'s fund operations is to be opened at Atlas National Bank, N.A. The account opening documentation is being prepared and is expected to be completed prior to first close.

> 4\. **Ongoing Compliance Filings.** Annual Delaware franchise tax filings and annual report filings will be required going forward. The Firm will coordinate with the registered agent, Cascade Systems, and with the fund administrator, Kendrick Thorne & Associates LLP, to ensure timely compliance with all filing and payment obligations.
**[III. Partnership Structure and Capitalization]{.underline}**
**[A. Partners and Interests]{.underline}**
The Partnership has two partners: the General Partner and the Limited Partner. The Vehicle is structured as a single-LP co-investment vehicle with no additional limited partners anticipated.
**1. General Partner: Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC**

Meridian Infrastructure GP IV LLC serves as the sole general partner of the Partnership. The General Partner is a Delaware limited liability company organized for the purpose of serving as the general partner of Fund IV and its related co-investment vehicles, including the Vehicle. The key details of the General Partner are as follows:
> • **Entity Type:** Delaware limited liability company
> • **Managers:**
> • David R. Hargreaves, Managing Partner
> • Lillian Fong, Partner, Portfolio
> • Graham Whitfield, Partner, Operations
> • **Partnership Interest:** 0.01%
> • **Capital Commitment:** Thirty Thousand Dollars (\$30,000), representing 0.01% of the total committed capital of \$300,000,000
> • **Legal Counsel:** Breckenridge Sloane & Pratt LLP, represented by Charles A. Delacroix, lead partner, with offices at One Federal Street, Suite 3600, Boston, Massachusetts 02110

The General Partner acts through its three managers --- Hargreaves, Fong, and Whitfield --- or such authorized officers as the managers may designate from time to time in accordance with the GP\'s operating agreement.
**2. Limited Partner: Ironside Capital Management LP**
Ironside Capital Management LP serves as the sole limited partner of the Partnership. The key details of the Limited Partner are as follows:
> • **Entity Type:** Delaware limited partnership
> • **Headquarters:** 590 Madison Avenue, 38th Floor, New York, New York 10022
> • **Principals:**
> • Marcus J. Calloway, Founder & Chief Investment Officer
> • Renata Obasi, Senior Managing Director, Infrastructure
> • **Partnership Interest:** 99.99%
> • **Capital Commitment:** Two Hundred Ninety-Nine Million Nine Hundred Seventy Thousand Dollars (\$299,970,000), representing 99.99% of the total committed capital of \$300,000,000
> • **Assets Under Management:** Approximately \$14.8 billion firm-wide; approximately \$3.2 billion in infrastructure strategy across three investment vehicles
> • **Registration Status:** SEC-registered investment adviser under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940

Ironside is a well-established institutional asset manager with a significant existing allocation to infrastructure investments. The Cascadia co-investment represents a strategic opportunity for Ironside to increase its exposure to the renewable-energy and water-infrastructure sectors in the Pacific Northwest at favorable co-investment economics.
**[B. Total Committed Capital]{.underline}**

The total committed capital of the Partnership is Three Hundred Million Dollars (\$300,000,000). As noted above, the General Partner has committed \$30,000 (0.01%) and the Limited Partner has committed \$299,970,000 (99.99%).

The Vehicle is structured as a single-LP co-investment vehicle. No additional limited partners are anticipated, and the admission of any additional limited partners would require the prior written consent of the existing Limited Partner (Ironside) pursuant to Section 5.01 of the LP Agreement.
**[C. Economics]{.underline}**

The economic terms of the Vehicle have been negotiated to reflect the co-investment nature of the arrangement and are significantly more favorable to Ironside than the standard economic terms applicable to Fund IV\'s main limited partnership. The key economic terms are summarized below:

**Management Fee.** No management fee (0%) is charged on the Vehicle. The Side Letter expressly confirms that no management fee, monitoring fee, or similar ongoing fee is payable by the Partnership to the General Partner or any of its affiliates in connection with the Vehicle. This is a material economic benefit to Ironside, as Fund IV\'s main limited partnership is subject to a management fee of 2% per annum on committed capital during the investment period and 2% per annum on invested capital thereafter.

**Carried Interest.** The General Partner is entitled to a carried interest of 10% of net profits above the preferred return, as compared to the 20% carried interest applicable in Fund IV\'s main limited partnership. The reduced carried interest rate reflects the co-investment nature of the Vehicle and Ironside\'s significant capital commitment. The carried interest is subject to the distribution waterfall mechanics described in Section XI of this memorandum.

**Preferred Return.** The Limited Partner and the General Partner are entitled to a preferred return of 8% per annum, compounded quarterly, on their respective contributed capital. The preferred return must be satisfied in full before any carried interest is payable to the General Partner.

**GP Commitment.** The General Partner has committed \$30,000 (0.01% of total committed capital) as its capital contribution to the Partnership. While the GP commitment is modest in absolute terms, it is typical for co-investment vehicles where the sponsor\'s primary capital commitment is made through the main fund.
**[D. Purpose]{.underline}**

The sole purpose of the Partnership, as set forth in Section 2.01 of the LP Agreement, is to co-invest alongside Fund IV in the acquisition of 100% of the outstanding equity interests of Cascadia Renewables Holdings, Inc. through Cascadia Acquisition Corp., a Delaware corporation to be formed as the acquisition subsidiary. Cascadia Acquisition Corp. will be wholly owned, directly or indirectly, by Fund IV and the Vehicle in proportion to their respective equity commitments (71.43% Fund IV / 28.57% Vehicle).

The Vehicle\'s co-investment percentage of total equity is 28.57%, calculated as \$300,000,000 divided by \$1,050,000,000 in total equity commitments. The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement governs the allocation mechanics and ensures parallel treatment of Fund IV and the Vehicle throughout the life of the investment.

The Partnership is not authorized to engage in any business or activity other than the foregoing, and the General Partner is not authorized to cause the Partnership to make any investment other than the Cascadia co-investment without the prior written consent of the Limited Partner.
**[IV. Governance and Decision-Making Authority]{.underline}**
**[A. General Partner Authority (§3.01 of LP Agreement)]{.underline}**

Pursuant to Section 3.01 of the LP Agreement, the General Partner has exclusive authority to manage and control the business and affairs of the Partnership. This broad grant of authority is consistent with the default rules under DRULPA and with customary market practice for sponsor-led co-investment vehicles. Specifically, the General Partner\'s authority includes, without limitation, the following:

> \(a\) making, monitoring, and disposing of the Partnership\'s investment in Cascadia, including all decisions relating to the acquisition, post-closing management, restructuring, refinancing, and ultimate disposition of the investment;
> \(b\) issuing capital calls to the partners and managing capital contributions in accordance with the terms of the LP Agreement;
> \(c\) making distributions to the partners in accordance with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.01 of the LP Agreement;

> \(d\) executing transaction documents on behalf of the Partnership, including the Equity Purchase Agreement, ancillary acquisition agreements, financing agreements, and all other instruments and documents necessary or desirable in connection with the Cascadia acquisition;

> \(e\) engaging service providers on behalf of the Partnership, including fund administrators, independent auditors, tax preparers, legal counsel, valuation consultants, and any other advisors or consultants deemed necessary or appropriate by the General Partner;
> \(f\) incurring and paying expenses on behalf of the Partnership, including organizational expenses, ongoing operating expenses, and transaction-related expenses;

> \(g\) taking all actions necessary or desirable in connection with the Cascadia acquisition, including the negotiation and execution of the Equity Purchase Agreement, the stockholders\' agreement, the management services agreement, and all related transaction documents; and
> \(h\) generally taking all actions that the General Partner deems necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes of the Partnership and to protect the Partnership\'s investment.

The General Partner acts through its managers --- David R. Hargreaves (Managing Partner), Lillian Fong (Partner, Portfolio), and Graham Whitfield (Partner, Operations) --- or such other authorized officers or representatives as the managers may designate from time to time in accordance with the GP\'s operating agreement. Decisions of the General Partner are made by majority vote of the managers, except as otherwise provided in the GP\'s operating agreement.
**[B. Limitations on GP Authority]{.underline}**

Notwithstanding the broad grant of authority to the General Partner described above, the LP Agreement imposes certain limitations on the General Partner\'s authority. Specifically, the General Partner may not take any of the following actions without the prior written consent of the Limited Partner (Ironside):
> \(a\) amend, modify, or waive any provision of the LP Agreement or the Side Letter;
> \(b\) admit additional limited partners to the Partnership;
> \(c\) increase the aggregate capital commitments of the Partnership beyond \$300,000,000;
> \(d\) merge, consolidate, or convert the Partnership into another entity or form of organization;

> \(e\) voluntarily file for bankruptcy, make an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or consent to the appointment of a receiver or trustee for the Partnership or any substantial part of its assets;

> \(f\) enter into any related-party transaction (including any transaction with the General Partner, its affiliates, Fund IV, or their respective principals, officers, or employees) that is not expressly contemplated by the LP Agreement or the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement; and
> \(g\) extend the investment period or term of the Partnership beyond the limits set forth in the LP Agreement.

These consent requirements are designed to protect Ironside\'s interests as the sole limited partner and to ensure that the General Partner does not take any material action that could adversely affect Ironside\'s investment without Ironside\'s knowledge and approval. The consent requirements are consistent with market practice for single-LP co-investment vehicles and reflect the negotiated balance of authority between the General Partner and the Limited Partner.
**[C. LP Advisory Committee]{.underline}**

No formal Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") is established under the LP Agreement. The absence of a formal LPAC is appropriate given the single-LP structure of the Vehicle --- there is no need for a committee to represent the interests of multiple limited partners, as Ironside is the sole limited partner and has direct consent rights on all material matters.

In lieu of a formal LPAC, the Side Letter provides for direct consultation between the General Partner and Ironside on material matters affecting the Partnership and its investment. The GP has agreed to consult with Ironside in good faith on matters that would customarily be brought before an LPAC in a multi-investor fund, including conflict-of-interest matters, related-party transactions, valuation issues, and material deviations from the investment thesis.
**[D. Investment Decisions]{.underline}**

All investment decisions relating to the Partnership\'s investment in Cascadia are made by the General Partner in its sole discretion, subject to the limitations described in Section IV.B above. This includes decisions relating to the initial acquisition of Cascadia, any post-closing add-on investments or capital expenditures at the portfolio-company level, any restructuring, recapitalization, or refinancing of Cascadia, and any ultimate disposition or exit of the investment.

The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement governs the parallel investment mechanics between Fund IV and the Vehicle, ensuring that both entities participate in the acquisition and all subsequent investment decisions on a pro rata basis (28.57% Vehicle / 71.43% Fund IV). The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement provides for parallel economic treatment, meaning that Fund IV and the Vehicle receive the same terms with respect to the acquisition, any subsequent investments, and the ultimate disposition of the investment, subject to differences in their respective economic terms (e.g., the Vehicle\'s lower carried interest rate).

Any deviation from the pro rata allocation set forth in the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement requires the prior written consent of the Limited Partner (Ironside). This provision protects Ironside against dilution or adverse reallocation of investment economics as between Fund IV and the Vehicle.
**[V. Fiduciary Duties]{.underline}**

The Partnership shall establish a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"**LPAC**\") consisting of three (3) members. The members of the LPAC shall be appointed by the General Partner from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives; provided, however, that Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be entitled to appoint one (1) member of the LPAC for so long as Pellegrino Capital Group LLC holds a Partnership Interest in the Partnership. LPAC members shall serve in a non-fiduciary, advisory capacity, except where specific approval or consent rights are expressly conferred upon the LPAC by this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, LPAC members shall not owe any fiduciary duties to the Partnership or to any other Partner by virtue of their service on the LPAC.
**Section 9.2 --- LPAC Functions**
The LPAC shall have the following functions and responsibilities:
\(b\) Review and approve (or disapprove) all other matters requiring LPAC consent as set forth in Section 7.3;
**Section 9.3 --- LPAC Meetings**

\(a\) The LPAC shall meet at least once per calendar year, or more frequently as the General Partner or any two (2) LPAC members may request. Meetings may be held in person at the offices of the General Partner, by video conference, or by telephonic conference, as determined by the General Partner in consultation with the LPAC members.

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide at least ten (10) Business Days\' prior written notice of each meeting to all LPAC members, together with a written agenda and copies of any relevant materials to be discussed at such meeting.

\(c\) A quorum for any meeting of the LPAC shall consist of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members). Actions of the LPAC shall be taken by the affirmative vote or written consent of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members).
\(d\) Actions may be taken by the LPAC without a meeting by written consent signed by a majority of the LPAC members, which consent shall be effective as of the date of the last signature.
\(e\) The General Partner shall prepare and distribute to all LPAC members written minutes of each meeting within fifteen (15) Business Days following such meeting.
**Section 9.4 --- Indemnification of LPAC Members**

Each member of the LPAC shall be indemnified by the Partnership on the same basis as Covered Persons under Section 7.9 with respect to any Losses incurred by such member arising out of or in connection with such member\'s service on the LPAC. LPAC members acting in good faith in the performance of their duties as LPAC members shall have no personal liability to the Partnership, the General Partner, or any Limited Partner for any actions taken or omitted to be taken in their advisory capacity as LPAC members.
\(a\) The General Partner may remove any LPAC member for Cause upon written notice to such LPAC member and the Limited Partner that appointed or designated such member.

\(b\) Any Limited Partner that appointed or designated an LPAC member may, at any time, designate a replacement for such LPAC member by written notice to the General Partner, and such replacement shall become effective upon receipt of such notice by the General Partner.

\(c\) In the event of a vacancy on the LPAC (whether by removal, resignation, or otherwise), the General Partner shall appoint a replacement LPAC member from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives within thirty (30) days of such vacancy; provided, however, that any vacancy in the LPAC seat held by a designee of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be filled by a designee of Pellegrino Capital Group LLC.

> \(iv\) During the ninety (90)-day period referred to in clause (iii) above, the General Partner shall consult with the LPAC regarding a management transition plan, including the identification and evaluation of potential replacement key persons and the impact of the Key Person Event on the Investment.

The \"**Term**\" of the Partnership shall commence on the date of the filing of the Certificate of Limited Partnership with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware and shall continue until the tenth (10th) anniversary of the Closing Date (i.e., January 30, 2036), unless earlier dissolved pursuant to Section 11.2. The General Partner may extend the Term for up to two (2) additional one (1)-year periods (each, a \"**GP Extension**\"), subject to the prior written approval of a majority of the members of the LPAC pursuant to Section 7.3(e). If both GP Extensions are exercised, the maximum Term of the Partnership shall expire on January 30, 2038. The Term of the Partnership is intended to be co-terminous with the term of Fund IV as it relates to the Investment.

**(c) Partnership Representative.** The General Partner shall serve as the Partnership Representative under Section 6223 of the Code for all taxable years of the Partnership. The General Partner shall not settle, compromise, or take any position with respect to any tax audit, examination, or proceeding that would disproportionately adversely affect any Limited Partner without prior consultation with the LPAC. In the event the Partnership is subject to any tax audit adjustment, the General Partner shall, to the extent permitted by applicable law, elect to push out any imputed underpayment to the Partners under Section 6226 of the Code rather than paying the imputed underpayment at the Partnership level.

No amendment that adversely and disproportionately affects the economic or governance rights of a particular Limited Partner (including such Limited Partner\'s Preferred Return, Carried Interest allocation, Capital Commitment, Partnership Percentage, or LPAC seat) shall be effective without the prior written consent of such affected Limited Partner. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the General Partner may amend Schedule A without the consent of the Limited Partners to reflect (i) the admission of additional or substitute Limited Partners, (ii) the withdrawal or removal of Limited Partners, (iii) permitted Transfers of Partnership Interests, and (iv) adjustments to Capital Commitments and Partnership Percentages resulting from any of the foregoing.

Except as expressly provided herein with respect to the indemnification of Covered Persons (including LPAC members) under Sections 7.9 and 9.4, nothing in this Agreement, express or implied, is intended to or shall confer upon any Person other than the parties hereto and their permitted successors and assigns any legal or equitable right, benefit, claim, or remedy of any nature whatsoever under or by reason of this Agreement.

The General Partner may enter into Side Letters with one or more Limited Partners. The terms of any Side Letter shall supplement and, where expressly stated therein, modify or supersede the terms of this Agreement solely as to the Limited Partner that is a party to such Side Letter. Side Letters shall not be deemed to amend this Agreement as to any other Limited Partner unless such other Limited Partner is expressly entitled to the benefits thereof pursuant to a most-favored-nation provision contained in such other Limited Partner\'s Side Letter or this Agreement. The General Partner shall notify the LPAC of the existence of any Side Letters (without being required to disclose the specific terms thereof, unless such disclosure is required by the terms of a Side Letter or a most-favored-nation provision). **[Section 11.1 --- Composition]{.underline}**

\(a\) The General Partner shall establish and maintain a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the **\"LPAC\"**) composed of five (5) members, each of whom shall be a representative designated by a Limited Partner or a group of Limited Partners.

\(c\) The General Partner shall designate LPAC members from among the Limited Partners, taking into consideration the diversity of the Limited Partner base (including investor type, geographic location, and commitment size), the size of each Limited Partner\'s Capital Commitment, and the willingness and ability of such Limited Partner to serve on the LPAC. **[Section 11.2 --- Meetings]{.underline}**

\(a\) The LPAC shall hold at least two (2) meetings during each Fiscal Year. Meetings may be held in person, by video conference, or by telephone conference, as determined by the General Partner in consultation with the LPAC members.

\(b\) Special meetings of the LPAC may be convened by the General Partner at any time, or upon the written request of a majority of the LPAC members. The General Partner shall provide at least ten (10) Business Days\' advance written notice of each LPAC meeting (or such shorter notice as the circumstances may require), together with an agenda and relevant supporting materials.

\(c\) The General Partner\'s personnel, including the Key Persons, shall attend LPAC meetings and shall be available to respond to questions from LPAC members regarding the Fund\'s investments, operations, and performance.
\(d\) The General Partner shall prepare and distribute written minutes of each LPAC meeting to the LPAC members within thirty (30) days following such meeting.
**[Section 11.3 --- Scope of Authority]{.underline}**

\(a\) The LPAC shall act in an advisory and consent capacity only. The LPAC shall not have any management authority over the affairs of the Partnership and shall not participate in the control of the Partnership\'s business within the meaning of Section 17-303 of the Act.
\(b\) The following matters shall require the prior approval or consent of the LPAC:

> \(i\) Conflicts of interest and related-party transactions involving the General Partner, the Sponsor, or their Affiliates (including investments in portfolio companies of predecessor Harrowgate funds and transactions with Associates);

> \(ii\) Material changes to the Fund\'s valuation methodology, the resolution of significant valuation disputes with respect to Portfolio Investments, or any material change in the Fund\'s approach to the valuation of Portfolio Investments;
> \(iii\) Extension of the Fund Term beyond the second GP discretionary extension (i.e., the third one-year extension described in Section 2.5(c) shall require LPAC approval);
> \(iv\) Waivers of or exceptions to the investment restrictions set forth in Section 5.3, including the Concentration Limit, geographic limitations, and sector limitations;
> \(v\) In-kind Distributions of securities or other property to Partners (other than in connection with the liquidation and winding up of the Partnership pursuant to Article XIII);
> \(vi\) Changes to the appointment of the Independent Auditor;
> \(vii\) The pursuit or consummation of any \"hostile\" acquisition (i.e., an acquisition opposed by the target company\'s board of directors or management) or any unsolicited tender offer;
> \(viii\) Material changes to the Fund\'s co-investment allocation policies; and

> \(ix\) Any amendment, modification, or supplement to a Subscription Credit Facility agreement that would increase the maximum aggregate borrowing capacity above the Subscription Facility Limit (twenty-five percent (25%) of unfunded Capital Commitments);

> \(x\) Any change in the General Partner\'s investment allocation methodology as between the Fund and any Parallel Fund or co-investment vehicle, other than adjustments arising solely from the exercise of excuse rights or regulatory restrictions; and
> \(xi\) Such other matters as may be submitted to the LPAC by the General Partner from time to time.
\(c\) The LPAC\'s approval or consent shall not be required for any matter not expressly set forth in Section 11.3(b) or elsewhere in this Agreement.
**[Section 11.4 --- Quorum and Voting]{.underline}**
\(a\) A quorum for the transaction of business at any meeting of the LPAC shall consist of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., three (3) out of five (5) members).
\(b\) All actions of the LPAC shall be taken by the affirmative vote of a majority of the LPAC members present and constituting a quorum.

**ACKNOWLEDGMENT OF LIMITED PARTNER CONSENT:**

The Limited Partners of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. have consented to this Amendment by written consent in accordance with Section 14.01 of the Agreement. Written consents were received from thirty-eight (38) of forty-seven (47) Limited Partners, representing aggregate capital commitments of \$2,412,800,000 (approximately 86.2% of voting Limited Partner capital commitments), which exceeds the required sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) threshold. **CARRIED INTEREST ALLOCATION**

This Exhibit A sets forth the amended and restated Schedule A to the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (as amended by the First Amendment dated as of August 26, 2024, the \"Agreement\"), and replaces the prior Schedule A in its entirety.
**1. Fund Economics**
The Partnership operates under a 2/20 fee structure, as follows:

> \(a\) **Management Fee:** Two percent (2.0%) of net asset value per annum, payable quarterly in advance. Based on the Partnership\'s net asset value of approximately \$2,870,000,000 as of May 31, 2024, the quarterly management fee is approximately \$14,350,000.
> \(b\) **Incentive Allocation:** Twenty percent (20%) of net new profits above the high-water mark, determined on a per-unit basis. The per-unit high-water mark as of December 31, 2023 is \$142.67.
